dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.modesIntro: Three ways families structure 4SD0 support, with the cost logic of each stated plainly. The right one depends on what the diagnostic finds, not on what sounds most thorough, and the most expensive option is rarely the one that moves a grade fastest.

modes.title: One science tutor, one hour a week
modes.description: The default for a student in Year 10 or early Year 11 whose three strands are uneven but none is in trouble. A single tutor carries all three papers, rotates according to what the school is teaching, and holds the revision calendar. It is the lowest-cost structure that still produces continuity, and it is the only structure where one person can see that a physics problem is actually a maths problem.
bullets: One booking, one rate, three papers covered
Rotation follows the school scheme of work, not a fixed order
Cheapest route to continuity across a two-year course
Weekly cadence suits content that is still being taught

modes.title: A paper-specific block of six
modes.description: Bought when the diagnostic names one paper. Six sessions on chemistry calculations, or on biology explanation structure, with a re-test at the end. The block has a defined endpoint and a defined cost, which makes it the easiest structure to evaluate. Families who have already paid for a term of general science tuition without movement usually get more from this than from extending that term.
bullets: Defined scope, defined session count, defined spend
Ends with a timed paper under exam conditions
Suits a known weakness rather than a general wobble
Can be repeated on a second paper if the re-test justifies it

modes.title: Pre-series and pre-mock intensives
modes.description: A short concentrated run before a mock window or an exam series, built around timed papers and the marking of them. It is the highest cost per week and the lowest cost per outcome when the content is genuinely known and the marks are being lost to timing, question reading and answer order. It is the wrong purchase when content gaps remain, because intensity does not teach moles.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week for three to five weeks
Every session built on a timed paper the student has already sat
Priced as a block so the total is known in advance
Not appropriate while content gaps are still open

sections.heading: The five variables that move a 4SD0 quote in Dubai
paragraphs: An hourly rate quoted without context is not information. The same tutor, the same subject and the same child can produce quotes a hundred dirhams apart depending on five things, and four of the five are visible to you before you commit. The table below sets out each variable, which direction it pushes the rate, roughly how far, and why the mechanism works that way in this emirate specifically rather than in general.

Read the table as a checklist for the first phone call. If a provider cannot tell you which tier their tutor sits in, whether the rate assumes travel, which paper the hours will target, and what changes if you book in September rather than March, the quote is not comparable with anyone else's. Three of those four answers should take under a minute to give.

The one variable that is not in your control is the timing of the emirate-wide demand wave. Dubai Year 11 cohorts sit the same series, so the whole city wants a chemistry specialist in the same eight weeks. That is a supply fact, not a sales tactic, and the only defence against it is booking earlier than the wave.

Note what is missing from the table: a line for the tutor's nationality, a line for the number of years they have taught, and a line for a brand name. None of those three reliably predicts movement on a 4SD0 paper. What predicts movement is whether the person has marked work at this level recently and can tell you, from a script, where the marks went.
bullets: Ask which tier the quoted tutor sits in, and what the next tier up costs
Ask whether the rate assumes travel, and what the online rate is
Ask which paper the first six hours will target, and why
Ask what the same plan costs if you start a term earlier

sections.heading: Why Dubai's school sector is the reason the rate card looks like this
paragraphs: Tuition prices in a city are a function of how many qualified people live there and how many families want them at once. Dubai's numbers are published, which makes this calculable rather than anecdotal. KHDA reported 387,441 students in 227 private schools for 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools taking 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian curricula 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent.

That UK-curriculum share is the single most useful figure for a parent costing International GCSE science. It means the supply of teachers who have actually taught and marked Pearson science at this level is large by regional standards, and a large supply holds the qualified tier near the AED 150 to AED 300 band rather than pushing every competent tutor into premium pricing. In a smaller market the same tutor would cost more because there would be fewer of them.

The sector is still growing, which matters for next year's prices rather than this year's. KHDA reported six new private schools opening during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6 per cent, and a further seven schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. More UK-curriculum places means more International GCSE candidates and more competing demand in the same spring window.

On the household side, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai do not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That is a genuine input to a tutoring budget conversation: for one year, the school line in your education spending is flat, which is the cleanest opportunity most families get to fund a targeted block of science support without increasing the total.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition, costed for a Dubai household
paragraphs: The home-tutor question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales position. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is a real service with real advantages: a younger child stays in a familiar setting, a parent can observe, and nobody has to manage a screen. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts it at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions.

Those numbers include something invisible: the drive. A tutor who spends seventy minutes on the road to deliver a sixty-minute lesson in Arabian Ranches has to recover that time somewhere, and it is recovered in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, or in a tighter geographic radius that shrinks your choice of tutor. None of those three is dishonest. They are simply what travel costs in a city this size.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For a Dubai family the practical consequence is that the pool is not limited to people who can reach your community on a weekday afternoon. If the diagnostic says the chemistry strand is the problem, the hour goes to whoever is strongest on that paper rather than to whoever is nearest, and the travel premium stays in your pocket.

Group classes at a tuition centre are the genuine low-cost option and should not be dismissed. They work when a student needs content delivered again at a steady pace and is capable of asking questions in a room. They work badly for a 4SD0 student whose three strands are uneven, because a group moves at one speed through one paper and your child is losing marks in a different one.

sections.heading: The costs that are not the tutor: entries, resits and the Pearson calendar
paragraphs: Two line items surprise Dubai families every year, and neither is a tuition cost. The first is the entry itself, which a school ordinarily handles and absorbs into fees for enrolled students, and which a private candidate pays directly to a centre that accepts external entries. The second is the resit, which is cheap in tuition terms and expensive in calendar terms, because the entry deadline sits months before the paper.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are examined in a May or June series and again in November each year. For the November 2026 series, the final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are Pearson's published dates, and they are the skeleton any 4SD0 plan hangs on.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and revises them. The practical rule is to work from the live official timetable on the Pearson support site rather than from a date printed on any tutoring page, including this one. Your school's exams officer has the authoritative version for your child's centre and will give it to you if asked.

Count backwards from the table below and the spending pattern becomes obvious. Tuition bought in the eight weeks before a series is buying exam technique at peak demand. Tuition bought two terms earlier is buying content at ordinary prices, and it is the content that determines whether the technique has anything to work with.

sections.heading: Measuring 4SD0 tuition against the Dubai school fee line
paragraphs: Tutoring spend only makes sense next to the other education numbers in a household. For Dubai families the dominant one is school fees, and for 2026-27 that number is unusually stable: KHDA confirmed no increase for the coming academic year. A flat school line is the context in which a science support decision should be taken, because it is the one year where adding a block does not compound with an annual fee rise.

The table below is a planning frame rather than a price list. IB Gram does not publish an hourly rate on these pages, and any figure attached to our name here would be an invention. What the table does is convert published market bands into the shapes families actually buy, so that a quote can be sanity-checked against a pattern rather than against a feeling.

The important column is the third one. One session a week for a school year is roughly thirty-two to thirty-six sessions, and at the qualified tier that is a four-figure monthly commitment maintained for most of a year. A six-session diagnostic block costs a fraction of that and answers the question the year-long plan assumes it already knows. Buying the block first is the cheaper sequence in almost every case.

Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those bands are the sanity check: a quote well outside them in either direction deserves a specific explanation before you accept it.

sections.heading: What the private tuition permit does and does not add to the price
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and parents are entitled to ask about it without embarrassment. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Because the permit costs nothing, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee, and any provider presenting one is describing something else. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route, and it is the page to check rather than any summary of it.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount can responsibly be quoted, and a figure circulating online is not a figure you should treat as real. What you can do is ask the question directly and note how the answer arrives.

There is one boundary worth knowing in advance. A teacher at your child's own school tutoring your child privately sits against the professional-ethics rules and the permit's code of conduct, which bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's rules for private and charter school staff are explicit on this. Treat an offer of paid tuition from your child's own class teacher as a problem to avoid rather than an opportunity, whichever emirate you are in. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no UAE premises.

sections.heading: Spending where the marks are: a 4SD0 diagnostic in four questions
paragraphs: Before buying any hours, four questions answered from evidence will tell you more than three consultations. Each one needs a document rather than an opinion, and all four documents already exist somewhere in your child's school bag or portal. This is the cheapest half-hour available in the whole process and almost nobody spends it.

First, how do the three strand marks actually split? A Double Award grade reported as two grades hides the internal distribution. School assessment data usually shows it. A student at grade 5 overall who sits at 7, 5 and 3 across the three papers has a completely different purchase to make than a student who sits at 5, 5 and 5, and the first student's plan is both shorter and cheaper.

Second, on the weakest paper, where did the marks go? Read one marked script with the mark scheme beside it. Marks lost on the final part of multi-step calculations point to content. Marks lost on explanation questions where the facts are all present point to answer order. Marks lost at the end of the paper point to timing. Those three findings buy three different products at three different prices.

Third, is the blockage actually maths? Take the chemistry and physics questions your child dropped and strip the science out of them. If what remains is rearranging a formula, handling a ratio, or converting units, the money belongs in Mathematics A, not in science. Fourth, what has the school already offered? Departmental clinics, revision sessions and past-paper packs are included in fees you have already paid, and a tutor should ask about them in the first conversation rather than the fifth.
bullets: Pull the strand-level marks, not just the reported grade
Read one marked script against the mark scheme before buying anything
Test whether the dropped marks are science or arithmetic
Ask the school what free support already exists this term

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not be paid to do on this qualification
paragraphs: 4SD0 has no coursework component, which removes the most common integrity problem in international qualifications. It does not remove all of them. A student still submits homework, mock responses and internal assessments that a school uses to set predicted grades, and those must be the student's own work. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback. A tutor does not supply answers for submission under a student's name.

The practical line is about sequence. A tutor who reads a student's attempt, marks it, explains why a mark was lost and sets a comparable question is doing the job. Someone who hands over a model response for a piece of work that will be submitted is not teaching, and the exposure lands on the student rather than on them. This distinction is worth stating to any provider you speak to, and worth noticing in how they answer.

The second boundary is material. Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Pearson. They are referenced and linked, not reproduced or distributed as downloads by a tutoring service. Any provider offering a bundle of papers as a selling point is describing something they are not entitled to supply, and that is a reasonable reason to be cautious about everything else they say.

The third is credentials. Nobody at IB Gram is described as a Pearson examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status is never presented as access to marking, boundaries or unreleased paper content. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from Pearson, Edexcel, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and no page on this site should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: Five questions that make two Dubai quotes comparable
paragraphs: Most parents ring three providers, hear three hourly rates and pick in the middle. The rates are not comparable, because they describe different products. Five questions turn three numbers into three like-for-like offers, and all five can be asked in one call.

Ask what is included beyond the lesson hour. Marking of a timed paper takes real time, and a provider who includes it has priced it in somewhere. Ask who marks it and what you receive afterwards. A written note naming the marks lost and the next piece of work is a different product from a verbal summary at the end of a call, and the difference shows up in whether anything changes by week four.

Ask what happens if the match is wrong. A clear replacement policy costs the provider something and is therefore a signal. Ask whether the trial is genuinely free and what condition attaches to it, because a conditional free trial that is not described as conditional is the first thing to distrust. Ask what the exit looks like after one month, in writing.

Ask for a plan with a stopping point. Six sessions and a re-test, with a decision at the end about whether to continue, is a proposal you can evaluate. An open-ended weekly commitment is a subscription. Finally, ask what the provider will do about the maths if the diagnostic says the science is not the problem. The honest answer involves sending you somewhere else for part of the work, and a provider who can say that is the one worth booking.
bullets: What is included beyond the hour, and who does the marking?
What does the written output after a session actually look like?
What is the replacement policy, and what conditions attach to the trial?
Is there a defined stopping point and a re-test?
What happens if the real weakness turns out to be Mathematics A?

process.title: Send the strand marks and one marked script
process.description: Share the latest school report, the strand-level breakdown across biology, chemistry and physics if the school publishes it, and one marked 4SD0 response. Three documents are enough to tell whether the problem is content, technique or the maths underneath, and they cost nothing to send.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor sets questions from the weakest paper, watches how the student approaches them, and writes down where the marks are going. The output is a short written finding you keep whether or not you continue.

process.title: A written plan with the cost attached
process.description: You receive a plan that names the target paper, the number of sessions, what each session covers and what the total comes to before anything is booked. If the finding is that school support or a maths intervention is the better first step, the plan says that instead.

process.title: Sessions at the intensity the evidence supports
process.description: Weekly where content is still being taught, blocked where a single paper needs rebuilding, intensive only when content is secure and marks are being lost to timing. Slots are set in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day and the family's actual evenings.

process.title: A re-test and a spending decision
process.description: At the end of a block the student sits a timed paper under exam conditions and it is marked against the published criteria. You then decide whether to continue, switch paper, or stop. The decision is based on a marked script, not on a progress adjective.

whyPoints.title: Every dirham figure here names its source
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page is attributed to the company or rate table that published it, with no figure presented as IB Gram's own price. A parent comparing quotes can check the originals rather than take ours on trust.

whyPoints.title: One tutor across three papers
whyPoints.description: 4SD0 is one qualification. A single lead tutor holding biology, chemistry and physics sees that the physics problem is a rearrangement problem and the biology problem is a writing problem, which three separate bookings structurally cannot.

whyPoints.title: The quote comes after the diagnostic, not before
whyPoints.description: Pricing a plan before reading a marked script prices the average student. The free trial is used to find where the marks are actually going, and the written plan and its cost follow that finding rather than preceding it.

whyPoints.title: Free school support gets named first
whyPoints.description: Departmental clinics, revision sessions and past-paper packs are already inside fees you pay. A plan that ignores them is overcharging you by omission, so the first conversation asks what the school already provides this term.

whyPoints.title: A stated line around the student's own work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, mark and give feedback on work the student has produced. No response is supplied for submission under a student's name, and no Pearson papers or mark schemes are distributed as downloads.

whyPoints.title: A plan you can stop
whyPoints.description: Blocks have a defined session count, a defined cost and a re-test at the end, so continuing is a decision rather than a default. Delivery is online one-to-one over live video, with no travel premium inside the rate.

faqs.question: What should I expect to pay for Edexcel IGCSE Science Double Award 4SD0 tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates for International GCSE science run from about AED 45 an hour at the university-student tier up to AED 650 at the named-examiner tier. EdFlik publishes AED 45 to AED 65, Tutopiya AED 33 to AED 52, Unitors from AED 150, TutorChase AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Most families with a specific 4SD0 paper problem land in the AED 150 to AED 300 online band. IB Gram quotes after a diagnostic rather than publishing a rate card.

faqs.question: Why do two Dubai tutors quote such different rates for the same 4SD0 paper?
faqs.answer: Because they are selling different products under the same name. The gap between AED 60 and AED 300 an hour usually reflects whether the person has marked work at this level recently, whether the rate includes marking a timed paper and writing up what it showed, and whether travel is inside the fee. A student-tier hour supervises practice. A qualified-tier hour diagnoses a mark loss and fixes it. Both are legitimate purchases for different problems, but a parent comparing only the number is comparing a lesson with a lesson plus marking plus a written finding.

faqs.question: Is 4SD0 cheaper to support than taking separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and the saving is in hours rather than in the hourly rate. Double Award covers less content per science than the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 courses, and one tutor can hold all three papers because they belong to one qualification. The separate route cannot carry a weak strand on the strength of the other two, so a gap there has to be closed with contact hours. Compare total tuition hours across two years rather than rates per hour, which is where the real difference between the two routes shows up.

faqs.question: Does an online 4SD0 hour cost less than a visiting tutor's hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: On published rates, yes. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, while Unitors lists online International GCSE tuition from AED 150. The difference is largely the drive: a tutor crossing Dubai in school-run traffic recovers that time in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, or in a smaller service radius. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the pool is not limited by distance and the hour goes to whoever is strongest on the paper you need.

faqs.question: Which of the three 4SD0 papers usually needs the most paid hours?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, in most cases. Moles, equation balancing, reacting masses and concentration work are sequential, so a gap three steps earlier makes the visible question impossible and no amount of practice on the visible question helps. That takes real teaching time. The biology strand is often the opposite: the content is known and the marks are lost on explanation order, which a short technique block can move. Physics sits between them, and physics work frequently improves the chemistry calculations as a side effect because the underlying numeracy is shared.

faqs.question: How many hours of 4SD0 tuition does a Dubai Year 11 student typically end up buying?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the diagnostic finds, which is why a credible provider will not answer this before seeing a script. A technique problem on one paper is commonly six sessions and a re-test. A content gap in the chemistry strand is a term of weekly work. A student uneven across all three strands in the spring of Year 11 is a different and larger purchase. The cheapest sequence is almost always to buy a defined six-session block first and let its re-test decide whether a longer commitment is justified.

faqs.question: Is there a practical exam in 4SD0 that we need to budget extra sessions for?
faqs.answer: No. Science Double Award has no coursework component and no separately examined practical, so there is no additional assessment to prepare or pay for. Experimental skill is tested inside the three written papers, through questions that describe an experiment and ask the student to identify variables, spot what was controlled, read data and write a conclusion grounded in that data rather than in the theory. Those marks are learnable in ordinary sessions, and they are a common quiet loss for students who revise content and never practise the experiment questions.

faqs.question: Do science tuition rates in Dubai rise as the exam series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effective prices rise even where advertised rates do not, because availability collapses. Dubai Year 11 cohorts sit the same series, so demand for chemistry specialists concentrates into the same eight weeks and the tutors with the strongest reputations are committed by January. What a family then pays is a higher rate, a less experienced tutor, or an awkward slot. Booking in the autumn buys content teaching at ordinary prices; booking in March buys triage at scarcity prices. The lever is the calendar, not the negotiation.

faqs.question: Are monthly packages better value than paying per hour for science tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They can be, and the thing to examine is not the headline saving but the terms. Market packages seen in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. A package is good value when the cadence is genuinely what the plan needs and the slot is held for you. It is poor value when it locks in a frequency a diagnostic has not justified, or when unused sessions expire. Ask what happens to a missed session in writing before committing.

faqs.question: Does the KHDA fee freeze for 2026-27 change what we can spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes the arithmetic rather than the advice. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai do not rise for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For one academic year the largest line in a family's education spending is flat, which is the cleanest window most households get to fund a defined block of science support without raising the total. It is not a reason to buy a year of weekly sessions. It is a reason to buy the diagnostic block you had been postponing.

faqs.question: Do we pay anything towards a tutor's UAE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: No, because the permit itself is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page for it lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Any rate component presented to you as a permit or licensing fee is describing something else. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted online as unverified.

faqs.question: What does it cost to sit 4SD0 again in the November series?
faqs.answer: The tuition part is usually small: a resit is a paper-level repair, not a two-year course repeated, so a defined block aimed at the weakest paper is the normal shape. The entry is the part that needs checking. A student still at a Dubai school ordinarily has entries handled by the school. A student who has left sits as a private candidate through a centre that accepts external entries, and that centre sets both its fee and its registration cut-off. Confirm the cut-off before buying hours, because the deadline fixes your calendar.

faqs.question: Can a small group class bring the per-child cost of 4SD0 down?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and that saving is real. What a group cannot split is the diagnosis. A class moves at one pace through one paper, which suits a student who needs content delivered again and can ask questions in a room. It suits a 4SD0 student much less well when the three strands are uneven, because the group will spend its time where the median student needs it rather than where your child is dropping marks. A sensible hybrid is group content work plus a short one-to-one block on the weakest paper.

faqs.question: Will a Double Award count as two subjects for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: 4SD0 reports two International GCSE grades, and the published MoE requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. How a specific awarding structure is counted is a decision for the Ministry and the attestation authority, not for a tutoring service, so verify your child's case on moe.gov.ae or with the school's registrar. IB Gram does not perform, guarantee or influence equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan hours affect a Dubai science tuition schedule?
faqs.answer: Shortened school days move the whole afternoon, and sessions that normally sit at 16:00 commonly shift later or to post-Iftar timing. Because delivery here is online over live video, that change costs nothing but a calendar edit, and no travel window has to be rebuilt around it. The planning point is content rather than timing: Ramadan often falls close to mock windows, so the sensible move is to finish content teaching before it and use the period for lighter, shorter consolidation work rather than for introducing the chemistry calculations.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.closingHeading: Price the job, then book the hour
dubai/edexcel-igcse-science-double-award.closingBody: You now have the published bands, the five variables that move them, the exam-cycle costs that sit outside tuition altogether, and the five questions that make two Dubai quotes comparable. The next step costs nothing: send the strand marks and one marked 4SD0 script, take the free trial as a diagnostic, and read the written finding. If the finding says the chemistry strand needs six sessions, you will have a plan with a number attached. If it says the school's own clinic or a Mathematics A intervention is the better first move, you will be told that instead. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work in Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications rather than in a generic Year 10 and 11 syllabus. Each lists the codes they teach, the papers they mark against and the tier they usually prepare students for, so you can match a tutor to an entry statement instead of to a subject label.

intro.heading: Start with the code, not the subject name
paragraphs: Most Dubai parents searching for an Edexcel IGCSE tutor describe the subject: maths, physics, English. The exam board describes something narrower. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A carries the code 4MA1 and is sat in two tiers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is 4PH1 and has no tiers at all. English Language A is 4EA1 and offers a coursework alternative to one written paper, which Cambridge's equivalent does not. Those are not trivia. They decide which grades are reachable, which papers are worth practising, and whether a piece of written work your child does at home counts towards the final mark.

The first thing to find, then, is the exam-entry statement your child's school issues. It lists each subject with its Pearson code and, for a tiered subject, the tier entered. A school in Al Barsha may enter Mathematics A at Higher while a school in Mirdif enters the same student at Foundation; the teaching that follows is different in content, pace and ceiling. A tutor who starts work without that sheet is guessing, and a term of guessing is expensive in a way that shows up only in May.

Dubai makes this more common than it would be in London. KHDA inspected 227 private schools in the emirate in 2024-25, serving 387,441 students across 17 different licensed curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest single group by enrolment. Families move between those schools mid-course far more often than they would at home, and a move can change exam board as well as uniform. A child who spent Year 10 on Cambridge 0580 and arrives in Year 11 on Pearson 4MA1 has met most of the content and almost none of the paper conventions.

What a specification-literate tutor does first is unglamorous. They read the entry statement, pull the current Pearson specification and sample assessment material from qualifications.pearson.com, and check the student's last two school assessments against the actual mark scheme rather than the teacher's percentage. That exercise usually relocates the problem. A student described as weak at physics turns out to lose nine marks across a paper on six-mark extended-response questions and two marks on everything else, which is a writing problem with a physics label on it.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run in-person tutoring in Dubai, and home visits in the UAE are not part of what we sell: that is an India-only service. The reason is practical rather than ideological. There are only so many people within a twenty-minute drive of Jumeirah who can teach 4CH1 organic chemistry properly, and the live-video format replaces that constraint with a different one — find the specialist, book them at 18:00 Dubai time, keep the same tutor through to the series.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: An Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Dubai is usually brought in at one of four points: the Key Stage 3 years where the gap opens quietly, the two IGCSE years themselves, the International A Level route that follows, or the IB Diploma route that a British-curriculum Dubai school often offers alongside it.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary (Key Stage 3)
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins. No external exam sits at the end, which is exactly why gaps survive here: negative indices, rearranging formulae, balancing equations and paragraph structure are all taught once in Year 8 and assumed forever afterwards. Work at this stage is cheap in hours and expensive to skip, because every one of those skills is load-bearing in a 4MA1 or 4CH1 paper two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's British-curriculum schools stream for maths from Year 8 or Year 9 in many cases, and that streaming decision is frequently what determines whether a student is later entered for Foundation or Higher tier at 4MA1. Families who only discover tiering in Year 11 are reacting to a decision made three years earlier. Checking the set your child is in, and what it implies for tier, is a ten-minute conversation with the head of maths.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year course assessed at the end, graded 9-1, with a separate code for every subject. Most Dubai students take eight to ten subjects. Pearson's International GCSE is designed for international centres, which is why it is untimetabled against UK GCSE and why its November series exists. Assessment is almost entirely by written paper, with a small number of subjects offering a coursework component as an alternative.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical consequence is scheduling. A student taking ten subjects across the May/June series sits something close to twenty papers in four weeks, against a school calendar that already includes Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies as mandatory subjects under KHDA rules. The revision plan that works is one built backwards from the actual paper order, which the school's exams officer publishes once Pearson's final timetable is out.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: The two-year route most Dubai Edexcel students continue into. Pearson's International A Level is modular in structure, assessed in units that can be sat across sittings, which changes revision planning completely compared with a terminal course. Students who learned to cram for one terminal series often mismanage the first unit sitting, because the unit arrives much earlier than they expect.
programmes.countryNote: The subject choice made at the end of Year 11 is partly decided by the IGCSE grade profile and partly by what the Dubai school can staff. A school may run Edexcel International A Level Mathematics but not Further Mathematics, or Chemistry but not Biology in a given cohort. Students in that position sometimes sit a unit as a private candidate, which is a logistical exercise worth starting early with the exams officer.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other post-16 route, offered by a sizeable group of Dubai schools alongside or instead of A Levels. The Diploma asks for six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. For a student coming out of Pearson International GCSEs, the hardest adjustment is not content but the internally assessed work, which has no equivalent in most 4-series specifications.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is one of the few cities where a family genuinely chooses between the two at sixteen, sometimes within the same school group. The IGCSE grade profile informs it: strong, even grades across nine subjects suit the Diploma's breadth, while a sharply peaked profile in three subjects often suits A Levels. Neither route is harder in the abstract, and no tutor should tell you otherwise without seeing the grades.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects Dubai families most often ask about, with the code, the structure and the place marks are usually lost. Confirm every code against your child's own entry statement, because Pearson publishes more than one specification in several of these subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, each two hours and 100 marks, weighted equally. Foundation tier reaches grade 5; Higher tier runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. Marks go missing on multi-step problems where method marks are available but no working is shown, and on the last three questions of Paper 2, which most students never reach in a timed run.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Paper 1P is two hours and 110 marks; Paper 2P is an hour and a quarter and 70 marks. Untiered, so a grade 9 is reachable from any set. The reliable losses are unit conversion, the difference between describe and explain, and practical-method questions where students report what happened instead of what would control the variable.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Same paper architecture as Physics: a long Paper 1C and a shorter Paper 2C. Organic chemistry and moles calculations absorb most tutoring time in Dubai. Students lose marks by writing unbalanced equations, omitting state symbols where the mark scheme requires them, and giving an observation where the question asked for an inference.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Paper 1B and Paper 2B, with the longer paper carrying the bulk of the marks. Biology looks like a memory subject and is marked like a precision subject: the mark scheme rewards named structures, directional language and correct comparatives. Extended-response questions on transport, genetics and ecology are where grade 7 students separate from grade 5 students.

subjects.name: Science (Double Award) (4SD0)
subjects.description: The combined route, covering biology, chemistry and physics content at reduced depth and awarding two grades. Students entered for Double Award sometimes revise from separate-science resources and waste weeks on content outside their specification. Checking the specification against the revision material is the single highest-value first session for this entry.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with a coursework route
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers non-fiction reading and transactional writing; the second component can be sat as a written paper or taken as coursework, depending on what the school offers. Marks are lost in the reading section by summarising rather than analysing, and in the writing section by ignoring the stated form, audience and purpose.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with a coursework route
subjects.description: Assessed on poetry, prose and drama, with a coursework option available to centres that offer it. The common failure is the unseen poetry response, where students write about theme and never about method. Quotation handling and the ability to write about structure rather than plot are the two skills that move a grade here.

subjects.name: History (4HI1)
subjects.description: Depth studies and a breadth investigation across two papers of equal weight. Source questions reward provenance and purpose, not content summary, and students who describe a source rather than interrogate it cap themselves. Essay questions need a sustained line of argument; narrative chronology scores in the middle bands and stays there.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1)
subjects.description: Physical and human geography across two papers, with case-study detail carrying real marks. Dubai students often have excellent generic knowledge and no named, dated, located case studies, which is precisely what the mark scheme asks for. Fieldwork-style questions on data presentation and sampling are a reliable recovery area.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1) and Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Both reward diagram accuracy and evaluation. Students draw a supply and demand diagram without labelling axes and lose the mark that was there for the labelling. Evaluation marks need a judgement with a stated condition, not a list of advantages and disadvantages, and that is a learnable sentence pattern rather than a talent.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Dubai families ask about an Edexcel IGCSE tutor from every part of the city, and the local detail that matters is rarely distance. It is what time a lesson can realistically start once the school run, the commute and the mandatory-subject homework have happened.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Tower living with short walks to school for some families and a Sheikh Zayed Road crossing for others. Evening slots from 17:30 work; a shared study space in a two-bedroom flat is usually the real constraint rather than the schedule.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubailand
regions.note: Villa communities with long school-bus routes. Students often get home after 16:30, which pushes a sensible first slot to 18:00. The upside is a quiet room and a desk, which makes a ninety-minute session viable midweek.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: A dense British-curriculum catchment with heavy afternoon traffic on Algeria Street and Tripoli Street. Families here frequently run two children through tutoring in the same evening, which only works if sessions are back-to-back rather than overlapping.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Short school runs, early finishes, and a strong preference for 16:30 starts in Years 10 and 11. The academic pattern here is high-performing students chasing grade 8 and 9 rather than students in difficulty, which changes what a session has to do.

regions.name: Al Barsha and TECOM
regions.note: A cluster of large British-curriculum schools and a correspondingly wide range of sets within a single year group. Tier questions in Mathematics A come up more here than anywhere else in the city, usually in Year 10 term two.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Long bus routes from across the city and a student body spread over several curricula. November-series entries and private-candidate questions appear more often here, partly because families moving mid-year land in this catchment.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown
regions.note: Apartment addresses with working parents and later evenings. A 19:00 or 19:30 slot is normal rather than exceptional, and the weekly rhythm survives better when the same slot is held all term rather than rebooked each week.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai: Al Barsha, Marina, Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: The densest concentration of British-curriculum secondary provision in the emirate. Which exam board a school enters is a school decision and can differ by subject within the same school, so confirm it with the exams officer rather than assuming from the curriculum label.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and central Dubai: Mirdif, Al Garhoud, Dubai Silicon Oasis
schoolClusters.note: A wider mix of fee bands and curricula, and a catchment where mid-year arrivals from other systems are common. Students here often sit a mixture of boards across their subject list, which makes the entry statement the only reliable source of truth.

The session follows the school's scheme of work rather than racing ahead of it, with the week's class content checked against the specification and the gaps dealt with while they are still small. This is the pattern that produces the least drama in Year 11.

sections.heading: Which Pearson Edexcel codes Dubai schools actually enter
paragraphs: A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subject is defined by its code, and the code is printed on the exam-entry statement the school issues each series. Mathematics A is 4MA1. Physics, Chemistry and Biology are 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The combined route is Science (Double Award), 4SD0. English Language A is 4EA1 and English Literature is 4ET1. History is 4HI1, Geography 4GE1, Economics 4EC1, Business 4BS1 and Information and Communication Technology 4IT1. Those codes are the search terms that return the right specification, the right sample assessment material and the right past papers.

The reason this matters more in Dubai than in most markets is movement between schools and between boards. A student may sit Cambridge in one subject and Pearson in another, because the decision is taken department by department. A tutor who assumes Cambridge conventions on a Pearson paper will teach a student to answer in a form the mark scheme does not reward, and the student will do exactly what they were taught and still drop marks.

The practical check takes one evening. Pull the entry statement, list every subject with its code and tier, and then open the current specification for each one on qualifications.pearson.com. Compare the topic list against what the school has actually taught by now. In most cases the match is close. Where it is not — a topic covered in class that is not on the specification, or a specification section the class has not reached by March of Year 11 — you have found the thing worth paying a tutor to deal with.

One further warning. Pearson publishes more than one specification in several subjects, and schools change between them. Mathematics A and Mathematics B are different qualifications with different papers. Checking that the revision guide on your child's desk carries the same code as the entry statement is a two-minute exercise that occasionally saves a term.

sections.heading: Tiering in Mathematics A, and the grade ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is sat at one of two tiers. Foundation tier covers less content and its grade range stops at 5. Higher tier covers more content and runs from 9 down to 4, with an allowed grade 3 for candidates who fall just below. This is the only mainstream decision in the IGCSE course that sets a hard ceiling on what a student can be awarded, and in Dubai schools it is often made quietly, by set placement, a year before anyone discusses it with parents.

The honest version of the trade-off is this. A student placed on Foundation who is capable of a grade 6 is being capped. A student pushed onto Higher who cannot reliably answer the first ten questions of Paper 1 will sit two papers where most of the content is out of reach, and will often come out below the grade 5 they could have secured at Foundation. Neither error is rare, and both are visible in mock data months before the entry deadline.

What a tutor can do about it is specific. Take two past papers, one Foundation and one Higher, sit them under timed conditions, and mark both against the published mark scheme rather than a percentage. The pattern that emerges is usually unambiguous: either the student is scoring comfortably at the top of Foundation, in which case the conversation with the head of maths is worth having, or they are scoring in the twenties on Higher with the easier questions already half-lost, in which case the content gap is in Year 9 material and that is what the next eight weeks should address.

Timing matters because entries are made months before the exams. Once the series entry is submitted, a tier change is a school and board process with its own deadline, not a decision a family can make in April. The time to run the comparison is autumn of Year 11 at the latest, and ideally the summer before it.
bullets: Foundation tier tops out at grade 5; Higher tier runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3
Set placement in Year 9 often predicts the tier entered in Year 11
Two timed past papers, marked against the scheme, settle the question in a week

sections.heading: How each Edexcel component is weighted, and where the marks sit
paragraphs: Revision planning goes wrong when a student spreads effort evenly across papers that are not evenly weighted. In Mathematics A the two papers are worth the same, so that problem does not arise. In the separate sciences it very much does: Paper 1 is the long paper, carrying substantially more marks than Paper 2, and a student who has practised only the shorter paper has been rehearsing the smaller half of their grade.

The weightings are published in each specification and should be read from there rather than from a revision site. What a tutor adds is the translation into hours. If a component carries roughly six marks in ten and the student is losing most of their marks inside it, that is where the next ten sessions go. If the loss is spread evenly, the problem is usually not topic knowledge but exam technique, and the fix is a different kind of session entirely.

There is a second layer underneath the weightings, which is the distribution of marks by question type. Across most Pearson science and humanities papers, a substantial block of marks sits in extended-response questions of four to six marks. Those questions are marked on the quality and sequence of the points made, not on the quantity of writing, and they are where the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 8 is usually located. They are also the most coachable thing on the paper.

The practical exercise is to take one marked past paper and total the marks lost by question type rather than by topic. Students who have never done this are routinely surprised. A physics student convinced they are weak at electricity often discovers that electricity cost them four marks and six-mark explanation questions across every topic cost them fourteen.

sections.heading: Where Edexcel marks actually go missing between Year 10 and the final paper
paragraphs: Marks are rarely lost where students think. The three repeat offenders across Pearson papers are command-term misreading, unshown working, and running out of time on the final questions. Each has a distinct remedy and none of them is more content.

Command terms are the vocabulary the mark scheme uses to decide what counts. State wants a fact with no justification. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a mechanism. Evaluate wants a judgement with a condition attached. A student who explains when asked to describe wastes time and gains nothing; a student who describes when asked to explain loses the mark entirely. Twenty minutes spent building a command-term list from the student's own marked scripts recovers marks across every subject at once.

Unshown working is a mathematics and science problem specifically. Pearson mark schemes award method marks. A correct final answer with no working scores full marks, but a wrong final answer with no working scores nothing, where the same wrong answer with two lines of method might score two of three. Students who work in their heads are gambling, and the gamble has a negative expected value over a two-hour paper.

Timing is the one families underestimate most. The last three questions on a paper carry some of the highest marks and are reached by fewer students than any other part of the paper. The remedy is boring and effective: sit the paper with a clock, note the time at each page turn, and practise abandoning a stuck question after ninety seconds. That single habit is worth more than another month of content revision for a student already sitting at grade 6.

sections.heading: Two Pearson series a year, counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November each year. That second series is the single most useful fact on this page for Dubai families, because it is almost invisible on competitor pages and it changes what is possible. A student who falls short in one subject in June does not have to wait a year. A student who arrives in Dubai mid-course can sometimes enter a subject early rather than waiting for the main series.

The dates that are confirmed are worth stating precisely. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, which is why any plan should be built against the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than against a restated date that can be revised.

Entry deadlines are the part families miss. The entry is made by the centre, months before the exam, and once it is in, changing a subject, a tier or a series becomes a board process with its own cut-off and sometimes a late fee. Your child's exams officer holds those dates. Asking for them in writing at the start of Year 11, and putting them in the family calendar alongside the exam window, removes the most common avoidable problem in this whole process.

Counting backwards from the exam window is how a revision plan stops being aspirational. Work out the number of weeks between today and the first paper, subtract the school holidays and the week of mocks, and divide the remaining specification by what is left. If the arithmetic does not work, the plan needs fewer topics covered properly rather than all of them covered badly, and that prioritisation is a decision a specification-literate tutor can make with you in one session.

sections.heading: What an Edexcel IGCSE tutor costs in Dubai, in dirhams
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the others quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The bands below are market rates drawn from what providers publish about themselves, with the source named. They are not IB Gram's price list, and no figure here should be read as a quote.

At the budget end, online tutoring from university students and early-career tutors is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour; EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits broadly in the AED 150 to 300 range, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home visit, with travel priced in, runs higher: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts it at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise up to AED 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. At the top, named or examiner-experienced tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

What actually moves the number for an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Dubai is narrowness. A tutor who can teach any Year 10 maths is widely available and priced accordingly. A tutor who knows the 4MA1 Higher tier mark scheme, has marked against it, and can tell you which method marks your child is forfeiting is a smaller pool. The honest framing is that you pay for specification depth, not for a job title, and that any rate quoted without naming what it includes — session length, marking between sessions, written reporting, cancellation terms — is not yet a price.

sections.heading: Why the search says tutor in Dubai and the lesson happens over video
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai type tutor in Dubai because that is how the question forms. The thing being bought, though, is not proximity. It is a person who knows what a 4CH1 mark scheme rewards on a six-mark organic chemistry question. Those two requirements point in different directions, and geography loses.

Consider the arithmetic from a family's side. A visiting tutor serving Jumeirah can realistically reach perhaps a dozen households a week, and the subjects they can teach are whatever they happen to know. The tutor your child needs may teach 4PH1 Paper 2P practical questions for a living and live in another city entirely. Live video removes the drive and keeps the specialist, which is why IB Gram delivers one-to-one online to UAE families and does not sell home visits here — that remains an India-only service.

There is a quieter advantage, which is what the format does to evidence. A screen-shared past paper can be annotated by both people at once, saved, and compared against last month's script. The marked work accumulates in one place instead of in a folder somewhere. For a subject where the whole argument is about which marks were lost and why, that record is the thing that makes progress visible rather than felt.

The format has real costs and it is dishonest to pretend otherwise. A student who needs someone physically present to stay on task will drift on video, and that is a question worth answering in the trial lesson rather than in week six. Practical science is harder to supervise remotely, which matters more for A Level than for International GCSE, where assessment is by written paper. A good tutor tells you which of these applies to your child before taking the booking.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and what may legitimately be used
paragraphs: Past papers are the most useful revision material in existence for a written-paper qualification, and they are also copyright material belonging to Pearson. The correct position is simple: reference them, link to the official source, and work from material the school or the board has legitimately made available. IB Gram does not host, reproduce or supply Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, and a tutor who offers to send you a folder of them has told you something about how they operate.

What a tutor can do is teach a student to use the material properly. Most students use past papers as a test and stop there. The value is in the second half of the exercise: marking the script against the published mark scheme line by line, writing down what the scheme wanted that the student did not give, and tallying those gaps by question type across three papers. That tally is a revision plan, and it is produced by the student rather than handed to them.

Schools in Dubai usually hold legitimate access to current series material through their Pearson centre account, and exams officers are generally willing to release past papers and examiner reports to students who ask. Examiner reports are the underused resource in this whole category. They say, in the board's own words, what candidates did badly in the last series, which is the closest thing to a forecast anyone outside the board has.

One caution about unreleased material. Anything circulating informally that claims to be a forthcoming paper is either fake or a malpractice exposure, and in either case your child should be nowhere near it. The consequences of being found with it sit on the student, not the person who sent it.

sections.heading: Coursework, academic honesty and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: Some Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects offer a coursework route, English Language A and English Literature among them where the centre chooses it. Where coursework exists, the work must be the student's own, produced under the centre's supervision arrangements and authenticated by the school. That is not a formality. A piece of writing that is substantially someone else's is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

The boundary a tutor holds is specific and worth stating in plain terms. A tutor may teach the skills a task requires, discuss a student's plan, ask questions about an argument, point at a paragraph that does not do what the student thinks it does, and explain what the assessment criteria reward. A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submitted piece, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. One competitor in this market openly sells completed coursework; that is the thing to walk away from, not a service to compare prices against.

In practice the honest version is more useful anyway. A student who has had their own argument interrogated for an hour writes a better second draft than a student handed a polished one, and they can defend it in a viva or an authentication conversation. A student handed a polished draft learns nothing and carries the risk.

Ask a prospective tutor directly what they do and do not do with coursework. The answer tells you more about them than any credential on a profile, and it takes thirty seconds. A tutor who hesitates, or who answers in terms of what the school will not notice, has answered the question.

sections.heading: Permits, equivalency and the mandatory subjects running alongside
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Equivalency is the second thing Dubai families need and rarely get told. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority, because IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency and no tutoring is required for it.

Running alongside all of this are the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson is at least 25 minutes.

For a Year 11 student that adds up to a real second timetable, and it is the load most revision plans forget to account for. Any honest weekly plan for an Edexcel IGCSE candidate in Dubai starts by subtracting the hours those subjects already take, then allocates what is left.

process.title: Send the entry statement, not a subject list
process.description: The first message that actually helps contains the Pearson codes and tiers your child is entered for, the school, the year group, and the most recent assessment result in the subject concerned. That is enough to match a tutor who works in the right specification rather than one who works in the right subject.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the marking done live
process.description: The trial is one lesson at no charge, with no card required to book it and no obligation afterwards. It should include a short piece of the student's own recent work being marked against the published scheme, because that is the part you are judging. If the tutor talks for an hour without touching a script, you have learned nothing useful.

process.title: Agree scope and the terms in writing
process.description: Before any paid block starts, get four things in writing: session length, what happens between sessions, the cancellation window, and whether the quoted rate includes VAT. Ask what the tutor will and will not do with coursework. A tutor who answers all five clearly is usually the one who also keeps records.

process.title: Run the first four weeks against evidence
process.description: Each week the student completes one timed component and the session opens on the marked script. By week four there should be a visible list of question types where marks have stopped leaking, and a shorter list of the ones still open. That list is the thing to look at, rather than a general sense that lessons are going well.

process.title: Review before the entry deadline, not after mocks
process.description: The decisions with deadlines — tier, series, subject entries, private-candidate arrangements — sit with the school and close months before the papers. Put a review in the calendar early in Year 11, bring the mock data and the past-paper tallies, and have the conversation with the head of department while changing something is still possible.

whyPoints.title: The specification is the starting point
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to the Pearson code on the entry statement, not to a subject label. For a tiered subject that means knowing what Foundation caps at and what Higher demands; for the sciences it means knowing which component carries the larger share of the marks and planning hours accordingly.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts, not impressions
whyPoints.description: Every session opens on something the student wrote and a mark scheme to judge it against. Progress is reported as question types where marks stopped being lost, which is checkable, rather than as effort or engagement, which is not.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated here so no family discovers it after paying.
