whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider who published it, with the tier it belongs to. None of it is a quote from IB Gram. A rate without a source, a date and a list of what it includes is not information you can use.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is drawn before you ask
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not supply sentences for submitted coursework or hand over model answers to be adapted. The risk in that market sits on the candidate, which is reason enough to be explicit about it.

faqs.question: Which Pearson Edexcel International GCSE code is my child actually entered for?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the exam-entry statement your child's school issues for the series. Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1 and English Literature 4ET1. The code matters because Pearson publishes more than one specification in several subjects, and because the correct specification, sample assessment material and past papers are all indexed by it on qualifications.pearson.com. If you cannot find the statement, the school's exams officer can confirm each subject code and tier in a single email, and that email is worth having before you book any tutoring.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A tiered, and which tier should my child sit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mathematics A is sat at Foundation tier, which stops at grade 5, or Higher tier, which runs from 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. The decision is usually implied by set placement well before anyone discusses it. The reliable way to settle it is to sit one Foundation and one Higher past paper under timed conditions and mark both against the published scheme. A student scoring at the top of Foundation is being capped; a student in the twenties on Higher with easy marks already lost needs Year 9 content repaired first. Raise it with the head of maths before the entry deadline closes.

faqs.question: How is a 4PH1 Physics entry split between Paper 1P and Paper 2P?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is assessed by two written papers. Paper 1P is the longer of the two at two hours and carries the larger share of the marks; Paper 2P runs an hour and a quarter and carries the smaller share. The qualification is single-tier, so grade 9 is reachable regardless of set. The practical consequence for revision is that a student who has rehearsed only the shorter paper has been practising the smaller half of their grade. Check the exact weightings in the current specification, because Pearson publishes them there and they are what the plan should be built on.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if my child's school entered Cambridge in one subject and Pearson in another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai that combination is common, because the board is chosen department by department rather than school-wide. What matters is that the tutor works in the right conventions for each paper. Cambridge and Pearson ask similar content in several subjects but reward different things in their mark schemes, particularly in English and the sciences. A tutor who teaches Cambridge habits on a Pearson paper will produce answers the scheme does not credit. Give the tutor the entry statement for every subject, and ask them to confirm which specification they are teaching to before the first paid session.

faqs.question: Does Pearson run an International GCSE series in November as well as the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. This is one of the least-known facts in the Dubai tutoring market and it changes planning considerably. A student who falls short in one subject in the summer can re-enter in November rather than waiting a full year, and a student arriving mid-course can sometimes sit a subject early. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Entry for either series is made by the school months in advance, so the exams officer holds the deadline that actually governs your options.

faqs.question: Which Pearson results milestones are already published and worth diarising?
faqs.answer: For the June 2026 series, results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. For the November 2025 series, results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes each series timetable and results schedule on qualifications.pearson.com, including provisional timetables ahead of time for series such as International GCSE November 2027. Because provisional dates can be revised, check the live page rather than relying on a restated date. Agree in advance with your child who collects the results and when, particularly if the family travels in August.

faqs.question: What does a specialist Edexcel IGCSE tutor charge per hour in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai span a wide range. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya AED 33-52. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors at AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are the providers' own figures, not IB Gram's prices. Always ask what the rate includes before comparing two of them.

faqs.question: Are lessons delivered online, or does a tutor come to a Dubai address?
faqs.answer: Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not operate home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The reason is the size of the specialist pool. A tutor who genuinely knows 4CH1 organic chemistry mark schemes may not live within driving distance of your community, and the video format keeps the specialist rather than the postcode. Screen-shared marking also leaves a saved record of every annotated script, which is the evidence a family needs when judging whether the sessions are working.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Edexcel IGCSE tutoring does one subject usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the problem is content or technique, and a diagnostic answers that in one session. A technique problem — command terms misread, working not shown, final questions never reached — often moves substantially in six to eight weekly sessions, because the fix transfers across every topic at once. A genuine content gap reaching back into Year 9 takes longer, frequently a term, because the missing material has to be rebuilt before paper practice means anything. No honest tutor gives a number before seeing a marked script, and any promise of a specific grade in a specific time should be treated with real scepticism.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supply Pearson past papers and mark schemes for my child to work from?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not host, reproduce or supply Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because they are the board's copyright material. The legitimate route is your child's school, which holds access through its Pearson centre account, and the official pages on qualifications.pearson.com. Ask the exams officer for past papers and, more usefully, for examiner reports: those state in the board's own words what candidates did badly in the last series. A tutor's job is teaching a student to mark their own script against the scheme, which is where the value in past papers actually sits.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my child's Edexcel English coursework, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: Where a centre offers the coursework route, the submitted piece must be the student's own work and the school authenticates it. A tutor may teach the skills the task needs, discuss a plan, question an argument, point out a paragraph that does not do its job, and explain what the assessment criteria reward. A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submission, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, or provide a model answer to be adapted. One provider in this market sells finished coursework outright; the consequences of using it fall on the candidate, not the seller.

faqs.question: Does my child need five Edexcel IGCSE subjects for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competitor page states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own circumstances on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, and no tutoring is required to obtain it.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit before teaching my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around an Edexcel IGCSE timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the guidance advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. For a Year 11 student that is a second timetable running alongside the IGCSE course, and any realistic weekly revision plan has to subtract those hours before allocating anything else.

faqs.question: Can Edexcel IGCSE sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families should plan for it rather than improvise. School days shorten during Ramadan and the usable study window shifts late, which matters most in the years when the month falls close to the summer series. The workable pattern is usually a shorter session after Iftar, two or three times a week, with the heaviest cognitive work moved earlier in the term rather than attempted during the month. Because lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, changing the slot is a scheduling decision rather than a logistical one, and the same tutor keeps the thread.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Find the code, then find the tutor
dubai/edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingBody: An Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Dubai earns their rate by knowing what a specific Pearson mark scheme rewards and where your child is currently forfeiting marks against it. Start by sending the exam-entry statement, the school, the year group and the latest assessment result. The trial lesson is free, requires no card and carries no obligation, and it should include a piece of your child's own work marked live against the published scheme. If that hour does not tell you something you did not already know, you have lost nothing but the hour.

dubai/emaar-beachfront.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and both IGCSE boards, and are matched with continuity in mind. For a household that moves, keeping one tutor across a whole course matters more than any single session.

intro.heading: A beachfront address, and a school year that is not continuous
paragraphs: Emaar Beachfront is a gated cluster of towers on a peninsula inside Dubai Harbour, between Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah, with its own beach and no schools, shops of any scale or school-bus depot on it. The housing is entirely apartments, a high proportion of them owned rather than long-leased, and a meaningful share of those owners do not live here all year.

That is the defining feature for tutoring. A conventional neighbourhood page assumes a family in one home, one school and one routine from September to June. Here the common patterns are different: a household that spends the summer and part of the winter elsewhere, a family newly relocated and still deciding whether Dubai is permanent, an owner who rents the apartment out for part of the year, and a long-stay family whose children are settled and whose relatives visit constantly.

An academic course is indifferent to all of it. An IB Diploma runs two continuous years with internal deadlines set by the school in Dubai time. An IGCSE course has entries made months in advance by the school, examinations sat in a fixed window and papers issued against a timetable zone. Nothing in either arrangement adjusts because a family is in Europe for five weeks, and the usual casualty is coursework rather than examination content, because coursework has deadlines a student can quietly miss.

The second casualty is continuity of teaching. Families who move find a tutor, lose them on departure, find another on arrival, and repeat. Each handover costs two or three sessions of re-diagnosis, the new tutor teaches a different method for the same topic, and the student ends up with three partial approaches to one problem. Over two years of a Diploma that is a significant and entirely avoidable loss.

There is a further complication that comes with the address rather than the travel. The peninsula has no school, no bus depot and very little of the ordinary infrastructure of a residential district, so every school day involves leaving it and the choice of school is made on direction rather than proximity. Combine that with a year broken into segments and the result is a household for whom nothing can be left to routine. Everything, from the slot to the subject to the term plan, has to be decided deliberately, which is why the families here who get good value from tutoring are the ones who treat it as a planned arrangement rather than a weekly habit.

So this page is about continuity. It covers who actually lives here, what a course does while a household is away, how to schedule one tutor across time zones, what a mid-course arrival needs in its first weeks, how examination entry works when a family is not in the country, when the November series is a genuine option, and what it costs to keep one tutor rather than three. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, which is what makes any of it possible. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

The taught content can be caught up. The internally assessed components cannot, because each has a school deadline and a supervisor who needs to see the work develop.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm every IB deadline, upload window and session with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. This page publishes no IB dates, because none could be verified from the IB directly for this project. For a travelling household the school's internal deadlines are the dates that matter, and they are set in Dubai time.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations with entries made by the school months ahead. Cambridge uses four-digit codes with a Core and Extended split; Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 with modular entry on some subjects. Content missed during an absence is recoverable; a missed entry deadline or a wrong tier is not.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a family who may sit papers in a different country, that detail is not trivia.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with a total converted to a 1 to 7 grade. Because assessment is continuous rather than terminal, an absence has a direct and immediate effect: missed tasks are missed criterion marks, and they are harder to make up than missed content.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP is the programme that travels worst, which is counter-intuitive given how international it is. A student away for five weeks misses assessed tasks rather than lessons, and the school decides how or whether those are replaced, so the conversation to have before leaving is with the coordinator rather than with a tutor.

dubai/emaar-beachfront.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested from this community, described by how well each one tolerates an interrupted term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Sequential and unforgiving of gaps, because each topic assumes the algebraic fluency of the last. This is the subject where a five-week absence does most damage, and the one most worth maintaining with a weekly session while a family is away.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling, more modular than Analysis and slightly more tolerant of an interrupted term. The exploration still needs a real dataset and a defensible question, which is a decision to make before travelling rather than after returning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content recoverable, practical work much less so. A student who misses the practical sessions underpinning their internal assessment has a scheduling problem the school must solve, and the sooner it is raised the more options exist.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Derivation-heavy at Diploma level and cumulative, so missed weeks compound. Uncertainty handling and graph analysis are examinable and can be taught from anywhere, which makes them good use of sessions during an absence.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most content-heavy and the most recoverable, because topics are relatively self-contained. The risk during an absence is the investigation rather than the syllabus, since data collection needs laboratory access and a supervisor.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline and command-term precision decide marks, both of which can be built entirely online. The commentaries need published articles, which a travelling student can gather anywhere, making this a good subject to work on while away.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one is unseen analysis and can be practised from any location. The individual oral needs a global issue and two prepared extracts, planned months ahead, which is exactly the kind of thing an interrupted year postpones until it becomes urgent.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation requires sources and careful referencing, both portable. What is not portable is the classroom discussion, so a student away for several weeks loses the argument practice rather than the facts.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The Core and Extended decision caps the grade and is taken by the school, often while a family is away over a break. Worth confirming in writing before any absence rather than discovering on return.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Taught in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. It is also the subject most damaged by absence, because language fluency decays faster than content knowledge.

sections.heading: Who actually lives at Emaar Beachfront
paragraphs: Four household patterns produce almost all the enquiries from this peninsula, and they are not the patterns most tutoring is designed for. The first is the part-year resident: a family with a long-term base elsewhere who spend a substantial but discontinuous portion of the year in Dubai. Their children may be enrolled in a Dubai school and absent for weeks at a time, or enrolled elsewhere and present here between terms.

The second is the recent relocation. A family arrived within the last year, children placed in whichever school had availability rather than the one they would have chosen, still deciding whether Dubai is a three-year posting or a permanent move. Their academic problem is almost always a curriculum mismatch rather than ability, and it is acute in the first two terms and then disappears.

The third is the owner who rents: an apartment held as an investment and occupied for part of the year, which produces short, intense periods of residence and a demand for concentrated work rather than weekly maintenance. The fourth is the settled long-stay family, whose children have been in one Dubai school for years and whose needs are entirely conventional, except that the household travels more than most.

Each of these needs something different, and the common failure is to sell all four an identical weekly retainer. A part-year resident needs continuity across absence. A recent arrival needs a gap audit before any teaching. An intermittent occupant needs blocks. A settled family needs the ordinary arrangement. Establishing which one you are is the first five minutes of any sensible conversation.

sections.heading: What a course does while the household is away
paragraphs: The instinctive worry about an absence is missed lessons, and that is the least serious part. Taught content can be caught up, often faster than a parent expects, because a tutor working one-to-one covers in an hour what a classroom covers in three. What cannot be caught up is anything with a fixed date attached, and those are the items that quietly do the damage.

For a Diploma student, the fixed items are internal assessment deadlines set by the school, supervisor meetings for the Extended Essay, and practical sessions that produce the data an investigation needs. For an MYP student they are assessed tasks, each carrying criterion marks that cannot be recovered by learning the content later. For an IGCSE student they are entry decisions, including the tier, which are made by the school on a calendar that takes no account of family travel.

The practical sequence before any planned absence is short. Ask the coordinator or form tutor for the list of assessed items and deadlines falling in the period away. Ask what the school's policy is on each: replaced, deferred, or counted as missed. Ask whether any practical or laboratory work is involved, because that has the fewest alternatives. Then plan the tutoring around whatever cannot move rather than around the subjects that feel most pressing.

Doing this three weeks before departure changes the outcome. Doing it on return changes nothing, because by then the decisions have been made by default. This is the single most useful thing a travelling household can do, and it costs one email.

sections.heading: Keeping one tutor across several time zones
paragraphs: Online delivery makes continuity possible and does not make it automatic. The practical obstacle is arithmetic: a tutor and a student in different places have a narrower overlap of civilised hours than either expects, and a slot that works in Dubai may be impossible from another continent. Working that out before departure rather than after is the difference between a reduced schedule and a four-week gap.

Dubai runs on a single offset all year with no seasonal clock change, which simplifies one half of the problem and complicates the other: countries that do change clocks will shift relative to Dubai twice a year, so a slot agreed in October may be an hour out by April. Families who travel between the same two places repeatedly should expect to re-agree the time rather than assume it holds.

The useful approach is to fix the slot in the student's local time while away and accept that the tutor adjusts, which is usually possible because our tutors are not all in one country. Where it is not possible, a reduced schedule in a workable window beats an ambitious one in an impossible window. One good session a week while away, on the subject that decays fastest, is worth more than three sessions scheduled at a time nobody can keep.

The deadlines, though, stay in Dubai time, and that catches people out. A coursework upload due at the end of a Dubai working day is earlier than it looks from the Americas and later than it looks from East Asia. We track the school's dates in Dubai time throughout and state them that way in session notes, because a deadline missed by a time-zone misreading is the most avoidable loss available.

sections.heading: Joining a Dubai school partway through a course
paragraphs: A student arriving in February of the first Diploma year, or in January of Year 11, is in a specific and under-discussed situation. They are not behind in the ordinary sense; they have covered a different selection of content in a different order, to different assessment conventions, and the new school's scheme of work assumes the selection it taught. The danger is that this looks exactly like weakness on an early assessment and gets treated as such.

The first task is therefore an audit rather than teaching. Take the new school's scheme of work for each subject, compare it against what the student actually covered, and produce a list of genuine gaps with an estimate of how long each takes to close. Most lists are shorter than the family fears. Two or three real gaps per subject is typical, and several apparent gaps turn out to be the same content under a different name.

The second task is coursework status, and it is urgent rather than important. A student joining in the second term of a Diploma year may have internal assessments already underway at their previous school, which may or may not transfer, and deadlines at the new school that assume work started months ago. That conversation belongs with the coordinator in the first week, because the number of available options falls weekly.

The third is assessment convention, which nobody warns about. A student from an American high school writing for Diploma command terms, or one from an Indian board meeting criterion-based marking, is writing good answers to the wrong brief. That gap closes quickly with deliberate work and slowly without it, and it accounts for a large part of the early-term shock that families mistake for an academic problem.

sections.heading: Examination entry when the family is not in the country
paragraphs: Entries are made by the school, not the candidate, and that is the fact a travelling family needs to internalise. A student enrolled in a Dubai school is entered by that school, on its calendar, for the series it uses, at the tier its department chooses. If the family intends to be elsewhere during the examination window, the conversation to have is with the school's examinations officer and it needs to happen months ahead.

There are complications worth knowing. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong timetable. A family assuming the paper is at the same hour in two countries has misunderstood how the system works.

Where a school cannot offer or enter a subject, or a student is not enrolled at a school at all, the route is a private candidate entry through an approved examination centre. That brings its own requirements: centre availability, entry deadlines earlier than a school's internal ones, fees, and in practical terms a decision made two terms before the paper. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is what should be checked rather than a restated date on any third-party page.

For the IB, the position is simpler to state and harder to arrange: confirm every route, deadline and session with your school's Diploma coordinator. This page publishes no IB dates because none could be verified from the IB directly, and anyone quoting you an IB examination date from a tutoring website should be treated with caution.

sections.heading: When the November series is the right answer
paragraphs: Most families treat the summer series as the only series and the November one as a consolation prize. For a household with an interrupted year it is sometimes the better plan from the outset, and thinking about it early rather than after a disappointing August result changes what is possible.

Three situations make it genuinely useful. The first is a student carrying too many subjects for the time they have, where splitting the load across two series produces better grades in all of them than attempting everything at once. The second is a student who lost a term to a move or an absence, where six more months of preparation converts a borderline grade into a secure one. The third is a recovery after a result that does not reflect the student, where the alternative is a year's delay.

The costs are real and should be weighed. A November entry means revising over the summer rather than resting, carrying a subject into the next academic year alongside new work, and in some cases a fee for a private candidate entry. Universities and sixth forms also have their own views on when results must be in hand, which has to be checked against the specific institution rather than assumed.

Pearson Edexcel's turnaround gives a sense of the timing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. A November result therefore arrives in the middle of the following academic year, which is fine for some purposes and too late for others. That is the calculation to make with the school in the spring, not in September.

sections.heading: What continuity costs, and what changing tutors costs
paragraphs: The figures below are Dubai market rates published in October 2026, each attributed to whoever published them, and offered because three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all. They are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list. For this community the more useful number is not the hourly rate but the cost of discontinuity.

Each change of tutor costs two or three sessions before any teaching happens: establishing the syllabus code and level, reading marked work, identifying error patterns, learning the school's deadlines and conventions. At the specialist band that is somewhere between AED 400 and AED 1,350 of re-diagnosis, repeated on every handover. A family who changes tutor three times across a two-year Diploma has paid for nine sessions of work that the first tutor had already done.

The second cost is methodological. Two tutors will teach the same topic by different routes, both valid, and a student who receives both ends up with two partial approaches and confidence in neither. This shows up most clearly in mathematics, where notation and method conventions vary, and in essay subjects, where structural advice differs.

The argument for a retained tutor is therefore financial as much as pedagogical. Paying a specialist rate for a tutor who stays is usually cheaper across a course than paying a mid rate for three who do not. And because every lesson is delivered over live video, retaining one is a matter of scheduling rather than geography, which is the only reason it is possible for a household that moves.

sections.heading: What a handover note should contain, if one is ever needed
paragraphs: Even with a retained tutor, a travelling household eventually needs a document: for a new school, for a new coordinator, or for a tutor covering an absence. Most tutoring produces nothing of the kind, which is why families moving between countries arrive at each new school with nothing but a parent's recollection of what has been happening.

A useful note is short and factual. It states the syllabus code and level, the topics covered and the dates, the topics the school has taught that the student has not yet secured, the error patterns still open, the status of each assessed component with its school deadline, and the next three things planned. One page. A teacher reading it should be able to place the student in ten seconds.

What it should not contain is a grade prediction, an assessment of the student's ability, or anything evaluative about their previous school. Those are judgements for the new school to make, and a tutor offering them oversteps. The note is a record of work, not a reference.

We produce a written record after every session as a matter of course, and a consolidated note on request. For a household that may move once or twice during a course, that record is the only continuous account of the academic work that exists outside the schools themselves, and it is worth asking any provider whether they keep one. Many do not, which is a reasonable thing to know before you commit.

sections.heading: Getting started from Emaar Beachfront
paragraphs: Begin by saying which household pattern you are, because it changes everything that follows: part-year resident, recent arrival, intermittent occupant, or settled family that travels. Then send the school, the exact syllabus code and level, the most recent marked work, the school's internal coursework deadlines, and the dates of any absence you already know about.

The first session is diagnostic, and for a recent arrival it is an audit rather than a diagnosis: the new school's scheme of work compared against what the student has actually covered, subject by subject, producing a gap list with an estimate of the weeks each item needs. For a part-year resident it is a priority exercise, deciding which subjects decay fastest and therefore which get the reduced schedule while away.

Then we fix a retained tutor and a slot, with an agreed approach for absences: the time re-agreed rather than the sessions cancelled, the schedule reduced rather than suspended, and the school's deadlines tracked in Dubai time throughout. That combination is what keeps a two-year course intact across a household that moves.

Three limits, stated before payment. We do not promise grades. We do not place tutors in homes anywhere in the UAE, since every lesson is one-to-one online. We do not arrange, guarantee or administer examination entries, which belong to schools and approved centres, and we will not quote you an IB date we could not verify. Where a scarce specialism is involved, or where a time zone makes a weekly slot genuinely difficult, you will hear it before you commit.

process.title: Say which pattern you are
process.description: Part-year resident, recent arrival, intermittent occupant or settled family that travels. The four need different arrangements, and selling all of them an identical weekly retainer is the main reason tutoring fails for households like these.

process.title: List the fixed dates
process.description: Coursework deadlines, supervisor meetings, assessed tasks and practical sessions, with the dates of any planned absence. Content can be caught up; anything with a date attached cannot, and the plan is built around whatever will not move.

process.title: Audit or diagnose
process.description: For a recent arrival, a subject-by-subject comparison of covered content against the new scheme of work, producing a gap list with estimated closing times. For everyone else, a diagnostic hour from marked work to establish what the real problem is.

process.title: Retain one tutor and plan the absences
process.description: The same tutor across the course, with the slot re-agreed on departure and return rather than the arrangement cancelled. A reduced schedule while away, prioritising mathematics and languages, which decay fastest.

process.title: Keep a written record
process.description: A note after every session and a consolidated one-page handover on request: syllabus code, topics and dates, open error patterns, component status with school deadlines, and the next three things planned. Useful for a new school and for a covering tutor.

whyPoints.title: One tutor across the whole course
whyPoints.description: Continuity is the product for a household that moves. A retained tutor already knows the error patterns, the syllabus code and the school's deadlines, which is two or three sessions of value a replacement has to rebuild on every handover.

whyPoints.title: Absences planned, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Before travel, the fixed dates are listed and the subjects that decay fastest get a reduced schedule. Coursework deadlines, not missed lessons, are what absences usually cost, and that is a conversation to have three weeks before departure.

whyPoints.title: An audit before a bill, for new arrivals
whyPoints.description: A student from another system is not behind; they covered different content in a different order to different conventions. A subject-by-subject gap list is usually shorter than the family fears and is the honest basis for deciding what to buy.

whyPoints.title: Deadlines tracked in Dubai time
whyPoints.description: School deadlines are set in Dubai time and read differently from other continents. We state them that way in every session note, because a deadline missed through a time-zone misreading is the most avoidable loss in this community.

whyPoints.title: Limits said out loud
whyPoints.description: We do not arrange or guarantee examination entries, promise grades, publish unsupported statistics, or claim accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We will not quote an IB date that could not be verified from the IB itself.

faqs.question: We are away for several weeks each year. Can one tutor stay with our child throughout?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement worth insisting on. Because every lesson is delivered over live video, retaining a tutor across an absence is a scheduling question rather than a geographic one. The slot is re-agreed in the student's local time while away and reinstated on return, with a reduced schedule in between rather than a suspension. The alternative, finding a new tutor in each location, costs two or three sessions of re-diagnosis every time and leaves the student with several partial approaches to the same topics.

faqs.question: What does an absence actually cost academically?
faqs.answer: Far less in taught content than parents fear and far more in anything with a date attached. One-to-one teaching covers in an hour what a classroom covers in three, so content is recoverable. What is not recoverable is a coursework deadline, a supervisor meeting, an assessed MYP task carrying criterion marks, or a practical session that produces data for an investigation. Ask the school for the list of fixed items falling in the period away, three weeks before departure rather than on return.

faqs.question: Which subjects suffer most while a family is travelling?
faqs.answer: Sequential ones. Mathematics is the clearest case, because each topic assumes the fluency of the last, so five missed weeks compound rather than simply leaving a gap. Languages, including Arabic as an additional language, decay faster than content knowledge does. Content-heavy but modular subjects such as biology tolerate an absence relatively well. That hierarchy is why a reduced schedule while away should prioritise maths and language rather than spreading thinly across everything.

faqs.question: How do we schedule lessons from another time zone?
faqs.answer: Fix the slot in the student's local time while away and let the tutor adjust, which is usually possible because our tutors are not all in one country. Dubai does not change its clocks, so a family travelling to a country that does will drift by an hour twice a year and should re-agree the time rather than assume it holds. Where the overlap is genuinely poor, one good weekly session beats three scheduled at hours nobody can keep.

faqs.question: Are school deadlines set in local time or Dubai time?
faqs.answer: Dubai time, which is the detail that catches travelling families out. A coursework upload due at the end of a Dubai working day is earlier than it looks from the Americas and later than it looks from East Asia, and a student working to their own clock can miss it by hours while believing they have a day left. We state every school deadline in Dubai time in session notes for exactly this reason, and it is worth confirming the exact hour with the coordinator rather than the date alone.

faqs.question: My son joined a Dubai school in February. Is he behind?
faqs.answer: Probably not in the way it looks. A mid-course arrival has covered a different selection of content in a different order, to different assessment conventions, and the new school's scheme of work assumes what it taught. That produces poor early assessments that resemble weakness and are not. The first step is an audit rather than teaching: compare the new scheme of work against what he actually covered, subject by subject. Most gap lists are shorter than families fear, typically two or three real gaps per subject.

faqs.question: What should a student arriving from an American school expect in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Content breadth usually transfers well, and presentation skills often transfer better than those of students from more examination-focused systems. What does not transfer is command-term precision and the depth demanded at Higher Level, and those take roughly six to ten weeks of deliberate written work to close. The student is writing good answers to a different brief rather than poor answers to this one, and naming it that way early prevents a capable student concluding they cannot do the programme.

faqs.question: Who makes the examination entry if we might be abroad?
faqs.answer: The school, not the family, for any student enrolled in a Dubai school. Entries are made on the school's calendar for the series it uses, at the tier the department chooses. If you expect to be elsewhere during the examination window, speak to the examinations officer months ahead, because the available options narrow sharply as the series approaches. Where a school does not offer a subject at all, the route is a private candidate entry at an approved centre, arranged by the family.

faqs.question: Does it matter which country my daughter sits a Cambridge paper in?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong timetable. A family assuming a paper sits at the same hour in two countries has misread the system. Confirm the zone and the timetable with the centre that holds the entry, in writing.

faqs.question: Is entering for the November series a sensible plan rather than a fallback?
faqs.answer: For an interrupted year, sometimes yes, and deciding in spring beats reacting in August. It helps a student carrying more subjects than their time allows, one who lost a term to a move, or one recovering a result that does not reflect them. The costs are revising over the summer, carrying a subject into the next academic year, and in some cases a private candidate fee. Check how the specific university or sixth form treats a result arriving mid-year before committing.

faqs.question: When do November results actually arrive?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives a realistic sense of the turnaround. By comparison, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. A November result therefore lands in the middle of the following academic year, which suits some purposes and is too late for others. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date anywhere else.

faqs.question: How much does changing tutors actually cost us?
faqs.answer: Two or three sessions before any teaching happens, every time. The new tutor has to establish the syllabus code and level, read marked work, identify error patterns and learn the school's deadlines and conventions. At the specialist band that is roughly AED 400 to AED 1,350 of re-diagnosis per handover, based on the published market rates on this page. There is also a methodological cost: two tutors teach the same topic by different valid routes, and a student who receives both often ends up confident in neither.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to the apartment here?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs home visits only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For this community that is the point rather than a limitation: an arrangement that depends on someone driving onto the peninsula cannot follow a household that spends part of the year elsewhere. Online delivery is the only way to retain the same tutor across a two-year course when the address changes, and it also removes the travel time that market figures show sits inside every in-home rate.

faqs.question: What should we ask a provider to give us in writing?
faqs.answer: A note after each session and a consolidated one-page handover on request, containing the syllabus code and level, topics covered with dates, topics the school has taught that are not yet secure, open error patterns, the status of each assessed component with its school deadline, and the next three planned items. It should not contain a grade prediction or an assessment of ability. Many providers keep no record at all, which is worth discovering before you commit rather than when you move.

faqs.question: What will IB Gram not take responsibility for?
faqs.answer: Examination entries, which are made by schools and approved centres and are not ours to arrange or guarantee. Grades, which nobody can honestly promise. IB dates we could not verify from the IB itself, which is why none appear on this page. We also place no tutors in UAE homes, write or complete no part of any assessed component, and hold no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

dubai/emaar-beachfront.closingHeading: Keep the course continuous even when the household is not
dubai/emaar-beachfront.closingBody: If your family is in Dubai for part of the year, arrived recently, or expects to move again, the most valuable thing you can arrange is continuity: one tutor who stays with the course, a plan for the weeks away, and a written record that travels with the student. Send the school, the syllabus codes, the coursework deadlines and the dates you already know you will be absent. One session will tell you which subjects need protecting while you are away, which gaps are real rather than apparent, and what to raise with the coordinator before you leave rather than after you return.

intro.heading: A community built beside an airport, and a question about a number
paragraphs: Emaar South sits inside the Dubai South development, beside Al Maktoum International Airport and the Expo City site, built around a golf course with a mix of townhouses, villas and apartments. The household profile follows the geography. A large share of residents work in aviation, logistics, freight and airport operations, which means rosters rather than office hours, and a working week that does not reliably clear at six in the evening.

The community is also young enough that most of its secondary-age children travel out of it, mainly towards the Dubai Investments Park cluster or north towards Al Furjan and Jumeirah Village. A child in Year 11 or DP2 therefore spends a real part of their day on a bus, and the family spends a real part of theirs working out what the marks coming home actually mean.

There is a second reason numbers dominate the conversation here rather than subjects. Dubai South is a new part of the city, and the schools serving it have small upper year groups, which means fewer teachers to explain the assessment system informally at a parents' evening and fewer older parents in the community who have already been through it. In an established district a family learns from the one two doors down whose daughter sat the same papers last June. Here that neighbour frequently does not exist, so the mechanics have to be read rather than absorbed. A page that sets them out plainly is worth more to this community than another list of subjects.

That is the gap this page addresses, because it is the one that generates most enquiries here. Parents receive a number and cannot act on it. A 4 in Higher Level Chemistry, a predicted 32 points, a Core entry in mathematics, a mock graded 6 when the school says the prediction will be 5. Each of those is a different situation with a different set of available actions, and some of them have deadlines that close months before the examinations.

Schools explain the taught course well and the assessment system briefly. The result is that families make consequential decisions, about Core against Extended, about which mathematics route to take, about whether to accept a prediction or challenge it, without knowing how the marks work. Those decisions are frequently irreversible by the time the consequence appears, which is why this page is organised around mechanics rather than around subjects.

What follows covers what each mark converts to, how predicted grades are produced and what they bind, why grade boundaries move between sessions, which routes exist after results day and when each closes, what UAE universities expect from the two Diploma mathematics courses, and the Core and Extended ceiling that is set at option time. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

dubai/emaar-south.programmesIntro: Three systems produce the numbers this page is about. Each converts performance into a grade differently, and each has a point at which a decision becomes irreversible.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes and many are tiered: a Core entry is graded C to G, an Extended entry A* to E. Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1, with tiering on some subjects and modular entry on others. The decisive moment is the entry, not the examination, because the tier fixes the grade ceiling before a paper is opened.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving this part of Dubai use both boards, and entries are submitted by the school months ahead. Cambridge publishes a final entry deadline of 27 November 2026 for the March 2027 series, with examinations from 3 February to 4 March 2027, so a tier decision taken in November decides a result awarded the following May.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1 to 7, three at Higher Level, plus core points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. The total runs to a maximum of 45. Each subject grade is built from external papers and an internal assessment weighted by the subject guide, so a strong investigation can carry a weak paper and a missing investigation cannot be recovered by revision.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the award requirements, failing conditions and every session and results date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. This page publishes no IB dates or points thresholds, because they could not be verified from the IB directly for this project.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, totalling thirty-two and converted to a 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. This is where students first meet the idea that a grade is assembled from parts rather than averaged from tests, and where a parent can first ask the genuinely useful question: which criterion sits closest to a boundary.
programmes.countryNote: Few families here have an MYP school inside the community, so this stage usually coincides with a long daily journey. The practical effect is that MYP students in Emaar South have less unsupervised homework time than their classmates who live near the school, which shows up in the criteria that reward process.

dubai/emaar-south.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested here, described by where the marks are won and lost rather than by syllabus content.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision dominates. A Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C at Cambridge, so a borderline student placed in Core for safety has had their ceiling lowered. Marks within the paper go on unshown method and on misreading what a question demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. Reasoning marks dominate, so an unjustified answer scores a fraction of what is available, and Higher Level adds a long problem-solving paper that rewards persistence. This is the course most engineering and mathematics degrees expect.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology. A strong course in its own right, and the one that occasionally closes a door: some engineering and mathematics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, so the route should be checked against target courses in DP1 rather than DP2.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, kinetics and organic mechanisms carry Higher Level difficulty, and the internal assessment weight means a weak investigation caps the achievable grade. Students lose marks on mole calculations presented without units or working.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The move from recall to derivation catches strong IGCSE students in the first Diploma term. Uncertainty handling and graph analysis are examinable and rarely practised, and at IGCSE the loss concentrates in circuit reasoning under changed conditions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content misleads students into reading rather than answering. Examiners award against command terms, so a description offered where an explanation was demanded earns nothing, and statistical treatment of investigation data is where Higher Level marks go missing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks follow application rather than recall: a framework named but not applied to the stimulus loses most of the analysis credit. The internal assessment depends on an organisation willing to supply real figures, which is a decision to take early.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides grades, and an unlabelled axis costs marks the written analysis cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative questions, and the commentaries need published articles chosen to support the required analysis.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading comprehension under time pressure. Students lose marks for answering the question they expected and for writing in the wrong register for the stated audience, both of which are fixable in weeks rather than terms.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Taught in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, in classes organised separately for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Children who arrive in Dubai after the early primary years need script and vocabulary work the school timetable cannot pace individually.

sections.heading: What each mark actually converts to
paragraphs: Three grading systems operate across the schools this community uses, and they are not comparable with each other. A Diploma subject grade of 1 to 7 is not a percentage, an IGCSE grade is not an average of coursework and papers, and an MYP grade is assembled from four criterion marks rather than from test scores. Most of the confusion parents arrive with comes from trying to translate one into another, usually into a percentage that does not exist.

Take the Diploma first. Each subject grade is built from external components and an internal assessment, weighted by that subject's guide, and the six subject grades combine with core points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay into a total out of 45. The important structural fact is that the internal assessment weight is fixed: if it is a fifth of the subject, a student who submits a weak investigation has capped their achievable grade before the papers begin, and no amount of revision changes that arithmetic.

At Cambridge IGCSE the decisive mechanism is tiering. A Core entry is graded C to G and an Extended entry A* to E, which means a Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform. Pearson Edexcel tiers some subjects and offers modular entry on others. In both cases the entry is made by the school well before the examination, and in both cases it is the single most consequential decision in the course. Confirm with the school in writing which tier and which code your child is entered for, and do it before the entry deadline rather than after results day.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, who produces them and what they bind
paragraphs: A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement of what a candidate will achieve, produced from work already completed: mocks, internal assessments, class assessments and the teacher's view of trajectory. It is not a target, a promise or a negotiation, and it is not produced by the examination board. For university applications it matters enormously, because conditional offers are made against predictions long before any final result exists.

The practical consequence is a timing one that catches families out. Predictions are compiled during DP2 or Year 13 on the basis of work completed by that point. A student who leaves an internal assessment unfinished in DP1, or who underperforms in the autumn mock, is affecting an offer that will be made in the following months. Revision in the final term cannot retrospectively improve the evidence the prediction was based on.

If a prediction looks wrong, the route is evidence rather than argument. Ask which pieces of work the prediction rests on, and ask what would need to change for it to be revised. Schools will usually answer both questions directly. A student who then produces a markedly better piece of assessed work has given the department something to act on; a parent who disputes the judgement without new evidence has not. This is the single most common situation in which a few weeks of focused tutoring produces a concrete, dated piece of work that changes a decision.

One further point about how predictions are used. Universities treat them as a filter rather than as a result, and many will make an offer with conditions set at or slightly below the prediction. That means a prediction one grade low does not necessarily cost a place, but it does narrow the list of institutions willing to consider the application in the first place. The practical response is to get the strongest possible assessed work in front of the department before predictions are compiled, rather than to spend the following months appealing a judgement that has already been submitted.

sections.heading: Why grade boundaries move, and what to use instead
paragraphs: Grade boundaries are set after each examination session, for each paper, once the board has seen how candidates performed. They move because papers vary slightly in difficulty despite careful setting, and the boundary adjustment is how a board keeps a grade meaning the same thing from one session to the next. This is a feature rather than a flaw, and it has a direct consequence for how a student should revise.

The consequence is that last session's boundary is not a target. A student who calculates that they needed sixty-two per cent for a particular grade last June, and aims at sixty-five to be safe, has built a plan on a number that will be different this time. Worse, aiming at a boundary encourages leaving marks on the table deliberately, which is the opposite of what examination technique should be training.

What to use instead is the mark scheme. Published schemes show exactly where each mark sits in an answer, which is information about the next paper rather than about the last one. A student who marks their own work against a scheme learns that method marks exist independently of the final answer, that command terms determine what is credited, and that two extra marks per long question is a realistic and specific goal. We do not supply board papers or mark schemes ourselves, for copyright reasons; schools hold them and the boards publish the official versions, and that is where they should come from.

sections.heading: The routes available after results day, and when each one closes
paragraphs: Results day produces a small number of possible actions, most of which have short windows. Families who learn about them in August are already losing days. The routes differ by board and are administered through the school rather than by the candidate, which is the first thing to know: an individual cannot usually approach a board directly, and the school's examinations officer is the person who matters.

The first route is a clerical or administrative check, which confirms that marks were added and recorded correctly. The second is a review of marking, where the script is looked at again against the mark scheme. A review can lower a mark as well as raise it, which is a real risk and should be weighed rather than ignored. Both carry fees and both have deadlines measured in weeks from results publication.

The third route is a resit in the next available session. Cambridge runs June and November series, with a March series in some regions, so a November entry is the normal recovery route for a June result. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and in November; its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. For the IB, confirm the retake routes and every date with your Diploma coordinator. The fourth route is accepting the result and adjusting the plan, which is sometimes the right answer and is never presented as an option by anyone selling a resit course.

sections.heading: The mathematics route decision, and what universities actually ask
paragraphs: The Diploma offers two mathematics courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. They are not an easy option and a hard option; they are different courses. Analysis and Approaches concentrates on algebraic technique, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation concentrates on modelling, statistics and the use of technology. Both are respected, and one of them occasionally closes a door.

The door is a specific one. Some engineering, mathematics, physics and quantitative economics programmes state Analysis and Approaches, usually at Higher Level, in their entry requirements, and will not accept the other course as equivalent. Others accept either. The only reliable way to know is to read the published entry requirements for the actual universities and courses a student is considering, including the UAE institutions many families here have in mind, and to do it in DP1 while the choice is still open.

This is the one subject decision that is genuinely difficult to reverse. A switch between the courses is possible early in DP1 and progressively less realistic after that, because the content diverges quickly. The practical sequence is therefore: list four or five target course areas in DP1, read the requirement for each, and choose the mathematics route to keep those open. Where a student has already chosen and the requirement does not match, the honest answer is sometimes that the target course needs to change, and we would rather say that than sell a term of catch-up that cannot fix it.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the ceiling set at option time
paragraphs: The tier decision in a Cambridge IGCSE subject is taken by the school, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11, and it fixes what the student can be awarded. Core papers assess a reduced content range and are graded C to G. Extended papers assess the full range and are graded A* to E. A student entered for Core who performs superbly is awarded a C, and a university or sixth form reading that C cannot tell the difference between a comfortable Core performance and a borderline Extended one.

Schools place students in Core for defensible reasons. A candidate who would be ungraded at Extended is better served by a C, and a student carrying eight subjects with real difficulty in one may be better protected. The problem arises when a borderline student is placed in Core early, for safety, and then improves over the following year without the entry being revisited. That happens more often than parents realise and it is reversible up to the entry deadline.

The practical steps are narrow and worth taking. Ask in writing which tier your child is entered for, in each subject, and by what date the entry can still be changed. Cambridge publishes a final entry deadline of 27 November 2026 for the March 2027 series, and runs June and November series as well, so the relevant date depends on the series your school uses. Then ask what evidence would support a move to Extended. Most departments will name a mark on a specific paper, which turns an argument into a measurable target a term of focused work can hit.

sections.heading: What this work costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Published rates are scarce in this market. Three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in. The table below collects Dubai market rates published in October 2026, with the publisher named against each band. These are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list, and their use is as a benchmark for any quote you receive.

Two patterns are worth knowing before you spend. Rates rise towards an examination session, so the specialist you can book in January for a reasonable figure is both more expensive and less available in March. And in-home delivery carries travel inside the rate whether or not it appears as a line item, which is why Bestimate's figures for home visits sit above its figures for online work at every level.

There is also a sequencing point specific to a results-led page like this one. Money spent before the entry deadline, on moving a student from Core to Extended or on finishing an internal assessment properly, changes what is achievable. Money spent after results day, on a review of marking or a resit course, is managing a consequence. The first is a better purchase at the same price, and the only way to make it is to understand the mechanics early, which is the entire argument of this page.

sections.heading: Scheduling around a roster rather than an evening
paragraphs: A standard tutoring arrangement assumes a weekday evening that is reliably free. In a community where a significant share of households work airport and logistics rosters, that assumption fails every few weeks, and the usual result is a cancelled session, then another, then a quiet end to the arrangement. The fix is to design around the roster rather than hoping it cooperates.

Three things make it work. Slots are agreed a month ahead against the published roster rather than week by week. Weekend mornings and early weekday mornings are treated as normal options rather than as fallbacks, which suits a student who is awake anyway and a parent who is not. And the student holds the arrangement themselves from about fourteen upwards, with session notes going to the parent so nothing depends on being in the house at the time.

Online delivery is what makes all three possible. A visiting tutor needs a fixed route and a fixed evening to make the economics work, and a 06:30 session before school is not something anyone will drive to Dubai South for. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes in any event; lessons are one-to-one over live video, which means the slot can follow the roster instead of the roster having to accommodate a car journey.

A note on the student's side of this. Teenagers in roster households often take on more domestic responsibility than their classmates, including younger siblings after school, and that is usually invisible to the school. It is worth naming it when a tutoring plan is set, because it changes which hour is realistically free and whether homework between sessions should be ten minutes or forty. A plan built on an hour that does not exist fails in the third week, and the fix is almost always to shorten the session and raise the frequency rather than to insist on the original slot.

sections.heading: Getting started from Emaar South
paragraphs: Send three things before booking anything: the most recent marked script, the exact syllabus code and tier from the examination entry, and the dates of the next school assessment and the school's internal deadlines. For a Diploma student, add the current predicted grades if the school has issued them. Those items let a tutor arrive with an opinion rather than a questionnaire.

The first session is diagnostic. The tutor reads the marked script with the student, question by question, and separates four different problems that look identical on a report: content not known, technique not trained, timing lost under pressure, and confidence gone. Each needs different work, and spending a term on the wrong one is the most common waste of money in this market. You receive a written summary.

Then three honest limits. We do not promise grades, points totals or prediction changes. We do not place tutors in homes anywhere in the UAE, so if in-person teaching is what you want we are the wrong provider. We do not supply board past papers or mark schemes, since those belong to the boards and schools hold the official versions. And where a tier decision or an entry deadline has already passed, we will say plainly what is still available rather than selling hours against a result that is already fixed.

A final word on what to expect in the first month. Week one is the diagnostic. Weeks two and three teach against whatever the script showed, with homework pinned to the next school assessment. Week four is normally a timed piece so that progress is measured on something marked rather than on an impression. You get a written note after every session, and a review at six weeks that either confirms the plan or changes it. If the marks have not moved by then we will change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than recommending more hours of the same arrangement.
