sections.heading: What experienced should mean on an IGCSE tutor's profile
paragraphs: Experience becomes checkable the moment it is stated as a number of series and a specification code rather than a number of years. Which board, which code, which tier, how many cohorts, which papers most often. A tutor who answers Cambridge 0620 Extended, eleven cohorts, mostly Paper 2 and Paper 4, some Paper 6 has told you something you can test in a session. A tutor who answers over ten years of experience in science has told you nothing that distinguishes them from anyone else on the page.

Years are a weak proxy because the IGCSE cycle is fast. Cambridge runs three series a year, in March, June and November, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a tutor working steadily sees several cohorts a year rather than one. Two years of continuous IGCSE teaching across those series can involve more marked scripts than a decade of occasional work, and specification content is revised periodically, which means older experience can be experience of a version your child is not sitting.

The table below is the audit. It is not a hostile list of demands; most good tutors answer all of it in a few minutes and are pleased to be asked, because the alternative is competing on adjectives. What it is designed to surface is the difference between someone who has taught this specification repeatedly and someone whose experience is adjacent to it: a Maths teacher who has never taught 0606, a Physics graduate who has never marked a Paper 6 answer, a tutor whose track record is on a different board's version of the same subject.

sections.heading: The twelve-week evidence trail
paragraphs: Tuition that is working produces a record whether anyone intends it to or not. Twelve weekly sessions generate twelve marked question sets, and if those sets are comparable, the trend in them is the only honest measure of whether the money is doing anything. What makes them comparable is deliberate: timed, from past papers, at consistent difficulty, marked against the published criteria rather than impressionistically. A tutor who sets easier work as the term goes on produces a rising line that means nothing.

The schedule below is the shape a readable trail takes. The important feature is week six, which carries a decision rather than a report. By session six there has been enough marked work to know whether the original diagnosis was right, and the professional response to a flat line at that point is to say the analysis was wrong and change it, or to say tuition is not the intervention this child needs. Families in Dubai most often lose money not to bad tutors but to arrangements with no review point, which run for terms because nobody ever set a date to ask.

Parents do not need to read mark schemes to use this. Three questions cover it. Is the work the same difficulty as it was in week two? What was the mark then and what is it now? And what did the tutor say would happen by now at week one? If a tutor cannot produce comparable scripts, the trail does not exist, and reported progress is a recollection rather than a measurement.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme literacy is the skill that separates experience from longevity
paragraphs: IGCSE papers are marked to published criteria, and those criteria are specific enough that a tutor who knows them can usually predict where a particular child will leak marks before they sit the paper. That predictive ability is what experience should have bought, and it is the one thing worth testing directly. Ask a prospective tutor to look at a piece of your child's returned work and tell you where the marks went. A confident, specific answer within a minute or two is a strong signal. A general comment about needing to show more working is not.

Command terms are the clearest example. On Biology and Chemistry papers, describe, explain and suggest demand different things, and a student who answers all three as if they said describe loses application and evaluation marks consistently across every paper they sit. That is not a content weakness and no amount of revision fixes it, because the child believes they answered the question. An experienced tutor recognises the pattern from the script rather than from a conversation, and treats it as a teachable rule rather than carelessness.

The same literacy shows up in method marks. Extended Mathematics awards marks for working, and candidates who do arithmetic mentally and write only the result lose marks on answers that were substantially correct. Physics awards marks for stating the formula used before substituting into it. These are not insights; they are the published structure of the papers. What distinguishes experience is noticing which of them is costing this particular child the most, and teaching that one first rather than all of them at once.
bullets: Ask a tutor to read one of your child's returned scripts and say where marks went
Expect a specific answer in a minute or two, not a general comment

sections.heading: Reading a marked script as a parent
paragraphs: Most of what a parent needs from marked work is in the annotations rather than the total. The total tells you where the child is; the annotations tell you why, and whether the tutor is diagnosing or decorating. Work that comes back with a number and the word good is not feedback. Work that comes back with a specific note at the point of loss, in language the student can act on, is the product you are paying for.

The table below translates the annotations that recur most often on IGCSE scripts. None of them require subject knowledge to interpret, which is the point: a parent who can read them can hold a sensible conversation about their child's work without having studied the subject. They also let you check consistency over weeks. The same annotation appearing in week two and week ten means something has not been taught, and that is a question for the tutor rather than for the child.

One warning about volume. A script covered in ink is not necessarily better marked than one carrying four precise notes. Students act on a small number of corrections and ignore a page of them, so selective marking is a professional judgement rather than a shortcut. An experienced tutor marks the two or three losses that recur, names which of them the student is changing this week, and leaves the rest alone until those are fixed. That is why the short written note after a session matters as much as the ink on the script itself: the note is where the week's instruction actually lives, and it is the part a parent can read in thirty seconds.

sections.heading: What an experienced tutor does in the first three sessions
paragraphs: The first three sessions are where experience is most visible, because an inexperienced tutor spends them being pleasant and an experienced one spends them narrowing. Session one should put timed written work in front of the student and read the working rather than the answers. Session two should teach exactly one of the causes identified, not a tour of the topic. Session three should test whether that fix survives when nobody is prompting, which is the only way to know whether anything was learned.

What should not happen in those three sessions is content coverage. A tutor who opens by working through the syllabus from the beginning has decided, without evidence, that the problem is coverage. Sometimes it is, but in most cases a child achieving grade 5 in Chemistry has met every topic on the specification and has a specific recurring failure that no amount of re-teaching the content will touch. Starting from a diagnosis rather than from chapter one is the difference between fourteen hours and forty.

By the end of session three a parent should hold three things in writing: the named causes, an hour estimate, and a review date. None of these is a promise about a grade, and an experienced tutor will say so explicitly. What they are is an account of a professional judgement that can later be shown to have been right or wrong, which is exactly what you want from someone charging by the hour.

sections.heading: Red flags on a Dubai tutor profile
paragraphs: Some claims in this market are not merely vague; they are signals of a problem. A promised grade is the clearest, because no tutor controls the paper, the marking or the boundaries, and the only honest way to offer such a promise is to publish refund terms that are actually honoured. A self-asserted star rating is another: one provider in this market publishes its own aggregate rating of 4.9, which is a structured-data policy problem as well as a trust one, and two providers show different review counts on the same page.

Offers to help with coursework deserve particular attention. A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student produced. Any offer to supply text for a submission, or to edit a piece to completion on the student's behalf, is an academic-integrity breach, and the consequence lands on the child rather than on the provider. One operation in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The boundary is not a nuance, and a tutor who is vague about it has told you where they stand.

The last category is misrepresented location and status. Several pages ranking for UAE tutoring queries route parents to Indian phone numbers without saying so, one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page, and claimed regulator approval is common. IB Gram does not hold or claim approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, does not operate a UAE office, and states plainly that UAE delivery is online. Where a provider is vague about any of those three things, ask directly.

sections.heading: Examiner claims and what they can honestly mean
paragraphs: Examiner status is the most asserted and least evidenced claim in this market, and it is worth being precise about what it could do for your child even if true. An examiner marks scripts to a published scheme during a marking window. That work gives a person real familiarity with how candidates lose marks and how the criteria are applied in practice. It does not give access to future papers, to grade boundaries before they are set, or to any material a teacher cannot otherwise obtain.

IB Gram does not describe tutors as Cambridge or Pearson examiners. The reason is practical rather than modest: current examiner status is a contractual relationship between an individual and a board, it changes between series, and a platform cannot verify it on a parent's behalf in a way that would be honest to publish. Where a tutor's own background includes examining, the right response is the same as for any other claim: ask which board, which component and which series, and weigh the specificity of the answer.

What you can test directly is the thing examining is supposed to confer. Put a marked script in front of the tutor and ask them to say where the criteria would and would not award a mark. Someone who has marked a lot of scripts answers that quickly and specifically, whatever their formal status has been. Someone who has not will generalise. That test is available to you in the trial lesson and costs nothing, which makes it more useful than the claim itself.

sections.heading: Where specification experience is worth paying for, and where it is not
paragraphs: Specification-specific experience carries a premium in this market, and it is not always worth paying. For a Year 8 child building algebraic fluency, a strong general maths teacher is entirely sufficient and often better, because the work is foundational rather than board-shaped. For a Year 11 candidate eight weeks from a Cambridge Paper 4, the premium is the whole point: the tutor's value is almost entirely in knowing that paper's mark distribution and the predictable losses on it.

Between those two poles, the test is whether the problem is content or assessment. Content problems respond to good teaching regardless of board. Assessment problems, which is what most grade-5-to-grade-7 situations turn out to be, respond only to someone who knows how the specific papers award marks. Families often buy the expensive version for a content problem and the cheap version for an assessment problem, which is the wrong way round and explains a good deal of disappointment.

Scarcity is the other half of the calculation. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode work, Arabic as a first language 0508 and private-candidate entries, the question is not what experience costs but whether anyone within reach has it. That is the situation online delivery addresses directly: the pool becomes everyone teaching that specification at an hour that works in Gulf Standard Time, rather than everyone willing to drive to your community after the school run. In those cases the premium is not really a premium at all, because there is no cheaper local option being declined; the choice is between the specialist and nobody, and the honest answer when nobody suitable is free is to say so rather than to substitute a generalist and hope.

faqs.question: How do I check that an experienced IGCSE tutor in Dubai is actually experienced?
faqs.answer: Convert the claim into numbers you can test. Ask which specification codes they have taught, which tier, how many cohorts, and which papers they have most often marked. Cambridge 0620 Extended, nine cohorts, mostly Paper 4 is an answer; many years across the main boards is not. Then test the skill directly in the trial lesson: hand them a piece of your child's returned work and ask where the marks went. A specific answer inside two minutes is the signal you want. Years of employment correlate only loosely with the ability to read a script and name the loss.

faqs.question: Why are years of teaching a weak measure for an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the IGCSE cycle is fast and specifications change. Cambridge runs March, June and November series and Pearson runs May/June and November, so two years of continuous teaching can involve more marked scripts than a decade of occasional work. Specification content is also revised periodically, which means older experience may be experience of a version your child is not sitting. The useful unit is cohorts of a named code, not calendar years, and it is a question most good tutors are pleased to be asked because the alternative is competing on adjectives.

faqs.question: What should twelve weeks of IGCSE tuition produce that I can actually inspect?
faqs.answer: Twelve marked question sets at consistent difficulty, a short written note after each session, and a review at week six with a decision attached. The consistency is what makes it readable: a tutor who sets easier work as the term goes on produces a rising mark that measures nothing. Three questions cover your side of it. Is this work the same difficulty as week two? What was the mark then and now? And what did the tutor say at week one would have happened by now? If comparable scripts do not exist, the record does not either.

faqs.question: What happens at the week-six review if my child's marks have not moved?
faqs.answer: The honest options are that the diagnosis was wrong, the plan was right but too slow, or tuition is not the intervention this child needs. All three are things a tutor should be willing to say out loud, and the third is the one families almost never hear. What should not happen is a report that describes effort and attitude instead of marks. Set that date before the first paid session and put it in your own calendar, because the single most expensive failure in this market is an arrangement that runs for terms with no point at which the question gets asked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really predict where my child will lose marks before the exam?
faqs.answer: To a useful degree, yes, because IGCSE papers are marked to published criteria and individual candidates lose marks in patterned ways. A child who answers every explain command as if it said describe will do so again in May. A child who does arithmetic mentally and writes only the result will lose method marks on every multi-step question. Those patterns are visible in a few marked scripts. What cannot be predicted is a grade, because that depends on the paper, the marking and the boundaries, none of which any tutor controls.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor who has taught my child's exact specification?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem. For Year 8 and 9 foundations, a strong general teacher is sufficient and sometimes better, because the work is pre-specification. For a Year 11 candidate weeks from a specific paper, the premium is the whole point: the value is in knowing that paper's mark distribution and its predictable losses. The practical test is whether the issue is content or assessment. Content problems respond to good teaching on any board; assessment problems respond only to someone who knows how these particular papers award marks.

faqs.question: How should I interpret a tutor who says they are an examiner?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a claim and ask which board, which component and which series. Examining means marking scripts to a published scheme during a marking window; it confers real familiarity with how criteria are applied, and it confers no access to future papers or to boundaries before they are set. IB Gram does not label tutors as Cambridge or Pearson examiners, because current status is contractual, changes between series, and cannot be verified on a parent's behalf. The underlying skill is testable on one of your child's own scripts in a trial lesson, which is better evidence than the label.

faqs.question: What does good marking on a returned IGCSE script look like?
faqs.answer: A small number of precise notes at the point of loss, in language the student can act on, plus two named things to change this week. Not a total and the word good, and not a page covered in ink: students act on three corrections and ignore thirty. Useful annotations are readable without subject knowledge, which is the point. No working shown, describe not explain, formula not stated and not applied to the data each name a different fixable habit, and the same note appearing in week two and week ten is a question for the tutor.

faqs.question: Our tutor is pleasant and my child likes the sessions, but nothing has changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask for the comparable scripts. Rapport is necessary and insufficient, and a session that is forty-five minutes of a tutor explaining and ten of a child nodding feels productive while producing nothing. The diagnostic question is whether the child attempts work unaided during the session and whether anything is marked between sessions. If the answer to both is no, the format's advantage has been given away. Raise it as a change of method rather than a complaint, and set a four-week point at which comparable marked work either moved or it did not.

faqs.question: Does an experienced tutor need to follow our Dubai school's scheme of work?
faqs.answer: In term time, yes, for a practical reason: the value of weekly one-to-one is fixing this week's lesson while the homework is still open and the content is fresh. A tutor running a parallel syllabus at their own pace creates a second set of deadlines and leaves the school's work untouched. Ask them to work from the scheme of work, the specification code on the statement of entry and the school's assessment calendar. The exception is the exam term, when the sequence should follow the mark distribution of the papers rather than the school's teaching order.

faqs.question: How many sessions before I can tell whether an IGCSE tutor is any good?
faqs.answer: Three for the tutor, six for the plan. By session three you should hold three named causes specific enough to be re-tested, an estimated hour count and a review date, all in writing. That tells you whether the tutor is diagnosing or coasting. Whether the plan works is a different question and needs comparable marked work at week six against a week-one baseline. Judging a tutor on week one is unfair; waiting a whole term to judge the plan is expensive. Three and six are the useful checkpoints.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects most often need a specialist rather than a good general tutor?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 where the published pseudocode conventions decide marks, Arabic as a first language 0508, and any subject for a private candidate without a school sequencing the work. The practical sciences also reward specialists at paper level: a tutor who has marked Physics Paper 6 answers knows the graph, significant-figure and control losses that a theory-only teacher does not. Extended Mathematics, Biology and English have a deep enough pool in Dubai that a strong general teacher is often the right choice.

faqs.question: Is an experienced tutor available to visit our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and in-home visiting is offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai exists and charges roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee. What online delivery changes is which experience is available to you: the pool becomes everyone who teaches your child's specification at an hour that works in Gulf Standard Time, rather than everyone willing to drive to your community after the school run.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Dubai families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE are covered by the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and those operating without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page is the route to verify an application.

faqs.question: What should an experienced tutor refuse to do with my child's written work?
faqs.answer: Produce any part of a submission. A tutor explains why the criteria would or would not award a mark, gives feedback on what the student has already written, and coaches planning and redrafting. They do not supply text for an assessed piece or edit one to completion on a student's behalf. That boundary matters because the consequence of crossing it falls on the child rather than the tutor, and because parts of this market sell precisely that. Ask the question directly and listen for a clear answer rather than a reassuring one.

dubai/experienced-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the evidence before you agree to the block
dubai/experienced-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Three requests settle most of what this page covers. Ask which specification codes and how many cohorts, so experience becomes a number. Ask the tutor to read one of your child's returned scripts in the trial lesson and say where the marks went, so the claim is tested rather than accepted. And ask for a hour estimate and a week-six review date in writing, so there is a point at which the plan is judged on comparable marked work. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card details and no commitment, and the answers you get in it are the evidence.

intro.heading: Expertise shows up in what a tutor notices in the first ten minutes
paragraphs: Put a marked Paper 2 script in front of two tutors and the difference is immediate. One reads the comments the teacher wrote and agrees with them. The other reads the question, then the answer, then the mark allocation, and says something like: this answer explains where the question asked for an evaluation, so the top two marks were never available no matter how accurate the content was. That second reading is expertise. It is specific, it points at a repeatable error, and it generates something to do on Tuesday.

Parents in Dubai are usually searching for an expert IB tutor at a particular moment: a first DP1 report came in lower than expected, a mock result contradicted the predicted grade, or an internal assessment draft came back with comments nobody in the house can decode. In each case the useful tutor is not the one with the longest biography. It is the one who can tell you which of three possible causes is the real one, because the fix for a content gap, a technique gap and an exam-conditions gap are three different plans.

That is why this page is built around artefacts rather than adjectives. A marked script, a criterion report, a timed answer written under observation, an internal assessment plan with a research question in it, a redone question from a previous session. Those are the things a tutor produces or interprets, and they are the things you can inspect yourself. If six weeks of tutoring has produced none of them, you have no way of knowing whether it is working, and neither does the tutor.

There is a second reason to care about evidence in this market. Grades in the Diploma move slowly and unevenly. A student can improve substantially in paper technique and see no change in a school report for a full term, because the report is averaging work completed before the change. Families who judge tutoring only on the next grade often stop something that was working, or continue something that was not. Leading indicators solve that, and they are easy to read once somebody names them.

The practical shape of our service: one-to-one lessons over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time, with a free first lesson so the diagnostic read happens before any money changes hands. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. What the online format gives a Dubai family is access to a specialist in the exact subject and level rather than whoever is available within a twenty-minute drive, and a written trail after every session that a working parent can read in half a minute.

dubai/expert-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: The evidence a tutor works from changes with the programme. A DP2 student produces marked papers; an MYP student produces criterion grades that need translating; a PYP student produces work samples and a teacher comment. Each needs reading differently.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Most of the grade comes from externally marked papers, with an internally assessed component that the school marks and the IB moderates. Evidence is plentiful here: mocks, timed questions, past-paper sets and a draft trail on the internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts sit in a minority of the emirate's schools, so a student's peer group for comparison is small and school-report language varies between them. A tutor working with a Dubai DP student should ask for the school's own assessment calendar early, because internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and subject internal assessments differ by several weeks between IB World Schools here.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as letters A to D with a number. The grade boundaries are set against descriptors rather than percentages, so a 5 on criterion C means something different from 5 out of 8 on a test. Reading those reports accurately is the single most useful thing a tutor does for an MYP family.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP students frequently sit alongside peers who will leave for a British sixth form, so their final MYP year is aimed at two destinations. The evidence that matters is the task-specific clarification sheet the teacher issues with each assessment, and a tutor should be asking to see those rather than working from the generic criteria.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry units rather than subject syllabuses, with the Year 6 Exhibition as the culminating piece. Evidence is work samples, reading-level data and teacher commentary. Useful tutoring at this stage targets fluency in reading and number, and the research and note-making habits the Exhibition rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Primary cohorts in Dubai turn over quickly with mid-year arrivals from British, Indian and American systems, which means the most common evidence a tutor is handed is a report from a different curriculum. Translating that into a PYP picture, and identifying the one or two genuine gaps rather than restarting everything, is the first job.

dubai/expert-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the entry names the artefact that reveals most about where a student actually stands. These are the things to bring to a trial lesson rather than a general account of how the term has gone.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Bring a marked Paper 1 with the non-calculator working visible. Most recoverable marks sit in method lines that were skipped rather than in final answers that were wrong, and the HL Paper 3 investigation exposes whether a student can structure an unfamiliar problem at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Bring a modelling or statistics question with the calculator output attached. The repeatable error here is a model presented without justification of fit, or a regression quoted without comment on what it means in context. Both are technique, not content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bring a marked extended-response answer and the internal assessment plan. Energetics and organic mechanisms produce most content losses; the investigation produces most criterion losses, usually because the research question is too broad to control.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Bring a question on fields or circuits and any practical write-up with uncertainty calculations in it. Students who can recite the physics still lose marks for applying a general law without reference to the specific situation named in the stem.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Bring a six-mark question and the markscheme if the school released it. The diagnosis is nearly always command-term discipline: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate are being answered as though they were the same instruction.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Bring a diagram-based answer and one internal assessment commentary. Lost marks cluster around unlabelled or partially labelled diagrams and around real-world material that is mentioned rather than used as evidence for the argument.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Bring a Paper 1 analysis of an unseen text. The dominant error is paraphrase in place of analysis, which looks like engagement but earns nothing. Individual oral recordings, where the school allows a student copy, are the other useful artefact.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Bring a source-based answer and the internal assessment investigation. The repeatable losses are source evaluation that describes provenance without drawing a consequence from it, and essays that narrate chronology instead of arguing a line.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Bring a case-study answer. The pattern is tool knowledge without application: a correctly drawn framework that never refers to the stimulus material loses the application and evaluation marks that carry the grade.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Bring the prescribed title the student has chosen and whatever they have written about it. Most weak essays are weak because of the title choice and the absence of a real knowledge question, both of which are visible before any drafting.

subjects.name: Extended Essay support
subjects.description: Bring the research question and the supervisor's written comments. The useful intervention is almost always narrowing the question and fixing the method, and the student does every word of the writing themselves.

sections.heading: What an expert IB tutor in Dubai does with a marked script in the first ten minutes
paragraphs: The diagnostic read has a shape to it. The tutor looks at the question stem before the answer, because the command term and the mark allocation together define what was available. Then they look at the answer for structure rather than content, since a well-informed answer in the wrong form loses marks that a less-informed answer in the right form keeps. Only then do they look at the teacher's comments, and often they disagree with the emphasis.

Next comes a test. The tutor asks the student to redo one question, or part of one, out loud or on the shared screen. This is the step that separates an expert from a careful reader: a hypothesis about what went wrong is worthless until it survives contact with the student doing the thing again. Three outcomes are possible. The student reproduces the error, which confirms the diagnosis. The student does it correctly, which means the original error was a one-off under pressure. Or the student cannot start, which relocates the problem from technique to content.

The output of that process is a sentence a parent can act on. Not 'needs to work on exam technique', which is true of everybody, but something closer to: this student answers evaluate questions as though they were explain questions, loses the top two marks every time, and the fix is a four-step structure practised on six past questions. That sentence is checkable. In three weeks you can look at a new piece of work and see whether it happened.

If a first session does not end with something that specific, the session has not done its job. That is the standard worth holding a tutor to, and it is the reason our trial lesson is free: the diagnostic read is the part of the service that is easiest to evaluate and hardest to fake, so it belongs before the payment rather than after it.

sections.heading: The first six weeks, and what should exist at the end of each one
paragraphs: Tutoring without a visible trail is unmanageable, because the only feedback loop left is the next school report, which arrives too late to change anything. The alternative is a short list of things that should exist by a given week. It is not a guarantee of a grade and nobody should offer one; it is a way of telling, early, whether a plan is working.

Week one produces the written diagnosis. Week two produces the first attempt at the fix, usually on past questions chosen because they share the error, not because they share the topic. Week three produces a redone version of the week-one question, which is the first real test of transfer. Week four is the review point: by now either the written work shows the new structure or it does not, and if it does not, the diagnosis was probably wrong and should be redone rather than repeated louder.

Weeks five and six widen the target. One error type is rarely the whole story, and once the first fix holds, the second diagnosis is faster because the tutor now knows how this student works. By the end of week six there should be a marked or self-marked piece of work that a parent can compare to the one they brought in week one. That comparison, not a grade, is the honest measure at this stage.

Two cautions. Grades lag technique, often by a whole reporting cycle, because reports average work produced before the change. And some problems are not tutoring problems: a student who is sleeping four hours, or who has an undiagnosed processing difficulty, will not be fixed by a better explanation of command terms. A tutor who notices that and says so is being more useful than one who books more sessions.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks in the Diploma and the most commonly lost
paragraphs: IB questions are written against command terms, and each term carries an expectation about the form of the answer as well as its content. A student who treats evaluate as a synonym for explain will write something accurate and well-organised and still lose the marks that distinguish the top band. This is the most common diagnosable error we see in Dubai DP work, across every subject group, and it is also the quickest to fix because it is a structural habit rather than a knowledge gap.

The reason it persists is that it is invisible in day-to-day work. Classroom questions are usually short and content-focused, homework is often marked for correctness, and nobody is penalised for writing a strong description. The penalty appears only in extended-response questions under exam conditions, which is precisely where the grade is decided. A student can be the best-informed person in the room and still cap out two marks below their ceiling in every long answer.

The fix is mechanical and it works. Name the term. Name what the examiner is asking for. Write the structure down as a template with the number of elements required. Practise on six past questions sharing the same term until the structure is automatic, then mix terms so the student has to identify which one they are facing. That sequence takes three to four sessions and transfers across subjects, which is why it is often the first thing we target.

Parents can check this without any subject knowledge. Take a long answer and ask your child what the command term was asking for. If the answer is vague, the habit is not there yet. If the answer is a structure with named parts, it is.

sections.heading: Reading a mock paper the way a marker reads it
paragraphs: A mock result arrives as a number and a grade, and most of the useful information is in neither. The number is a raw mark against a paper the school chose; the grade comes from boundaries the school applied, which may be last year's, an average, or a deliberately conservative set. Two students with the same grade can be in quite different positions, and the difference is visible only in the distribution of lost marks.

The first thing to look at is where the marks went missing: spread evenly across the paper, or concentrated in the last two questions? Even spread suggests a content or technique issue. Concentration at the end suggests time management, which has a completely different remedy. Then look at the ratio of short-answer to extended-response losses. Strong short answers with weak long answers is the classic command-term signature. The reverse pattern usually means content gaps in specific topics.

The third read is about near misses. Questions where a student scored two out of four are more valuable than questions where they scored zero, because partial credit shows the thinking was close. A revision plan built on near misses typically moves more marks per hour than one built on topics the student never understood, and it is also better for morale in the eight weeks before final papers.

A caution about boundaries. Grade boundaries vary between sessions and are published by the board after results, not before, so nobody can tell a student in March exactly what mark a 6 will require in May. A tutor who claims to know is guessing. What can be said is where this student's marks are being lost and which of those losses is cheapest to recover, which is a more useful thing to know anyway.
bullets: Check whether losses are spread evenly or concentrated at the end of the paper
Compare short-answer accuracy against extended-response marks
List every question scored at roughly half marks: these move fastest
Ignore the predicted grade when planning; plan from the lost marks
Treat any confident claim about future grade boundaries as a guess

sections.heading: Feedback on an internal assessment draft, and how to tell good from useless
paragraphs: Internal assessment carries real weight in most DP subjects, commonly around a fifth of the final grade, and it is marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated by the IB. That structure has a consequence parents rarely hear: the single highest-value intervention is usually before any writing happens, at the point where the research question and method are chosen. A badly framed question caps the marks available no matter how well the write-up is executed.

Useful feedback is criterion-shaped and interrogative. It says: criterion B rewards a method that controls the variables you have named, and your method does not say how you will control temperature, so what will you do? It does not say: this needs more detail. It asks questions the student has to answer, and it leaves the student holding the pen. A tutor who hands back a marked-up draft with sentences inserted has crossed a line that puts the candidate at risk.

The boundary is not negotiable and it is worth stating to any tutor before the first session. Everything submitted must be the student's own work. A tutor teaches the skills, asks questions about material the student has already produced, and gives feedback against the criteria. The school supervisor is the person formally responsible for the Extended Essay and for authenticating internal assessment. In this market at least one site openly sells completed internal assessments; a family that buys one is risking the student's whole candidature for a few marks.

What a parent can inspect: ask to see the feedback. Good feedback is readable by a non-specialist because it is phrased as questions and criteria. If the feedback consists of tracked changes in the student's document, something has gone wrong, regardless of how helpful it looks.

sections.heading: What progress looks like before the grade moves
paragraphs: The most common reason families stop tutoring that was working is that they were watching the wrong indicator. School grades are lagging measures: a term grade averages assessments written over months, most of them before any change in technique. A student whose extended-response structure improved in October may not see it reflected until a January report, and by then a decision may already have been made.

Leading indicators are available and easy to read. First, the redone question: can the student now do, unaided, the thing they could not do three weeks ago? Second, self-correction during a session: does the student catch their own error before the tutor points it out? That shift, from being corrected to correcting, is the clearest single sign that learning has transferred. Third, the quality of the student's questions. A student who asks whether the question wants evaluation or explanation has internalised something a student asking what the answer is has not.

Fourth, time behaviour. Finishing a paper with time for review, where previously the last question was rushed, is a real gain even if the raw mark has not yet changed. Fifth, the spread of marks: losses becoming concentrated in fewer topics means the technique issues have been cleared and what remains is content, which is a better problem to have.

None of this is a promise about outcomes, and no honest tutor will offer one. External results depend on papers nobody has seen, on boundaries published after the event, and on what the student does on the day. What a tutor can be held to is whether these indicators are moving, and whether they can show you the evidence when you ask.
bullets: Unaided repetition of a previously failed question
Self-correction before the tutor intervenes
Better questions from the student about what is being asked

sections.heading: What the evidence trail looks like in an online session, and what you receive
paragraphs: Lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, which has a practical consequence for evidence: everything worked on is already in a document. A past-paper question can be annotated live and kept. A method can be built on a shared whiteboard and saved. A session can be recorded on request so the student can rewatch the part they lost. None of that exists after a session held at a kitchen table with a pen.

After each session you receive a short note. It names what was covered, what the student did unaided, what the target is for next week and anything the parent should know. For working parents, that note is the oversight mechanism, and it is deliberately written to be read in thirty seconds. Over a term the notes become the record that the fourth-session review and any later decision are made from.

The format choice also changes who can teach your child. A Dubai family choosing on geography picks from the tutors who can reach their community in rush-hour traffic. A family choosing online picks on subject and level, which for a narrow combination such as Computer Science HL or Maths AA HL Paper 3 is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available generalist. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses: home visits are a service we run only in India, and we would rather say that plainly than imply otherwise.

The honest limits: some things do not transfer well to video. A student who needs a physical laboratory practical needs their school's laboratory. A student who will not engage with a screen at all is better served by a different intervention. And the first session needs a quiet room with a stable connection, which in a shared apartment is a real planning problem rather than a trivial one.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market pays for demonstrated expertise
paragraphs: Rates in this market sort by what a tutor can show, and the published figures make the structure visible. Budget online tutoring, often undergraduate-delivered, advertises from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Exam-level IB and IGCSE specialists run around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching AED 450 and beyond. The premium end, advertised as named or examiner-experienced, reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Those are other providers' published figures with their names attached, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. What they show is that the market prices demonstrated specialism, and that the in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 carries a travel component rather than a teaching one. Monthly packages advertised locally include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The more useful question is what a higher rate buys in evidence terms. At the specialist end you should expect accurate knowledge of the current subject guide, the ability to mark to published criteria, and a diagnosis in the first session. If you are paying a specialist rate and receiving generic explanation with no written trail, the rate is wrong for what is being delivered, and that is a conversation to have in week two rather than week ten.

One thing a rate cannot buy is an outcome. Nobody can promise a grade, and in the UAE a promise like that is a commercial representation about something outside the provider's control. What can be promised is process: a diagnosis, a target, a written note, a review point, and an honest recommendation to stop if the evidence says tutoring is not the answer.

sections.heading: When the evidence says tutoring is not the right intervention
paragraphs: Some problems look like subject weakness and are not. A student who performs well in conversation and badly on paper may have a writing-speed or processing issue that a school learning-support assessment would identify. A student whose marks collapsed in one term across every subject is usually telling you something about sleep, health or circumstances rather than about chemistry. A student who has chosen three Higher Levels that do not suit them has a timetable problem, and the school is the only body that can change it.

We would rather say this before taking money than after. A short diagnostic block exists partly for this reason: four to six sessions with a defined question, ending in a written answer that may be a recommendation to do something other than continue. Families tell us that recommendation is the thing that made them trust the rest of the service, which is a reasonable response.

There is also a timing judgement. A DP2 student three weeks from final papers with four subjects in trouble cannot fix four subjects. The honest plan names the two where marks can still move, usually on near misses and technique, and leaves the others alone. Spreading eight sessions a week across everything produces exhaustion and no gain, and a tutor who sells it anyway is not reading the evidence.

Where tutoring is the right intervention, the evidence is usually clear within four sessions. Where it is not, it is also clear within four sessions. That is why the review point exists and why it is early, and why we would rather lose a booking than let a family spend a term finding out.

process.title: Send the artefact, not the story
process.description: A marked script, a criterion report or an internal assessment draft, plus the subject, level and school. That package tells us which tutor to put forward far more accurately than an account of how the term has gone, and it means the trial lesson starts with real material.

process.title: We match on the exact level and component
process.description: Not just the subject, but the level and the part of the course where the evidence says the problem sits. HL Paper 3, an internal assessment criterion, an unseen-text paper: these need different teachers, and we say which one we are proposing and why.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full first lesson at no cost, built around your marked work. It ends with a written diagnosis naming one repeatable error and the first target. You keep that whether or not you continue, and nothing has been paid.

process.title: Agree the target and the review date
process.description: Frequency, session length, the first measurable target and the date it will be checked, usually against the school's next assessment. Writing it down is what makes the fourth-session review possible rather than a matter of impressions.

process.title: Review at session four on evidence
process.description: We look at the redone question, the session notes and the most recent piece of school work. If technique has not moved, we question the diagnosis rather than adding sessions. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor at no extra cost.

process.title: Close the block or set the next target
process.description: A block ends with a written summary comparing the current work to the artefact you brought in week one. Then either a new six-week target, a reduced frequency, or a recommendation to stop. All three are normal outcomes.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis you can check
whyPoints.description: The first session produces one named, repeatable error and a plan aimed at it. Three weeks later you can look at a piece of work and see whether it happened. That is a different standard from general reassurance about exam technique.

whyPoints.title: A written trail after every session
whyPoints.description: A short note naming what was covered, what the student did unaided and the next target. For parents who cannot sit in on lessons, it is the oversight mechanism, and it becomes the record the review is made from.

whyPoints.title: Matched on component, not reputation
whyPoints.description: The level and the specific component drive the match. A tutor strong on Maths AA Paper 1 is not automatically the right person for HL Paper 3, and we would rather say so than place the convenient match.

whyPoints.title: Leading indicators, not just grades
whyPoints.description: We track unaided repetition, self-correction, question quality and time behaviour, because grades lag technique by a reporting cycle. That stops families stopping something that is working.

whyPoints.title: A published coursework boundary
whyPoints.description: The student writes every submitted word. A tutor asks questions and gives criterion-based feedback on material the student has already produced. We state it here so you can hold us to it.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to stop
whyPoints.description: If the evidence points at learning support, health, timetable or workload rather than subject weakness, we say so in writing. A recommendation to stop costs us a booking and is still the right answer.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether an IB tutor is genuinely expert before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Give them a marked script and watch the first ten minutes. An expert reads the question stem and the mark allocation before the answer, because those define what was available. They then ask your child to redo a question to test whether the error repeats. By the end you should have one specific, repeatable error named and a plan aimed at it. A tutor who talks about confidence and revision technique without locating a mark on the page has given you nothing checkable. Run that test in a free trial lesson rather than paying for the privilege of finding out.

faqs.question: What should the first tutoring session actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis. Not a list of topics to cover, which any syllabus provides, but a statement of what this particular student does that costs marks, and what the first fix is. Good examples look like: answers evaluate questions as explain questions, loses the top two marks in every long response, fix is a four-part structure practised on six past questions. That sentence is checkable in three weeks. If the first session ends with general encouragement and a plan to start at chapter one, the diagnostic work has not been done and you are paying for a course rather than for expertise.

faqs.question: Why has my child's grade not moved after six weeks of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Often because the grade is a lagging measure. A term grade averages assessments written over months, most of them before any change in technique, so a real improvement in October can be invisible until a January report. Check the leading indicators instead: can your child now do, unaided, the question they failed in week one? Do they catch their own errors before the tutor does? Are papers being finished with time to review? If those are moving, the plan is working. If none of them has moved in six weeks, the diagnosis was probably wrong and should be redone rather than repeated.

faqs.question: Which IB command terms do Dubai students misread most often?
faqs.answer: Every IB question is written against a command term that governs the form of the answer, not just its content. Explain asks for reasons linked to consequences; evaluate asks for a judgement supported by weighted evidence. A student who answers evaluate as though it said explain writes something accurate and loses the top band every time. The error is invisible in classroom work, which is mostly short and content-focused, and it surfaces only in extended responses under exam conditions. It is also the quickest thing to fix, usually three or four sessions, because it is a structural habit rather than a knowledge gap.

faqs.question: How should I read my child's IB mock result?
faqs.answer: Look past the grade at where the marks went. Losses spread evenly across the paper point at content or technique; losses concentrated in the final questions point at time management, which has a different remedy entirely. Compare short-answer accuracy with extended-response marks: strong short answers and weak long ones is the command-term signature. Then list every question scored around half marks, because those near misses move faster per hour of work than topics never understood. Treat the grade itself cautiously, since the school chose the boundaries it applied and real session boundaries are published only after results.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me what mark my child needs for a 6?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who says otherwise. Grade boundaries vary between examination sessions and are set after the papers have been marked, which is why boards publish them with results rather than in advance. Any specific figure quoted in March for a May session is a guess dressed as information. What a tutor can tell you, usefully, is where this student's marks are currently being lost, which of those losses is cheapest to recover, and what the work would look like if it moved. That is more actionable than a boundary estimate would be even if one existed.

faqs.question: What does good feedback on an internal assessment draft look like?
faqs.answer: It is phrased as criteria and questions, and it leaves the student holding the pen. A useful comment names the criterion, says what that criterion rewards, points at the gap and asks the student what they will do about it. A useless comment says the section needs more detail. A dangerous comment is a tracked change that inserts a sentence, because everything submitted must be the student's own work and the consequences of that boundary being crossed land on the candidate. Ask to see the feedback: if it is readable by a non-specialist as comments and questions, it is the right kind.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child choose an internal assessment research question?
faqs.answer: A tutor can critique a question the student has drafted, which is where most of the value sits, because a badly scoped question caps the marks available regardless of how well the write-up is executed. The questions are about whether the variables can be controlled, whether the data can actually be gathered, and whether it can be answered within the word limit. What a tutor should not do is supply a question, or pick from a list of ones known to score well. The wording must be the student's own, and their school supervisor remains the person formally responsible for the work.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP student need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one session a week per subject in trouble, which is enough to set a target, practise it and check transfer before the next session. Two a week makes sense in a defined push: the six weeks before mocks, or a period of catching up after illness or a move. More than two a week in one subject is usually a sign the plan is wrong rather than that more is needed, because the limiting factor is independent practice between sessions, not contact time. For a DP2 student close to final papers, two subjects at two sessions each is generally the realistic ceiling.

faqs.question: My child is three weeks from final papers with four subjects in trouble. What now?
faqs.answer: Pick two. Four subjects cannot be fixed in three weeks, and attempting it produces exhaustion and no gain. The honest plan identifies the two where marks can still move, which usually means subjects with near misses in the mock rather than subjects never understood, and works on technique and partially credited questions rather than new content. Leave the other two to the school's own revision programme. A tutor who sells eight sessions a week across everything at that point is not reading the evidence. We would rather state the limit and work within it than take a booking we cannot justify.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring produce better evidence than in-person tutoring?
faqs.answer: It produces more durable evidence, which is a practical advantage rather than a pedagogical claim. Everything worked on over a shared screen already exists as a document: annotated past papers, whiteboard working, and a recording if the student asks for one. A session at a kitchen table leaves a page of handwriting. Our lessons run one-to-one over live video, with a short written note afterwards naming the target. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, since home visits are a service we run only in India. The other gain is choice: you match on subject and level rather than on driving distance.

faqs.question: What does the session note after each lesson contain?
faqs.answer: Four things, written to be read in half a minute. What was covered, what the student managed unaided, the specific target before the next session, and anything a parent should know or do. It is deliberately not a transcript. For working parents in Dubai who cannot sit in on a 19:00 session, that note is the oversight mechanism, and over a term the collected notes are what the review at session four is actually based on. If notes stop arriving, that is a signal in itself and worth raising immediately rather than at the end of term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor work on both the subject papers and the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and there is an argument for it: the same person sees how the student thinks on paper and in extended work, and the two inform each other. The practical caution is time. Internal assessment work expands to fill whatever is available, and a family that intends to work on paper technique can lose a whole term to coursework feedback. We normally set the split explicitly, for example three sessions on papers and one on the internal assessment in a four-week cycle, and review it. The coursework boundary is identical either way: feedback and questions only.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us to stop tutoring?
faqs.answer: Several things. Evidence pointing at a learning-support need that a school assessment should investigate rather than a tutor should work around. A collapse across every subject in one term, which usually reflects sleep, health or circumstances. A Higher Level combination that does not suit the student, where only the school can change the timetable. Or four sessions with no movement in any leading indicator after the diagnosis has already been revisited once. In each case we say so in writing and explain what we think the actual problem is. Losing a booking is a smaller cost than a family losing a term.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a Dubai DP student to a subject specialist?
faqs.answer: Common subjects at common levels, such as Maths AA SL or English A, are usually matched within a few days. Narrow combinations take longer: Computer Science HL or a specific HL science in the February to May window can take one to two weeks because demand concentrates across the whole emirate at once. If no UAE-based specialist is free we say so and match from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, keeping the session at a Dubai-friendly hour on Gulf Standard Time. The format and the subject depth do not change; the tutor's location does.

dubai/expert-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Bring the marked script and let the evidence decide
dubai/expert-ib-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up an expert IB tutor in Dubai, the shortest route to an answer is a marked piece of your child's work and a free first lesson. Watch whether the tutor reads the question before the answer, whether they test the error by asking your child to redo something, and whether the session ends with one specific thing to fix. Lessons from IB Gram run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school week, with a written note after each one and a review at session four. Send us the subject, the level and the script, and we will tell you what we think is actually going wrong.

dubai/female-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students at Dubai schools. Where a family has asked for a female tutor, that is applied as a filter before subject matching begins, so the shortlist you see is already restricted to tutors who meet it.

intro.heading: Why Dubai families specify a female tutor, and what the specification should not cost you
paragraphs: The request arrives in three recognisable forms. Some families want a female tutor for a daughter in Years 11 to 13 because the sessions are long, repeated and conducted one-to-one, and the parent would rather the adult in that relationship be a woman. Some want it for Arabic as a first language or Islamic Education, where the household follows a convention about who teaches religious content to a teenage girl. And some ask because a previous male tutor talked over a quiet student and the family is correcting for that rather than for gender. All three are legitimate reasons to state a requirement. None of them should force the family to accept weaker subject knowledge as the price.

That trade-off is what a thin tutor pool creates. If the available tutors are the ones who live within driving distance of Mirdif or Al Khawaneej, a family asking for a female Chemistry HL specialist is choosing from perhaps two or three people, and the gender filter may leave one. Online delivery removes the geography from the problem. The filter still removes candidates, but it removes them from a pool defined by subject and level rather than by postcode, which is why a Dubai family can usually hold both requirements at once instead of trading one away.

The second half of this page is about the Diploma itself, because a match on gender that misses on subject is not a match. The IB rewards a very specific skill set: reading a command term precisely, writing to published criteria, and handling an internal assessment as a piece of extended independent work. Students lose marks in predictable places, and a parent who knows where those places are can tell within three sessions whether tutoring is working. The component tables further down name them by paper and by criterion letter.

Dubai is an unusual market to do this in. KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 students in the emirate in 2024-25, running 17 different curricula between them, with British-curriculum schools the largest group by enrolment and International Baccalaureate schools a smaller but growing slice. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, three of them running the IB, adding 16,846 places. A tutor working across that market sees the same Diploma assessed by a dozen different school cultures, which is useful experience and also a reason to ask what a tutor has actually taught rather than what they studied.

What follows is practical rather than promotional: who is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE and how you check it, what the Dubai market charges by provider model, how the KHDA mandatory subjects sit alongside the Diploma, how safeguarding should work in an online one-to-one lesson, and what happens in the honest case where nobody who meets every one of your requirements is free this term.

dubai/female-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: A Dubai family asking for a female IB tutor is rarely asking about one year group only. Siblings run across Primary Years, Middle Years and the Diploma, and the same requirement usually applies to all of them. These are the programmes the request attaches to and what tutoring looks like in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated by the IB. Tutoring at this level is mostly criterion work and timed-paper technique rather than new content delivery, because the content is already being taught at school five times a week.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma cohorts are small, often 40 to 90 students per year group, so subject choice is constrained by what the school can timetable. A student who wants Chemistry HL and History HL may find the blocks clash. Tutoring is frequently used to carry a subject the school could only offer at Standard Level, or to support a student taking a Diploma subject by self-study with the school's agreement.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, lettered A to D, with no external papers unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Marks are reported on a 1-8 scale per criterion and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Most families discover the criteria exist only when a report arrives, which is the point at which tutoring becomes useful.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP-to-Diploma transition is where the gap shows. A student used to criterion-based tasks with redrafting meets timed Paper 1 and Paper 2 conditions for the first time in Year 12. Mirdif and Al Qusais families often start tutoring in Year 11 for exactly this reason: to build timed-writing stamina before the Diploma starts rather than during it.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word commentary plus a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a named school supervisor. Together they carry up to three bonus points on the 45-point total, which is the difference between a conditional and a firm offer for many students.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay supervisor is appointed by the Dubai school and the school's internal deadlines, not the IB's, drive the calendar. A tutor's role sits beside that: asking whether a research question is answerable in 4,000 words, whether the sources are reachable from Dubai, and whether the argument actually responds to the question. The supervisor signs the reflections; nobody else can.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, finishing in the Year 6 exhibition. Reading fluency, number sense and written structure are the three things that transfer forward, and a weak foundation in any of them surfaces again in MYP assessment criteria B and C. Tutoring here is short, frequent and focused on one skill at a time.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP parents usually come to tutoring after a KHDA inspection report or a parent-teacher meeting flags reading age. Because Arabic is mandatory from FS2 in Dubai private schools, a non-Arab child may also be carrying a second script and a second grammar at the same time as learning to read in English, which is a genuine load and worth naming rather than treating as slowness.

dubai/female-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Dubai families most often request, with the place marks are actually lost in each. A tutor who cannot name that place for your child's subject is not the right tutor, regardless of which other requirements they satisfy.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate grades. Students lose marks by writing a correct answer in the wrong form: no state symbols, an unbalanced half-equation, a calculation quoted to the wrong number of significant figures. The internal assessment is graded on personal engagement, exploration, analysis, evaluation and communication, and most lost marks sit in evaluation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and complex numbers at Higher Level; the Standard Level course is narrower but assessed just as precisely. Marks disappear in method presentation rather than in arithmetic. A correct final answer with no working scores a fraction of the available marks, and the calculator paper rewards knowing which of the five standard graphical approaches to reach for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields are usually secure; students fall on the extended-response questions that ask them to explain rather than calculate. The command terms carry fixed expectations, so a question that says explain needs a causal chain, not a formula. Uncertainty propagation in the internal assessment is where a good investigation loses a whole criterion band.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise the recall topics they enjoy and arrive at data-analysis questions untrained, which is where a third of the paper marks sit. Correct biological terminology is marked strictly: cell respiration is not breathing, and a mark scheme written for one word will not accept a paraphrase that means roughly the same thing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are assessment objects, not illustrations. An unlabelled axis or a shift drawn in the wrong direction costs marks that the accompanying paragraph cannot recover. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published articles, each 800 words, and the most common failure is a commentary that summarises the article instead of applying a single economic concept to it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and students write about content when the marks are for how the text produces its effect. The individual oral requires a global issue linked to one literary and one non-literary extract, prepared in advance and delivered without a script. Preparation is structural rehearsal, not memorisation.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.levels: HL and SL · also KHDA-mandated at school
subjects.description: Dubai students often carry Arabic A alongside the school's mandatory Arabic provision, with different expectations in each. The Diploma course assesses literary analysis in Standard Arabic, and students who speak a Gulf or Levantine dialect at home can read fluently yet write below their level. This is the subject where a female tutor is most often requested outright.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Not part of the Diploma, but required by KHDA in every Dubai private school and examined internally by the school. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support here is about terminology, memorisation technique and written structure in the language the school teaches it in.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is source-based and marked on provenance and cross-referencing rather than on knowledge. Students write everything they know about the period and score in the lowest band for the question that asked them to compare two sources. The HL regional option adds a third paper that rewards a bank of specific, dated examples rather than general narrative.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools and theories are only credited when applied to the stimulus material in front of the student. A generic SWOT scores almost nothing. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study, which rewards months of structured preparation and punishes students who meet it for the first time two weeks before the paper.

dubai/female-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery means your address does not limit the tutor pool, but it still shapes the timetable. These are the Dubai communities from which this request most often arrives, with the scheduling reality in each.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: A dense family catchment feeding several British and IB schools in Al Mizhar and Al Warqa. Bus routes drop between 15:15 and 16:00, so a 16:30 start is realistic on four days a week and a 19:00 slot suits households with two working parents.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Villa communities with longer school runs towards Mirdif and Al Mizhar. Students often arrive home after 16:30 and need a later start. Weekend mornings are the easiest slot to protect here, because Saturday activity schedules are usually lighter than in the Marina corridor.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed Arab and South Asian households, high demand for Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education alongside the school curriculum. Families here are the most likely in Dubai to state a female-tutor requirement for those two subjects specifically rather than across the board.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Newer villa stock with school runs out towards Meydan and Dubai Hills. Siblings in different year groups frequently share a tutor across the same evening, which works online because there is no travel gap to pay for between two consecutive sessions.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: Older established community with a strong Indian and British school presence and a lot of MYP-to-Diploma transition work. Evening slots from 18:00 are the most requested, and Ramadan timetables here shift firmly to post-Iftar sessions.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: Dubailand community where the school commute is long in both directions. A 17:00 start is often impossible during term; 17:45 onwards works. Holiday weeks are used heavily here to catch up on internal assessment drafts before school deadlines land.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Apartment-heavy, with a large contingent at the British and IB schools in the Academic City corridor. Quiet study space is the practical constraint rather than travel, so headphones and a fixed corner of the flat matter more here than start times.

sections.heading: What a female IB tutor request actually changes in the matching process
paragraphs: Stated plainly: a gender requirement is applied as a filter before subject matching, and it narrows the pool rather than reordering it. On an online model the pool being narrowed is every tutor who teaches that subject at that level and can work a Gulf Standard Time evening, which is large enough that the filter usually leaves a real choice. On a home-visit model the pool being narrowed is tutors willing to drive to your community at 17:00, which is small before the filter is applied and sometimes empty after.

That difference is the whole argument for online delivery on this particular search, and it is worth being concrete about it. A family in Al Khawaneej asking for a female Physics HL tutor is, in the in-home market, choosing from the handful of specialist Physics tutors who will cross the emirate on a weekday evening. Narrow that by gender and the result is frequently a Physics generalist who teaches up to Standard Level, or a long wait. The same request online is filled from a pool defined by what the tutor teaches, not by where the tutor sleeps.

What the requirement does not change is the quality bar. The match still has to clear subject and level: a tutor who has taught the Diploma course the student is sitting, who knows the published criteria for its internal assessment, and who can mark a past paper response to the current markscheme. If no tutor clears both the subject bar and the gender filter for a given term, we say so rather than offering a partial match quietly. The coverage table later on this page sets out what that honest answer looks like in practice.
