sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies: the subjects behind most of these requests
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, because the federal rule requires it and KHDA enforces it. These are the subjects where a female-tutor request is most often specific rather than general: a family may be entirely comfortable with a male Mathematics tutor and still want a woman teaching Islamic Education to a sixteen-year-old daughter. Naming that as a per-subject requirement rather than a blanket one usually produces a better match on both subjects.

KHDA's own guidelines carry details that shape how support can honestly be described. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further constraints matter for tutoring. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach those subjects, which is a school-level credential rather than something a private tutor carries. And for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support must work from what the school actually teaches rather than from an alternative syllabus. A tutor who offers their own Islamic Education curriculum has misunderstood the rule.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks are actually lost, component by component
paragraphs: A parent who wants to judge tutoring on evidence rather than on atmosphere needs to know which components carry which weight and what a lost mark looks like in each. The pattern across Diploma subjects is consistent: external papers carry roughly 70 to 80 per cent of the subject grade and the internal assessment carries the rest, and students under-perform on the internal assessment relative to their papers because it is the only component with no time limit and therefore no forcing function.

The second pattern is that marks are lost to form rather than to knowledge. A chemistry answer without state symbols, a maths solution with the right answer and no method, an economics diagram with an unlabelled axis, a history essay that narrates where the question said compare. None of these are knowledge failures and all of them are expensive. This is also why a tutor's first session should involve marking something the student has already written, rather than teaching a topic: the diagnosis is in the script.

The third pattern is the command term. Diploma markschemes are written against a fixed list of command terms, and each one sets the expected shape of the answer. State wants a fact. Explain wants a causal chain. Evaluate wants both sides weighted and a judgement. Discuss wants a balanced argument. Students who read the question for topic rather than for command term write good material that answers a question nobody asked, and that single habit is often worth a full grade band across a paper.

sections.heading: Safeguarding an online one-to-one lesson: what a Dubai parent should insist on
paragraphs: A one-to-one lesson between an adult and a teenager needs a structure, and online delivery makes that structure easier to enforce than a closed door in a study would. The baseline is simple: the lesson happens on a platform the parent can join, in a room the household uses rather than a bedroom, with the student's camera on and the session visible to anyone walking past. Families requesting a female tutor are often doing so partly for this reason, and the answer should be an arrangement rather than a reassurance.

Recording is the part worth settling in advance. A recorded session gives the student something to revise from and gives the parent a way to see what was taught without sitting in. It also creates personal data about a minor, which under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection should be collected for a stated purpose, kept for a stated period and deletable on request. Ask who holds the recording, where it is stored and how long it is kept. A provider who cannot answer those three questions has not thought about it.

Communication channels matter as much as the lesson itself. Scheduling and feedback should run through the platform or a group that includes the parent, not through private messages between a tutor and a student. Payment should never be arranged directly with the tutor outside the platform, because that removes the record that protects both sides. And the family should be able to change tutor without explaining why, which is the single most useful safeguarding mechanism available to a parent who has a feeling but not a fact.

sections.heading: What Dubai tutoring costs by provider model, and whether a gender requirement moves the price
paragraphs: It should not, and in the online market it generally does not. A gender filter narrows the pool rather than changing what an hour of specialist teaching is worth, so the number that moves your quote is the level you need and the format you choose, not the requirement you state. The in-home market behaves differently, because there the filter interacts with travel: the fewer tutors who will cross Dubai to your community, the stronger the bargaining position of the one who will.

The figures below are market rates collected from published 2026 rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, not IB Gram prices. They are here because three of the six pages currently ranking for Dubai IB tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. A parent comparing quotes needs the bands to know whether a number is reasonable.

Read the table as a map of what you are paying for. Budget online tutoring at the bottom of the range is usually a university student working from the markscheme rather than from teaching experience, which is fine for a content gap and poor for internal assessment feedback. The specialist band buys someone who has taught the course through a full cycle. The premium band buys a named reputation, and it is worth the difference only when the specific thing you need is rare: a Higher Level option topic, a language A combination, or examiner-level familiarity with one paper.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor your child in the UAE, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a stated completion time of two working days. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting you a specific figure is guessing.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 can all hold the permit. That last category surprises people, and it is a useful reminder that holding a permit says someone is allowed to tutor, not that they can teach the Diploma. The permit is a legal check, not a quality check, and the two should be asked about separately.

One restriction is worth stating because it is the most common unlawful arrangement in this market. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. Dubai families sometimes ask whether their daughter's own class teacher can tutor her privately. The answer should be no, and a provider that arranges it is putting the teacher's position at risk as well as the family's.

sections.heading: The honest version of academic honesty when a tutor works on an internal assessment
paragraphs: This is the line that separates tutoring from malpractice, and it needs saying on a page like this because the same search results that show tutoring agencies also show sites selling finished internal assessments. The IB's position is that assessed work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each published criterion is asking for, ask questions that expose a weak argument, and point out that a section does not answer the research question. A tutor may not supply sentences, insert sources, rework a paragraph into its final form, or produce assessed material of any kind.

In practice the boundary is easy to hold if the feedback stays in the form of questions and criteria. Instead of rewriting an evaluation section, the tutor asks which limitation most affected the result and why the student has not mentioned it. Instead of fixing a research question, the tutor asks how the student would answer it in 4,000 words and lets the impossibility surface. The student leaves the session with a list of decisions to make rather than a corrected document, which is slower and is the only version that is safe for them.

Parents should treat an offer to produce coursework as a warning about everything else on the page. A provider willing to breach academic honesty for a fee has told you how it handles the rules it finds inconvenient, and the consequence of being caught falls on the student, not the provider: an IB malpractice finding can cost a candidate the Diploma. Any tutor working with a Dubai student should also be working inside the school's own process, because the Extended Essay supervisor and the subject teacher are the people who sign the declarations.

sections.heading: Coverage, scheduling and what happens when nobody meets every requirement
paragraphs: Three requirements stacked together, a specific Diploma subject at Higher Level, a female tutor and a 17:00 Gulf Standard Time slot, will occasionally produce no match. The useful thing a provider can do at that point is say so quickly. What no competitor page in this market discloses is a coverage limit, and it is the single most common cause of a bad first experience: a family states three requirements, is told yes, and discovers in week two that one of them quietly was not met.

Our position is stated in the table below. Common Diploma subjects at both levels are covered quickly. Rarer combinations take longer, and the scarcest requests are Higher Level option topics and second-language A subjects, where a gender filter on top of a small specialist pool may mean waiting for a slot rather than accepting a generalist. Where a UAE-based tutor is not available, the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching online into Gulf Standard Time, which we say up front rather than concealing behind a local-sounding number.

Scheduling has its own constraints in Dubai. School buses return between roughly 15:15 and 16:30 depending on the community, so a weekday session before 16:30 is unrealistic for most families, and the 18:00 to 20:00 window is the most contested. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar timings and sometimes to late morning on weekend days. Holiday weeks are the best time to do internal assessment work, because the student has a clear day rather than ninety minutes between dinner and bed.

process.title: State the requirement in writing
process.description: Say that a female tutor is required and whether it applies to every subject or only to some. Name the subjects, levels and the school, because the school sets the internal deadlines that shape the first month of work. A per-subject requirement usually produces a stronger match than a blanket one.

process.title: Free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: One lesson, no card details taken and no obligation to continue. The tutor marks a piece of work the student has already done rather than teaching a topic, because the diagnosis is in the script. You get a written note naming the two or three specific things that are costing marks.

process.title: Agree a slot and a term plan
process.description: Pick a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time that survives the school bus, activities and the 18:00 crush. The plan names what is being worked on for the next six weeks and which school deadline it is aimed at, so progress is measurable against something other than a feeling.

process.title: Review at session six
process.description: Compare marked work from session one against marked work from session six on the same criteria. If the movement is not visible, the plan changes or the tutor changes. Asking for a different tutor needs no explanation and does not restart anything you have already paid for.

process.title: Re-plan around the exam calendar
process.description: Before the examination series the focus shifts from content to timed papers and markscheme work. Dates come from the school's own calendar and the board's published timetable, which for Diploma candidates means confirming the session dates with the school's IB coordinator rather than relying on a figure on a tutoring website.

whyPoints.title: The requirement is a filter, not a footnote
whyPoints.description: Gender is applied before subject matching, so every tutor you are offered already satisfies it. You are not asked to choose between the requirement you stated and the subject specialist your child needs, which is the trade-off the in-home market usually forces in a community with a thin local pool.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not nearby generalists
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run online, the shortlist is drawn from tutors who teach that course at that level rather than from those who can drive to your community by 17:00. For a Higher Level subject that difference is the whole quality gap, and it is the honest reason to prefer online in this market.

whyPoints.title: Safeguarding as an arrangement
whyPoints.description: A shared room, camera on, a parent able to join, feedback in a channel the parent sees, and recordings with a stated purpose and retention period under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. Changing tutor needs no reason. These are arrangements you can check rather than promises you have to trust.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to published 2026 rate cards and to the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, and they are the market's numbers rather than ours. Most pages ranking for this query publish no price at all, which leaves parents comparing quotes with nothing to compare them against.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and asks questions. The student writes every sentence of their own work. We say that plainly because the same search results contain sites selling completed internal assessments, and the consequence of using one falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: Where a requirement cannot be met this term, you are told before a lesson is booked, including when the tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. No page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and it is the most common cause of a bad first month.

faqs.question: Can I ask for a female IB tutor for my daughter in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth stating in writing rather than mentioning in a call. The requirement is recorded on the request and applied as a filter before subject matching begins, so every tutor you are shown already meets it. It is also useful to say whether it applies to all subjects or only to some: many families want a female tutor for Arabic as a first language or Islamic Education and have no preference for Mathematics. A per-subject requirement keeps the specialist pool wider for the subjects where you have no preference.

faqs.question: Does asking for a female tutor mean accepting a less experienced one?
faqs.answer: It should not on an online model. The filter narrows a pool defined by subject and level, which is large enough that a Diploma Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics, Biology, English, Economics or History request is normally filled within a few days with a choice of tutors. The combinations where it bites are Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects, where the specialist pool is small before any filter is applied. In those cases the honest answer is to wait for the right tutor or accept a tutor based outside the UAE teaching online, and we say which it is before anything is booked.

faqs.question: Why is a female tutor requested most often for Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Because those are the subjects where a household convention is most likely to apply. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its international curriculum, and the content is religious and cultural rather than technical. KHDA itself requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arab students, so families are already used to the idea that these subjects are organised differently from the rest of the timetable. Stating the preference for those subjects alone is common and entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: Do lessons happen at our home in Dubai or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate model rather than a limitation, because the tutor your daughter needs for Chemistry at Higher Level is chosen from everyone who teaches that course rather than from the few specialists willing to drive to your community on a weekday evening. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Dubai school day.

faqs.question: What should I insist on for an online one-to-one lesson with a teenager?
faqs.answer: Five things. The lesson happens in a shared room rather than a bedroom, with the camera on. The platform allows a parent to join at any point without arranging it in advance. Scheduling and feedback run through a channel that includes you, not through private messages to the student. Payment goes through the platform rather than directly to the tutor. And you can change tutor without explaining why. The fifth is the most useful of the five, because it lets you act on a feeling before it becomes a fact.

faqs.question: Can sessions be recorded, and who keeps the recording?
faqs.answer: They can, and it is genuinely useful for revision. Before agreeing, ask three questions: what purpose the recording is kept for, where it is stored, and how long before it is deleted. A recording of a lesson is personal data about a minor, and under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection it should be collected for a stated purpose and removable on request. A provider that cannot answer those three questions in writing has not thought about it, which tells you something beyond the recording itself.

faqs.question: Is a private tutor in Dubai required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE lists the application route through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are all eligible. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, treat any page quoting a specific amount with scepticism.

faqs.question: Can my daughter's own teacher at her Dubai school tutor her privately?
faqs.answer: Treat it as off limits. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a similar restriction on serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it puts the teacher in the position of marking work they have been paid to prepare. A tutor from outside the school gives your daughter a second opinion on the same work, which is more useful anyway.

faqs.question: How much does a female Diploma tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The gender requirement should not change the rate; the level and the format do. Market bands published in 2026 put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit in Dubai at AED 180 to 500 once travel is built in, and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium named tutors are published at AED 500 to 650 and above. Those are market figures from published rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, not our price list.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 12 and below target in Maths AA. Where does tutoring start?
faqs.answer: With her last two pieces of marked work rather than with a topic. The first session is a diagnostic: the tutor marks what she has already written against the current markscheme and identifies whether marks are going to content gaps, method presentation, calculator technique or question reading. Those four problems have different fixes and only one of them is solved by re-teaching content. You get a written note naming the two or three specific habits costing marks, which also gives you something concrete to compare against at session six.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Mathematics internal assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the statistics or calculus a chosen topic needs, explain what each published criterion is asking for, and ask the questions the criteria ask: is the aim focused, is the mathematics at the right level, has the limitation been acknowledged. What a tutor cannot do is supply sentences, insert sources or rework a section into its final state. Your daughter leaves with decisions to make rather than a corrected document. The school supervisor and subject teacher remain the official process, and they sign the declarations.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Middle Years Programme as well as the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the same stated requirement carries across both, which matters for households with siblings in different year groups. Middle Years work is mostly criterion literacy: the four lettered criteria per subject, what a 7-8 band answer looks like compared with a 5-6, and how a criterion mark becomes a reported grade. Year 11 is the most valuable year to start, because that is when timed-writing stamina can be built before the Diploma demands it rather than during the first term of Year 12.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share a tutor on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is what makes it affordable. Two consecutive 45 or 60-minute sessions with the same tutor cost two sessions rather than two sessions plus a second travel charge, and there is no dead half hour while someone drives across the emirate between them. Each child gets a separate written note. Where the subject allows it the same tutor can cover a Middle Years student and a Diploma student; where it does not, two tutors can be booked back to back in the same window.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Dubai families ask for it. School days shorten during Ramadan, afternoons are quieter and the useful study window moves to after Iftar. Sessions commonly shift to a later evening slot on weekdays and to late morning on weekend days. It is worth booking the change two weeks ahead rather than week by week, because the post-Iftar window is the most contested slot in the calendar and a fixed time is easier to protect than a flexible one.

faqs.question: How long does it take to be matched after we ask?
faqs.answer: For common Diploma subjects at either level, usually a few days, with a choice of two or three tutors who meet the stated requirement. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education or UAE Social Studies, about a week in term time. For Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects, longer, because the specialist pool is small before any filter is applied. If a requirement cannot be met this term we say so before a lesson is booked, including when the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/female-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the diagnostic, then judge the match
dubai/female-ib-tutor.closingBody: State the requirement, name the subjects and levels, and take the free 45-minute diagnostic lesson, which takes no card details and carries no obligation to continue. The tutor marks something your daughter has already written and sends a note naming the two or three habits costing marks. That note is the thing to judge: it tells you whether the person on the call can read a Diploma script, which is the part a gender filter cannot tell you. If the match is wrong at any point, ask for a different tutor and say nothing more than that.

Where a female tutor has been stated as a requirement, the shortlist is filtered on that first and then matched to the specific syllabus code the school has entered.

intro.heading: The two years that set the sixth-form conversation, and why the board matters more than the brand
paragraphs: IGCSE is a two-year course that behaves like a one-year course. Year 10 is content delivery, usually at a pace that assumes everything lands first time, and Year 11 is the year in which papers, coursework and the January mock arrive together. By the time a family in Al Barsha or Al Furjan starts looking for a tutor, there is normally a trigger: a mock grade two bands below the target, a science that has stopped making sense, or an English Language mark that will not move however much the student revises.

A female-tutor requirement at this stage is usually about the student rather than the subject. Fifteen and sixteen-year-olds who have gone quiet in class do not volunteer their confusion to a stranger, and families often judge, reasonably, that their daughter will say the words I do not understand sooner to a woman. Some requests are subject-specific instead: Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education, or the human biology topics that sit inside IGCSE Biology. Both versions of the request are recorded the same way, as a filter applied before matching.

The thing most families have not checked is the board. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award an International GCSE and Dubai schools use both, sometimes mixing boards between departments in the same school. The syllabus codes differ, the tiering differs, the practical assessment differs and the exam timetables are published separately. A tutor who prepares a student for Cambridge Physics 0625 Paper 6 when the school entered Pearson 4PH1 has wasted a term on the wrong paper format, and nobody notices until the mock.

Dubai makes this more likely than most markets, because the school population is so varied. KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 students in the emirate in 2024-25, running 17 curricula between them, and British-curriculum schools are the largest group by enrolment. That is a lot of schools making independent departmental decisions about boards and tiers, which is exactly why the first question in a diagnostic lesson is which syllabus code is on the entry, not which topic is hard.

The rest of this page is the detail a Year 11 family needs: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel in a table, what the Core and Extended decision does to the grade ceiling, how science practicals are assessed when tuition is online, the entry deadlines that sit months before the papers, the five-subject rule for Ministry of Education equivalency, and what IGCSE tutoring actually costs in this market. Each of those is a question a Dubai parent can act on within a week, and most of them are questions the pages currently ranking for this search leave unanswered. Where a figure appears below it carries its source and its date, because a rate or a deadline without either is not information a family can plan around.

dubai/female-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Most Dubai families who ask this question are looking at two or three years of the same British track rather than one exam series. These are the stages the request spans and what support looks like at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject qualification graded A* to G or 9 to 1 depending on the syllabus, with most subjects assessed entirely by written papers sat in a June or November series. Several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, which sets a grade ceiling at the point of entry rather than at the point of marking. Syllabus codes identify the exact course: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre worldwide to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Dubai schools sit in a Gulf zone, so a revision plan copied from a United Kingdom timetable can put a paper on the wrong day. Always work from the timetable the school's exams officer issues.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Parallel qualification with its own specifications and codes: 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Papers are available in a May/June series and a November series. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher, and the science specifications assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical examination.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson published results to centres for the June 2026 series on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so a Dubai family should work from the live timetable on the Pearson qualifications site rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. These tests are diagnostic rather than qualifications, and their value to a family is that they show whether a student is on track for Extended entry in Year 10 while there is still time to do something about it. Weak algebra and weak written structure are the two findings that matter most.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use Checkpoint results and internal data to set Core and Extended groups, sometimes as early as the end of Year 9. Families who want their daughter on the Extended track in Mathematics or the sciences are far better off starting support in Year 9 than appealing a set decision in Year 10, because the set determines which textbook and which papers she is taught from all year.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The most common route out of IGCSE in Dubai British-curriculum schools, alongside the IB Diploma. Entry to an A Level course normally requires a grade 6, 7 or A at IGCSE in the same or a related subject, which is why the Year 11 grade is a gate rather than a summary. International A Level examinations run in June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, in addition to five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE at grade E or 3 or above. That is the published British-track rule and it is worth reading before subject choices are locked at the end of Year 11.

dubai/female-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Dubai families request most, with the syllabus codes and the specific place marks are lost in each. Codes matter: a tutor should confirm yours against the school's entry in the first session.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge · 4MA1 Pearson)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Marks are lost to method presentation and to the non-calculator paper. Students who can solve a problem on paper with a calculator often cannot do it without one, and the tiering decision made in Year 10 caps the grade regardless of how well the paper goes. Algebraic manipulation is the single topic that makes the most other topics tractable.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge · 4PH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are where Extended candidates lose most marks, usually because circuit reasoning was never secured in Year 9. Cambridge assesses practical skills in a separate paper, either the practical test or the alternative to practical; Pearson assesses them inside the written papers. Knowing which applies decides what revision looks like.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge · 4CH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Moles and ionic equations separate grades. The commonest failure is a correct calculation written without units or to the wrong number of significant figures. Qualitative analysis questions reward memorised observations: a precipitate colour, a gas test result, a flame colour. Those are learnable marks that students repeatedly leave on the table.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge · 4BI1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Content volume plus strict terminology. Markschemes written for one term will not accept a near-synonym, so a student who writes breathing for respiration loses the mark they earned. Human physiology topics, including reproduction and hormones, are the part of the specification families most often ask a female tutor to cover with a daughter.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 Cambridge · 4EA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: The grade is decided by response structure, not by vocabulary. Directed writing tasks are marked on whether the student has written in the required form and register for the stated audience, and a well-written piece in the wrong form caps low. Reading questions reward precise selection from the passage rather than general comment.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Taken by a large share of Dubai candidates and often under-prepared because students assume fluency is enough. Marks sit in exercise-specific technique: note-making to the required headings, summary within the word limit, and a speaking component assessed against published criteria rather than on confidence.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both reward applying a concept to the stimulus material on the paper. Generic answers about marketing or supply and demand score almost nothing. Data-response questions in Economics require reading a table or diagram accurately before writing, and that reading step is where most lost marks originate rather than in the theory.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Dubai students often sit Arabic A as an IGCSE while also taking the school's mandatory Arabic provision. Students who speak a dialect at home read fluently and write below their level in Standard Arabic. This is the subject in which a female tutor is most frequently requested outright rather than as a general preference.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and the bridge that makes the first term of Year 12 survivable. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive with no scaffolding, and students who were comfortable in 0580 are often surprised by the step in abstraction rather than in difficulty.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: Two option subjects where lost marks are highly specific. Computer Science rewards pseudocode written to the published convention and trace tables completed row by row. Accounting rewards format: a correctly laid out statement earns marks that a correct answer in the wrong format does not.

dubai/female-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The tutor pool is not limited by your address, but the Dubai school run and the activity timetable decide which slots exist. These are the communities this request most often comes from and the practical window in each.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Dense cluster of British-curriculum schools within the community itself, so commutes are short and a 16:30 start is realistic four days a week. Year 11 families here often book two subjects on the same evening rather than spreading them across the week.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Apartment community on the Sharjah border where the school run can run long in both directions. Later starts from 18:00 work better, and families frequently move to weekend mornings during the January mock season to protect weekday evenings for homework.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Large expatriate apartment population with children spread across schools in Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and the Marina corridor. Study space rather than travel is the constraint, so a fixed corner of the flat and headphones matter more than the start time.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Growing villa and townhouse catchment with several British schools nearby. Two-subject weeks are common in Year 11: one science and one Mathematics session, deliberately on different evenings so the student is not asked to concentrate twice in one night.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: Newer community with a long commute to the established school corridors, so weekday sessions rarely start before 17:45. Half-term and holiday weeks are used heavily here for past-paper work, because a clear morning is worth more than three tired evenings.

regions.name: Remraam
regions.note: Quieter Dubailand community where bus routes arrive late in the afternoon. Weekend morning slots are the easiest to keep across a whole term, and families often pair a Saturday session with marked homework returned mid-week.

regions.name: International City
regions.note: Mixed population with students at schools in Al Warqa, Mirdif and Academic City. English as a Second Language and Mathematics are the two most requested subjects, and the female-tutor requirement here is most often stated for the whole subject list rather than per subject.

dubai/female-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats carry nearly all Year 10 and Year 11 work. Each runs online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard, and each can be booked with a stated female-tutor requirement.

modes.title: Single-subject weekly sessions
modes.description: One 60-minute session a week in one subject, through the term, with the same tutor. This is the format for a subject that is one or two grades below target rather than in trouble, and it works because the tutor sees the same student's written work accumulate week by week.

modes.title: Two subjects on separate evenings
modes.description: The standard Year 11 arrangement in Dubai: Mathematics on one evening and a science on another, deliberately not stacked on the same night. Two tutors rather than one generalist, because IGCSE marks are lost in subject-specific technique and a generalist cannot diagnose a Chemistry observation question.

modes.title: Mock-season and past-paper blocks
modes.description: Short intensive blocks in the weeks before the January mocks or the live series, spent entirely on timed papers and markscheme work. The student sits a paper, the tutor marks it to the published markscheme and the session is about the marks that were available rather than the topic.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the check to make before booking anything
paragraphs: Ask the school which board and which syllabus code your daughter has been entered for in each subject. Both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel award an International GCSE, Dubai schools use both, and some schools run different boards in different departments, so the answer can be Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for Mathematics in the same Year 11. The entry code is the only reliable identifier, and the exams officer has it.

The practical consequences are large. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended with different papers for each; Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher and leaves most other subjects untiered. Cambridge assesses science practical skills in a dedicated paper, either the practical test or the alternative to practical; Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. Grading scales differ by syllabus too, with some reporting A* to G and others 9 to 1.

Timetables are published separately and behave differently. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a timetable per zone, and states that it is essential to use the correct version because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series and then issues a final version. A revision plan should be built from the document the school's exams officer gives you, not from a date copied off a website. Ask for it as a file rather than a summary, because a paper moved by a day changes which evening the last session before it should sit on.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects, the entry decides the highest grade available. A Core entry caps the outcome, typically at grade C or 5, while an Extended entry reaches A* or 9. This is not a marking adjustment made afterwards; it is a property of the papers sat. A student placed on Core in Year 10 who then works hard all year cannot produce an A at the end of it, which is why the set decision deserves a conversation with the school rather than quiet acceptance.

Schools place students on evidence, usually Checkpoint results and internal assessment, and the placement is often made at the end of Year 9 or early in Year 10. It is reversible in some schools and not in others, and the window is usually narrow. If your daughter is close to the boundary, the useful question to the department is what evidence they would need to see to move her, and by what date. That is an answerable question; are you sure is not.

For a family whose daughter is already on Core and whose target is a sixth-form course requiring a 6, the honest answer may be that the tier, not the teaching, is the binding constraint. That is worth hearing early. Tutoring can still raise the grade inside the tier, secure the Core content properly and build the algebra or written structure that the next stage needs, but a tutor telling you an A is available from a Core entry is either confused or selling.

sections.heading: How science practicals are handled when tuition is online
paragraphs: Parents ask this reasonably: if the lessons are online, how does a student prepare for a practical paper. The answer is that neither board awards marks for a performance in front of a tutor. Cambridge assesses practical skills either in a practical test sat at the school or in the alternative to practical paper, which is a written paper about experiments. Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. In both cases the examined skill is reading, designing and evaluating experiments on paper.

That makes the practical component highly coachable online and, in fact, easier to coach than in a laboratory. The recurring marks are the same every series: identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables, improving a method so results are repeatable, reading a scale correctly, plotting a line of best fit, calculating a gradient with units, and explaining an anomaly. A tutor can put a method on the shared screen, ask what is wrong with it, and mark the answer against the markscheme.

Where school practical work still matters, and it does, is in building the physical intuition that makes those written answers sensible. A student who has handled a burette knows why a reading is taken at the meniscus. The division of labour is straightforward: the school does the apparatus, the tutor does the paper. A provider claiming to deliver the practical examination itself has misread the specification. What a tutor can add is the habit of reading every method for its weakest control before answering, which is the question examiners keep asking in different clothes.
bullets: Cambridge: practical test or alternative to practical, depending on the entry
Pearson: practical understanding assessed within the written papers

sections.heading: Where the female-tutor request attaches in the IGCSE specification
paragraphs: Some of these requests are general and some are precise, and it helps the match to know which you are making. The general version is about the relationship: a quiet fifteen-year-old, a long one-to-one course, and a parent who would rather the adult in that relationship be a woman. The precise version attaches to specific content, and in IGCSE the content it attaches to is predictable: human reproduction and hormones in Biology, Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education, and sometimes Physical Education theory.

Stating which version you mean has a practical payoff. A family that needs a female Biology tutor for the human physiology unit and has no preference for Mathematics gets a wider pool for Mathematics and a faster match overall. A family that wants a female tutor across five subjects should expect the match to take longer in the scarcer subjects, and should know that before the first lesson rather than during the third week.

The one thing the requirement should not do is lower the subject bar. A Biology tutor still has to know whether the entry is 0610 or 4BI1, which paper assesses practical skills and how the markscheme treats a near-synonym. If the only available tutor who meets the requirement is a generalist who teaches up to Core, the right answer is to say so and wait, not to fill the slot and hope the family does not notice until the mock. Waiting a week for the right specialist is a smaller cost than a term spent at the wrong level, and it is a choice the family should get to make with the facts in front of them.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the paper, and nobody tells you twice
paragraphs: This is the gap no competitor page in the Dubai market fills, and it costs families real money. Entries close long before the examinations are sat, and they are made by the school, which means a student who decides in February to add a subject, move tier or sit a retake may already be too late for that series. The published dates for a Cambridge series make the scale of the lead time obvious.

For the Cambridge March 2027 series, the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results are released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Read that sequence backwards: the decision about what a student sits is made more than two months before the first paper, while Year 11 is still in the middle of its content teaching.

Pearson works to its own calendar. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. The practical rule for a Dubai family is to ask the exams officer for three dates in writing at the start of Year 11: the entry deadline, the mock window and the first paper. Everything else in the plan hangs off those.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the five-subject rule, published correctly
paragraphs: Families applying to UAE universities need the Ministry of Education equivalency, and the British-track requirement is specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is worth repeating because it is routinely got wrong. One page currently ranking for Dubai tutoring queries tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count rather than added to it. A Year 11 family making option decisions on the strength of the wrong number may enter an extra subject they did not need, which costs an entry fee and a term of revision.

Two things we will not do on this page. We will not publish an IB points threshold for equivalency, because the figure has not been read on a Ministry source and the British-track numbers are the only ones verified. And we will not describe equivalency as something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees. It is an application a family makes to the Ministry, and the authority's own channel is the place to verify the current requirement before subjects are locked. Nor does tutoring become a requirement for equivalency: the process is paperwork about grades already earned, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in Dubai, by subject count rather than by hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are easy to compare and tell you very little, because the real variable in Year 11 is how many subjects you are supporting and for how long. Two subjects for two terms is a different financial decision from one subject for six weeks before the mock, and the market publishes almost nothing that helps a parent model it. Three of the six pages currently ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars.

The bands below come from published 2026 rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, and they are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

Use the table to decide where the money does most work. For a subject one grade below target, a weekly session across one term usually beats a block of intensive sessions in April, because the gap is habit rather than content. For a subject two or more grades below, the honest plan starts earlier and costs more. And for a subject where the tier itself is the cap, the most valuable conversation is with the school about the tier, which costs nothing.

sections.heading: Scheduling, coverage and the answer when the match cannot be made
paragraphs: Dubai school buses return between roughly 15:15 and 16:30 depending on the community, which rules out most weekday sessions before 16:30 and makes the 18:00 to 20:00 window the most contested in the emirate. Year 11 families with two subjects are better off placing them on different evenings than stacking them, because the second hour of concentration on a school night produces notes rather than learning. Weekend mornings are the most reliably protectable slot across a full term.

Term rhythm matters as much as the weekly slot. The January mock window and the coursework deadlines are the two pressure points, and they fall on different weeks in different Dubai schools, which is why the plan should be built from your school's calendar rather than a generic one. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar timings on weekdays and to late morning on weekend days, and it is worth booking that shift a fortnight ahead because the post-Iftar window fills quickly.

On coverage, the honest position is the one stated in the table above for the Diploma and it applies here too: Mathematics, the three sciences, English and the main humanities are matched quickly, English as a Second Language and Arabic within about a week in term time, and the scarcer option subjects take longer. If a stated requirement cannot be met this term, you are told before a lesson is booked, including where the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Get the entry codes from the school
process.description: Ask the exams officer for the board and syllabus code per subject, the tier where the subject is tiered, and the entry deadline for the series your daughter is sitting. Three lines in an email. Everything a tutor does afterwards depends on those codes being right, and assuming them is how a term gets spent on the wrong paper format.

process.title: State the requirement and its scope
process.description: Say that a female tutor is required and whether that applies to every subject or only to some, such as Biology human physiology, Arabic as a first language or Islamic Education. Scoping it per subject widens the pool for the subjects where you have no preference and usually produces a faster overall match.

process.title: Free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: One lesson, no card details taken, no obligation. The tutor marks a past-paper answer or a recent piece of marked work against the markscheme for the correct syllabus code and reports where the marks went: content, technique, question reading or presentation. Those four problems have four different fixes.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot and the term target
process.description: Choose a time that survives the school bus and activities, and name the target in the terms the paper uses: a grade, a tier, a specific paper. The plan then has something to be measured against at the halfway point rather than a general sense of whether sessions are going well.

process.title: Switch to timed papers before the series
process.description: In the final six to eight weeks the format changes: the student sits a paper under timed conditions, the tutor marks it to the published markscheme, and the session covers only the marks that were available. Dates come from the school's zone or series timetable, not from a date copied off a website.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the board, not to the subject name
whyPoints.description: The tutor is matched to the syllabus code your school entered, so Cambridge 0625 preparation is not sold to a Pearson 4PH1 candidate. Boards differ on tiering, practical assessment and timetables, and a mismatch is invisible until the mock, which is the worst possible moment to discover it.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation happens early
whyPoints.description: If a Core entry caps the grade below your target, you hear that in the first session rather than in May. Tutoring can raise a grade inside a tier and build the content the next stage needs, but it cannot lift a ceiling set at entry, and a tutor who implies otherwise is not worth the fee.

whyPoints.title: The requirement is a filter, not a footnote
whyPoints.description: A stated preference for a female tutor is applied before subject matching, so the shortlist already satisfies it. Scope it per subject and the match is usually faster, because the subjects where you have no preference are drawn from the full specialist pool.

whyPoints.title: Practical papers taught as written papers
whyPoints.description: Neither board awards practical marks for a performance in front of a tutor. The examined skills are variables, method improvement, graph work, gradients and anomalies, all of which are written skills. Online delivery is a good fit for that, and the school keeps the apparatus.

whyPoints.title: Entry deadlines published, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Final entries for the Cambridge March 2027 series are due on 27 November 2026 for papers sat from 3 February 2027. Reading the calendar backwards is how a family avoids discovering in March that a retake or a tier change was decided months earlier.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A competitor page currently publishes six. Getting the number right saves a family an entry fee and a term.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my daughter sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the board and the syllabus code per subject, in writing. The code is the reliable identifier: 0625 is Cambridge Physics, 4PH1 is Pearson Physics, and they are different courses with different papers. Dubai schools sometimes run different boards in different departments, so the answer can be Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for Mathematics in the same Year 11. Any tutoring plan built before you have those codes is a guess, and a guess here costs a term of preparing for the wrong paper format.

faqs.question: Can a female tutor cover the human biology topics in IGCSE Biology?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the two or three places the request is most often made specifically rather than generally. Human reproduction, hormones and coordination sit inside both the Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1 specifications, and families frequently want a woman teaching that unit to a daughter while having no preference for other subjects. Scoping the requirement that way is useful: it keeps the pool wide for Mathematics and the other sciences, which usually means a faster match overall and a stronger specialist in each subject.

faqs.question: Does a Core entry stop my daughter getting a grade 7 or an A?
faqs.answer: In a tiered Cambridge subject, yes. The tier is a property of the papers sat, not an adjustment made at marking, so a Core entry caps the outcome at around grade C or 5 while Extended reaches A* or 9. If the target is a sixth-form course needing a 6 or better, the tier is the binding constraint and the most valuable conversation is with the department: what evidence would they need to move her, and by what date. Tutoring can still raise the grade inside the tier and build the content the next stage requires.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals prepared for if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The examined practical skills are written skills. Cambridge assesses them in a practical test sat at the school or in the alternative to practical paper; Pearson assesses practical understanding inside the written papers. Either way the marks go to identifying variables, improving a method for repeatability, reading scales, plotting lines of best fit, calculating gradients with units and explaining anomalies. All of that is coachable on a shared screen with a method and a markscheme. The school supplies the apparatus and the laboratory experience that makes those written answers sensible.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE entries close for a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Long before the papers. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due on 27 November 2026 for an examination period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027. Pearson works to its own published calendar for the May/June and November series. Entries are made by the school, so a decision in February to add a subject, change tier or sit a retake may already be too late. Ask the exams officer for the entry deadline at the start of Year 11.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish more than one exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Because every centre worldwide is allocated to one of six administrative zones and each zone has its own timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Dubai schools sit in a Gulf zone, so a revision calendar built from a United Kingdom timetable found online can place a paper on the wrong day. Work only from the timetable your school's exams officer issues.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my daughter need for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One page currently ranking for Dubai tutoring queries states six subjects, which is wrong and could cost a family an unnecessary entry. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before options are locked.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 market rates put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Budget online tutoring starts lower, around AED 45 to 150. In-home sessions in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 once travel is built into the rate. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey puts monthly spend for one weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures, not our price list.

faqs.question: Is one subject a week enough in Year 11, or should we book two?
faqs.answer: It depends on the gap rather than the year. A subject one grade below target is usually a habit problem, which a weekly session across a term fixes well. A subject two or more grades below needs either an earlier start or more sessions. Where two subjects are supported, place them on different evenings: the second hour of concentration on a school night produces notes rather than learning. Most Dubai Year 11 families settle on two subjects on separate evenings, with a third added only during the mock season.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my daughter's past papers to the real markscheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most useful thing a tutor does in the final term. The student sits a paper under timed conditions, the tutor marks it against the published markscheme for the correct syllabus code, and the session covers the marks that were available rather than the topic in general. What a tutor should not do is circulate board materials: official papers, markschemes and grade-boundary tables are referenced on the board's own site and worked through there, not redistributed as downloads.

faqs.question: My daughter is predicted a 5 in Mathematics and needs a 7. Is that realistic in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the first session should tell you honestly. Three questions decide it: is she entered on the Extended or Higher tier, how much of the gap is algebraic manipulation rather than topic knowledge, and how far through the specification her school has taught. A two-grade move from a secure Extended base with algebra as the main weakness is a realistic term's work. The same move from a Core entry is not available at all, and no amount of tutoring changes that, so the tier is the first thing to check.

faqs.question: Do you tutor English as a Second Language as well as First Language English?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are genuinely different courses. First Language English is assessed on response structure, register and precise selection from the passage. English as a Second Language rewards exercise-specific technique: note-making to the given headings, summary inside the word limit and a speaking component marked against published criteria. Dubai has a large cohort sitting the second-language syllabus who are fluent speakers and under-prepared for the paper format, which is a solvable problem and usually a fast one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with coursework without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills a task assesses, explain what the published criteria ask for, and question whether a draft actually answers the task. A tutor cannot supply sentences, insert sources or rework a section into its final state. The student makes every change. The school remains the official process and signs any declaration of authenticity required by the board. Treat an offer to produce assessed work as a warning about everything else on that provider's page, because the consequence of being caught falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Can sessions be rearranged around the January mock window?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Dubai families restructure around it rather than adding to it. In the three weeks before mocks the sessions usually switch from content teaching to timed papers with marked returns, and some families pause one subject to double up on another. Mock windows differ by school, so the plan is built from your own school's calendar. Rescheduling a single session is routine; moving a whole slot is easier to do with a fortnight's notice, because the 18:00 to 20:00 window fills quickly in January.

faqs.question: How quickly can a female IGCSE tutor be matched in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and the main humanities, usually within a few days, with a choice of tutors who meet the stated requirement and the right syllabus code. For English as a Second Language and Arabic as a first language, about a week in term time. Scarcer option subjects such as Accounting or Computer Science take longer. If the requirement cannot be met this term we say so before a lesson is booked, including where the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/female-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Two emails decide how useful the next term is. One to the school's exams officer asking for the board, syllabus code, tier and entry deadline per subject. One to us stating the subjects, the target grades and whether the female-tutor requirement applies to all of them or only to some. Then take the free 45-minute diagnostic lesson, which takes no card details and carries no obligation: the tutor marks a real piece of work to the markscheme for the correct code and tells you where the marks went. That note is what the decision should rest on.

intro.heading: The part of the course a school cannot teach, and the market that exploits it
paragraphs: Green Community sits inside Dubai Investments Park: low-rise apartments, townhouses and villas arranged around planted courtyards, with an IB continuum school inside the development and the rest of the Dubai Investments Park school cluster a few minutes away. The households here are long-stay rather than transient, which means the enquiries we get are about whole courses rather than about next week's test, and more of them are about coursework than about lessons.

That reflects how the programmes are built. An IB Diploma student produces an internal assessment in every subject, a four-thousand-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and a CAS record. An MYP student finishes with a Personal Project assessed on their own process journal. Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework components. In each case the school teaches the surrounding content and then supervises work the student must produce independently.

Supervision is deliberately limited. Schools cap the number of formal meetings for an Extended Essay, require a process journal for a Personal Project, and ask the supervisor to confirm the submitted work is the candidate's own. The design is sound. The side effect is a gap that a parent can see and cannot fill: a teenager with four unfinished components, a supervisor they are allowed to meet three times, and six weeks to go.

Into that gap has grown a market. The research behind these pages found a Dubai site advertising finished internal assessments at AED 3,750 each. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach with a student's diploma attached to it, and the person who carries the consequence is the sixteen-year-old whose name is on the submission, not the operator who took the payment. Several ranking pages in this search cluster sit uncomfortably close to that line in how they describe coursework support.

It is worth being clear about why a tutoring company would write this page at all, since the obvious commercial move is to say nothing and let a parent assume the most generous interpretation. The reason is that the alternative is worse for everyone involved. A family who buys the wrong kind of help exposes their own child to a process that can end a diploma, and a provider who allows the ambiguity to stand is relying on that confusion to make a sale. Stating the boundary in public costs us a small number of enquiries and removes the argument from the point at which it usually happens, which is late at night, two days before a deadline, with a frightened teenager in the room.

So this page is about the boundary rather than about subjects. It covers what the IB treats as malpractice, how authentication actually works in a school, where generative AI and translation tools sit, exactly what a tutor may and may not do, how to recognise an operator selling the other thing, what honest supervision costs in this market, and the referencing mechanics students get wrong without any dishonest intent at all. Every lesson described runs online, one-to-one. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

dubai/green-community.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested here, described by the independent component each one carries and where its marks are decided.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The individual investigation needs a measurable variable, a repeatable method and real statistical treatment. Most lost marks sit in analysis and evaluation rather than in the biology, and a student who collects data before defining the hypothesis has already lost them.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Investigations fail on scope more than on technique: a question broad enough to be interesting is usually too broad to measure with school equipment. Energetics, kinetics and organic mechanisms carry Higher Level difficulty in the papers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation and error analysis are examinable, rarely taught deliberately and heavily rewarded in the investigation. At IGCSE the recurring loss is circuit reasoning when conditions change rather than recall of definitions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration must contain genuine mathematics rather than the application of a formula, and choosing a topic that permits real manipulation is most of the work. In the papers, reasoning marks dominate and unjustified answers score a fraction of what is available.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use. Explorations here commonly repeat a textbook procedure instead of interpreting a result, and papers lose marks where a test is presented without its hypothesis, assumptions or a conclusion in context.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper one is unseen guided analysis, so rereading set texts does not prepare it. The individual oral requires a global issue and two extracts prepared months ahead, and Higher Level adds an essay that must argue rather than summarise.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is where referencing and source evaluation are assessed most directly, and where unintentional plagiarism most often occurs. Paper marks follow command terms and the discipline of using evidence rather than narrating it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The internal assessment depends on an organisation that will supply usable figures, and that choice has to be made early. In the papers, a framework named but not applied to the stimulus loses most of the available analysis credit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects with a written commentary. Marks go to precise claim and counterclaim structure, which is coachable, and the component fails most often because it is left until the term everything else is due.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Translation tools make this subject the one where the honesty line is crossed most casually and most often.

sections.heading: Where the integrity question actually comes from
paragraphs: Almost nobody sets out to cheat. The breaches that get students into trouble in Dubai schools are mostly produced by pressure and poor technique rather than by intent. A student with four unfinished components and three weeks left makes a decision at midnight that they would not make in September. A student taking notes without separating quotation from paraphrase ends up with sentences in a draft that are not theirs and cannot say where they came from. A student whose Arabic is weak runs a paragraph through a translation tool and submits it without thinking of it as dishonest.

The structural cause is the one described at the top of this page. The independent components are substantial, the supervision is deliberately rationed, and the deadlines cluster. A parent who understands that is in a position to intervene early, which is the only intervention that works. A parent who discovers it in the final fortnight is choosing between a poor submission and a dishonest one, and a market exists to make the second option easy.

The second cause is that nobody states the rules plainly to the student. Schools publish academic-honesty policies, and most students have signed one without reading it. They know plagiarism is wrong. They are far less clear about collusion, about submitting the same work twice, about whether a parent may proofread, about whether a tutor may suggest a structure, and about where a language tool sits. Those are the grey areas where real cases arise.

This page sets the boundary out explicitly because that is more useful than a reassurance. A student who knows exactly what is permitted works more confidently, asks better questions of their supervisor, and does not reach the midnight decision in the first place. It also makes a tutor's role clearer: the help that is legitimate is substantial, and knowing its shape is what stops a family buying the wrong thing in a panic.

sections.heading: What counts as malpractice, in the categories schools actually use
paragraphs: School and board policies tend to describe four or five categories rather than one. Plagiarism is representing someone else's words, ideas or data as your own, including from a website, a textbook, a sibling's old work or a generative tool, and including when it is accidental. Collusion is supporting another candidate in presenting work that is not their own, which catches the student who shares a completed answer as well as the one who copies it.

Duplication of work means submitting the same piece for two different assessments, which students do innocently when a topic suits both an essay and an investigation. Fabrication of data covers inventing results or adjusting them to fit a hypothesis, which happens quietly in science investigations where an experiment went wrong and the deadline did not move. Misconduct during an examination covers unauthorised material and disruption, and is a separate matter handled by invigilation rules.

The consequences are set by the board and the school rather than by any tutor, and they are proportionate to the component. A finding against a Diploma component can mean no grade awarded in that subject, which can mean no diploma. The point worth making to a sixteen-year-old is not the severity but the asymmetry: the operator who sold the work faces nothing, and the candidate faces the outcome.

What protects a student is evidence of process. A dated process journal, draft versions saved as they were written, notes that record where each source came from, and a supervisor who has seen the work develop. Students who keep those things are rarely in difficulty even when a similarity report flags something, because they can show how the work came to exist. Students who produce a finished document from nowhere have no defence available to them.
