dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic runs through every IB programme a Dubai school offers, and it changes character at each transition. The four blocks below set out what Arabic looks like in each one and what that means for a family deciding whether to buy tuition hours now or in two years.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic in the Diploma sits in Group 1 or Group 2. Group 2 holds Arabic ab initio at Standard Level and Arabic B at Standard and Higher Level; Group 1 holds Arabic A: Language and Literature and, in a handful of Dubai schools, Arabic A: Literature. The assessment split is published by the IB per course, and under the current language syllabuses a Language B candidate faces a writing paper, a combined listening and reading paper and an individual oral, while a Language A candidate faces guided textual analysis, a comparative essay and an oral on a global issue.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Group 1 Arabic cohort is small at most schools, which has two consequences for a parent. Class teaching is often shared across SL and HL in one room, and a weak reader is harder to spot early. Tuition hours at this level are the most expensive Arabic hours in the market, roughly AED 250 to AED 450 online, because the person has to be comfortable with literary criticism in Arabic and able to explain it in the language of the school's report card.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Arabic is organised as Language Acquisition in six phases, or as Language and Literature for students working at first-language standard. Phases are not year groups: a student can sit in Phase 2 for three years if nothing changes. Assessment runs on four criteria, with comprehension of spoken and written text weighted alongside production, so a student who speaks confidently but cannot handle an unseen written passage will see criterion marks that look inconsistent to a parent.
programmes.countryNote: Phase placement is where Dubai families lose the most ground. A child placed in Phase 2 in Year 7 because the family speaks Arabic at home, then never moved, arrives in DP1 with a spoken register and no academic reading. MYP Arabic tuition in Dubai runs roughly AED 120 to AED 200 an hour online, which is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to fix a problem that costs three times as much to fix in Year 12.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP Arabic is taught as an additional language for most non-Arab students and as a first language where the school streams for it. There is no external assessment, which makes progress hard for a parent to read. The useful markers at this stage are script fluency, whether the child can decode unfamiliar words rather than recognise memorised ones, and whether listening comprehension is keeping pace with spoken production.
programmes.countryNote: Because KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, a Dubai primary child may be streamed on arrival into a group that does not match their actual level, particularly if the household language is Arabic but the previous school was English-medium. A short block of tuition at PYP rates, around AED 120 to AED 180 an hour, is usually spent on evidence for a re-streaming conversation rather than on content.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the IB
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: Separate from the IB course, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and the guidance advises no mandatory lesson should be shorter than twenty-five minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited.
programmes.countryNote: This matters to a Dubai parent in one concrete way: a tutor cannot invent a syllabus for these lessons. Support has to work from what the school is teaching, because the content is set and the school is accountable for it. We treat mandatory-subject tuition as exam-technique and comprehension work on the school's own material, and we say so before the first session rather than after it.

dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic tuition is only useful when it is matched to the exact course. These are the Arabic and Arabic-adjacent courses Dubai students bring to us, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks usually leak away.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: For students with little or no prior Arabic. Three prescribed themes, controlled writing tasks and a listening paper built on slow, clearly enunciated audio. Marks are lost on script accuracy, on confusing the sun and moon letters in reading aloud, and on writing that answers the prompt in the wrong text type.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Writing, a combined listening and reading paper and an individual oral based on a visual stimulus. The listening component is the single biggest source of unexpected low marks for Dubai students, because classroom Arabic is slower and more forgiving than examination audio.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of an unseen literary or non-literary text, a comparative essay on studied works and an oral on a global issue. Fluent speakers lose marks here for describing a text rather than analysing how it produces meaning, and for quoting at length without commentary.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Literature
subjects.description: Offered by a smaller set of Dubai schools. Works in translation sit alongside Arabic originals, and the HL essay demands a sustained line of argument over 1,200 to 1,500 words. Tutors here are scarce in the UAE market, which is visible in the rate.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Four assessment criteria covering listening, reading, speaking and writing. The common pattern in Dubai is a strong speaking criterion mark propping up a weak reading mark, which masks the gap until DP entry testing exposes it.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic Language and Literature
subjects.description: For students at first-language standard. Analytical writing about texts, in Arabic, with criteria that reward structure and terminology. This is the natural feeder to Arabic A, and a student who has not written analytically here will find DP1 brutal.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language (KHDA mandatory)
subjects.description: Required of Arab students in Dubai private schools and taught in separate classes from non-Arab groups. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction. Report grades here are a school judgement rather than an external one, which makes them easy for parents to misread.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language (KHDA mandatory)
subjects.description: Required of non-Arab students in Dubai private schools. Weekly time is counted in forty-minute units. Tuition here is about keeping pace with the school's own scheme of work, since additional content needs Ministry of Education permission.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students. KHDA requires separate classes for the two groups and requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval from KHDA to teach these subjects.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Arabic is the primary language of instruction for Arab students; non-Arab students follow Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the curriculum language. Content is fixed, so support is comprehension, vocabulary and structured written answers rather than new material.

subjects.name: Arabic for the Extended Essay
subjects.description: An essay written in Arabic, or about an Arabic text, needs a supervisor who can read the sources. Our role is question framing, source evaluation and feedback on the student's own successive drafts, with the student as sole author throughout.

subjects.name: Arabic oral and interview preparation
subjects.description: Structured rehearsal for the individual oral: stimulus description, unprepared follow-up questions, register control. Recorded so the student hears their own hesitation markers, which is the fastest fix available in oral assessment.

dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.regionsIntro: Arabic demand is not spread evenly across Dubai, and neither is the local supply of specialist teachers. These notes are about what a family in each area is realistically shopping for, and what the local market tends to quote.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: The heaviest concentration of Arabic A demand in the city, from Emirati and Arab expatriate households whose children need literary Arabic rather than conversational. Local in-home quotes here sit at the top of the Dubai band, AED 300 and above, partly because the pool of Language A specialists is small.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Dense with large international schools and with non-Arab families who need ab initio and additional-language support rather than literature. Rates quoted locally are nearer the AED 150 to AED 250 online band, and the common booking is a short Phase 2 to Phase 4 catch-up block.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: Strong Arab-expatriate enrolment, so first-language streams are full and competition for Arabic A tuition hours is real in exam term. Families here are the most likely to be choosing between the school's mandatory Arabic grade and the DP course grade, and to need both explained.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: Apartment living and long commutes make in-home Arabic tuition expensive in practice: a tutor crossing from Deira at 6pm is charging for the car as much as the lesson. This is where the online argument lands hardest, and where ab initio is the dominant request.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Villa communities with crowded after-school schedules. The scheduling constraint is sport, not traffic, so Arabic sessions here usually land at 7.30pm or later, or on a Friday morning. Local in-home quotes include travel into the community and sit high.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: A younger cohort and plenty of families newly arrived mid-year, which produces late ab initio starts and Phase 1 placements in Year 9. Short diagnostic blocks matter more here than long-term weekly hours, because the first question is which course is survivable.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to the university cluster, with a visible population of retake and private candidates who need Arabic for equivalency or admission purposes rather than for a school report. Sessions here are often short, intense and tied to a specific external deadline.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: A growing IB continuum population and a high proportion of students moving between curricula. Arabic phase placement on transfer is the recurring problem, and a two-session diagnostic usually saves a term of misplacement.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
schoolClusters.note: The older Jumeirah-corridor schools carry the largest Arabic A cohorts in Dubai and the most settled first-language streams. Students we support from this cluster most often want literary analysis work and oral rehearsal rather than grammar.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and Dubai Media City
schoolClusters.note: A cluster where IB continuum schools sit beside large British and American schools, so the same neighbourhood produces ab initio beginners and Phase 5 MYP students in the same week. Course identification matters more here than anywhere else in the city.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Dubai Festival City and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: Higher Arab-expatriate enrolment and full first-language streams. Students we support from this cluster typically carry both a mandatory Arabic grade and a DP Group 1 or Group 2 grade, and the two are often moving in different directions.

sections.heading: What an IB Arabic tutor in Dubai actually costs, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Online one-to-one Arabic tuition in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour as of October 2026, and the single biggest determinant is the course rather than the tutor's seniority. Ab initio and MYP phase work sits at the bottom of that band. Arabic B at Higher Level sits in the middle. Arabic A: Language and Literature sits at the top, because the person has to be able to analyse a literary text in Arabic and then explain the analysis in the language of the school report. Nothing else about the booking changes the price as much as that one fact, which is why a quote given before the course is identified is close to meaningless.

Three other variables move the number in Dubai specifically. Format: in-home one-to-one across the city is quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to AED 500 by individual home tutors, and a meaningful part of that premium is travel rather than teaching. Timing: the 4.30pm to 7.30pm window is the one every family wants, so the scarcest tutors price it accordingly, and a 9am Friday slot is routinely cheaper for the same person. Season: demand concentrates in the eight weeks before the May session, and the Arabic A pool in the UAE is small enough that late bookings simply do not get the specialist they wanted at any price.

What does not move the number, despite being sold hard, is package length. A twenty-hour block at a discount is only cheaper if all twenty hours get used, and families who buy before a diagnostic frequently find that six of those hours should have gone to the oral component and fourteen to reading. We quote the market bands here because no competitor in this search result publishes an AED figure at all: three of the six ranked pages show no price, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A parent comparing options in Dubai is comparing dirhams, so the dirham figures belong on the page with the provider named.

sections.heading: Which Arabic course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that determines everything else, and a surprising number of Dubai families cannot answer it with certainty in October of DP1. The school knows, the student half knows, and the parent is often working from a timetable line that just says Arabic. Before buying a single hour, get the course name and level in writing from the school: Arabic ab initio SL, Arabic B SL, Arabic B HL, Arabic A: Language and Literature SL or HL, or Arabic A: Literature. The difference between the second and the fifth of those is not a matter of difficulty. They are different disciplines with different examiners looking for different things.

The routing is partly about prior learning and partly about household language, and the two often disagree. A student from an Arabic-speaking family who attended English-medium schools from Year 1 may speak at near-native level and read at Phase 3 level. Put that student into Arabic A and the oral goes well and the guided textual analysis collapses. Put them into Arabic B HL and the listening paper is trivially easy while the writing task exposes a register problem nobody has ever corrected. Neither placement is wrong in principle; both need to be made with evidence, which means an unseen reading passage and a timed written response, not a conversation.

Switching is possible but it is expensive in hours rather than in fees. A move from Arabic A to Arabic B in DP1 means learning a different set of text types and a different oral format with eighteen months to go. A move from Arabic B HL to SL reduces the reading load but not the listening demand. Our first session on any Arabic booking is a diagnostic for exactly this reason, and if the diagnostic says the school's placement is right, that is a useful hour too: it stops the family from spending a term on the wrong fix.

sections.heading: The Arabic a Dubai school must teach, and the Arabic the IB grades
paragraphs: Dubai is unusual among IB markets because the regulator sets a parallel Arabic requirement. Under KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The guidance counts instructional time in forty-minute lesson units, allows schools to vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes.

Two of KHDA's rules have direct practical consequences for tuition. The first is streaming: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. The second is content: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A tutor who promises a better syllabus for these lessons is describing something a Dubai school cannot accept.

So a family can end up holding two Arabic grades that tell different stories. The mandatory subject grade is a school judgement against a set national curriculum, delivered in Standard Arabic for Arab students and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. The IB grade is an external judgement against a published assessment model. A student can be comfortable in one and in trouble in the other, and the honest answer to which one to tune is usually the one with the external examination attached, because that is the grade that travels. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the relevant approval from KHDA to teach those subjects, which is a credential question worth asking your school directly.

sections.heading: Where Arabic marks actually leak away
paragraphs: In Arabic B and ab initio the loss is concentrated in listening. Classroom Arabic is slower, repeated, and supported by a teacher's face and gesture. Examination audio is none of those things, and a student who has only ever listened to their own teacher will hear the first thirty seconds and then lose the thread. The fix is mechanical rather than clever: listen at full pace from the first tutoring session, pause nothing on the first pass, and build vocabulary from the words that were actually missed instead of from a printed list. Six weeks of that moves a listening mark more reliably than a term of grammar.

In Arabic A the loss is interpretive. A fluent speaker reads the unseen passage, understands every word, and writes a summary. The examiner wanted an account of how the text produces its effect: the choice of register, the structure, the imagery, the implied reader. Fluency is what makes this trap so effective, because the student feels successful while writing the wrong kind of answer. The remedy is a repeated drill on the gap between what a text says and how it says it, with the student's own paragraphs marked against the published criteria rather than against a model answer.

In the oral, across every course, the loss is in the unprepared section. Students rehearse the stimulus description until it is fluent and then fall apart on the examiner's follow-up questions, which are the part that cannot be scripted. The intervention that works is uncomfortable and quick: unprepared questioning from session one, recorded, with the student listening back to their own hesitations. The third variety of loss is pure process, and it costs more marks in Dubai than anyone admits. Mandatory-subject deadlines, school internal assessment dates and the DP timeline collide in DP1, and the student who is behind on a school Arabic project borrows time from DP preparation. Sequencing that calendar is part of what a tutor is for.
bullets: Listening: practise at full examination pace from day one, no pausing on the first pass
Reading: build vocabulary from missed words rather than a generic frequency list
Arabic A: analyse how a text works, never summarise what it says
Oral: rehearse the unprepared questions, not the prepared description

sections.heading: The Diploma Arabic year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody in this search result publishes a calendar, which is strange, because every decision a family makes about Arabic tuition is a decision about timing. The IB's own session dates and results dates are published by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around them; this page deliberately does not restate an IB date it cannot verify. What can be set out is the sequence, counted backwards from the May session that Dubai schools sit, because the sequence is stable even when the dates move.

Working back from the examinations themselves: the final weeks are paper practice at speed, not content. Before that sits the window where the school's predicted grades are formed, and a student whose listening mark is weak should have fixed it before that judgement is made rather than after. Before that sit the internal deadlines for the oral components and for any Group 1 or Group 2 coursework, which in most Dubai schools fall in the first half of DP2. Before that, in DP1, sits the only comfortable window there is for a course change, and the only cheap window for fixing a reading gap carried up from MYP.

The practical consequence is a buying pattern, not a sales pitch. Families who book Arabic support in DP1 buy one hour a week for a long time and spend less in total. Families who book in the February before the examinations buy two or three hours a week for eight weeks, pay a premium for scarce specialists, and get a smaller improvement because the components that respond fastest to tutoring are the ones already assessed. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates in the same household the pattern is documented more precisely: Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, which is a clean illustration of entry deadlines sitting months ahead of the papers.

sections.heading: Online versus in-home Arabic tuition in Dubai, honestly compared
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, so take the comparison below as a comparison of models rather than an advertisement. In-home Arabic tuition is a real and reasonable choice, especially for younger children and for students who need the physical presence of an adult to stay on task. It is quoted in Dubai at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour by Bestimate's rate table, with individual home tutors quoting up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions advertised around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799.

What a Dubai family is actually buying with that premium is proximity, and proximity has a cost that does not appear on the invoice. The tutor who can reach Jumeirah Lake Towers at 6pm on a Tuesday is selected from the people who live near enough to do it, which for Arabic A: Language and Literature may be a pool of a handful across the whole emirate. Travel time also sets the session length: a tutor who has driven forty minutes will not sell a forty-five minute session, so families buy ninety minutes whether or not ninety minutes is the right dose for oral work.

Online, the selection constraint disappears and the scheduling constraint loosens. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, forty-five or sixty or ninety minutes as the work requires, with screen-sharing for annotated text work and recording for oral components. The real trade-offs are worth naming rather than hiding: a younger child needs a parent in earshot for the first few sessions, handwriting practice in Arabic script needs the student to photograph their work, and a weak internet connection ruins a listening exercise faster than anything else. Our position is simply that for a scarce, course-specific skill like Arabic A, choosing the teacher beats choosing the postcode.

sections.heading: What an Arabic tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: This matters more in Arabic than in most subjects, because the language barrier makes it easy for a family to lose sight of who is producing the words. The IB's academic honesty rules make the student the sole author of every assessed piece, and a tutor who supplies sentences for an oral script, corrects a draft into fluency the student cannot reproduce, or supplies a ready-made commentary on a set text is creating a malpractice risk for the student rather than a grade advantage. The consequences land on the candidate, not on the tutor.

The boundary is workable and we state it plainly before the first session. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and what each one rewards. A tutor can discuss the suitability of a global issue or an Extended Essay research question. A tutor can read the student's own draft and say where the argument is thin, where the register slips, where a quotation is unsupported by commentary. A tutor can model analysis on a different text entirely, so the technique transfers without the content being handed over. A tutor can mark a timed practice answer against the published descriptors.

What a tutor must not do is become the author. No supplied paragraphs, no translation of the student's English thinking into Arabic prose that becomes the submitted work, no line-by-line rewriting that leaves the student unable to explain their own choices. One of the pages competing for this search sells finished Internal Assessments outright at an advertised price; that is an integrity breach and we will not imitate it. If a family wants that, we are the wrong platform, and we would rather say so on the page than in a refund conversation. The practical test we use with Arabic students is simple: could the student defend every sentence, in Arabic, to their own teacher without notes?
bullets: Allowed: teaching the criteria, feedback on the student's own drafts, modelled analysis on other texts
Allowed: research-question framing, source evaluation, timed practice marked to the descriptors
Not allowed: supplied sentences, rewriting to completion, any form of authored submission
Our test: the student can defend every line of the work to their teacher, unaided

sections.heading: Arabic, MoE equivalency and the five-subject rule
paragraphs: Families in Dubai often assume Arabic is the gatekeeper for UAE university entry, and for the British curriculum track the published rule says something more specific. For equivalency of secondary certificates, students on the British track must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count.

That exclusion is worth reading twice, because it is the opposite of what most parents expect, and because a competing page in this cluster publishes a six-subject requirement that does not match the reported rule. It does not make Arabic optional in any practical sense: the subject is required in Dubai schools by the regulator, it appears on the school report, and it carries weight with the schools themselves. It simply means a family choosing between an extra IGCSE and an Arabic resit should know which one the equivalency count recognises before they spend tuition money on it.

For the IB track specifically, no points threshold is published on this page, because the figures circulating for IB equivalency could not be verified against a Ministry of Education source. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat any tutoring provider quoting an IB equivalency number without a citation with caution. The American-track requirements are documented: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. Equivalency is a process the authority runs, not a service a tutoring platform performs, and no tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and when an Arabic session actually happens
paragraphs: The Dubai school year has rhythms that a generic tutoring timetable ignores, and Arabic is the subject most affected, partly because of who studies it and partly because of when it gets studied. During Ramadan, school days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops sharply, and the productive window for a demanding oral session moves to after Iftar. Families who try to hold a 5pm slot through Ramadan usually lose three or four sessions to fatigue and rescheduling, which is money spent on a calendar rather than on teaching.

The practical answer is to move the slot rather than pause the work. Post-Iftar sessions, typically between 8.30pm and 10pm, work well for oral rehearsal and reading, and less well for timed writing. Early morning weekend sessions are the other option, and a 9am Saturday hour is often easier to protect than a weekday evening in any season. Because tuition runs online, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation with someone's driving schedule, which is one of the quieter advantages of the format.

The rest of the year has its own pinch points. The long summer break creates a three-month gap in which listening skill degrades faster than anything else; two short sessions a month through July and August hold it in place at low cost. The weeks around National Day and the winter break collide with school internal assessment deadlines. Mid-term breaks are when families travel, and a tutor who can follow a student across time zones for two weeks is worth more than a cheaper tutor who cannot. We ask about the family's travel pattern before setting a schedule, because a slot that survives the year is worth more than a slot that looks ideal in October.

process.title: Send the course name, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us the exact course and level from the school: Arabic ab initio SL, Arabic B SL or HL, Arabic A: Language and Literature SL or HL, or the MYP phase. Add the school's own Arabic stream if the student carries a mandatory-subject grade too. This one detail determines the tutor, the plan and the rate band.

process.title: A trial lesson before any payment
process.description: The first session is a trial with a course specialist, run live online at a time that suits the family. It is a working lesson rather than a sales call: an unseen reading passage, a short timed write and a few minutes of unprepared speaking, so both sides can see where the student actually stands.

process.title: Diagnostic report and an hours estimate
process.description: After the trial you get a short written diagnosis: which component is weakest, whether the school's course placement looks right, and how many hours the fix plausibly needs. If the honest answer is six focused hours rather than a year of weekly sessions, that is what the note says.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written notes
process.description: Sessions run to the agreed slot on Gulf Standard Time, with a short note after each one covering what was done, what was marked and what to practise before the next. Recordings of oral work go to the student. Nothing about the schedule depends on traffic, so a changed week is a calendar edit.

process.title: Review at the point it matters
process.description: We review before the school forms predicted grades, and again six to eight weeks out from the live session, because those are the two moments when changing the plan still changes an outcome. If a different tutor is a better fit by then, we say so and arrange the switch rather than defend the original match.

whyPoints.title: Priced as the market, with the source named
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market band attributed to the provider or research that published it, not an IB Gram price list. Three of the six pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A family comparing dirhams deserves dirhams and a citation.

whyPoints.title: Matched by Arabic course, not by language
whyPoints.description: An Arabic A: Language and Literature specialist and an ab initio teacher are doing different jobs, and the wrong match wastes a term before anyone notices. We route on the course code and level the school confirms, and we run a diagnostic in the first session to check that the school's own placement holds up.

whyPoints.title: The regulator's requirements treated as fact, not decoration
whyPoints.description: KHDA's mandatory-subject rules shape what Arabic tuition in Dubai can and cannot do: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, set content that cannot be substituted without Ministry permission, and forty-minute lesson units. We work inside those rules and explain them rather than selling around them.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach the criteria, give feedback on the student's own drafts and mark timed practice. We do not supply sentences, rewrite work to completion or hand over a commentary. One page competing for this query sells finished Internal Assessments; the student carries that risk, which is reason enough never to copy it.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. Saying so on the page means no family discovers it after booking, and it is why the comparison table above includes formats we do not sell.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Dubai year
whyPoints.description: Post-Iftar slots through Ramadan, Friday and weekend mornings when weekday evenings are full of sport, short holding sessions through the summer so listening does not decay, and a schedule that follows a travelling family across time zones. The slot that survives the whole year is the one that produces the grade.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Arabic tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour for online one-to-one Arabic tuition as of October 2026, and the course drives the figure more than the tutor's seniority does. Ab initio and MYP phase work sits near the bottom, Arabic B HL in the middle, and Arabic A: Language and Literature at the top because literary analysis in Arabic is a scarcer skill. In-home rates across Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate's 2026 table, with some individual home tutors at AED 500. Those are market bands with the publisher named, not an IB Gram price list; our own terms start with a trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does Arabic A: Language and Literature tuition cost more than ab initio?
faqs.answer: Because the two jobs need different people. Ab initio asks a tutor to build script, high-frequency vocabulary and controlled writing from a low base, which many competent Arabic teachers can do well. Arabic A asks for analysis of an unseen literary or non-literary text in Arabic, with the reasoning explained in the language of the school's report card, and for comparative essay work on studied authors. The UAE pool of teachers who can do that fluently is small, and the price reflects scarcity rather than a claim that one tutor is better than another. Expect roughly AED 250 to AED 450 an hour online for Arabic A against AED 150 to AED 250 for ab initio.

faqs.question: My child's Dubai school already teaches Arabic. Why would we pay for more?
faqs.answer: Often you should not. The school's Arabic lessons are a KHDA requirement with set content, and extra hours on the same material rarely change much. The cases where tuition earns its fee are narrower: the Diploma course grade is diverging from the school Arabic grade, the listening component is the weak link and nobody is drilling it at examination pace, the course placement looks wrong, or the oral is weeks away and the unprepared section has never been rehearsed. Our diagnostic session exists to tell you which of those applies, and it is a legitimate outcome for that session to conclude that no weekly tuition is needed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the individual oral without scripting it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters. A tutor can teach what the oral rewards, build a bank of stimulus material, rehearse the unprepared follow-up questioning that most students never practise, and record sessions so the student hears their own hesitation. What a tutor must not do is supply sentences for the student to memorise, because the student becomes unable to handle any question off the script and because authored material in an assessed component is a malpractice risk under IB rules. The work that actually raises an oral mark is unscripted practice under time pressure, which is also the work students avoid without a tutor in the room.

faqs.question: Is Arabic counted among the subjects the UAE Ministry of Education asks for in equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British curriculum track, reported equivalency requirements say students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A further Advanced Level subject at E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, is also required. That does not make Arabic optional, since Dubai schools must teach it under KHDA rules, but it changes the arithmetic for a family deciding where to spend tuition hours. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before acting on it.

faqs.question: My child is Arab but has only been schooled in English. Which Arabic course fits?
faqs.answer: This is the single most common placement problem in Dubai, and it cannot be settled by household language. A student in this position usually speaks at a high level and reads several phases below it. Placed in Arabic A, the oral goes well and the guided textual analysis collapses; placed in Arabic B HL, the listening is easy while the written register exposes gaps nobody has corrected. The decision needs evidence rather than instinct: an unseen reading passage, a timed written response and a few minutes of analytical talk about a text. Our first session produces exactly that, and the written diagnosis is something you can take back to the school.

faqs.question: How many weekly Arabic sessions do Dubai Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One hour a week is the common starting point in DP1, and it is usually the right one, because the gains in Arabic come from steady reading and listening rather than from intensity. Families starting in DP2 with an examination in sight more often take two sessions a week, split so that one is component drilling and one is marked written work. Before the live session, six to eight weeks at two or three hours a week is a recognisable pattern. The honest caution is that the February sprint costs more per mark gained than the DP1 hour did, because the components that respond fastest to teaching have already been assessed by then.

faqs.question: Can Arabic lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we recommend planning for it rather than reacting to it. School days shorten during Ramadan and late-afternoon concentration drops, so a 5pm slot usually bleeds into cancellations. Sessions between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm after Iftar work well for oral rehearsal and reading, while timed writing is better moved to a weekend morning. Because lessons run online, changing a slot is a calendar edit rather than a renegotiation around someone's travel. We ask about Ramadan timing, family travel and sports fixtures before setting a schedule, since a slot that survives the whole year is worth more than one that looks ideal in October.

faqs.question: Do sessions teach Modern Standard Arabic or Gulf dialect?
faqs.answer: Assessment work is in Modern Standard Arabic, because that is what the IB courses examine and what KHDA specifies as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Dialect still appears in sessions where it is useful: listening components sometimes carry regional colour, and a student living in Dubai hears Gulf and Levantine Arabic daily, which can interfere with written register. A good tutor names the difference explicitly rather than letting a student discover in an examination that the phrasing they use at home is not the phrasing the paper wants. Dialect coaching for family or social reasons is a different service and we say so.

faqs.question: What should an Arabic Extended Essay supervisor expect a tutor to do?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is the school's; a tutor works alongside that relationship, not instead of it. Useful tutor input is narrowing a research question until it is answerable in the word limit, judging whether the Arabic sources are substantial enough to sustain an argument, teaching how to handle quotation and translation, and giving feedback on the student's own successive drafts against the published criteria. What a tutor must not do is author or rewrite the essay, because the student must be the sole author of assessed work and the student carries the consequence if that is not true. A fair test: can the student explain every choice in the essay, in Arabic, without notes?

faqs.question: Is online Arabic tuition workable when the course is so oral-heavy?
faqs.answer: The oral components are the ones that transfer best to video, which surprises families. Recording is trivial online, so the student can hear their own filler words and self-corrections, and that single feedback loop moves an oral mark faster than anything else available. Screen-sharing suits annotated text work for Arabic A, and listening practice runs at genuine examination pace through headphones rather than through classroom speakers. The real constraints are worth naming: a weak connection ruins a listening exercise, handwriting practice in Arabic script needs the student to photograph their work, and a child under about ten needs a parent in earshot for the first few sessions.

faqs.question: Does an Arabic tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services system, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. Ask any tutor directly about their permit position.

faqs.question: What does Arabic support cost a Dubai family across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Take the arithmetic rather than a package price. One hour a week of online Arabic B tuition at the mid-market band of roughly AED 250 an hour, across about 36 teaching weeks a year, is in the region of AED 9,000 a year before any exam-term intensification. Arabic A at AED 350 an hour on the same pattern runs materially higher; ab initio at AED 180 runs lower. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those are market figures, not our quote.

faqs.question: What happens if no Arabic A specialist is free in Dubai evening hours?
faqs.answer: We tell you, before you pay, rather than substituting a general Arabic teacher and hoping. The Arabic A pool is genuinely small, and in the eight weeks before a live session it can be fully booked. The realistic options are then a different slot, often a weekend morning or an early evening before the peak window, a tutor in a different time zone whose availability fits a Dubai morning, or a shorter diagnostic-plus-marking arrangement where the student does the volume of work and the tutor marks it against the criteria. If none of those fits, that is a no from us, and we would rather say it than take the booking.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Arabic B HL to SL in DP1, and what does the switch cost in hours?
faqs.answer: Moving down a level inside the same course is the cheapest of all the switches, because the text types, the oral format and the paper structure stay familiar; what changes is reading volume and the literary works studied at Higher Level. Expect a handful of catch-up hours rather than a term. Moving between Arabic A and Arabic B is the expensive change, since the assessment model itself is different, and it is only comfortable in the first two terms of DP1. Any change is the school's decision under IB registration rules, so start with the coordinator, and get the diagnostic evidence first so the conversation is about the student's work rather than a preference.

dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the course code, then the rate
dubai/ib-arabic-tutor.closingBody: Send us the exact Arabic course and level your child's Dubai school has entered them for, along with the MYP phase or school Arabic stream if that is also in play. We will match a specialist in that course, run a trial lesson live online at a Gulf Standard Time slot that works around school, sport and Ramadan, and send a short written diagnosis of which component is weakest and how many hours the fix plausibly needs. If the honest answer is fewer hours than you expected, or a different course placement, that is what the note will say. Every AED figure on this page is a market band with its source named, so you can compare the Dubai market before you commit to anything.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach DP Chemistry at Higher and Standard Level: organic mechanisms, energetics and thermodynamics, equilibrium, and the data-based half of Paper 1. Each has taught the Structure and Reactivity organisation of the current subject guide. You meet one in a free diagnostic lesson first.

intro.heading: Jumeirah 3 or the next community over: the chemistry does not change
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IB chemistry tutor in Jumeirah 3 frequently search twice, once with their own community name and once with the one next door, because a neighbour in Umm Suqeim or Al Safa has recommended someone and the family wants to know whether distance matters. The useful answer is that for Chemistry it matters less than for any other Group 4 subject, and here is why: the subject is taught almost entirely through worked reasoning on a shared screen. Mechanisms are drawn, not demonstrated. Equilibrium problems are argued through, not performed. A whiteboard the student can annotate beats a kitchen table, and the drive between communities buys nothing.

What does change between these communities is logistics, and this page sets that out in a table rather than pretending otherwise. A Jumeirah 3 family whose child is bussed to Al Barsha gets home later than a Jumeirah 2 family whose child walks out of school in Al Safa. A villa in Al Manara with two children at two schools has two different pick-up times to work around. Those differences move a session by thirty or forty minutes; they do not change which tutor your child should have, and they are the entire practical content of most area-based tutoring pages in this market.

The second comparison worth making is between communities and the thing families actually compare them against, which is the local tutor pool. Hiring within a two-kilometre radius means choosing from whoever happens to live nearby and has a free weekday evening. Hiring a specialist online means choosing from everyone who has taught HL organic chemistry to candidates sitting the current guide. For a subject where the difference between a 5 and a 7 is usually mechanism fluency and uncertainty handling rather than general enthusiasm, the second pool is the one worth drawing from.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one online lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. Nothing on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at a villa in Jumeirah 3, Umm Suqeim or anywhere else in Dubai. What we do offer is a Chemistry specialist, a fixed weekly time that works around the school run, and a written diagnostic after the first free lesson.

The rest of the page is chemistry. It covers how the current subject guide is organised and assessed, the four topics where Jumeirah-strip students most reliably lose marks, how Higher Level differs from Standard Level in ways that change how many hours are needed, what the internally assessed investigation is marked on, how Dubai's published tutoring rates compare across delivery models, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons that sit alongside the Diploma in every Dubai private school and quietly eat into the week.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Two IB programmes matter for a Chemistry request from this part of Dubai, plus the IGCSE route that most Jumeirah 3 students arrive by. The notes below describe what each one leaves a student able and unable to do when Chemistry HL starts.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Chemistry sits in Group 4 and is examined by two papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. The current subject guide drops the old option topics and organises everything under Structure and Reactivity, so a student who learned chemistry as a list of topics has to relearn it as a set of linked ideas. A data booklet is supplied in the examination.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run Chemistry HL in small sets, and in several Jumeirah and Al Barsha schools there is one HL class per cohort. Families here therefore use tuition for a reason that has nothing to do with weakness: if that single class moves faster than their child, there is no second set to transfer into, and a weekly online session is the only parallel support available.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences in the MYP are assessed on four criteria out of eight marks each, rewarding understanding, inquiry design, data processing and reflection on the role of science. It builds genuinely good investigators. It does not build the stoichiometric fluency Chemistry HL assumes, because MYP tasks rarely demand mole calculations at speed and under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students from the Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha continuum schools usually transfer into DP Chemistry comfortable with laboratory reasoning and uncomfortable with moles. The first block of sessions for this group is quantitative: moles, concentration, limiting reagents and percentage yield, practised until the arithmetic stops being the obstacle.

programmes.name: IGCSE Chemistry into DP Chemistry
programmes.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 both end with recall-weighted theory papers plus a practical or alternative-to-practical component. DP Chemistry then asks why rather than what: why a bond is polar, why an equilibrium shifts, why an enthalpy change has that sign. Students who collected A grades by learning reaction lists hit that change in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 students in Al Safa and Al Sufouh planning Chemistry HL benefit from a short bridging block over the summer on bonding, moles and energetics sign conventions. Six sessions in July removes most of the October difficulty, and it is far cheaper than the eight-week intensive those same families book in February.

dubai/ib-chemistry-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Chemistry is usually one of three or four subjects a family is thinking about at once. These are the pairings Jumeirah-strip students actually ask for, with what each one assesses and where it bites.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure 1-3 and Reactivity 1-3, examined through a multiple-choice and data-based Paper 1 and an extended-response Paper 2, with an internal investigation worth 20%. Marks go missing on organic mechanisms, enthalpy sign conventions, equilibrium reasoning and significant figures.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The commonest pairing for medicine applicants from this strip. Shares the investigation criteria with Chemistry, which is an efficiency a tutor can use: teach uncertainty and evaluation once and apply it twice, rather than writing two weak reports in the same term.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paired with Chemistry by engineering applicants. The overlap is quantitative reasoning and graph work; the divergence is that Physics rewards derivation while Chemistry rewards mechanism and justification, so revision technique has to differ between them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Logarithms for pH and rate work, and algebraic rearrangement for equilibrium expressions. A Chemistry HL student weak in AA algebra loses Paper 2 marks on arithmetic, not chemistry, which is why some families run both subjects with one tutor at first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content helps with the data-based part of Paper 1 and with evaluating uncertainty in the investigation. It provides less symbolic practice, so equilibrium and rate algebra need explicit attention in sessions.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want a second science without a second set of mechanisms. Its biochemistry sections overlap usefully with Chemistry Reactivity content, and the two can be revised together where a student takes both.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary alternative that satisfies Group 4 for some students. It demands systems reasoning and data interpretation rather than mechanisms, so it is not a substitute for Chemistry on a medicine or engineering application.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Chemistry
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation supervised in school. Tutoring here is process coaching: judging whether a measurement is feasible with school apparatus, checking the research question is answerable, and reading a draft critically. The data, the argument and the words stay the student's own.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Chemistry supplies unusually good TOK material: models that are known simplifications, measurement uncertainty, and the question of when a mechanism counts as known. Sessions focus on turning that into a knowledge claim rather than a chemistry summary.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry IA support
subjects.description: The investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. Support means stress-testing the question before data collection, teaching uncertainty propagation on the student's own results, and giving feedback as questions the student answers alone.

sections.heading: This community against the next one over, compared honestly
paragraphs: The direct answer: for online Chemistry tuition, moving between Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara and Al Wasl changes the time a session can start by up to about forty minutes and changes nothing else. The tutor pool is identical. The materials are identical. The price is identical, because no part of it pays for a car. Any page that tells you a neighbourhood has its own dedicated tutors is describing a sales territory rather than a teaching reality.

Where real differences exist, they come from schools rather than streets. A student at an IB continuum school in Umm Suqeim has a different internal deadline calendar from a student bussed to Al Barsha, and a different one again from a Year 11 student at a selective British school in Al Sufouh who will sit IGCSE and then A Level. Two families living two hundred metres apart in Jumeirah 3 can therefore need completely different tutoring plans, which is the opposite of how area pages usually describe the market.

The second real difference is sibling logistics. Families in Al Manara and Jumeirah 2 frequently have two children at two schools, and the window where both are home and neither is at football is narrow. An online slot can be split: forty minutes for one child, forty for the other, back to back, with one tutor and no travel between them. That arrangement is impractical for a visiting tutor and routine for a video session.

The honest conclusion is the one in the heading of this page. The answer is the same either way, so choose on subject specialism and on whether the tutor has taught the current guide at the level your child sits, not on which community the tutor lives in. sections.heading: How the current Chemistry guide is organised, and what that changed
paragraphs: DP Chemistry is now taught under two headings rather than eleven topics. Structure covers models of the particulate nature of matter, molecular structure and bonding, and the classification of matter. Reactivity covers what drives a reaction, how much, how fast and how far it goes, and the mechanisms by which chemical change happens. Higher Level material sits inside those same headings rather than in a separate block, and the old option topics are gone.

That reorganisation matters for tutoring in a specific way. A student who revises by topic list will revise bonding on Monday and intermolecular forces on Thursday and never connect them, which is exactly the connection Paper 2 asks about. Sessions therefore work across the structure and reactivity boundary deliberately: why does this bonding model predict that solubility, why does that entropy change follow from this structure. Marks in the extended-response paper are awarded for the link, not the recall.

Assessment is two papers and the investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% and contains multiple choice plus a data-based section on an unseen experiment; Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response; the internally assessed scientific investigation is the remaining 20%, marked in school against IB criteria and externally moderated. A data booklet is provided in the examination, which changes revision priorities: knowing where a value lives and what it implies is worth more than memorising it.

Higher Level is wider and deeper in the same framework, and the practical consequence is hours rather than difficulty. HL students meet additional content inside each heading and sit longer papers, so the same weekly hour covers proportionally less ground. A family moving a child from SL to HL in DP1 should expect the tutoring requirement to rise by roughly half, not to stay flat. Confirm the exact structure for your child's cohort with their DP coordinator, who holds the version of the guide in force for that intake.

sections.heading: The four places Chemistry marks disappear on this strip
paragraphs: Organic mechanisms come first, and they are the clearest divider between a 5 and a 7. Students learn the names of mechanisms and then draw arrows that start in the wrong place, from an atom rather than from a lone pair or a bond. An examiner marking a mechanism is reading the arrows, not the label, so the fix is to draw mechanisms repeatedly while someone questions each arrow aloud. That is an ideal use of a shared screen and a poor use of a textbook.

Energetics is second. Enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy work is mostly sign management, and a student who has not internalised the conventions will produce a numerically correct magnitude with the wrong sign and lose the mark. Hess cycles are where this shows: the arithmetic is simple, the direction of each arrow is not. A tutor who makes the student narrate each step catches the error pattern in a single session.

Third is equilibrium and reasoning under Le Chatelier. The common failure is describing a shift rather than explaining it in terms of the quantity that changed and the system's response, and then applying the same sentence to a question about rate instead of position. Chemistry Paper 2 pays for the distinction. Fourth is quantitative care: significant figures, units, and uncertainties carried through a multi-step calculation. None of these is a knowledge gap and all four are trainable within a term.

There is a fifth that only appears in the internal investigation, and it is a design failure rather than a chemistry failure. A research question with an independent variable that cannot be cleanly controlled, or with too few levels to establish a relationship, caps the grade before the first measurement. Students who come to a tutor after data collection have usually lost marks that nobody can recover, which is why the clinic begins with the question.
bullets: Mechanisms drawn aloud, arrow by arrow, until origins are automatic

Equilibrium answers structured as change, response and consequence
Significant figures and uncertainty carried through every multi-step answer

sections.heading: The investigation: criteria, marks, and what a tutor will not do
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation carries 20% of the Chemistry grade and is marked against four criteria worth six marks each, twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Naming those criteria and their mark allocation is unusual in this market, and it should not be. A parent who knows the split can ask a tutor a precise question, which is where in those four does my child lose marks, and get a precise answer instead of reassurance.

Research design is decided before any chemistry happens: a focused question, clearly identified variables, a method that controls the rest, and a justified range and number of measurements. Data analysis rewards correct processing with uncertainties carried through to the final result and graphs that show the relationship. Conclusion must answer the research question using the data and compare it with accepted chemistry. Evaluation must weigh weaknesses by their impact on the result rather than cataloguing everything that could have gone better.

The boundary on a tutor's role is not negotiable, and it is worth being explicit because this market contains businesses selling finished coursework at four-figure prices. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards, challenges a research question, teaches uncertainty handling on the student's own measurements, and reads a draft and responds with questions. A tutor does not supply text, does not restructure a report, and does not hand over a method. The work must be the student's own; under IB academic-honesty rules the consequence of anything else falls on the candidate.

In practice, feedback sounds like interrogation rather than correction. What was your independent variable, and how did you keep the others constant? Does your uncertainty allow the claim you have made? Which of your weaknesses actually changed the result, and which merely annoyed you? A student who answers those and then revises their own report has learned the criterion and kept authorship intact, which is the only version of this that is safe.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what a Jumeirah 3 family is actually buying
paragraphs: Rates published by Dubai providers during 2026 group into bands. Budget online tutoring, often delivered by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to AED 300. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 with travel included in the price. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors at about AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in the same period ran near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures taken from provider rate cards and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, not an IB Gram price list; we quote after the free diagnostic lesson.

The comparison that matters is not the hourly number but what the hour contains. An hour with a Chemistry HL specialist who diagnoses an arrow-pushing error in the first fifteen minutes is a different product from an hour of general science support at a lower rate, and families who have bought both usually describe the cheaper one as the more expensive. The second variable is continuity: a lower rate with a rotating tutor costs a month of re-diagnosis every time the person changes.

In-home pricing carries a structural cost that no rate card shows. A tutor travelling into the Jumeirah strip for a 4.30pm lesson spends an hour or more in a car for a sixty-minute session, and that time is paid for somewhere, either in the rate or in the shrinking of the pool prepared to accept the booking. It also pushes sessions late, which is why visiting arrangements in this area cluster at 7pm and at weekend mornings.

One more honest note about cost and timing. Specialist availability in Chemistry thins in the weeks before an examination session, so the same specialist is both cheaper and more available in October than in March. Families who begin weekly work early get a better match for less; families who start late pay a premium for whoever is free. Anything advertised as free should state its conditions on the same screen: our trial is one lesson, with no card details and no obligation.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects that sit alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for, and KHDA's guidance required those arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a DP student in Jumeirah 3 this is not a footnote. It is timetable time that sits alongside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service, and it is a frequent reason a Chemistry HL student says there is no room left in the week.

The organisation of those lessons is prescribed in detail. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details are useful when a parent is reading a timetable. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should be shorter than twenty-five minutes. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly.

For tutoring purposes, the practical consequence is scheduling rather than content. Count the mandatory lessons when you work out how much homework time a Chemistry HL student genuinely has, and set the weekly session where it does not collide with the subjects that carry the nearest deadline. Where families want support in Arabic itself, note that for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so any tutoring there follows the school's own material.

sections.heading: Starting from the Jumeirah strip, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is deliberately short. Send the year group, the level, the two or three Chemistry areas causing trouble, the school and the next assessed deadline. We propose one or two specialists and a slot in Gulf Standard Time. The first lesson is free and diagnostic: the student works problems aloud while the tutor records where each error occurs, and you receive a written summary of the error pattern with an honest estimate of what a term can move.

Availability deserves a straight answer, because most pages in this market imply infinite supply. Chemistry HL specialists with current experience of the Structure and Reactivity guide are a narrow pool, and in the two months before an examination session that pool is mostly committed. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred time, we say so, and offer either a specialist in another time zone whose evening matches your afternoon or a place for the next slot that opens. We will not seat a general science tutor in a Chemistry HL slot and describe them as a specialist.

What progress looks like after four sessions is checkable. Mechanism arrows start in the right place without prompting. Hess cycle answers carry the correct sign the first time. The student can state which of the four investigation criteria is weakest in their own draft. Timed Paper 2 sections are finished rather than abandoned. If none of that has happened, the match is wrong, and changing tutor early is cheaper than persevering politely for a term.

Families across Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara and Al Wasl compete for the same 4pm to 6pm weekday windows, so the slot is the scarce resource rather than the tutor. Booking it before the term starts is worth more than adding hours in April, and one reliable weekly session over twelve weeks outperforms a crammed fortnight on every measure we can observe.

whyPoints.description: Back-to-back forty-minute sessions for siblings at different schools are routine online and impractical for a visiting tutor. Families in Al Manara and Jumeirah 2 use this constantly, with one tutor and no gap spent travelling between them.
