sections.heading: Spending well in exam season without wasting it
paragraphs: Exam season is when most coaching money in Dubai is spent and when it is least efficient, which is an uncomfortable combination. The reason is that the work available in the last weeks is narrow: technique, timing, error-class reduction and confidence under pressure. All four are real and all four are limited in how much they can move a grade compared with the same hours spent earlier.

There is one exception, and it is the strongest argument for spending here at all. Timed papers marked against the published criteria produce diagnosis and teaching from the same artefact, which is the most efficient hour available at any point in the two years. A student who sits a paper to time, has it marked properly and is then taught from their own lost marks gets more from sixty minutes than from any amount of syllabus review.

What to avoid in this period is also specific. Avoid new content unless a whole topic is genuinely missing. Avoid adding a second subject in the final month, because split attention produces two marginal gains instead of one real one. Avoid long sessions, which exhaust a student who is already tired. And avoid any provider whose exam-season pitch includes a promised outcome, which is both unachievable and a warning about everything else they say.

The May session is the one Dubai schools sit, and the internal deadlines that precede it sit with the school rather than with the board. No specific IB date appears on this page because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in a revision plan is worse than none. Confirm every deadline with your child's Diploma coordinator before building a spend around it.

sections.heading: What no amount of money should buy
paragraphs: There is a part of this market where more money buys something a family should refuse. Operations in this search sell completed internal assessments, with one advertising finished work at AED 3,750. That is not expensive coaching. It is an academic honesty breach that exposes the student to a malpractice investigation reaching beyond a single subject grade, and the money buys the risk rather than removing it.

The line is clear and worth stating in full. A coach may explain what a criterion asks for in the criterion's own language, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is not met and why, teach the content or statistics the work needs, ask the questions the criteria ask until the student finds the gap, and hold a schedule. A coach may not supply sentences, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, provide a research question the student then adopts, or edit work from one band into another.

The same applies to claims about examiners and boundaries. Nobody should be describing coaches as IB or Cambridge examiners without evidence of current status, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. If a provider's pitch rests on inside knowledge, the pitch is the problem.

What is left after those exclusions is a slower product and the only one worth paying for. Marked work, named error classes, criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own drafting, a dated record, and an honest view on whether the hours a family is considering can do what they hope. Send the subject, the level, the school and a recent marked script, and the first lesson is free for one student per family with no card details taken.

process.title: Price the job, not the hour
process.description: Decide whether you are buying diagnosis, a component block, weekly subject coaching or exam-season marking. Each has a different sensible duration and a different band, and families who choose the arrangement first almost always spend less than families who shop on hourly rate alone.

process.title: Send marked work before asking for a quote
process.description: A recent mock, topic test or internally assessed draft with teacher comments changes a quote from guesswork into an estimate. It also tells you something about the provider: anyone willing to price a Higher Level plan without reading a script is pricing a hope rather than a job.

process.title: Ask the extras questions once
process.description: Rescheduling window, package expiry, minimum session length, whether marking is in the hour, whether the rate holds in exam season, and whether the quoted figure is tax-inclusive. Six questions, asked before payment, that account for most of the gap between an advertised rate and a final bill.

process.title: Use the free session on the marking
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, one student per family, no card details collected. Spend it watching the coach mark your child's own work against the published criteria and explain the lost marks by category, then judge the written note that follows rather than the conversation.

process.title: Review at four sessions with the money in view
process.description: At session four you get a written continue, change or stop recommendation. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we would rather give that recommendation than carry a family through a term that is not working. Changing coach, subject or frequency at that point costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: The numbers are on the page
whyPoints.description: Market bands in dirhams, by level and format, each attributed to the provider or source that published it and dated. This is the asset the rest of the search is missing: three of the best-ranking pages for IB coaching in Dubai publish no price at all and two quote in dollars.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium is explained, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai sit well above online rates for the same expertise, and the difference is largely the slot a coach loses to the drive. Removing the journey removes a real cost without touching the one-to-one ratio a family is paying for.

whyPoints.title: Phasing advice that costs us bookings
whyPoints.description: Hours bought in the autumn of the first year move more marks per dirham than hours bought in the final fortnight. Saying so loses late-season work, and it is the single most useful thing a Dubai family can know before setting a two-year budget.

whyPoints.title: No rate card, and a stated reason
whyPoints.description: An honest figure depends on a marked script nobody has read yet, so the first lesson is free rather than quoted. One per student, one student per family, no card details collected, and that condition appears in the same sentence as the word free every time it is used.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on what money cannot buy
whyPoints.description: Completed internal assessments are sold in this market at published prices. We will mark, question and teach, and we will not supply sentences, restructure a draft or hand over a research question. The dated feedback log exists so a school supervisor can see exactly what was given.

faqs.question: What is the realistic monthly cost of IB coaching in Dubai for one Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Market estimates for weekly one-hour specialist exam-year support run from around AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 a month, with the upper end reflecting criterion-referenced marking included in the hour. Standard Level in the same subject sits roughly in the AED 600 to 1,200 band. Published package examples give another reference: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. These are market figures from providers' own pages, not an IB Gram quote, and the first lesson here is free.

faqs.question: Why do Dubai coaches charge so much more for a visit than for a video session?
faqs.answer: Because of the slot they give up to the drive. A coach crossing Dubai at five o'clock can lose forty minutes each way, which means the visit consumes the time of nearly two sessions. That cost sits inside the hourly figure whether it is itemised or not, which is why published in-home bands in this emirate run AED 180 to 500 while online bands for comparable expertise sit lower. The second cost is narrower choice: the pool becomes whoever can physically arrive rather than whoever is strongest in that subject.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper coach seen twice a week better value than a specialist seen fortnightly?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the problem has been diagnosed. If nobody yet knows why marks are being lost, the specialist fortnightly is better value, because diagnosis requires someone who can mark the work and the frequency is irrelevant until that has happened. If the error class is already identified and the work is practice and consolidation, the cheaper coach twice a week can be excellent value. Buying frequency before diagnosis is the most common way money is wasted in this market.

faqs.question: Which extras should I ask about before paying for a Dubai coaching package?
faqs.answer: Six: the rescheduling notice period, the package expiry date, the minimum session length, whether marking of the student's work is inside the hour or billed separately, whether the agreed rate holds during exam season, and whether the quoted figure is tax-inclusive. Those six account for most of the difference between an advertised hourly rate and the amount a family actually pays. Ask them before payment rather than after, and be wary of any charge for board-owned papers or mark schemes.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years does coaching money go furthest?
faqs.answer: The autumn of the first year, which is when almost nobody spends it. Hours bought early are the cheapest per mark because there is time for a changed habit to become automatic and the content being fixed is still being taught in class. Hours bought in the final fortnight are the most expensive, because technique has no time to settle. One weekly hour across a year moves more than two weekly hours in one term, even though the first costs more overall, which is the argument for starting earlier at lower intensity.

faqs.question: Does dropping a subject from Higher Level to Standard Level save money?
faqs.answer: Usually a substantial amount, and it is the largest single saving available to a Dubai family in this market. Higher Level means more content, an additional paper in most subjects and marking against higher demand, which is why every published band separates the two levels. The constraint is admissions: some quantitative degrees require a specific level, so read the published entry requirements for the actual course at the actual university before changing anything. Where the level is not required, a confident Standard Level grade costs far less to reach than a held Higher Level 4.

faqs.question: Can anyone in Dubai coach my child towards a specific IB point total?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so should be treated as a warning rather than a service. Nobody has access to marking or grade boundaries in advance, and no provider can honestly promise a number. What can be done is narrower and more useful: identify from marked evidence which component is losing the most marks, estimate roughly how many marks sit in that error class, and propose a realistic number of sessions to address it. Component coaching has a definable end. Score coaching is open-ended by construction, which is how budgets disappear.

faqs.question: Are small group sessions worth it for Diploma coaching in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For revision of content a student already broadly knows, yes, and the per-student saving is real. For diagnosis or internally assessed feedback, no, because both require someone to read one student's specific work and adjust the explanation until it lands. A useful test is to ask how many questions your child asked in the last group session. If the honest answer is none, the ratio is wrong for them regardless of what the group costs. The efficient pattern is individual diagnosis first, then cheaper group consolidation.

faqs.question: How should I budget for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: As a block rather than as a monthly commitment, because the work is finite and schedulable. Supervision here is process work: narrowing a research question until it is answerable, explaining criteria in their own language, holding deadlines and giving feedback on drafts the student has written. Derived from the specialist hourly band, four to six sessions comes to roughly AED 800 to 2,700 in this market. Budget it separately from subject coaching and schedule it backwards from the school's own internal draft deadlines rather than the examination window.

faqs.question: Does the price of coaching in Dubai rise closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, because demand concentrates into the same few weeks and the same evening slots. Some providers publish a higher exam-season figure, and others simply have no availability at the earlier agreed rate. That is one more reason the autumn of the first year is the cheapest point to buy, and it is worth asking explicitly whether a rate agreed now will hold in the final term. If the answer is vague, treat the quoted figure as an introductory one rather than a standing one.

faqs.question: Is Dubai coaching cheaper now that school fees have been frozen?
faqs.answer: The two are unrelated, though the context is useful. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That affects the school bill, not the tutoring market, which is priced by supply and demand for specialists. What the freeze does give a family is a stable base against which to size a coaching budget for the year.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai family refuse to pay for, at any price?
faqs.answer: Completed internally assessed work, which is sold in this market with one operation advertising finished pieces at AED 3,750. The money buys an academic honesty exposure that reaches beyond a single subject grade. Also refuse to pay for copies of board-owned syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, which should be referenced and linked rather than distributed. And treat any pitch resting on examiner status or inside knowledge of boundaries as a reason to look elsewhere entirely.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish an IB Gram hourly rate on this page?
faqs.answer: Because an honest figure depends on a marked script nobody has read yet, and quoting before reading one is guesswork presented as a price. What we publish instead is the market: the bands by level and format, each attributed to whoever published it and dated October 2026, so a family can compare any quote they receive. The only commitment made here about money is one free trial lesson per student, one student per family, with no card details collected and nothing to cancel afterwards.

faqs.question: How many sessions should a Dubai family book to start with?
faqs.answer: Four, then decide. Four is enough to produce a diagnosis, two or three marked pieces of work, a named recurring error class and an honest view on whether the arrangement is working, and short enough that stopping costs little. Buying a term up front removes the one decision point that protects a family's money. If a provider will not sell four sessions, that is informative. At the end of four you should receive a written continue, change or stop recommendation with the evidence behind it.

faqs.question: Is online coaching genuinely as effective as paying for someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For one-to-one work the evidence that matters is what gets marked, and marking happens the same way on a shared whiteboard as on paper. What changes is the pool: online, a Dubai family chooses from specialists rather than from whoever can reach their community by five o'clock, which matters most for minority Higher Level subjects. Presence in the room is a real preference and some students work better with it, which is why published in-home rates exist. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

dubai/ib-coaching.closingHeading: Get the number before you get the pitch
dubai/ib-coaching.closingBody: Decide which job you are buying, ask the six extras questions, and send the subject, the level, the school and a recent piece of marked work. We come back with a named coach, a session length and a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, usually within two working days. The first lesson is free for one student per family with no card details collected, and it is spent marking the work you sent. Coaching runs one-to-one over live video across every Dubai community, and if the hours you are considering cannot realistically do what you are hoping for, you will be told that before you pay for them.

intro.heading: Four moving parts, assessed four different ways
paragraphs: The Career-related Programme is the least documented of the three IB programmes a Dubai sixth-former can be in, and the gap in public information is wider than the gap in difficulty. Search for help with it and what comes back is Diploma Programme marketing with the letters CP substituted into the headline. That is not a small editorial failure. A CP student is assessed in at least four structurally different ways at once, by at least two different organisations, and a tutor who treats the whole thing as a Diploma with fewer subjects will spend the year teaching the wrong component.

Here is the shape. A CP student takes at least two Diploma Programme courses, graded on the familiar one-to-seven scale by the IB. They take a career-related study, which is provided and certificated by an external body rather than by the IB, so its rules, deadlines and grading are not the IB's. And they take the CP core, which has four parts: a taught course in Personal and Professional Skills, Service Learning, the Reflective Project, and Language Development. The Reflective Project is graded on a letter scale rather than a number scale. Nothing about that arrangement is intuitive, and almost nothing about it is explained to parents.

The practical consequence is that CP candidates lose ground in places a Diploma candidate never visits. The Reflective Project is the clearest example. It asks a student to identify an ethical dilemma arising from their own career-related study and examine it in depth, which means the quality of the dilemma decides the quality of the project before a word of it is produced. A student who picks a topic rather than a dilemma has already capped the mark, and no amount of later polishing recovers it. Nobody can see that from outside, which is why it is worth saying out loud on a page like this.

Personal and Professional Skills is the second place. It is a taught course with its own assessment, it sits in the timetable like a subject, and students routinely treat it as an administrative obligation until the point at which it is not. Service Learning is the third: it requires sustained engagement and documented reflection, both of which are difficult to reconstruct in April if nothing was recorded in October. Language Development runs quietly across the whole programme as a portfolio, and portfolios built retrospectively look exactly like portfolios built retrospectively.

What a CP tutor in Dubai should therefore do is unglamorous. Establish which two or three DP courses the student is sitting and at what level, and teach those properly to the published assessment shape. Separate the career-related study's deadlines from the IB's, because they are set by different bodies and collide at predictable moments. Work the Reflective Project at the dilemma stage rather than the drafting stage. Audit the Service Learning and Language Development records early enough to fix them. And be honest that structural details in this programme change between guides, so every claim on this page should be confirmed against the current CP documentation with your school's coordinator.

One more thing belongs at the top. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, and we do not run in-person lessons anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Everything described below is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For the CP specifically that format has an unusually strong case, because the cohort is small, the component knowledge is scarce, and a family's chance of finding a tutor who has actually supervised a Reflective Project within driving distance of their villa is poor.

dubai/ib-cp-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run at secondary level and a Dubai student may meet two of them. The CP and the DP share courses but not structure, and the difference in structure is where the tutoring work actually sits.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma Programme courses, a career-related study delivered and certificated by an external provider, and a four-part core: Personal and Professional Skills, Service Learning, the Reflective Project and Language Development. The outcome is a CP certificate together with DP course results and the external provider's own qualification, rather than an IB Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is thin relative to the Diploma. The emirate licenses seventeen curricula across 227 private schools, and the IB accounts for a smaller share of private-school enrolment than the British, Indian or American curricula. Ask a school directly which IB programmes it is authorised to offer rather than assuming that an IB World School offering the Diploma also runs the CP.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Externally examined with internally marked components moderated by the IB. The courses a CP student takes are these courses, with the same published assessment structure and the same one-to-seven grading.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six openings in 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment. More Diploma capacity in the emirate does not automatically mean more CP capacity, because authorisation is programme by programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria marked out of eight and reported as levels from one to seven. Students arriving in the CP from the MYP already understand criterion marking, which is a real advantage for the Reflective Project; students arriving from IGCSE usually do not.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the MYP and then offer only the Diploma at sixth form, so a student who would suit the CP sometimes has to change school at sixteen to find it. That transfer, and the question of whether it is worth making, is one of the more common CP conversations a Dubai family has.

dubai/ib-cp-tutor.subjectsIntro: A CP student carries Diploma Programme courses, usually at Standard Level and usually chosen to sit alongside the career-related field rather than against it. These are the ones that appear most often in Dubai CP timetables, with what each one is actually assessed on.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Written papers plus an internally assessed research component. Marks are lost on tool application rather than knowledge: a student who describes a framework without applying it to the stimulus organisation scores in the lower bands. Pairs naturally with business, hospitality and management career studies.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Assessed on command-term precision more than recall. The difference between describe, explain and evaluate decides whole mark bands, and students routinely answer a lower command term well. Study evaluation, not study description, is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Inquiry-led, with an internally assessed component built on real-world examples. Candidates who choose familiar examples rather than well-evidenced ones lose claim-support marks. Suits career studies in technology, media and digital operations.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and data-handling rather than proof. Technology is assumed in part of the assessment, and the common loss is unjustified rounding and context-free answers. This is the mathematics route most CP students take and the one most career fields actually use.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary material, with an oral component. Weak scripts summarise the text; strong scripts analyse how meaning is constructed. The analytical habit here transfers directly to the Reflective Project.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Physiology and research methods with an internally assessed investigation. Data handling and evaluation of method carry more marks than content recall. A frequent pairing with sports management and fitness career studies in this market.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus evaluation. Candidates who draw correctly and evaluate thinly plateau in the middle bands. Real-world application is explicitly rewarded, which suits a CP student who already has a career-related context to draw on.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Portfolio-based assessment with comparative and curatorial components. The recurring failure is documentation: strong work with thin process evidence scores below weaker work that is properly recorded. Pairs with design and creative-industry career studies.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Design cycle work with an internally assessed project, plus written papers. Candidates lose marks on justification rather than making: a decision that is not evidenced is treated as a decision that was not made. A natural fit with engineering and product career fields.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary, with a strong emphasis on evaluating environmental value systems. Useful to CP students because its ethical-reasoning demands overlap with what the Reflective Project is marked on, which makes the two reinforce each other rather than compete.

sections.heading: What the Career-related Programme actually is, and who takes it in Dubai
paragraphs: The Career-related Programme is an IB qualification for students aged roughly sixteen to nineteen that combines three things: at least two Diploma Programme courses, a career-related study delivered by an external provider, and a four-part CP core. A student who completes it receives a CP certificate alongside their DP course results and whatever qualification the external provider awards. They do not receive an IB Diploma, and the distinction matters more in a university admissions office than it does in a school corridor.

That structure exists to solve a real problem. The full Diploma asks for six subjects with three at Higher Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. It is a heavy, broad, deliberately academic load. A sixteen-year-old with a clear vocational direction and strong practical ability can be badly served by it, and the alternative in most markets is to drop the IB framework altogether for A Levels or a BTEC. The CP lets a student keep IB courses and IB-style reflective assessment while carrying a genuine career-related qualification.

In Dubai the practical question is availability rather than suitability. The emirate licenses seventeen curricula across 227 private schools, and IB enrolment is a smaller share of the private-school total than the British, Indian or American curricula. IB authorisation is granted programme by programme, so a school running the Diploma is not thereby running the CP. Families regularly discover this late, after a year of assuming their school's IB status covered everything. The only reliable answer comes from asking the school which IB programmes it is specifically authorised for.

Who ends up in the CP, in this market, falls into three groups. There are students with a settled vocational direction who chose it deliberately. There are students who began the Diploma, found three Higher Levels unsustainable, and moved across rather than out. And there are students who arrived in Dubai mid-sixth-form from a system that did not map onto the Diploma and were placed into the CP as the nearest fit. Those three groups need different tutoring, and the first thing a tutor should establish is which one is in front of them.

sections.heading: The four parts of the CP core
paragraphs: The core is where the CP stops resembling a lighter Diploma. It has four components and they are assessed in four different ways by at least two different bodies. Personal and Professional Skills is a taught course with its own assessment. Service Learning requires sustained engagement with documented reflection. The Reflective Project is an extended piece of work examining an ethical dilemma, graded on a letter scale. Language Development runs across the whole programme as a portfolio of evidence.

Each of these fails in a characteristic way, and the failures are mostly administrative rather than intellectual. Personal and Professional Skills fails because students treat a timetabled course as an obligation rather than a subject. Service Learning fails because the engagement happens and the reflection does not get recorded, which is indistinguishable at the deadline from the engagement not happening. The Reflective Project fails at the choice of dilemma, months before anyone looks at a draft. Language Development fails because a portfolio assembled in one weekend reads exactly like a portfolio assembled in one weekend.

What that means for tutoring is that the highest-value intervention in the CP core is an audit, and the best time to buy it is early in the first year rather than late in the second. A session that establishes what is currently documented, what the school's internal deadlines are, which deadlines belong to the career-related provider instead, and what reflection routine the student can actually sustain through a term is worth more than five sessions of rescue work in April.

Treat the detail in the table as a map rather than as a specification. Component requirements, recommended hours and criterion structures are set in the IB's current CP documentation and they change between editions. Every CP school has a coordinator whose job includes exactly this, and the correct instruction to any family is to confirm the specifics with that person before planning around them. A tutor who states hour requirements as settled fact without that caveat is guessing.

sections.heading: The Diploma Programme courses inside a CP, and how they are graded
paragraphs: The courses a CP student takes are ordinary Diploma Programme courses. Same guides, same published assessment structure, same examinations, same one-to-seven grades. The only difference is how many of them there are and, usually, at what level: CP students commonly take two or three courses, frequently at Standard Level, chosen to sit alongside the career field rather than to assemble a broad academic spread. A tutor working on these courses is doing exactly what a Diploma tutor does, which is the one part of CP support that is not specialised.

What changes is prioritisation. A Diploma candidate with six subjects and three Higher Levels is managing breadth. A CP candidate with two Standard Level courses is carrying a smaller academic load but a larger administrative one, because the career-related study and the core are both live at the same time. The marks available in those two courses matter proportionally more to the overall record, and a single weak internally assessed component has nowhere to hide. That argues for front-loading the internal component rather than leaving it where most students leave it.

Course choice itself deserves a conversation. The strongest CP combinations are the ones where the DP course and the career field genuinely reinforce each other: Business Management with a business or hospitality study, Sports Exercise and Health Science with a sports study, Digital Society with a technology study, Design Technology with an engineering one. Environmental Systems and Societies is an underrated choice for a CP student because its demands on evaluating value systems overlap directly with what the Reflective Project is marked on, so the two components teach each other.

sections.heading: The Reflective Project: an ethical dilemma, and the criteria that mark it
paragraphs: The Reflective Project is the component that most distinguishes the CP, and it is the one most commonly handled badly. It asks the student to identify an ethical dilemma arising from an issue in their own career-related study and examine it in depth over an extended period, producing a substantial piece of work assessed against published criteria and reported on a letter scale rather than as a number out of seven.

Almost everything that decides the final letter happens in the first fortnight. An ethical dilemma is not a topic and it is not a problem; it is a situation in which two defensible positions conflict and something has to give. A student who writes about the environmental impact of the construction industry has a topic. A student who writes about whether a site manager should report a safety breach that will halt a project and cost colleagues their income has a dilemma. The second project can reach the top bands and the first cannot, however well it is written, because the criteria reward the examination of competing positions.

A supervisor's job at that stage is to test, not to supply. Useful tests are blunt. Can you state the two positions in one sentence each? Can you name a person who would hold each one, and what they would lose? Is there evidence available for both sides, or only for the one you already agree with? Would someone reasonable disagree with your conclusion? A student who cannot answer those questions does not have a dilemma yet, and the honest thing a tutor can do is say so in week two rather than in month four.

After that the work is the student's and must remain so. A tutor reads what the student has produced, maps it against each criterion, and names what is missing. A tutor does not supply sentences, restructure paragraphs into their own prose, or research the counter-position on the student's behalf. This is the same academic-honesty principle that governs assessed work throughout the IB, and the record of sessions should make it obvious which words are the student's and which are feedback. Criterion names, mark allocations and length requirements are set in the current CP documentation and should be confirmed with the school.

sections.heading: Personal and Professional Skills, and the Language Development portfolio
paragraphs: Personal and Professional Skills is a taught course and the single most underestimated part of the CP. It sits in the timetable like a subject, it has its own content and its own assessment, and it covers professional conduct, ethical reasoning, intercultural understanding, communication and applied skills. Students treat it as an administrative requirement because it does not look like Business Management, and then meet an assessment that expects them to use its vocabulary accurately. Schools commonly timetable a substantial number of hours for it; confirm the current requirement with your coordinator rather than assuming.

The tutoring work here is mostly translation. The course's concepts have precise meanings and students use them loosely, which is exactly the failure mode that costs marks in any criterion-assessed component. A session spent making a student define intercultural understanding in their own words and then apply it to a real situation from their own placement does more than a session spent reviewing notes. The overlap with the Reflective Project is substantial: the ethical reasoning taught here is the reasoning the project is marked on, and students who connect the two get two components for the price of one.

Language Development is quieter and easier to neglect. It asks for ongoing development in a language other than the student's best language, evidenced in a portfolio. In Dubai this is often genuinely useful rather than nominal, because a large share of students are already operating across Arabic, English and a home language, and because the emirate's schools teach Arabic as a mandatory subject in any case. The difficulty is evidence over time. A portfolio is a record of development, and a record assembled in a single weekend shows it.

The practical fix for both components is the same and it is dull: a short, repeatable routine set up early. Ten minutes of dated reflection a week, in whatever form the student will actually maintain, produces at the deadline something no amount of concentrated effort can reconstruct. A tutor can set that routine up, check it monthly, and name the gap while it is still a gap. This is unglamorous work and it is the highest-return hour a CP family buys.

sections.heading: Service Learning: the component left until it is too late
paragraphs: Service Learning asks for planned, sustained engagement with an identified community need, with reflection recorded through the process rather than summarised afterwards. It is not volunteering hours and it is not a charity drive, although both can form part of it. The emphasis is on identifying a need with the community rather than for it, acting over time, and showing what the student learned and how their thinking changed.

The failure is almost always documentation rather than activity. Dubai students are generally busy and generally engaged; schools here run substantial service programmes and many students are involved in more than the CP requires. What does not happen is the recording. A student who spent eight months supporting a literacy programme and wrote nothing down has, at the deadline, the same evidence as a student who did nothing, and no supervisor can honestly sign off what cannot be shown. This is the single most recoverable loss in the CP and the one most often left unrecovered.

The geography of Dubai matters here in a way it does not for tutoring. A placement or service partner has to be physically reachable on a school night, and the emirate's commercial clusters are not evenly distributed. Students in Business Bay, Dubai Silicon Oasis or Media City have options within a short radius. Students in Dubai Investments Park or Jebel Ali lose more of the evening to travel than anyone else, and their plans need to account for it rather than assume it away.

What a tutor contributes is structure and honesty. Structure means a reflection prompt the student will actually answer, a monthly check, and a format that matches what the school will accept. Honesty means saying when a plan is too thin to produce a defensible record, and saying it early. It also means staying out of the activity itself: the service is the student's, the reflection is the student's, and a supervisor who helps compose the reflection has removed the only thing being assessed.

sections.heading: CP, the full Diploma, A Levels and BTEC compared for a Dubai sixth form
paragraphs: Most Dubai families arrive at the CP question from the other direction: they are deciding between sixth-form routes and want to know what the CP gives up and what it buys. The honest comparison is structural rather than evaluative, because the right answer depends entirely on the student. A broad academic load suits some sixteen-year-olds and damages others, and a vocational route that is a sensible match for one university plan is a dead end for another.

The full Diploma offers breadth, three Higher Levels, and the widest recognition. It is also the heaviest load and the least forgiving if a student's strengths are uneven. A Levels offer depth in three or four subjects with no required core, which suits a student who already knows what they want and is comfortable dropping everything else. A BTEC or similar vocational qualification offers applied assessment, often coursework-weighted, with a direct line into related employment and into some degree routes but not all.

The CP sits between them in a specific way: IB courses and IB-style reflective assessment, plus a genuine vocational certification, plus a core that is explicitly about professional conduct and ethical reasoning. What it gives up is the IB Diploma itself and the breadth that comes with six subjects. What it adds, and this is the part most comparisons miss, is a documented record of reflective and ethical reasoning tied to real work, which some admissions processes and most employers read more readily than a grade profile.

The thing to check before choosing is the destination, not the programme. University recognition for the CP is not uniform across institutions or countries, and the UAE's own equivalency route treats curricula differently. Write down the three or four destinations the student is actually considering, then ask each one in writing what it does with a CP certificate plus DP course grades plus the external qualification. That takes a fortnight and settles the question better than any comparison table, including this one.

sections.heading: UAE equivalency and university admission for a CP graduate
paragraphs: A UAE secondary qualification normally has to be recognised through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process before it can be used for university admission or for certain employment purposes here. The rules are published by curriculum track, and they are specific. For the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

For the American track the published requirements include an English proficiency threshold, met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and a mathematics requirement of at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. These figures are sourced and quotable. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects for UAE candidates, which does not match the published rule; being correct on a detail like that is worth more than any amount of reassurance.

For the IB, and specifically for the Career-related Programme, no equivalency figure is published that this page can stand behind. The sourced material on equivalency does not state an IB points threshold at all, and nothing available states how a CP certificate plus DP course grades plus an external vocational qualification is treated. Anyone telling you confidently what the CP converts to in the UAE should be asked for the moe.gov.ae page it comes from. The correct route is to check with the Ministry of Education or the emirate's attestation channel directly, and with each target university's own admissions office.

Two cautions follow from this. Equivalency is a regulatory process carried out by the authority, not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates; our role is to describe it and point you at the official channel. And nobody should imply that tutoring is required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. It is not, and framing a regulatory process as something that needs purchasing is the kind of false urgency this market has too much of already.

sections.heading: A thin cohort, and what that means for finding a CP tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: The CP is a small programme. That is the plain reason this page exists and the plain reason it has to be honest about coverage. A family looking for someone who has actually supervised a Reflective Project, or who knows what Personal and Professional Skills assesses, is looking for a narrow specialism inside an already narrow programme. Searching for that person within a twenty-minute drive of a Dubai villa is a poor use of a short list, which is the practical argument for the format we use rather than a marketing one.

What we will say plainly is what we have and what we do not. DP course teaching at Standard Level in the subjects CP students commonly take is well covered, because those are ordinary Diploma courses. Reflective Project supervision, extended reflective writing and ethical reasoning are covered by tutors who do that work in the Diploma core as well. The career-related study itself is not ours to teach: it belongs to an external provider with its own syllabus, its own assessors and its own calendar, and a tutor who claims to cover it should be asked which provider and which qualification.

When a specialist is not free, we say so rather than matching whoever is available. That costs us enquiries and it is the right position; the alternative is a family paying specialist rates for general support, which is the most common quiet failure in this market. Where a component genuinely needs the school rather than a tutor, the honest answer is the school: a CP coordinator can confirm requirements, deadlines and acceptable evidence formats in one conversation, and no external party can do that for them.

Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the career-related study and the placement rather than against them. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai and holds no centre, office or branch anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We state that here rather than after an enquiry, because two providers found in this market route UAE families to numbers outside the UAE without disclosing it, and disclosure is the cheapest trust signal available.

process.title: Tell us which components are live
process.description: Send the two or three DP courses and their levels, the career-related study and its provider, and where the Reflective Project currently stands. A single message with that in it is worth more than a long description of the student, because it tells us immediately which of the four CP core components needs the first session.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a diagnostic job
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, nothing to pay and no card required. For a CP student the trial usually tests two things: how precisely they use the vocabulary of their taught courses, and whether their Reflective Project rests on a dilemma or on a topic. Both answers change the plan.

process.title: Two calendars on one page
process.description: We map the IB component deadlines and the career-related provider's assessment points onto a single calendar, because they are set by different bodies and collide at predictable moments. Most CP spring crises are a scheduling failure rather than an academic one, and this step prevents a share of them.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a visible record
process.description: Each session ends with the student's own work, the feedback against the published criteria, and a note of what to attempt next. The student's words and the tutor's feedback stay visibly separate, which matters for every assessed component and matters most for the Reflective Project.

process.title: A review at six weeks, and an honest verdict
process.description: At six weeks we compare against the diagnostic from the trial and say what has moved. If a component is beyond useful recovery we say so and redirect the hours to one that is not. If the right answer is the school's CP coordinator rather than a tutor, we say that too.

whyPoints.title: Built on the CP's own structure
whyPoints.description: The page and the teaching follow the four core components and the DP courses as they are actually assessed, rather than treating the CP as a Diploma with subjects removed. That distinction is the whole reason a CP family struggles to find useful help in this market.

whyPoints.title: The Reflective Project worked at the dilemma stage
whyPoints.description: Most of the final letter is decided in the first fortnight, when the dilemma is chosen. We test it with blunt questions early and refuse to move on until it holds, which is less comfortable than drafting and considerably more useful.

whyPoints.title: Structural claims flagged, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Component requirements, criterion letters and recommended hours live in the IB's current CP documentation and change between editions. Everything structural on this page is marked for confirmation with your school's coordinator, because a confident wrong number is worse than a hedged right one.

whyPoints.title: Two sets of deadlines treated as two sets
whyPoints.description: The career-related study is run by an external provider with its own calendar and its own assessors. We map those dates against the IB's instead of assuming they are the same, which is where a surprising number of CP spring collapses actually originate.

whyPoints.title: The academic honesty boundary stated and kept
whyPoints.description: A tutor tests, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. No part of a Reflective Project, a reflection or a portfolio is supplied by us, and the session record makes clear which words belong to whom.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: Standard Level DP course teaching is well covered; Reflective Project supervision takes longer to match; the career-related qualification is not ours to teach. If nobody suitable is free, we say so rather than matching whoever is available.

faqs.question: What is the IB Career-related Programme, in plain terms?
faqs.answer: It is an IB qualification for students roughly sixteen to nineteen that combines at least two Diploma Programme courses, a career-related study delivered and certificated by an external provider, and a four-part core: Personal and Professional Skills, Service Learning, the Reflective Project and Language Development. The student leaves with a CP certificate, their DP course grades on the usual one-to-seven scale, and the external provider's own qualification. It is not an IB Diploma, and that difference matters to admissions offices. Confirm the current component requirements with your school's CP coordinator, because they are set in IB documentation that changes between editions.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools offer the IB Career-related Programme?
faqs.answer: Ask each school directly, because IB authorisation is granted programme by programme and a school running the Diploma is not automatically running the CP. This catches families out every year. Dubai licenses seventeen curricula across 227 private schools, and IB enrolment is a smaller share of the private-school total than the British, Indian or American curricula, so CP provision is thin in absolute terms. We will not name a school as a CP provider on this page, because stating a school's authorisation without verifying it against the school's own information would be exactly the error we criticise competitors for making.

faqs.question: How is the Reflective Project graded compared with a DP subject?
faqs.answer: Differently, and this surprises most families. Diploma Programme courses are graded one to seven. The Reflective Project is assessed against published criteria and reported on a letter scale, which means a student's record carries two different kinds of result side by side. The practical implication is that the project cannot be mentally averaged into a subject profile; it is read separately. Criterion letters, mark allocations and length requirements sit in the current CP documentation, so confirm them with your coordinator before planning around a particular total.

faqs.question: What counts as an ethical dilemma for the Reflective Project?
faqs.answer: A situation in which two defensible positions genuinely conflict and something has to be given up. Not a topic, and not a problem with an obvious right answer. The environmental impact of construction is a topic. Whether a site manager should report a safety breach that will halt a project and cost colleagues their income is a dilemma, because both choices have a real cost and a reasonable person could take either. The criteria reward examining competing positions, so a weak dilemma caps the mark before any writing begins. Test it in the first fortnight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Reflective Project without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can test whether the dilemma holds, ask where the counter-evidence is, role-play the opposing position aloud, map the student's own draft against each criterion, and name what is missing. A tutor cannot supply sentences, rewrite paragraphs into their own prose, or research the other side on the student's behalf. The work has to be the student's, in the student's words, from the student's notes. Our session records keep the student's text and the tutor's feedback visibly separate so that the distinction is checkable rather than asserted.

faqs.question: Is the CP easier than the full IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It is lighter academically and heavier administratively, which is not the same as easier. A full Diploma candidate carries six subjects with three at Higher Level plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. A CP candidate carries two or three courses but also an external vocational qualification with its own calendar, a taught professional-skills course, a documented service requirement, a language portfolio and an extended ethical project. Students who struggle with the CP usually struggle with the number of simultaneous obligations rather than with the difficulty of any one of them.

faqs.question: Why do CP students in Dubai run into trouble in the spring?
faqs.answer: Because two calendars collide. The IB sets deadlines for the core components, and the career-related study's external provider sets its own assessment points under its own rules. Those dates are not coordinated, and in most CP years they converge in the same few weeks as the examined DP components. A student working to one mental calendar meets three deadlines at once. Mapping both sets of dates onto a single page early in the first year is dull, takes one session, and prevents a meaningful share of the crises we are called about in March and April.

faqs.question: What does Personal and Professional Skills actually assess?
faqs.answer: It is a taught course covering professional conduct, ethical reasoning, intercultural understanding, communication and applied skills, with its own assessment against the published course requirements. Students treat it as timetable filler because it does not look like a subject, then meet an assessment that expects precise use of its vocabulary. The useful tutoring here is translation: making a student define each concept in their own words and apply it to a real situation from their own placement. The ethical reasoning taught in this course is the reasoning the Reflective Project is marked on, so the two reinforce each other.

faqs.question: How much Service Learning does the CP require, and how is it recorded?
faqs.answer: The requirement is sustained, planned engagement with an identified community need, with reflection recorded throughout rather than summarised at the end. Confirm the current specifics with your school, because requirements are set in IB documentation that changes. What matters practically is the record. Dubai students are generally busy and generally engaged, and the component almost never fails on activity. It fails because nothing was written down, and at a deadline an undocumented eight months looks identical to no months at all. A dated ten-minute weekly reflection solves it at almost no cost.

faqs.question: What is the Language Development portfolio and how do we build one properly?
faqs.answer: It evidences ongoing development in a language other than the student's best language, across the whole programme. The point is the trajectory, not the folder: a portfolio assembled in one weekend is visibly a portfolio assembled in one weekend. In Dubai this component is often genuinely substantive, because many students already operate across Arabic, English and a home language, and because Arabic is a mandatory subject in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed for. Set up a short dated routine in the first term and check it monthly; nothing else reconstructs a record of change over time.

faqs.question: Which DP courses go best with a career-related study?
faqs.answer: The ones that reinforce the career field rather than sit beside it. Business Management with a business or hospitality qualification, Sports Exercise and Health Science with a sports study, Digital Society with a technology study, Design Technology with an engineering one. Environmental Systems and Societies is an underrated choice for any CP student because its demands on evaluating competing value systems overlap directly with the Reflective Project's criteria, so the two components teach each other. Economics and Psychology both work widely. Confirm which courses your school actually timetables for CP students before planning around a combination.

faqs.question: Will UAE universities accept an IB Career-related Programme certificate?
faqs.answer: Check each one in writing, and check the Ministry of Education's equivalency route separately. The sourced equivalency material available for this page sets out requirements for the British and American tracks but states no IB points threshold and says nothing about a CP certificate, so no figure can honestly be published here. Anyone who tells you confidently what the CP converts to should be asked for the moe.gov.ae page it came from. Write down the three or four destinations the student is actually considering and ask each one how it treats a CP certificate plus DP course grades plus the external qualification.

faqs.question: Does the career-related study come from the IB as well?
faqs.answer: No, and this is one of the most useful things to understand about the programme. The career-related study is provided and certificated by an external body, not by the IB. Its syllabus, its assessors, its deadlines, its grading and its appeals process are all its own. A tutor who claims to cover your child's career-related study should be asked which provider and which qualification they mean, because the answer is specific and checkable. We do not teach it, and we say so rather than taking the enquiry and working it out afterwards.

faqs.question: My child started the full Diploma and cannot carry three Higher Levels. Is moving to the CP sensible?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a decision to make with the school rather than from a website. Moving across keeps IB courses and IB-style reflective assessment while replacing breadth with a vocational certification, which suits a student whose direction is settled and whose strengths are uneven. Two things to establish first. Whether the school is authorised for the CP at all, since Diploma authorisation does not cover it. And how each of the student's realistic university destinations treats a CP certificate, in writing. Get both answers before the transfer rather than after.

faqs.question: Why are CP lessons online when I searched for a tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the cohort is small and the specialism is narrow, and because we would rather say so than quietly. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai and holds no centre, office or branch anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For the CP the format matters more than usual: finding someone who has supervised a Reflective Project within driving distance of a particular Dubai community is a poor use of a short list, and geography should not decide which specialist a family reaches.

dubai/ib-cp-tutor.closingHeading: Start by telling us which component is actually the problem
dubai/ib-cp-tutor.closingBody: Send the DP courses and their levels, the career-related study and its provider, and one line on where the Reflective Project stands. The trial lesson is free, one per family, with nothing to pay and no card required, and for a CP student it works as a diagnostic: how precisely the student uses their taught courses' vocabulary, and whether the project rests on a dilemma or on a topic. After it you get a written plan, both calendars on one page, and an honest statement of what we cover and what belongs with your school's CP coordinator instead.

dubai/ib-crash-course.tutorsIntro: These tutors run intensive Diploma blocks into Gulf Standard Time. An intensive tutor is chosen for one specific ability: deciding in the first session which parts of a syllabus to abandon, which is the only way a short block produces marks.

intro.heading: Start with the money, because the money is what makes the decision
paragraphs: Almost every page about intensive IB revision opens with reassurance. This one opens with a number, because the number is the thing families are actually weighing. At the published Dubai market rate for an IB subject specialist, AED 200 to 450 an hour, a 20-hour block is AED 4,000 to AED 9,000 for one subject. At the qualified-online-tutor band of AED 150 to 300, the same block is AED 3,000 to AED 6,000. Those bands come from published 2026 rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, and they are market figures rather than a price list of ours.

Put that against what the hours can reach. A Diploma subject is assessed by two or three external papers carrying most of the grade and an internal assessment carrying roughly a fifth. Twenty hours cannot re-teach two years of content in any subject. It can rehearse one paper format to competence, close two or three specific topic gaps, and rebuild the way a student reads questions. Those three things, done in the right subject at the right moment, move a grade. Spread thinly across five subjects, the same hours and the same money move nothing.

So the first useful question is not how much does a crash course cost but what is the cost per mark recovered, and that depends almost entirely on what is missing. A student losing marks to form and question reading is cheap to fix, because those faults are habits and habits respond to a few hours of marked practice. A student missing a year of Higher Level content is expensive to fix and may not be fixable in the time available at any price, which is a thing worth being told in writing before money changes hands.

The second question is what changes the number in Dubai specifically, and several things do. Lead time is the largest factor: a block booked in February is a different market from one booked in the last fortnight before papers, when specialist availability tightens and families end up buying whatever is free rather than whichever tutor they need. Level matters, because Higher Level option topics are a smaller specialist pool. Format matters, because group intensives are cheaper per hour and give a student fewer of their own questions answered.

This page is organised around those two questions. It sets out block sizes against market bands, what each block size can honestly cover, the factors that move the price in this emirate, how an intensive block compares against the same money spent on a term of weekly sessions, where the hours should go when a block is bought, and the situations in which we decline the booking because the arithmetic does not work. Every figure carries its source and its date.

dubai/ib-crash-course.programmesIntro: Intensive blocks are bought at four distinct points in the IB continuum, and the arithmetic is different at each. These are the stages Dubai families buy them for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: The classic crash-course purchase: one or two subjects, bought between the January mocks and the May session, aimed at paper technique rather than content. Each subject has two or three external papers and an internal assessment already submitted, so the entire addressable mark pool is the external components. That makes the targeting unusually clean.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools sit the May session, and the exact examination window, results release and enquiry deadlines should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site rather than taken from a tutoring page. Internal deadlines for the components already submitted were set by the school, which is why two Dubai students can arrive at an intensive block with very different amounts of work behind them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: A smaller and better-value purchase that few families consider: a short block in the summer or at a half-term, aimed at the transition gap rather than at an examination. Ten hours spent securing the mathematics or the written structure a Higher Level subject assumes is cheaper than thirty hours spent repairing the consequences in Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Year 12 students arrive from Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel, the Middle Years Programme and American high-school tracks, so the transition gap differs by route. The diagnostic matters more here than the hours: ten hours aimed at the wrong gap produces nothing, and the gap is identifiable from one marked piece of work.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Short blocks bought against a school deadline rather than an examination. The exhibition, the prescribed-title essay and the 4,000-word Extended Essay carry up to three bonus points between them. A six-hour block spread over three weeks is usually the right shape, because the student needs thinking time between sessions.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay supervisor is appointed by the Dubai school and signs the reflection sessions. An intensive block works beside that process and cannot replace it. Where a family arrives asking for a draft to be finished, the answer is no: the student writes every word, and a provider offering otherwise is creating a malpractice risk that falls on the candidate.

programmes.name: The November session and retakes
programmes.description: The IB offers a November session as well as a May one, which turns a missed university condition into a decision with options. An intensive block here is unusually efficient, because the student has already sat the papers and knows exactly which components cost them the grade, so the targeting is evidence-led rather than predictive.
programmes.countryNote: Session dates, registration deadlines and the enquiry-upon-results window are set by the IB and administered through the school. Confirm all of them with your school's IB coordinator before planning a retake block, and treat any specific date published on a tutoring site, including dates for the November session, as unverified until the coordinator or the IB confirms it.

dubai/ib-crash-course.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects most often bought as an intensive block in Dubai, with what twenty hours can realistically reach in each. The third consideration in every case is whether the loss is habit or content, because that decides the cost per mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Twenty hours covers one paper format to competence plus two or three topic gaps, typically calculus technique and one proof method. The cheapest marks are in method presentation: a student who shows working consistently recovers marks already earned mathematically, which costs perhaps three hours to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Long contextual questions, so hours go further on reading technique than on content. A 20-hour block can usually cover the statistics content properly and rehearse the modelling questions, which together carry a substantial share of the papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium absorb most of an intensive block at Higher Level. Significant figures, state symbols and unbalanced half-equations are two or three hours of work and recover marks on every paper, which makes them the first thing a short block should address.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Extended-response explanation is the highest-yield target: a repeatable answer structure taught in three or four hours transfers across the whole paper. Fields and circuits can be rebuilt in a 20-hour block; a complete absence of mechanics cannot, and that is a feasibility question rather than an effort question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes this the subject where triage matters most. Data-analysis questions carry a large mark share and are usually the least practised, so an intensive block that starts there buys more marks per hour than one that starts with recall topics the student partly knows already.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is finite, visibly improvable and worth real marks, which makes it ideal intensive material. Higher Level quantitative content is the other target. Twenty hours is enough for both if the internal assessment commentaries are already submitted, which by the final term they are.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis responds well to intensive work because the skill is a transferable method rather than a body of content. Twenty hours can rebuild it. Paper 2 depends on the texts studied, so an intensive block there is constrained by what the student actually remembers of them.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source technique for Paper 1 is method rather than knowledge and can be taught in six to eight hours. The Higher Level regional option needs a bank of dated specifics, which an intensive block can build but only by abandoning parts of the syllabus deliberately and saying which.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level pre-released case study is the one Diploma component where intensive preparation is the standard approach rather than a rescue, because it is published in advance and rewards concentrated work. Twenty hours against the case study is a well-understood purchase.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A short block of six to eight hours, spread across three weeks, aimed at whether the essay answers its prescribed title and whether the exhibition objects can carry the argument. Hours beyond that produce diminishing returns, because the limiting factor is the student's own thinking time.

dubai/ib-crash-course.regionsIntro: Intensive blocks are bought from across Dubai, and the only local variable that matters is when a student can sit for three or four hours at a stretch. These are the communities the requests most often come from.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Villa community with schools inside or adjacent to it, so weekday mornings in the holidays are easy to use. Intensive blocks here are usually taken as four-hour mornings across a single week rather than spread over a month.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Established coastal community with short runs to the Jumeirah and Al Safa school corridor. Families here often buy a block in the spring break and a second shorter one in the final fortnight, which is the more expensive way to buy the same hours.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed villa stock with a strong British and IB school presence nearby. Requests cluster in February and March, which is the right time: specialist availability tightens sharply from mid-April and the choice narrows to whoever is free.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Central location with a short commute, so students arrive home earlier and can take a late-afternoon intensive session during term. This makes a spread block of two hours twice a week viable here, which is a better format than it looks.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Apartment and villa mix close to the Jumeirah schools. Blocks are often shared between two siblings in consecutive sessions, and the economics of that are straightforward online: two sessions cost two sessions, with no travel gap between them.

regions.note: Family villa community with heavy weekend activity schedules, so holiday-week mornings carry most of the intensive work. The spring break is the most requested period and the slots go from February onwards.

modes.description: Three or four hours a day across four or five consecutive days, almost always in a holiday week. Best for rebuilding a paper format or a connected body of content, because the student holds the thread from one day to the next and nothing decays between sessions.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of an intensive block: hours against AED
paragraphs: Take the published market bands and multiply. A qualified online subject tutor in Dubai is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, with premium named tutors published as high as AED 650. Those figures come from published 2026 rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey. Multiplying them by realistic block sizes produces the table below, and the table is the most useful thing on this page because it makes the decision visible before the first session rather than after the fifth.

The second column of the decision is what each block can actually cover, and this is where most crash-course marketing goes quiet. Ten hours is one component or one connected topic set. Twenty hours is one paper format plus two or three topic gaps. Forty hours is a genuine rebuild of one subject at Standard Level, or most of one at Higher Level if the foundations are intact. Nothing in this range re-teaches two years of a Higher Level science from nothing, and a provider implying otherwise is selling hope.

A third number belongs in the calculation and is usually left out: what the same money does spread differently. Twenty specialist hours at AED 300 is AED 6,000, which at the same rate is also a weekly hour for two full terms, or ten hours now and ten hours after the mocks when the evidence is better. For a student whose losses are habits, the spread version produces more because habits need repetition rather than immersion. For a student rebuilding a paper format three weeks out, the block wins.

sections.heading: What moves the number in Dubai specifically
paragraphs: Seven factors account for nearly all the variation, and only two of them are about the tutor. The largest is lead time. A block booked in February draws on the full specialist pool at ordinary rates; a block booked in the last fortnight before papers draws on whoever has a gap, which both raises the effective price and lowers the match quality. Families consistently underestimate this, and it is the single most expensive mistake available in this market.

Level and subject scarcity come next. A Standard Level Economics block is straightforward to staff. A Higher Level option topic or a second language A subject is a small pool before any timing constraint is applied, and scarcity shows up as either a higher rate or a longer wait. Format is the third factor: a group intensive in a Dubai tuition centre is materially cheaper per hour than one-to-one and gives a student fewer of their own questions answered, which is a real trade rather than a false economy.

The remaining factors are the ones parents can actually control. Session length changes the effective rate, because four-hour days are usually quoted as hours rather than at a premium. Whether the internal assessment is already submitted changes what the hours are allowed to do. And the tier of tutor you buy should follow the problem: paying specialist rates to fix significant-figure errors is spending AED 450 an hour on something that a careful tutor at the lower end of the qualified band fixes equally well.

sections.heading: Twenty hours now against a weekly hour for two terms
paragraphs: This is the comparison that actually decides value, and almost nobody publishes it. Twenty specialist hours and a weekly hour for two terms can cost the same money at Dubai market rates, and they produce different results depending on one thing: whether the problem is a habit or a hole. Habits need repetition across weeks, because the student has to practise the new behaviour under their own steam and come back with evidence. Holes need immersion, because partial content taught in fragments decays between sessions.

In practice most Diploma problems are a mixture, which argues for splitting the money. Ten hours as a block to rebuild the paper format, then a weekly hour to maintain and extend it, is usually stronger than either pure option, and it has the practical advantage of putting a measurement point in the middle. The block produces a marked paper; the weekly hour produces practice; the second marked paper six weeks later shows whether the money worked.

There is also a timing asymmetry worth naming. A weekly hour started in September can still become a block in April if the evidence says so. A block bought in April cannot retrospectively become a term of weekly hours. Families who start early keep both options; families who wait have one, at the worst price, with the smallest choice of tutor. That is the strongest financial argument on this page and it has nothing to do with teaching quality.
