sections.heading: Where the hours should go: triage by component weighting
paragraphs: Hours should follow marks, and marks are not evenly distributed. In a typical Diploma subject the external papers carry roughly 70 to 80 per cent of the grade and the internal assessment the remainder, which means that by the final term, with the internal assessment submitted, the entire addressable pool is the papers. That sounds obvious and is routinely ignored: families buy intensive blocks that spend a quarter of the hours on an internal assessment that is already gone.

Within the papers, the allocation should follow both weighting and recoverability. A Paper 2 worth 35 per cent of the grade where the student scores badly for structural reasons is the best target available: large pool, repairable fault. A Paper 3 worth 20 per cent at Higher Level where the student has never seen the format is also strong, because format is quick to teach. A paper where the student already performs near their ceiling is the worst target, however much they dislike it.

The practical method is to mark one recent paper per candidate subject before any hours are allocated. That produces a mark breakdown by question type, and the breakdown decides the plan. It routinely changes which subject gets the block: a family convinced that Chemistry is the problem often discovers that the Chemistry losses are content, slow and expensive, while the Mathematics losses are presentation, fast and cheap. The same money then buys two grade bands instead of half of one.

sections.heading: The calendar that decides whether a block is still worth buying
paragraphs: Dubai schools sit the May session, and the practical consequence is that the useful buying window for an intensive block runs from about January to early April. Before January the evidence is thin, because the mocks have not happened. After early April two things happen together: specialist availability tightens, and the number of weeks left stops being enough for content work, which narrows what the hours can do to format and technique alone.

Exact IB dates are not published on this page on purpose. The IB sets the session window, the results release and the enquiry-upon-results deadlines, and they are administered through the school, so the only reliable source is your school's IB coordinator or the IB's own site. Any tutoring page quoting you a specific IB examination or results date should be treated as unverified until you have checked it there. Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates openly and those can be relied on; the IB restricts automated access to its pages, so we do not reproduce its dates.

What is worth planning around are the school's own dates, which the school will give you: the mock window, the internal assessment deadlines, the last teaching day and the study-leave start. A block that begins the week after study leave starts is the most common shape in Dubai and often the least effective, because by then the student is self-managing six subjects. A block in the spring break, two or three weeks earlier, does more with the same hours.

sections.heading: Group crash courses in Dubai, and the arithmetic of a shared rate
paragraphs: Group intensives are the main competitor to a one-to-one block, and the honest comparison is about what each format is good at rather than which is better. A tuition centre running a Higher Level Chemistry revision course for eight students can charge materially less per student per hour, because the cost of the teacher is divided. For content delivery where the whole group shares a gap, that is efficient and sensible.

What a group cannot do is diagnose. The reason an intensive block produces marks is that the first session identifies which two or three things are costing this particular student their grade, and the remaining hours attack those. In a group of eight, the hours attack the average of eight different problems, which is nobody's problem. A student whose losses are idiosyncratic, and most are, gets the content they already had delivered again in a different voice.

The sensible structure, where a family wants both, is to use the group course for content coverage and buy a short one-to-one block for diagnosis and paper marking. Four hours of one-to-one spent marking the student's own papers against the markscheme, alongside a group revision course, is usually a better purchase than either alone. It also makes the group course more useful, because the student arrives knowing which parts to pay attention to. The sequence matters as well: the marking should come first, so the group hours are spent listening for the right things rather than being reviewed afterwards for whatever stuck.

sections.heading: What a crash course cannot do, and when we decline the booking
paragraphs: Three declines come up regularly and all three are arithmetic rather than policy. The first is a Higher Level science or mathematics with a near-total content deficit and under four weeks left. Twenty hours against two years of missing foundations produces a student who has seen the material once, which is not the same as being able to use it under time pressure. The honest answer is to say which two subjects still have reachable marks and spend the money there.

The second is a request to produce or finish assessed work. Students arrive in the final term with an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay unfinished and ask for it to be handled. A tutor can teach the content, explain the published criteria, read what the student has written and ask the questions the criteria ask. A tutor cannot supply sentences, insert sources or complete a section. An IB malpractice finding falls on the candidate and can cost the Diploma, which makes this the easiest refusal in the business.

The third is a block bought as reassurance rather than for marks. A parent two weeks from the session who buys forty hours across five subjects is buying the feeling of having acted. The student loses revision time to sessions that cannot be absorbed, and the family spends in the region of AED 8,000 to 18,000 at specialist rates for it. We would rather set out the arithmetic, decline part of the booking and keep the part that works than take the whole thing and explain afterwards.

sections.heading: How delivery, scheduling and coverage work for an intensive block
paragraphs: Sessions run online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For an intensive block that model has a specific advantage: the tutor is chosen for having taught the exact component the block targets, rather than for being able to reach your community for four consecutive mornings, which in April is a very short list.

Scheduling an intensive block works best in the mornings. A four-hour block from 09:00 in a holiday week produces materially better retention than the same four hours from 16:00, and a student who sits a paper at 09:30 is working at roughly the time the real examination will run. During Ramadan the pattern changes: late morning and post-Iftar are the viable windows, and timed-paper work is harder during fasting hours, so blocks in that period are usually better spent on content and technique.

Coverage is stated before anything is sold. Common Diploma subjects at both levels can usually be staffed within a few days, including for a consecutive-day block. Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects take longer and tighten sharply from mid-April. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so rather than implying a local presence. If we cannot staff the block properly in the time available, we say that instead of substituting a generalist.

process.title: Send one recent marked paper per candidate subject
process.description: Not a report and not a predicted grade. A marked paper, for each subject you are considering funding. The mark breakdown decides which subject gets the hours, and it frequently overturns the family's assumption about which subject is the problem.

process.title: Free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: One session, no card details taken, no obligation. The tutor marks a paper against the current markscheme and reports whether the losses are form, question reading, narrow content or wholesale content absence. Those four findings have very different costs per mark recovered.

process.title: Get the feasibility answer in writing
process.description: Before any hours are bought: what the block can reach in the weeks remaining, what it is going to abandon deliberately, and what it cannot do at any size. If the answer is that a subject is not recoverable in the time available, you should have that sentence in writing rather than discovering it in week two.

process.title: Choose the shape as well as the size
process.description: Consecutive days for a paper format or connected content; two hours twice a week for topic gaps and habit work; six to eight hours for a single named component. The same hours at the same rate produce different results in different shapes, and the shape should follow the diagnosis.

process.title: Measure at the start and at the end
process.description: A marked paper before the block and a marked paper after it, under the same conditions. That is the only way to know whether AED 4,000 to 9,000 bought anything. Ask for both totals in writing, with the breakdown by question type, and keep them.

whyPoints.title: The arithmetic is published before you buy
whyPoints.description: Block sizes against the published Dubai market bands, with what each size can honestly cover. No page in this market shows the multiplication, which is why families routinely buy forty hours when twenty aimed properly would have done more.

whyPoints.title: Hours allocated by component weighting
whyPoints.description: Marks are not evenly distributed, so the hours are not either. Nothing is spent on an internal assessment already submitted, and the largest paper with a repairable fault gets the biggest allocation. The allocation is written down before the block starts.

whyPoints.title: A written feasibility answer
whyPoints.description: Including when the answer is no. A Higher Level content deficit with four weeks left is not recoverable at any block size, and saying so in writing is more useful to a family than selling the hours and explaining in May.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here comes from a published 2026 rate card or Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey, with the band and the format named. They are the market's numbers, not ours. Three of the six pages ranking for Dubai IB queries publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: Dates from the school, not from us
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson publish their series dates openly and we cite them. The IB restricts automated access to its pages, so we do not reproduce IB session or results dates; your school's IB coordinator is the source. A tutoring page quoting IB dates should be checked before you plan around it.

whyPoints.title: Refusals we are willing to make
whyPoints.description: We will not write, finish or produce an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and we will not sell forty hours across five subjects a fortnight before the session. Both refusals cost us the booking and protect the candidate.

faqs.question: What does an IB crash course cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Work it out from the published bands. A qualified online subject tutor in Dubai is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, so a 20-hour block runs roughly AED 3,000 to 6,000 at the first band and AED 4,000 to 9,000 at the second. An eight-hour targeted block is AED 1,200 to 3,600. Those figures come from published 2026 rate cards and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey; they are market rates rather than our price list, and group courses are materially cheaper per hour.

faqs.question: How many hours does a crash course actually need to be?
faqs.answer: It depends on the target rather than the subject. Eight hours is enough for one narrow component finished properly: a Paper 1 format, an essay structure, the quantitative half of Higher Level Economics. Twenty hours covers one paper format plus two or three topic gaps. Forty hours can rebuild a Standard Level subject or most of a Higher Level one where the foundations are intact. Nothing in this range re-teaches two years of content from nothing, and a provider implying it can is selling hope rather than hours.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start six weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: For technique, no. For content, usually. Six weeks is enough to rebuild a paper format, fix form faults such as unshown working or dropped units, and teach a repeatable structure for extended-response questions. It is not enough to install a year of missing Higher Level content in a way that survives time pressure. The honest answer comes from marking one recent paper: if the losses are form and question reading, six weeks is plenty, and if they are wholesale content, we will say which subjects still have reachable marks.

faqs.question: Which subject should get the block if we can only fund one?
faqs.answer: The one where the marks are most recoverable, which is not always the one with the lowest grade. Mark one recent paper per candidate subject and look at the breakdown: a subject losing marks to presentation and question reading is cheap and fast to fix, while a subject losing them across the whole syllabus is slow and expensive. Weigh consequence too, since a university condition may rest on one subject. Families often arrive certain it is Chemistry and leave having funded Mathematics, because that is where the same money buys more.

faqs.question: Why does booking in April cost more than booking in February?
faqs.answer: Because availability collapses. In February the full specialist pool is reachable at ordinary published rates and you can choose the tutor who has taught your exact component. In the last fortnight before papers you are choosing from whoever has a gap, which raises the effective price and lowers the match quality at the same time. Lead time is the single biggest controllable factor in both the cost and the usefulness of an intensive block, and it is the mistake this market makes most often.

faqs.question: Is a group revision course in Dubai a false economy?
faqs.answer: No, it is a different product. A centre running a group course divides the teacher's cost across the group, so content coverage is genuinely cheaper per hour, and for a cohort sharing one gap that works well. What a group cannot do is diagnose one student's specific losses or mark their own papers properly. The strongest combination for most families is a group course for content plus four hours of one-to-one spent marking the student's own scripts, which also makes the group hours more useful.

faqs.question: Should we buy twenty hours now or a weekly hour for two terms?
faqs.answer: They can cost the same at Dubai market rates and they fix different problems. Habits, form faults and question reading need weekly repetition, because the student has to practise under their own steam and come back with evidence. Content holes need immersion, because fragments decay between sessions. Most Diploma problems are a mixture, so splitting the money works well: a ten-hour block to rebuild the method, then a weekly hour to embed it, with a marked paper at each end to show whether it worked.

faqs.question: Can a crash course help with an unfinished internal assessment?
faqs.answer: It can help the student finish it themselves, and no further. A tutor can teach the content the investigation needs, explain what each published criterion asks for, read what the student has written and ask the questions the criteria ask. A tutor cannot supply sentences, insert sources or complete a section. We refuse those requests because an IB malpractice finding falls on the candidate and can cost the Diploma, and because the school-appointed supervisor is the person who signs the authenticity declaration.

faqs.question: When are the IB exams, and why will you not print the dates?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools sit the May session, and the exact window, the results release and the enquiry-upon-results deadlines are set by the IB and administered through your school. We do not reproduce IB dates because the IB restricts automated access to its own pages, which means no date we could print here would be verified, and an unverified date on a revision page is worse than no date. Ask your school's IB coordinator, or check the IB's site directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published openly and we do cite those.

faqs.question: Does a crash course work better in the morning?
faqs.answer: Clearly, yes. A four-hour block from 09:00 in a holiday week retains materially better than the same hours from 16:00, and a student sitting a timed paper at 09:30 is working close to the time the real examination runs. During Ramadan the viable windows are late morning and after Iftar, and because timed-paper work is harder during fasting hours, blocks in that period are usually better spent on content and technique. The spring break is the most requested period and those slots go from February.

faqs.question: Can one block cover two subjects?
faqs.answer: It can be split, but understand what that buys. Forty hours across two subjects is two 20-hour blocks, which at specialist rates is AED 8,000 to 18,000, and it delivers paper technique in both subjects with content recovery in neither. If both subjects have format problems that is a reasonable purchase. If one has a content deficit it is not, and the better plan is to fund one subject properly and spend a smaller sum on marking the other's papers.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor says the block will not work?
faqs.answer: You get that in writing before you pay, with the reason and an alternative. The usual alternatives are to fund a different subject where the marks are reachable, to buy a shorter targeted block against one component, or to spend the money on marking and feedback rather than teaching. We would rather decline part of a booking than take the whole thing and explain in May, and declining happens most often with a Higher Level content deficit inside four weeks.

faqs.question: Is an intensive block useful for a November session retake?
faqs.answer: It is one of the better uses of the format, because the targeting is evidence-led rather than predictive. The student has sat the papers and the component marks show exactly where the grade went, so the hours can be allocated precisely instead of being spread as insurance. Session dates, registration deadlines and the enquiry window are set by the IB and administered through the school, so confirm all of them with your IB coordinator before planning the block or committing to a retake.

faqs.question: How quickly can a 20-hour block be staffed in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For common Diploma subjects at either level, usually within a few days, including for four consecutive mornings. Higher Level option topics and second language A subjects take longer, and availability tightens sharply from mid-April, which is the argument for booking in February. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so rather than implying a local presence. If we cannot staff it properly in the time left, we say that rather than substituting a generalist.

faqs.question: Where do the sessions take place?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. For an intensive block that matters practically: the tutor is chosen for having taught the exact component the hours are aimed at, rather than for being able to reach your community for four consecutive mornings, which in April is a very short list in any Dubai community.

dubai/ib-crash-course.closingHeading: Send one marked paper, get the arithmetic back
dubai/ib-crash-course.closingBody: The decision needs two inputs. A recent marked paper for each subject you are considering funding, and the number of weeks left on your school's calendar. Take the free 45-minute diagnostic, which takes no card details and carries no obligation, and you get the third: a written answer saying what a block of each size could reach, what it would deliberately abandon, and what it cannot do at any price. Then buy the smallest block that covers the target rather than the largest one you can afford.

intro.heading: Most Diploma tutoring decisions in Dubai are really about the evening
paragraphs: A Diploma student's weekday is already full. School finishes, there is a journey home, there may be sport or music, there is homework across six subjects, and somewhere in there a sixteen-year-old needs to eat and sleep. When a family searches for a home tutor, the attraction is usually not pedagogical. It is that somebody else handles the logistics: no travel for the student, no reorganising the household around a lesson, an adult physically present so the hour actually happens.

Those are good reasons and this page does not argue with them. It does the arithmetic instead, because the logistics of a visiting tutor in Dubai are harder than they look. A tutor crossing the emirate at 17:00 may spend twenty to forty minutes each way, which means a sixty-minute lesson occupies two and a half hours of their evening and allows them two bookings a night at most. That constraint shows up in the family's experience as a narrow choice of slot, a minimum session length of ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes, and a lesson that starts late when the road does not cooperate.

The second effect is on who teaches your child. A visiting tutor has to live within range of your community, which filters the available specialists by geography rather than by subject. For Maths Analysis at Standard Level that filter costs little. For Chemistry at Higher Level, for Maths Paper 3 investigation work, or for a specific internal assessment criterion, it is the difference between the right teacher and the nearest one. Diploma provision sits in a minority of Dubai's schools, so the specialist pool for any given Higher Level component is small to begin with.

IB Gram's answer is to remove the journey. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we would rather say that plainly on a page about home tutoring than let the wording imply otherwise. What a Dubai family gets instead is a session that starts on time, a length matched to what the student can absorb, and the subject specialist rather than the local one.

The rest of this page is practical. A realistic map of a Dubai school night, the Ramadan and holiday pattern that decides how many usable revision weeks actually exist, what to set up at home so a session is not spent fixing a microphone, how the schedule survives a travel month, and what each lesson should leave behind so a parent working late can still tell whether it is working. That last point is the one families underrate: a session nobody observed and that produced no record is a session you cannot evaluate.

dubai/ib-diploma-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Scheduling pressure differs by programme, and it is worth knowing which one your child is in before fixing a weekly slot, because the right length and time are not the same for an eleven-year-old and a DP2 candidate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus a core, which means the competition for a weekday evening is not between tutoring and leisure but between tutoring and six sets of homework. Sixty to ninety minutes is the usual session, and later slots work better than early ones for DP2 students who need the first part of the evening to clear immediate deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students commonly commute some distance to school, because provision is concentrated rather than spread evenly across the emirate. That journey eats the first part of the afternoon, which is why a 16:00 session that looks sensible on paper is often the slot families cancel most.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Shorter sessions, usually forty-five to sixty minutes, and earlier slots work better because concentration falls away in the evening. Criterion-based tasks mean work arrives in bursts rather than nightly, so a flexible slot is more valuable here than a rigid one.
programmes.countryNote: MYP families in Dubai often have a younger sibling in the same household, and the practical scheduling question is whether two children can be taught consecutively. Online that is simple; a visiting tutor who can teach both levels well is a much narrower search.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Thirty to forty-five minutes, and as early in the afternoon as the school run allows. This is the age group where a parent being physically nearby genuinely matters, so the realistic set-up is a shared room with an adult in earshot rather than a child alone with a screen.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's primary school day ends early enough that a late-afternoon session is feasible, which is not true of the senior years. Arabic as an additional language is the most requested primary subject in the emirate, and short frequent sessions suit it better than long weekly ones.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and internal assessment work
programmes.description: Scheduled in blocks around the school's deadlines rather than weekly, because the work is bursty: heavy at the scoping stage, light in the middle, heavy again before a supervisor meeting. Sessions are feedback and questioning on what the student has already written, and nothing more.
programmes.countryNote: The long Dubai summer break between the two Diploma years is where Extended Essay progress most often stalls. A handful of sessions scheduled deliberately across that break, even while a family is travelling, prevents the loss of several weeks in the second year.

dubai/ib-diploma-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below, each subject carries a note about how it behaves in a weekday evening slot, because the right time of day is not the same for an investigation session and a timed-paper session.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Works in any slot, including late, because the work is procedural enough to survive tiredness. Paper 3 investigation work is the exception and needs a fresher student, so it is better placed at a weekend slot than at 20:00 on a school night.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics work benefits from a screen and a saved file, which makes it one of the subjects that gains most from an online format. Interpretation writing needs more energy than calculation, so keep it out of the latest slots.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content sessions tolerate a late slot; investigation design does not, because it requires sustained decision-making rather than practice. The tightest Higher Level market in Dubai between February and May, so slot choice narrows exactly when families most want it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving sessions work late; uncertainty and evaluation work does not. A shared screen helps here, since working can be annotated and kept rather than rewritten from a photographed page.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response practice is best early in the evening, when a student can still write to time without flagging. Recall work is the exception and is genuinely effective in a short late session.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram work is efficient at any hour; evaluation writing is not, and a tired student produces explanation where the question wanted judgement. Internal assessment commentary feedback suits a weekend block.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The subject most sensitive to timing, because unseen analysis requires concentration a student may not have at 20:30. Where the schedule forces a late slot, use it for planning and structure rather than for writing.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work holds up late; essay writing does not. The historical investigation benefits from a longer weekend session where the student can work and be questioned in the same sitting.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application work needs an alert student, since the whole skill is reading a stimulus carefully. Framework recall is fine late and can be left to independent practice rather than paid time.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Needs thinking time rather than energy, which makes it one of the few components that works in a quiet late slot. Title choice and knowledge-question framing are best handled in a weekend session with the parent informed afterwards.

subjects.name: Extended Essay process support
subjects.description: Scheduled in blocks around supervisor deadlines, including deliberately across the summer break. Sessions are questioning and criterion feedback on the student's own material, with the school supervisor formally responsible throughout.

sections.heading: What a Dubai IB Diploma home tutor's evening actually looks like
paragraphs: Take a tutor living in a central community with a 17:00 booking in an outer villa development and a 19:00 booking two communities away. The first journey is twenty-five to forty minutes depending on the road. Arrival, settling and set-up takes five to ten. The lesson runs. Then the second journey, which at that hour is often the worse of the two. By the time they are home they have worked a four-hour evening and taught two hours of it.

Every feature of the in-home market follows from that arithmetic. The minimum session length of ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes exists to reduce journeys per paid hour. The narrow choice of slot exists because only two bookings fit. The hourly rate, published in this market at roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is included, has to cover the unpaid time in the car. None of that is a provider being difficult; it is the shape the service has to take.

The family-side consequences are specific. A 17:00 start requires the student to be home, fed and ready at 17:00, which for a Diploma student commuting from a concentrated school cluster frequently does not happen. A tutor delayed twenty minutes has lost a third of a sixty-minute lesson, and over a term that attrition is real rather than theoretical. And a session that runs to 120 minutes because the booking required it contains, for most Diploma students, about seventy minutes of useful work.

Removing the journey changes all three. An online session at 19:30 starts at 19:30. A seventy-minute session is bookable because nobody needs to justify a drive. And the tutor can be the person who has taught your child's exact Higher Level component rather than the person who lives fifteen minutes away. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and this arithmetic is the main reason we built the service the way we did.

sections.heading: A Dubai school night, mapped against realistic session windows
paragraphs: Dubai schools run a Monday-to-Friday week, with many operating a shortened Friday, and senior students frequently travel a reasonable distance because Diploma provision is concentrated in particular parts of the emirate. That produces a predictable evening shape, and the mistake most families make is booking a session at the time that suits the diary rather than the time that suits the student.

The late afternoon, roughly 15:30 to 16:30, is the worst slot for a Diploma student despite looking like the most sensible. They have just travelled, they have not eaten properly, and the day's work has not yet been sorted into what is urgent. The 16:30 to 18:00 window is workable for content and practice. The 18:30 to 20:30 window is better for a DP2 student who needs the earlier part of the evening to clear immediate deadlines, and it is also when an online slot has a clear advantage, because a visiting tutor at 20:00 is an unusual ask.

After 20:30, the only work worth doing is recall and light practice. Anything requiring sustained judgement, which means investigation design, unseen analysis, evaluation writing or coursework decisions, produces poor work and a discouraged student. We would rather move that work to a weekend block than take the booking and pretend the hour was equivalent.

Friday and the weekend are where the heavy thinking belongs. A longer session with a fresher student is where Extended Essay scoping, Theory of Knowledge title choice and internal assessment planning actually get done. The efficient Diploma pattern for most Dubai families is one weekday evening slot for subject practice plus an occasional weekend block for the core, rather than two identical weekday sessions.

sections.heading: What each session leaves behind, for a parent who was not in the room
paragraphs: The hardest part of buying tutoring in a household where both parents work is that nobody observes the product. A visiting tutor leaves after ninety minutes, the student says it was fine, and three months later a report arrives. That is not oversight, it is hope. The question worth asking any provider is what exists after the session that you can look at yourself.

In our format, four things do. A short written note naming what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target before the next session and anything a parent should act on, written to be read in half a minute. The annotated material itself, since work done on a shared screen is already a document. A recording on request, which students use more than parents do. And over time the accumulated notes, which are what the review at session four is actually based on.

Those artefacts let you see progress before a grade shows it, which matters because Diploma grades lag technique by a reporting cycle. The specific things to look for are a redone question the student previously failed, now done unaided; self-correction, where the student catches an error before the tutor does; and better questions from the student, asking what the command term wants rather than what the answer is. All three are visible in the notes if the tutor is writing them honestly.

There is a parallel evidence trail on coursework, and it matters for a different reason. Because internal assessment and the Extended Essay must be the student's own work, version history showing the student making the changes is a protection as well as a progress record. Feedback should arrive as comments and questions against criteria, never as inserted text. If you ever see a tutor's sentences in your child's document, something has gone wrong regardless of how helpful it looks.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the breaks, and how many usable weeks actually exist
paragraphs: A two-year Diploma looks like plenty of time until you count the weeks that are actually usable. The Dubai school year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a winter break and a spring break inside it. Ramadan moves earlier each year and shortens the school day, lowering late-afternoon energy and shifting many families to a post-Iftar slot. Eid holidays follow. National holidays punctuate the autumn term.

Counted honestly, a DP2 student has far fewer weeks of normal evening availability between the start of the year and final papers than a generic plan assumes. That is not a reason for panic; it is a reason to plan around the pattern rather than to discover it. Families who map the breaks onto their school's assessment calendar in September end up using them, because a break is also the only period in the year with uninterrupted daytime hours for coursework.

The practical adjustments are simple and worth agreeing up front. During Ramadan, move sessions to a post-Iftar slot and shorten them rather than cancelling, since continuity matters more than duration. Over winter and spring breaks, switch from weekly subject practice to coursework blocks, which is the work that benefits from daytime concentration. Over the long summer between the Diploma years, keep a small number of sessions running specifically on the Extended Essay, which is the single most common casualty of that break.

An online format makes each of those adjustments trivial rather than negotiable. A post-Iftar session requires no tutor to drive anywhere at an awkward hour. A session during a family's holiday in another time zone is a rescheduling question, not a cancellation. And a daytime block during a break can be scheduled with a specialist whose own working day is in a different part of the world.

sections.heading: Setting up at home so the hour is spent on chemistry
paragraphs: Online sessions fail for mundane reasons, and all of them are fixable in advance. The commonest is a shared room: a Diploma student working in a living space with a sibling and a television will lose a third of the session to interruption, and will also be reluctant to speak, which matters because speaking is how a tutor diagnoses. The second is kit: a phone screen is unusable for annotating a past paper, and a laptop with a working microphone is the minimum.

The third is material. A session where the first ten minutes are spent finding the marked script is a session a tenth shorter than it should be. Agree that the student has the relevant paper, the school's assessment brief and anything the tutor asked for, open before the start. We send a one-line reminder for this reason, and families who adopt it notice the difference inside two weeks.

The fourth is supervision, which is a safeguarding matter as well as a practical one. For a younger child, an adult should be within earshot and the session should run in a shared space rather than a bedroom. Keep lessons on the platform link rather than a tutor's personal channel, and ask that the first minute of a new match includes the tutor confirming their name, subject and level on camera with you present. None of that is burdensome and all of it is reasonable.

The fifth is connectivity, and it is the one honest limitation of this format. Most Dubai households have perfectly adequate connections, but a family in a building with genuinely unreliable service will have a worse experience online than with a visiting tutor, and we would rather say so than sell into it. Test it in the free first lesson, which is partly what the free first lesson is for.

sections.heading: When the family travels, and the schedule has to follow
paragraphs: Dubai households travel more than most, and a Diploma schedule that breaks every time a family leaves the emirate loses more weeks than it keeps. This is the single largest practical advantage of an online format and it is rarely discussed, because providers prefer to talk about teaching quality. A visiting arrangement stops entirely the moment the student is not at the address. An online arrangement is a rescheduling question.

The useful discipline is to agree in advance what happens. For a short trip, move the session rather than cancelling it, and shorten it if the itinerary is tight: thirty focused minutes keeps the habit and the target alive, whereas a cancellation resets both. For a long trip, switch the content to the work that travels well, which means coursework scoping, reading, and planning rather than timed paper practice that needs a quiet desk.

Time zones are easier than families expect. Gulf Standard Time sits between South Asia and Europe, so a student travelling west or east within a few hours of Dubai can usually keep roughly the same slot. A student in North America needs a different arrangement, which is worth setting up before departure rather than discovering mid-trip. Our tutors are in several time zones, which is why a repositioned slot is usually coverable.

The period that matters most is the long summer between the Diploma years. Extended Essay progress stalls there with great reliability, and students who return with no usable draft spend the weeks they needed for revision writing an essay instead. Three or four sessions scheduled deliberately across that break, at whatever hour the family's location allows, is the cheapest insurance available in the entire two-year programme.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for a visiting tutor, and what we deliver instead
paragraphs: For completeness, the published figures. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages are advertised at around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions, which works out near AED 200 to 225 an hour. Online qualified subject tutors sit lower at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and exam-level specialists run around AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270.

Those are other providers' published prices read in October 2026, named so you can verify them, and they are not IB Gram's rates. The useful observation is the overlap: a specialist online hour and a generalist visiting hour cost about the same, and one of them contains forty minutes of driving. For a Diploma family whose problem is a specific Higher Level component, that overlap is the whole argument.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We quote per match after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card, and we tell you which band a request sits in and why before anything is paid. Because no journey is involved, there is no minimum session length designed around a drive, so a seventy-minute booking is available where a visiting arrangement would have required two hours.

One thing worth stating about the permit, since it comes up in in-home conversations more than online ones. Any individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which u.ae states is granted free of charge for two years. It costs the tutor nothing, so asking to see it is reasonable, and no quote should itemise a charge for it.

sections.heading: Coverage, matching and what we will not promise
paragraphs: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time, with a short written note afterwards. Matching for common subjects at common levels usually takes a few days. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, longer between February and May when every Diploma cohort in the emirate is looking for the same specialists in the same eight weeks.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to the format or the subject depth. We tell you that before you commit rather than after, because a disclosed limit costs a family nothing and a concealed one costs them a fortnight at the worst possible moment of the year.

What we will not do: send anyone to a UAE address, because that is not a service we offer here; produce any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge piece, because everything submitted must be the student's own work and the risk falls on the candidate; or promise a result, because external outcomes depend on papers nobody has seen and boundaries set after marking.

What we will do is tell you when the problem is not a tutoring problem. A Diploma student whose work collapsed across all six subjects in one term is usually telling you about sleep, health or circumstances. A student with three Higher Levels that do not fit needs a timetable conversation with the school's coordinator while a change is still possible. Saying that costs us bookings and is the advice we would want for our own children.

process.description: Internal deadlines, mock windows, breaks and Ramadan. We ask for your school's assessment calendar and plan the hours into the fortnights where they change what is submitted, rather than spreading them evenly.

process.description: Post-Iftar timing, shortened sessions over busy periods, and rescheduling rather than cancelling during trips. Agreeing this in week one is what keeps a schedule alive through a year that contains several disruptions.

process.title: Use the notes as your oversight
process.description: A short written note follows every session naming the target. For a household where nobody is in the room at 19:30, that note is the product you are checking, and it is the record the session-four review is built from.

process.title: Review and adjust at session four
process.description: We look at whether the slot is working as well as whether the teaching is. Sometimes the fix is a different time, a shorter session or a weekend block for the heavy work, rather than more hours or a different tutor.

whyPoints.description: Because nobody is driving, there is no minimum booking designed to justify a trip. A Diploma student who works well for seventy minutes books seventy minutes instead of paying for a two-hour block.

whyPoints.description: Diploma provision sits in a minority of Dubai schools, so geographic matching would hand you the nearest science teacher. Online matching gives you the person who has taught your child's exact Higher Level component.

whyPoints.title: A record you can actually check
whyPoints.description: Annotated material, a short written note, and a recording on request. For working parents this is the only realistic oversight, and it is also what makes progress visible before a school report catches up.

whyPoints.title: The schedule survives the year
whyPoints.description: Post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, daytime blocks during breaks, and rescheduling by time zone when a family travels. Each of those is routine online and difficult or impossible with a visiting arrangement.

whyPoints.title: We say what we do not do
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. No production of assessed work. No promised results. Stating the limits is what makes the rest of the offer worth anything.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our address in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around the school week in Gulf Standard Time. We are explicit about this because the search term is the phrase parents use and it would be easy to let the wording imply otherwise. The practical trade is that you give up physical presence and gain a tutor chosen for your child's exact Higher Level component rather than for living nearby.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start on a school night?
faqs.answer: For most Dubai Diploma students, between 16:30 and 20:30, with 18:30 to 20:30 the most reliable window for a DP2 candidate who needs the earlier evening to clear immediate deadlines. The 15:30 to 16:30 slot looks sensible on a calendar and is the one most often cancelled, because the student has just finished a commute, has not eaten properly and has not yet sorted what is urgent. After 20:30, keep the work to recall and light practice; anything needing sustained judgement produces poor work and a discouraged student.

faqs.question: How much of a visiting tutor's session is lost to Dubai traffic?
faqs.answer: The teaching time is not lost, but the reliability is. A tutor crossing the emirate at 17:00 faces a twenty to forty minute journey each way, and evening traffic here is variable rather than merely slow. A twenty-minute delay costs a third of a sixty-minute lesson, and over a term that attrition is real. The arithmetic also explains the rest of the in-home market: a sixty-minute lesson occupies two and a half hours of the tutor's evening, which is why minimum session lengths of ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes exist and why slot choice is narrow.

faqs.question: How do we handle Diploma sessions during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Move them rather than cancelling them, and shorten them rather than fighting the energy curve. School days are shorter during Ramadan and late-afternoon concentration drops noticeably, so most families switch to a post-Iftar slot. Continuity matters more than duration here: a focused forty minutes keeps the target and the habit alive, while a month of cancellations resets both and lands the student back at the start in the weeks before final papers. Because no tutor has to drive anywhere at an awkward hour, the change is a rescheduling question rather than a negotiation.

faqs.question: What do we need at home for an online Diploma lesson to work properly?
faqs.answer: Five things, all mundane. A quiet space, or at least one without a television and a sibling, because a student who will not speak cannot be diagnosed. A laptop or tablet rather than a phone, since annotating a past paper on a phone screen is unusable. A working microphone. The relevant marked script and assessment brief open before the start, which saves the ten minutes otherwise spent hunting for them. And an adult within earshot for younger students, with the session in a shared room rather than a bedroom. Test all of it in the free first lesson.

faqs.question: Can the tutoring schedule follow us when we travel out of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and agreeing how in advance is what stops a travel month costing a term's momentum. For short trips, move the session and shorten it if the itinerary is tight. For longer trips, switch the content to work that travels well: coursework scoping, reading and planning rather than timed paper practice needing a quiet desk. Gulf Standard Time sits between South Asia and Europe, so a family travelling a few hours either way usually keeps roughly the same slot. North American travel needs a different arrangement, set up before departure rather than discovered mid-trip.

faqs.question: How do I know what happened in a lesson if I was not in the room?
faqs.answer: By looking at what the session left behind. Ours leaves a short written note naming what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target before the next session and anything you should act on, written to be read in half a minute. The annotated material is already a document, and a recording is available on request. Over a term those notes accumulate into the record the session-four review is built from. If notes stop arriving, raise it immediately rather than at the end of term, because they are the only oversight a working parent realistically has.

faqs.question: Should Diploma sessions continue through the winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: Change their purpose rather than their existence. A break is the only period in the Dubai year with uninterrupted daytime hours, which makes it the right time for the work a tired student cannot do on a school night: investigation design, Extended Essay scoping, Theory of Knowledge title choice, internal assessment planning. Trying to maintain a normal weekly practice timetable through a break usually fails, because the household rhythm has gone. Switch to a small number of longer daytime blocks aimed at coursework, then resume the weekly subject slot when term restarts.

faqs.question: Can two Diploma siblings be taught one after the other?
faqs.answer: Yes, and consecutive sessions are almost always better than a shared one. Where two students are at genuinely different levels, a shared session becomes two half-lessons and each child works above or below where they need to be. Back-to-back slots keep the attention undivided, allow a different specialist for each level, and still solve the household problem of disrupting one evening rather than two. We also keep the notes separate, so feedback on one child's Higher Level chemistry does not arrive blended with the other's Standard Level maths.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: For different work, yes. Weekday evening slots suit practice, content teaching and timed paper work, which a reasonably tired student can still do well. Weekend sessions suit the work that needs decisions rather than energy: investigation design, Extended Essay scoping, internal assessment planning and prescribed-title choice for Theory of Knowledge. The efficient pattern for most Dubai Diploma families is one weekday evening slot plus an occasional longer weekend block, rather than two identical weekday sessions competing with six subjects' worth of homework.

faqs.question: What happens if my child misses a session at short notice?
faqs.answer: Ask any provider this before you book, because school events, fixtures, illness and travel are routine in a Dubai term rather than exceptional. A reasonable policy names a notice period you can actually meet and says what happens to a session the tutor cancels as well as one the family cancels. We would rather move a session than lose it, and where a week is genuinely impossible we would rather shorten the next one than pretend the target survived untouched. A vague policy is worse than a strict one, because it gets interpreted after the disagreement.

faqs.question: How long should a Diploma session be on a school night?
faqs.answer: Sixty to ninety minutes for most students. The limiting factor is not willingness but the amount of genuinely demanding work a sixteen-year-old can produce after a full school day, which for most is around seventy minutes before the session turns into revision of ground already covered. Two-hour weekday bookings generally exist because a tutor needed the journey to be worthwhile, which is not a constraint online. If more time is genuinely needed, a weekend block is a better use of it than extending a school-night session past the point of usefulness.

faqs.question: Does my child need a room to themselves for an online lesson?
faqs.answer: Not a room to themselves, but a space where they will speak freely and will not be interrupted every few minutes. Speaking is how a tutor diagnoses, so a student who will not talk in front of a sibling loses much of the session's value. For younger students the opposite consideration applies and a shared space with an adult in earshot is the right arrangement rather than a bedroom. In a crowded apartment the practical fix is usually a time rather than a place: a slot when the main living space is quiet.

faqs.question: How do we keep Extended Essay work moving over the long summer?
faqs.answer: Schedule three or four short sessions deliberately across the break, at whatever hour the family's location allows, and give them a specific job: a scoped research question, a source list the student can actually reach, and a method they can defend. This is the single most reliable point of failure in a Dubai Diploma, because no deadline is visible and families travel. Students who return to the second year with no usable draft spend the weeks they needed for revision writing an essay instead. The work remains entirely the student's; a tutor questions and gives criterion feedback.

faqs.question: Does it matter if the tutor is in a different time zone from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not for the lesson, and it often helps the schedule. Gulf Standard Time sits between South Asia and Europe, so a Dubai evening slot falls within normal working hours for a wide pool of IB subject teachers, which is precisely why a specialist for a scarce Higher Level component is findable at all. What matters is that the slot is fixed in your time zone rather than theirs, and that it holds through term. If no UAE-based specialist is free for your component, we say so when quoting and tell you where the match would come from.

dubai/ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingHeading: Plan the evening, then plan the teaching
dubai/ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB Diploma home tutor in Dubai, start with the week rather than the subject: when your child is actually home, fed and able to think, and what happens to that slot during Ramadan, a break or a travel month. Then choose the format that survives it. IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, starting on time because nobody is driving, at a length matched to your child rather than to a journey, with a written note after each session. We do not offer home visits in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-diploma-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma subjects over live video to Dubai students. Each profile names the subjects, levels and components taught, and because the match is not constrained by geography, the specialist for a narrow Higher Level component is usually reachable.

intro.heading: What a Dubai family is actually buying when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: An online Diploma session is not a video call about chemistry. It is a shared document with two people working on it, one of whom knows where the marks are. That distinction is the whole thing, and it explains both why the format works and why some online tutoring is worthless: a tutor who talks at a camera for an hour has delivered a lecture, while a tutor who puts a past-paper question on a shared screen and makes the student work on it has delivered a lesson. The medium does not determine which one you get; the tutor does.

What the medium does determine is what survives. Work done on a shared screen is already a file. An annotated question, a method built up on a whiteboard, a marked answer with the criteria beside it: all of it can be saved and looked at again on Thursday. A session at a kitchen table leaves a page of handwriting and a student's memory of it. For a Diploma student revising across six subjects over two years, that accumulation is worth a surprising amount.

The second thing the medium determines is who is available. Diploma provision in Dubai sits in a minority of the emirate's 227 private schools, so the pool of teachers who have taught a specific Higher Level component to examination here is small. Online matching lifts the geographic constraint, which matters little for Maths Analysis at Standard Level and matters entirely for Chemistry at Higher Level, Paper 3 investigation work, or a specific internal assessment criterion. Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, between South Asia and Europe, so a Dubai evening slot falls inside working hours across a wide area.

The third thing is cost, which is the angle this page takes most seriously. Published in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included, while online qualified subject tutors are advertised from AED 150 and exam-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. The overlap is the useful part: a specialist online hour and a generalist visiting hour often cost the same, and one of them contains forty minutes of driving. Remove the journey and two things follow, a different price for the same teaching and a session length chosen by the student rather than by the road.

This page also states the limits, because a page that only sells the format is not worth reading. Laboratory practical work belongs to the school and always will. A student who genuinely will not engage with a screen is better served by a different intervention. And a household with unreliable connectivity will have a worse experience online than with a visiting tutor, which is one of the things the free first lesson exists to test. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

dubai/ib-diploma-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The online format suits the IB programmes differently, and it is worth knowing which parts of your child's programme it serves well before fixing a plan around it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The programme the format suits best. Six subjects with externally marked papers, internally assessed components and a core, all of which are document-based work that benefits from annotation, saved files and a specialist who may not live nearby. Sixty to ninety minutes is the usual session, with the shared screen carrying the past paper and the criteria side by side.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai Diploma candidate's scarcest resource is a teacher who has taught their exact Higher Level component. Because provision is concentrated in relatively few schools here, geographic matching narrows that pool sharply, while an online match at a Dubai evening hour does not. That is the practical reason most of our Diploma work is delivered this way.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Works well with shorter sessions of forty-five to sixty minutes, particularly for criterion literacy: putting a task sheet and the criteria on screen together and working out which criterion is holding a grade down. Younger MYP students need a shared family space and an adult in earshot rather than a closed door.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP families often have two children at different stages, and consecutive online sessions solve that more cleanly than a shared session does. It also removes the need to find one visiting tutor who can teach two levels well, which is a much narrower search than it sounds.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme where the format needs most care. Thirty to forty-five minutes is the ceiling, an adult should be nearby, and the session should run in a shared room. Reading fluency and number work transfer well; anything requiring physical manipulation of materials transfers poorly and we say so.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary timetables end early enough for an afternoon slot, which suits short frequent sessions. Arabic as an additional language is the emirate's most requested primary subject, and short repeated practice works better for it than a long weekly block.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and internal assessment
programmes.description: The components where the saved-document advantage is clearest. Feedback is given as comments and questions against criteria on material the student has already written, and version history shows who made each change, which is a protection as well as a record. Nothing is drafted or supplied by the tutor at any stage.
programmes.countryNote: Internal deadlines differ by several weeks between Dubai IB World Schools, so blocks are planned from your own school's calendar. The long summer break between the Diploma years is when Extended Essay work stalls, and an online schedule can follow a travelling family through it.

dubai/ib-diploma-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below, each subject carries a note on what the online format specifically adds or cannot provide. The honest entries are the useful ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Gains most from the format. Working is built on a shared whiteboard, saved and revisited, and method communication, the commonest source of lost marks, is easier to coach when both people can see the same line of working at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics work involves calculator output and spreadsheets, all of which are screen-native. A tutor can watch regression work being produced rather than hearing about it afterwards, which is where interpretation marks are won.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content, mechanisms and calculation work transfer fully. The scientific investigation can be designed, critiqued and written about online, but the practical work itself happens in the school laboratory, and no online provider should suggest otherwise.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving and uncertainty treatment work well on a shared screen, where a graph with error bars can be annotated jointly. Apparatus handling and measurement technique remain the school's domain.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response practice and data analysis transfer completely, and marked answers sit beside the criteria on one screen. Microscopy and dissection skills do not transfer and are not claimed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram work is better online than on paper, because a diagram can be built step by step, corrected and saved. Higher Level quantitative papers and the internal assessment commentaries both work entirely within the format.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis suits a shared screen, with the text annotated jointly in real time. The individual oral can be rehearsed on camera, which is closer to the assessed conditions than a rehearsal across a kitchen table.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source analysis is screen-native and essay planning benefits from a saved outline the student can return to. Archive-based investigation work depends on what the student can access, which is a library question rather than a format one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study work transfers fully, with the stimulus and the answer visible together so the application marks can be pointed at precisely. Group presentation practice is the one element that works better in a classroom.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Spoken practice is effective one-to-one over video, which gives a student more speaking time than a class of twenty does. Script writing works with a tablet and stylus or a document camera; agree which before the first session.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Entirely suited to the format, since the work is argument rather than material. Prescribed-title choice and knowledge-question framing happen in conversation with a shared document, and the student keeps the notes.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The subject with the strongest case for online delivery: code, documentation and theory all live on a screen already. It is also the thinnest specialist market in Dubai, which is why UAE-based coverage most often runs out here.

sections.heading: An online IB Diploma session in Dubai, minute by minute
paragraphs: A session that works has a predictable shape, and knowing it lets you judge whether you are getting one. The first five minutes are the previous target: what was set last week, what the student did with it, and whether it held. Not a general enquiry about how the week went, but a specific check on a specific thing, usually by asking the student to do it again.

The next forty to sixty minutes are the student working. A question appears on the shared screen and the student attempts it while the tutor watches the working appear. This is the part that distinguishes a lesson from a lecture, and it is also where the online format has a quiet advantage: the tutor can see the working being produced line by line, which is harder across a table where a student instinctively covers what they are writing. Interventions are short and specific, and a good tutor says less than a parent expects.

The last ten minutes are the record. The tutor marks or part-marks what was produced, states where the marks were and were not available, saves the annotated file, and sets the next target. Then a short note goes to the parent: what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target, and anything to act on. That note is the product a parent can actually inspect, and it should be readable in half a minute.

What should not be happening: a tutor explaining for forty minutes, a student watching a screen share passively, or a session that ends without anything written down. If any of those is the pattern after three sessions, the format is not the problem and the match should change. We review at session four partly to catch exactly that, and changing tutor at that point costs nothing.

sections.heading: Science and the laboratory: the limit we will not talk around
paragraphs: Every Diploma science subject includes a substantial internally assessed investigation, and a large part of that work is practical. An online tutor cannot run a laboratory, cannot supervise apparatus, and cannot substitute for the hours a student spends measuring something that behaves unexpectedly. Any provider implying otherwise is selling something they do not have, and the student is the one who discovers it.

What an online tutor genuinely can do with the investigation is considerable, and it sits either side of the practical work. Before: critique the research question for scope and controllability, ask what is uncontrolled, test whether the data can actually be gathered with school apparatus in the time available, and talk through the method until the student can defend each step. Those conversations are where most investigation marks are won or lost, and they are entirely document-based.

After: work on uncertainty treatment, graph construction with error bars, the distinction between a limitation and an improvement, and the evaluation writing that most students underprepare. All of that is screen-native and benefits from the shared annotation, since a graph can be marked up jointly in a way a photographed page cannot.

The same honesty applies elsewhere. Group presentation practice works better in a classroom. Microscopy and dissection skills do not transfer. A student who needs an adult physically present to start working at all may need something other than an online tutor, and a household with genuinely unreliable connectivity will have a worse experience in this format than with a visiting arrangement. We would rather name those cases than argue with them.

sections.heading: Oral components over video, which is closer than it sounds
paragraphs: Several Diploma components are spoken: the individual oral in language and literature subjects, the oral assessments in language acquisition, and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary where schools ask for a presented version. Parents reasonably assume these need a person in the room. In practice video rehearsal is closer to the assessed conditions than a kitchen-table rehearsal is, because the student is speaking to a device, to time, with notes they are not allowed to read from.

The work itself is structural rather than conversational. An individual oral fails for predictable reasons: a global issue chosen too broadly, extracts that do not actually support the argument, time mismanaged so the second text gets three minutes, and a reliance on notes that the conditions do not allow. Each of those is diagnosable from one rehearsal and fixable in two or three. None of it requires physical presence.

For language acquisition, the gain is speaking time. A student in a class of twenty speaks for a small fraction of a lesson; a student in a one-to-one video session speaks for most of it. That is the single biggest determinant of oral fluency improvement, and it is a quantity argument rather than a pedagogical one. Recording a rehearsal and watching it back is also unusually effective here, and students who resist it the first time generally ask for it the second.

The limits: a tutor cannot conduct the actual assessment, cannot see the stimulus material the school will use, and should not be rehearsing a script. The school runs the assessment under its own conditions. What a tutor rehearses is a shape that survives an unseen extract, which is exactly what the criteria reward.

sections.heading: What disappears from the price when the journey disappears
paragraphs: Here is the cost argument, stated as plainly as the numbers allow. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Published online rates for qualified subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and exam-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are other providers' figures, named, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's prices.

Three cost components come out of the hour when nobody drives. The first is the travel time itself, twenty to forty minutes each way across the emirate at the hours families want. The second is the minimum session length, usually ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes, which exists to make a journey worthwhile and which obliges a family to buy time their child cannot use. The third is less visible: the geographic filter on who can teach, which pushes a family towards the nearest available tutor rather than the right one, and a mismatched tutor is the most expensive purchase in this market because the hours achieve nothing.

What does not change is the teaching itself. The subject guide is the same, the criteria are the same, the marked script is the same script. Anyone claiming online teaching is inherently superior is overselling, exactly as anyone claiming it is inherently inferior is. The honest claim is narrower: for document-based assessed work, which is most of the Diploma, the format is equivalent, and it removes three costs that have nothing to do with teaching.

There is one cost the format adds, and it is small but real. A household needs a usable device, a workable space and a stable connection. Most Dubai homes have all three. Where one is missing, the free first lesson will show it, which is part of why that lesson exists rather than a fifteen-minute introductory call.

sections.heading: Buying by session length instead of by package
paragraphs: Once travel is out of the equation, session length becomes a genuine choice rather than a constraint, and that is where a Dubai family can take real money out of a tutoring budget without taking anything out of the teaching. Most Diploma students sustain roughly seventy minutes of genuinely demanding work after a school day. Past that, a session becomes revision of what has already been covered, which is useful at a quarter of the intensity and not worth a specialist rate.

So the efficient purchase for a weekday evening is sixty to ninety minutes, and for a primary or lower-MYP student thirty to forty-five. A two-hour weekday booking is almost always a legacy of a travel constraint rather than a teaching judgement. Where more time is genuinely needed, a weekend block with a fresher student does more than extending a school-night session past the useful point.

Packages deserve the same scrutiny. Advertised monthly figures in this market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions, which implies roughly AED 100 a session and tells you which band of tutor is teaching, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which implies roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Convert any package to a cost per hour before comparing it with anything.

Our approach is to quote per match after a free trial rather than publish a rate card, and to pay per session until the match has proven itself. The risk in a prepaid package is not the price, it is the expiry and the notice period: unused hours lapsing at month end during a travel week turns a discount into a loss. Ask four questions of any package before buying one, and reasonable answers to all four make it a genuine saving.

sections.heading: A Dubai evening slot and the tutor pool it reaches
paragraphs: Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, which is an unusually convenient position for this purpose. A Dubai session at 18:00 falls in the late afternoon for a tutor in Europe, mid-evening for one in South Asia, and the middle of the working day for one further east. That means an evening slot that suits a Diploma student after school also suits a wide pool of IB subject teachers at a reasonable hour of their own day, which is the structural reason a narrow Higher Level component is findable at all.

That matters because of how concentrated Diploma provision is locally. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools with 17 curricula in 2024-25, and the UK curriculum is by far the largest share by enrolment while the International Baccalaureate is a much smaller one. The emirate is adding three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools for 2026-27, creating 16,846 new places, so the pool is growing. It is still the case that a specific Higher Level component may have very few resident teachers who have taught it to examination.

The practical upshot for a family: ask where the tutor is based, because it affects the slot's stability rather than the teaching. A tutor whose own evening is your evening will hold a slot through term more reliably than one for whom your slot is the middle of their night. We set slots in your time zone and tell you where the tutor is, so that a schedule is agreed on real information.

The format also makes the slot portable, which matters in a city where families travel. A session can be repositioned to the time zone a family is actually in, which is a rescheduling question rather than a cancellation. That is particularly useful across the long summer break between the Diploma years, where Extended Essay progress stalls with great reliability.
