sections.heading: Safeguarding, recordings and data when the student is a minor
paragraphs: Online lessons with a child involve personal data and a live video connection, and both deserve clear rules rather than a privacy page nobody reads. The UAE has a federal data protection framework in Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection, and the sensible posture for any tutoring provider is to collect the minimum needed, say what it is for, and delete it on request.

What we need is narrow: a name, a contact for the parent, the school, the subjects and levels, and whatever work the family chooses to share. What we do not need and do not ask for is a photograph of the child, a full academic history or any medical information, unless a parent volunteers something relevant to how a session should run. If a form ever asks your child's school, grades and photograph without saying why, that is a reasonable moment to stop filling it in, wherever you are buying from.

On recordings, the rule is that they happen on request rather than by default, they are shared with the family that asked for them, and they are deleted on request. Students use them more than parents do, usually to rewatch one difficult explanation. A recording is not a substitute for being told what happened, which is what the written note is for.

On safeguarding, four practical things. Sessions run on the platform link rather than a tutor's personal channel. A new match begins with the tutor confirming their name, subject and level on camera with the parent present. Younger students work in a shared family space with an adult in earshot rather than behind a closed door. And a parent is welcome to sit in on any session, at any time, without arranging it in advance; a provider who discourages that is telling you something.

sections.heading: Coverage, honest limits and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Matching for common Diploma subjects at common levels usually takes a few days. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, and longer between February and May, when Diploma cohorts across the emirate converge on the same specialists in the same eight weeks. Computer Science at Higher Level is the request most likely to exhaust UAE-based coverage at any time of year.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones, at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or subject depth. We tell you at the quoting stage rather than later. Where we cannot cover a request at all, we say so instead of substituting a generalist and leaving you to find out in week three.

What we will not claim. That online teaching is inherently better than a tutor in the room; it is equivalent for document-based assessed work and worse for some things, and we have named which. That we can run laboratory practical work; we cannot, and that stays with the school. That we can produce any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge piece; everything submitted must be the student's own work and the risk of crossing that line falls on the candidate. And that we can promise a result, which nobody can.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We quote per match after a free trial lesson with no card details taken, tell you which band the request sits in and why, and recommend paying per session until the match has proven itself at the session-four review.

faqs.question: What actually happens during an online IB Diploma lesson?
faqs.answer: A good session has a shape. Five minutes checking the previous target by asking the student to redo it unaided. Then forty to sixty minutes of the student working on a question on the shared screen while the tutor watches the working appear and intervenes briefly at the point of error. Then ten minutes marking what was produced, saving the annotated file and setting the next target, followed by a four-line note to the parent. What should not be happening is a tutor explaining for forty minutes to a passive student. If that is the pattern after three sessions, change the match rather than the format.

faqs.question: Is an online tutor as effective as one sitting beside my child?
faqs.answer: For document-based assessed work, which is most of the Diploma, the two are equivalent, and the online format has one specific advantage: the tutor sees the working appear line by line on a shared screen, where across a table a student instinctively covers what they are writing. Where online is genuinely worse is laboratory practical work, group presentation practice, and any student who will not start working at all without an adult physically present. We name those cases rather than arguing with them, and the free first lesson exists partly to test which situation you are in.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the Diploma scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: With most of it, but not the laboratory part, and no honest provider should suggest otherwise. What transfers fully is the work either side of the practical: critiquing the research question for scope and controllability, checking whether data can realistically be gathered with school apparatus, talking through the method until the student can defend each step, then uncertainty treatment, graphing with error bars, limitations and evaluation writing. Those are where investigation marks actually move. The practical execution happens in your school's laboratory under the subject teacher, who also authenticates the work.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor prepare my child for the individual oral?
faqs.answer: Yes, and video rehearsal is closer to the assessed conditions than a rehearsal across a kitchen table, because the student is speaking to a device, to time, without reading from notes. Individual orals fail for predictable reasons: a global issue chosen too broadly, extracts that do not support the argument, time mismanaged so the second text gets three minutes. Each is diagnosable from one rehearsal. What a tutor cannot do is conduct the assessment, see the school's stimulus material, or rehearse a script, since the criteria reward a shape that survives an unseen extract.

faqs.question: What does my child keep after an online session?
faqs.answer: Four things. The annotated material worked on, since anything done on a shared screen is already a file. The marked answer with the criteria beside it, showing where marks were and were not available. A named target for the week, which gives the days between sessions a job. And a recording of a difficult explanation if the student asked for one. For a Diploma student revising across six subjects over two years, that accumulation becomes genuine revision material, which a page of handwriting from a session at the table does not.

faqs.question: Is online Diploma tutoring cheaper than a tutor who travels in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures say yes at the qualified level and overlapping at the specialist level. In-home one-to-one is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included; online qualified subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; and online exam-level specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The interesting part is the overlap: a specialist online hour and a generalist visiting hour often cost the same, and one of them contains forty minutes of driving. Those are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Can we book a 45-minute online session rather than a full hour?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for younger students it is usually the right length. Minimum bookings of ninety or a hundred and twenty minutes exist because a visiting tutor needs the journey to be worthwhile, which is not a constraint here. Most Diploma students sustain about seventy minutes of genuinely demanding work after a school day, so sixty to ninety is the usual range for them, while a primary or lower-MYP student is better served by thirty to forty-five. Matching length to what a child can actually use is the simplest way to reduce a tutoring budget without reducing the teaching.

faqs.question: Where are your tutors based, and does the location matter?
faqs.answer: It matters for the stability of your slot rather than for the teaching. Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, so a Dubai session at 18:00 is late afternoon in Europe, mid-evening in South Asia and inside the working day further east, which is why a wide pool of IB subject teachers can hold a Dubai evening slot at a reasonable hour of their own day. A tutor for whom your slot falls in the middle of their night will hold it less reliably through term. We set slots in your time zone and tell you where the tutor is, so the schedule is agreed on real information.

faqs.question: What personal data do you collect about my child?
faqs.answer: The minimum needed to match and teach: a name, a contact for the parent, the school, the subjects and levels, and whatever work the family chooses to share. We do not ask for a photograph of the child, a full academic history or medical information unless a parent volunteers something relevant to how sessions should run. The UAE has a federal data protection framework in Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, and the sensible posture is to collect little, say what it is for and delete on request. If any provider's form asks for a child's photograph and grades without explaining why, that is worth questioning.

faqs.question: Are lessons recorded, and who can see a recording?
faqs.answer: Recordings are made on request rather than by default, shared with the family that asked, and deleted on request at any time. In practice students use them more than parents do, usually to rewatch a single difficult explanation rather than a whole hour. A recording is not a substitute for being told what happened in the session, which is what the short written note is for: what was covered, what the student managed unaided, the target and anything to act on. You are also welcome to sit in on any session without arranging it beforehand.

faqs.question: What kind of internet connection does an online Diploma lesson need?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect, but it has to be stable rather than fast. A shared screen with annotation and a video window runs comfortably on an ordinary household broadband connection; the thing that breaks a session is intermittency rather than bandwidth. The practical requirements are a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, since annotating a past paper on a phone screen is unusable, and a working microphone, since speaking is how a tutor diagnoses. Test all of it during the free first lesson, which is part of why that lesson is a full one rather than a short call.

faqs.question: Can the tutor see my child's working as they write it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the format's real advantages. On a shared document or whiteboard, the working appears line by line to the tutor as the student produces it, which means a missing method line can be caught at the moment it is omitted rather than after the mark is lost. Across a table, students instinctively shield what they are writing until it is finished. For mathematics and the quantitative sciences, where most recoverable marks sit in unwritten method rather than wrong answers, that visibility is worth more than it sounds.

faqs.question: How do we handle a textbook or calculator during an online session?
faqs.answer: Agree it before the first lesson rather than losing ten minutes to it. A graphical calculator's screen can be shared directly or shown to the camera, and spreadsheet output can be screen-shared, which is usually better than a photograph. For a textbook or a school worksheet, a photograph sent before the session works, or the student can hold it to the camera for a quick reference. The one habit worth building is having the marked script, the assessment brief and anything the tutor asked for open before the session starts, which protects the first ten minutes.

faqs.question: What if my child will not engage with a screen at all?
faqs.answer: Then say so early and we will tell you honestly whether we think this is the right service. Some students need an adult physically present to start working, and no amount of good teaching over video substitutes for that. More often, though, the resistance is about the shape of the session rather than the medium: a student who was lectured at for three sessions will disengage from any format. Our first check is whether the student is being asked to work within the first five minutes. If they are and the resistance persists, a different intervention is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: How soon can an online Diploma tutor start in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Common subjects at common levels are usually matched within a few days, with the free first lesson scheduled in the slot you actually want. Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks, and longer between February and May when Diploma cohorts across the emirate converge on the same specialists. Computer Science at Higher Level is the request most likely to exhaust UAE-based coverage at any point in the year. Where nobody local is free, we say so when quoting and match from our wider pool at a Dubai-friendly hour, with the format and subject depth unchanged.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a timetable problem before it is a subject problem
paragraphs: Most families arrive at Diploma tutoring thinking they have a chemistry problem or a maths problem. Often they have a loading problem. A Diploma candidate carries six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course with two assessed pieces, a CAS programme, and in Dubai the mandatory subjects every private school must teach whatever curriculum it is licensed for. The grade that slipped is frequently the symptom of a week that does not fit, and the useful tutor is the one who notices that before selling thirty hours of chemistry.

That makes a Diploma tutor's first job diagnostic in a broader sense than usual. Which of the six subjects is actually at risk, as opposed to merely uncomfortable? Is the Extended Essay running quietly behind and about to consume a term? Are three Higher Levels producing more written work per week than this particular student can produce at all? Those questions have different answers for different students, and the answers determine whether tutoring, a timetable conversation with the school, or simply a better plan for the holidays is the right next move.

Dubai adds its own structure to this. The emirate's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK curricula at well over a third of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate a much smaller share. Diploma provision therefore sits in a minority of schools, specialist teachers are correspondingly thinner on the ground, and a DP candidate's peer group for comparison is small. For 2026-27 the emirate adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, so that balance is shifting rather than fixed.

The other Dubai-specific feature is the mandatory subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Diploma candidate that is additional timetabled time that does not appear in any IB document, and it is one of the reasons a Dubai DP week feels fuller than the programme structure suggests.

IB Gram matches Diploma students to subject specialists for one-to-one lessons delivered over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school week. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical gain for a Diploma family is that the tutor is chosen for the group, level and component the evidence points at, rather than for living within driving distance of your community, and every session leaves a written note you can read in half a minute.

dubai/ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: The Diploma is one of four IB programmes, and a Dubai family may meet two or three of them in the same school. Knowing where your child sits in the sequence explains what the next transition will demand.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects chosen across six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, assessed through externally marked papers plus internally assessed components the school marks and the IB moderates. The core adds the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Award conditions, including how the core contributes, are set by the IB and confirmed by your school's coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma competes with a well-established A Level route, so many candidates arrive having considered both and some switch after DP1 term one. A tutor working here should know what the student would have been doing on the other route, because the comparison shapes how the family reads every result for the next two years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, judged against descriptors rather than percentages. Students arriving in the Diploma from MYP have met criterion marking and inquiry-led work, which helps with internal assessment and leaves them underprepared for the volume of timed written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP often offer a choice at 16 between the Diploma and a British sixth form, so the final MYP year points at two destinations. Where a student is heading for the Diploma, the most useful preparation is timed extended writing, which MYP assessment does not demand in the same quantity.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry units ending in the Year 6 Exhibition, with no external assessment. Relevant to Diploma families mainly as context: a student who came through PYP and MYP in the same school has a decade of criterion-based feedback behind them and reads a rubric fluently.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's primary cohorts turn over quickly with arrivals from British, Indian and American systems, so a single Year 6 class may contain children with four different assessment vocabularies. That is also why Arabic as an additional language is the most requested primary subject in the emirate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. The DP courses inside it are examined exactly as they are for Diploma candidates, so tutoring requests for CP students are usually about those specific subject papers.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme, so UAE-based tutor coverage is thin and most matches come from our wider pool. The online format and the subject depth are unchanged; the tutor's location is what differs.

dubai/ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects sit in six groups and a candidate takes one from each, with a permitted substitution. Below are the subjects Dubai families most often ask about, grouped as the programme groups them.

subjects.name: Studies in Language and Literature: English A
subjects.description: Group 1. Language and Literature or Literature, assessed through unseen textual analysis, a comparative paper, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an additional essay on a studied work. The scarce skill is analysis rather than content knowledge, which catches out students arriving from content-heavy systems.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition: Arabic B and ab initio
subjects.description: Group 2. Arabic is the most commonly taken acquisition language in Dubai, partly because the emirate requires Arabic teaching in all private schools. Streams differ sharply, so a tutor must know whether your child sits ab initio, B at Standard or B at Higher before planning anything.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies: Economics
subjects.description: Group 3. Diagram accuracy and real-world application decide the grade, with Higher Level adding a quantitative paper that exposes students who revised theory only. The internal assessment commentaries are marked against published criteria and are where early feedback pays most.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies: History
subjects.description: Group 3. Source analysis plus essay writing on prescribed topics, with a historical investigation as internal assessment. Match a tutor to the specific prescribed subject your school teaches, because strength in one region of study does not transfer to another.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies: Business Management
subjects.description: Group 3. Case-study application separates the grades: a correctly drawn framework that never refers to the stimulus forfeits the application and evaluation marks. Popular in Dubai, with reasonable supply at Standard Level and thinner coverage at Higher.

subjects.name: Sciences: Chemistry
subjects.description: Group 4. Structure and reactivity content with a single scientific investigation as internal assessment. The tightest Higher Level market in Dubai between February and May, which makes it the subject where booking early changes what is available to you.

subjects.name: Sciences: Physics
subjects.description: Group 4. Method and reasoning marks reward stated steps, so answers given without working score below their potential. Uncertainty treatment in the investigation is the component Dubai students most often underprepare for.

subjects.name: Sciences: Biology
subjects.description: Group 4. Extended responses are marked against lists of creditable points, so making five accurate plain statements beats writing elegantly about one. Command-term discipline is the dominant diagnosable error across Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Group 5. The route most often expected for mathematics-heavy degrees, with Higher Level adding a third paper that rewards structured investigation of an unfamiliar problem. Check your target universities' stated requirements rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Group 5. Statistics, modelling and technology use, with marks available for interpretation in context as well as calculation. Growing in Dubai faster than the number of teachers who have genuinely taught both maths courses.

subjects.name: The Arts and group substitutions
subjects.description: Group 6, which a candidate may replace with a second subject from groups 1 to 5. Dubai students aiming at science or engineering frequently take that substitution, which produces the two-science or two-maths patterns that make a week heavy.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Assessed against published criteria with stated limits, including 4,000 words for the Extended Essay. The school supervises both. A tutor may question, critique method and give criterion-based feedback on what the student has already written, and nothing beyond that.

dubai/ib-diploma-tutor.regionsIntro: Diploma provision clusters, and that shapes what families in each community are dealing with. These are the areas our Diploma requests most often come from.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Long-established Diploma catchment with two-generation familiarity in some households. Requests here are typically specific: one Higher Level subject, one component, often an internal assessment criterion rather than a whole course.

regions.name: Al Barsha South
regions.note: Large newer schools with fast-growing Diploma intakes, so many families are navigating the programme for the first time and the useful conversation is about the whole timetable rather than one grade.

regions.name: Dubai Internet City
regions.note: Apartment community with students commuting to schools across the emirate, which pushes sessions late and makes the Extended Essay the component most likely to slip in a busy term.

regions.name: Dubai Knowledge Park
regions.note: Close to several senior schools and higher-education providers, so parents here ask early about university expectations and the Maths Analysis against Applications decision.

regions.name: Tecom
regions.note: Dense residential stock feeding a mix of curricula. A common pattern is siblings on different routes, one on IGCSE and A Level, one on the Diploma, with parents comparing two incompatible report formats.

regions.name: The Sustainable City
regions.note: Self-contained community with a school on site, which means a small Diploma cohort and very few local comparisons. Online matching matters more here because the local specialist pool is tiny.

regions.name: Dubai Academic City
regions.note: University-adjacent, with senior school provision nearby and a strong focus on post-Diploma destinations. Equivalency and attestation questions come up here more than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Rapidly grown villa community with students spread across many schools, so internal deadlines in neighbouring households can differ by a month, which breaks the habit of copying a neighbour's tutoring plan.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools running the full Diploma
schoolClusters.note: These schools between them cover most of the emirate's Diploma cohort. Their internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines differ by several weeks, which is why a plan should be built from your own school's assessment calendar rather than from a general two-year timeline.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where the Diploma sits alongside other routes
schoolClusters.note: Students at these schools often choose between the Diploma and a British sixth form, and a minority switch after the first Diploma term. That decision, rather than any single subject, is the most consequential thing a tutor can help a family think through clearly.

sections.heading: What the IB Diploma asks a Dubai student to carry
paragraphs: The Diploma's shape is six subjects taken across six groups, with one subject from each group and a permitted substitution of a sixth-group subject for a second from groups one to five. Normally three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Alongside those sit three core elements: the Extended Essay, an independent research piece with a 4,000-word upper limit; Theory of Knowledge, which produces an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title; and CAS, a programme of creativity, activity and service that is not graded but is a requirement for the award.

Assessment is split. Most of each subject grade comes from externally marked papers sat at the end of the course. A further portion, commonly around a fifth, comes from an internally assessed component which the school marks against published criteria and the IB then moderates. Award conditions, including how the core contributes and what constitutes a pass, are set by the IB; your school's coordinator is the right person to confirm the current rules for your child's cohort rather than any tutoring page.

The honest description of why this is hard is not that any one subject is harder than its A Level equivalent. It is that six subjects, two of which the student may not have chosen enthusiastically, run simultaneously with three pieces of independent extended work, over two years, with the heaviest coursework deadlines landing in the same months. Students who struggle in the Diploma are usually competent in every individual element and overwhelmed by the aggregate.

That is why the first useful conversation is about load rather than content. Count the written work due per week across six subjects. Find out where the Extended Essay actually stands rather than where it is supposed to stand. Ask whether the Higher Level combination produces three sets of long written assignments in the same fortnight. A tutor who starts there will often recommend fewer paid hours than one who starts with the chemistry grade.

sections.heading: The core, and what a tutor may legitimately do with it
paragraphs: The core is where Diploma plans most often come apart, and it is also where the boundary around tutoring is tightest. All three elements belong to the student and the school. The Extended Essay has a school supervisor who holds formal responsibility and runs the reflective sessions. Theory of Knowledge is taught as a course with an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. CAS is a programme of experiences with its own reflective requirements, overseen by a coordinator.

What a tutor may do is teach skills, ask questions about material the student has already produced, and give feedback against the published criteria. What a tutor may not do is supply content, restructure a draft or provide text. Everything submitted must be the student's own, and the consequences of that boundary being crossed fall on the candidate. In this market at least one site openly sells completed internal assessments; buying one puts an entire Diploma at risk for a handful of marks.

Given that boundary, the highest-value intervention is early and cheap. A few hours spent testing whether an Extended Essay research question can actually be answered within 4,000 words, with sources the student can reach, prevents the crisis that otherwise arrives in the final year. The same is true of Theory of Knowledge: the prescribed title chosen effectively sets the ceiling, and a poor choice cannot be recovered by polishing later.

The practical failure pattern in Dubai is seasonal. Extended Essay progress stalls over the long summer break between the two Diploma years, when families travel and nobody is chasing a deadline. Students who return in the second year with no usable draft lose the weeks they needed for subject revision. Putting a small amount of structured support into the term before that break is worth more than a large amount of support after it.

sections.heading: Two years, counted from the end rather than the beginning
paragraphs: Diploma plans fail when they are built forwards from September rather than backwards from the final papers. Counted backwards, the structure is clear: final papers are preceded by a mock window, which is preceded by the last internal assessment deadlines, which are preceded by the Extended Essay submission, which is preceded by the long summer break where everything stalls. Each of those is a hard date set by a school or a board, and each one has work that must be finished before it.

Specific dates differ by school and by board, and some of them cannot be published responsibly. Cambridge and Pearson publish their series and key dates openly: Cambridge runs IGCSE and International A Level exams in June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and its March 2027 series has an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026 and results on Direct on 13 May. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November, and its provisional timetables are published ahead of each series. IB session dates, by contrast, are not confirmable from automated sources, so this page does not publish one: confirm every IB date with your school's coordinator or on ibo.org.

The useful discipline is to take your own school's assessment calendar, mark the internal deadlines and mock windows, and then count backwards from each. A plan built that way reveals the two or three fortnights in the whole programme where support actually changes what is submitted. Hours spent in those fortnights are worth several times the same hours spent in a quiet month.

Dubai adds two calendar features worth planning around. The school year runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with winter and spring breaks. And Ramadan moves earlier each year, shortening school days and reshaping evening availability, which is why many families shift sessions to a post-Iftar slot. A revision plan built on a normal evening pattern can quietly lose its best fortnight.

sections.heading: The IGCSE jump, subject by subject
paragraphs: A large share of Dubai's Diploma candidates arrive from an IGCSE background, either by transferring at 16 or by choosing the Diploma inside a school that offers both. The gap is real and it is specific rather than general. Students arrive with strong content recall and weak extended-response structure, because IGCSE rewards accurate short answers and the Diploma rewards sustained argument. They also arrive unused to independent extended work, because nothing in IGCSE resembles a 4,000-word essay with a supervisor.

Subject by subject the gap differs. In mathematics the jump is in abstraction and in the expectation that method is communicated, not just performed. In the sciences it is in quantitative treatment and in the single extended investigation replacing a series of short practicals. In English the jump is from comprehension and directed writing to unseen analysis and comparative argument. In the humanities it is from recall with some explanation to evaluation with weighted evidence.

The useful response is a short mapped block in DP1 term one, not a term of general support. Six to ten hours spent on timed extended writing, on command-term structure and on scoping the Extended Essay will close more of the gap than thirty hours of content coverage, because content is not where the gap is. That is also the cheapest tutoring a Diploma family will ever buy, since DP1 rates and availability are both better than DP2's.

One caution about the transition decision itself. Where a student is genuinely unsuited to three Higher Levels, no amount of tutoring substitutes for a timetable change, and only the school can make one. A tutor's job in that case is to say so clearly and early, while a change is still possible, rather than to sell a plan that manages the symptoms for eighteen months.

sections.heading: Higher Level choices and what universities actually ask for
paragraphs: The Higher Level decision shapes two years and it is usually made in a fortnight with incomplete information. Two patterns cause most of the later trouble in Dubai: three Higher Levels that each demand long written assignments in the same weeks, and a mathematics route chosen by preference rather than by what the student's intended degrees expect.

On mathematics, the practical rule is to check rather than assume. Analysis and Approaches is the route most often expected for mathematics-heavy degrees including engineering, physics, mathematics itself and many economics courses; Applications and Interpretation suits data-oriented and social-science destinations. Requirements differ by university and by course, they change, and universities in the UAE, the United Kingdom, North America and Europe do not state them identically. The only reliable method is to read the stated entry requirements for the specific courses on the specific universities' own admissions pages, in the year your child applies.

On subject combinations, count the written load rather than the difficulty. Two Higher Level sciences plus a Higher Level humanity produces three internal assessments and three sets of extended written work, often bunched. That is manageable for a well-organised student and brutal for a disorganised one, and the difference is a timetable judgement rather than an ability judgement. The school's coordinator can usually show which combinations their own cohorts find heavy.

Nothing on this page implies that tutoring is required for university admission or for equivalency. It is not, and any claim that it is would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory and admissions process. What tutoring can legitimately do is help a student meet a requirement they have chosen, and help a family read that requirement accurately before two years of work are organised around a guess.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for Diploma graduates in the UAE
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university, or on using a school certificate inside the country, meet the equivalency process. It is run by the Ministry of Education rather than by a school or a tutoring provider, and it has published requirements that differ by curriculum. Describing it accurately matters, because at least one ranking competitor in this market publishes the wrong subject count for the British track.

On the British track the published requirements are specific: students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the International Baccalaureate specifically, no points threshold is published on this page, and nobody should quote you one from a tutoring site. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB figure, so any IB equivalency number would be unsourced. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, or ask your school's coordinator who deals with these submissions every year.

Two boundaries worth stating. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anyone; we describe the process and point to the authority. And equivalency is a documentation process rather than an academic one, so it is not something tutoring prepares a student for. Where it interacts with tutoring at all, it is in making sure a student's subject choices do not accidentally leave a gap the process will notice two years later.

sections.heading: What evidence of Diploma progress looks like across two years
paragraphs: Across a two-year programme a parent needs indicators that move faster than school reports do. Reports average work produced over months, so a real improvement in October can stay invisible until January, by which point a decision may already have been taken. The alternative is a short list of artefacts that exist or do not exist at a given point.

In DP1 the artefacts are a tested Higher Level load, a scoped Extended Essay research question, and evidence that the student can write a timed extended response in each subject. If those three exist by the end of DP1, the programme is on track regardless of what any individual grade says. If the Extended Essay question is still vague at the end of DP1, that is a more serious signal than a disappointing chemistry mark, and it is the one families most often miss.

In DP2 the artefacts are internal assessment drafts at a stage where feedback can still change them, marked timed papers in each subject, and a short list of near-miss questions from the mock. The progress indicator inside sessions is narrower: can the student now do unaided what they could not do three weeks ago, and do they catch their own errors before the tutor does? Both are visible long before a grade moves.

None of this predicts a result and no honest provider will offer one. External outcomes depend on papers nobody has seen, on boundaries set after marking, and on what the student does on the day. What can be held to a standard is whether these artefacts exist, whether the indicators are moving, and whether the provider shows you the evidence when asked. At session four we review exactly that, and sometimes the right recommendation is fewer hours or none.

sections.heading: Delivery, scheduling and honest coverage for Diploma families
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week in Gulf Standard Time. Most Diploma sessions land between 16:30 and 20:30 after the school run and activities, and sixty to ninety minutes is the usual length, since that is what a Diploma student can sustain at the level of demand these subjects require. A short written note follows each session.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a Diploma family the relevant consequence is choice of tutor. Diploma provision sits in a minority of Dubai schools, so the specialists for a given Higher Level component are few, and geographic matching would hand you the nearest available science teacher rather than the person who has taught that component to examination.

Coverage is uneven and we publish the position rather than discovering it with you. Common subjects at common levels are matched within a few days. Scarce components, Chemistry at Higher Level between February and May or Computer Science HL at any time, take one to two weeks or longer. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers in other time zones at a Dubai-friendly hour, with no change to format or subject depth.

Two things we will decline. Anything that involves producing assessed work, because everything submitted must be the student's own and the risk of crossing that line falls on the candidate. And a large plan where a timetable conversation with the school is the actual remedy. Saying so costs us bookings and is the reason the programme planning session exists as a separate, smaller thing you can buy instead.

process.title: Start with the whole timetable
process.description: Tell us the six subjects, the three Higher Levels, where the Extended Essay stands and which component prompted the call. A Diploma request framed at programme level gets diagnosed properly; one framed as a single bad grade often produces a plan aimed at the wrong thing.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson on real material
process.description: One full lesson at no cost, built around a marked script, an internal assessment draft or a research question. It ends with a written statement of what is actually at risk across the programme and roughly how many hours that needs.

process.title: We name what belongs to the school
process.description: Timetable changes, supervisor deadlines, moderation outcomes and equivalency submissions belong with your school's IB coordinator. We say which parts of your problem are theirs, including when that means you need less tutoring than you expected.

process.title: Match on group, level and component
process.description: Not the subject alone. A Higher Level Paper 3, a scientific investigation criterion and an unseen-text paper need different teachers, and we say which specialist we are proposing and what they have taught.

process.title: Build the plan from your school's calendar
process.description: Internal deadlines and mock windows differ by several weeks between Dubai IB schools. We ask for your calendar and count backwards from it, so the hours land in the fortnights where they change what is submitted.

process.title: Review at session four, then decide
process.description: We look at the artefacts: a redone question, a changed draft, a marked paper. If the indicators have not moved we revisit the diagnosis rather than adding hours, and if the match is wrong we change the tutor at no extra cost.

whyPoints.title: We work to the programme, not one subject
whyPoints.description: A Diploma problem is often a loading problem. We look at the six-subject week, the Higher Level combination and where the core stands before proposing subject hours, which regularly produces a smaller plan than a family arrived expecting.

whyPoints.title: Matched on component, not proximity
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered online, so the tutor is chosen for the group, level and component the evidence points at. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

whyPoints.title: A published boundary on core work
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and every internal assessment must be the student's own work. We question, critique method and give criterion-based feedback, and we state that in writing before a block starts.

whyPoints.title: Dates handled honestly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson key dates are quoted from their published pages. IB session dates are not confirmable from automated sources, so we do not publish one and we point you to your coordinator or ibo.org instead.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency described, never promised
whyPoints.description: We set out the ministry's published requirements with the source named, state plainly that no IB points figure is published there, and point you to the authority. We neither perform nor guarantee any part of the process.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits before you commit
whyPoints.description: Scarce Higher Level components take one to two weeks to match and longer between February and May. If no UAE-based specialist is free we say so and explain where the match would come from instead.

faqs.question: How many subjects does an IB Diploma student in Dubai take?
faqs.answer: Six, chosen across six groups, with one subject from each group and a permitted substitution of a sixth-group arts subject for a second subject from groups one to five. Normally three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Alongside those six sit the three core elements: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. In Dubai there is additional timetabled content that does not appear in IB documentation, because private schools in the emirate must also teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies whatever international curriculum they are licensed for.

faqs.question: How should my child choose which three subjects to take at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: By counting written load as well as interest and requirements. Two Higher Level sciences plus a Higher Level humanity produces three internal assessments and three sets of extended written assignments, frequently bunched into the same weeks. That is manageable for a well-organised student and punishing for a disorganised one, which is a timetable judgement rather than an ability judgement. Check your intended degrees' stated entry requirements on the universities' own admissions pages before choosing, and ask the school's coordinator which combinations their own cohorts find heavy. Changing later is possible but much harder.

faqs.question: How long does the Extended Essay have to be and who supervises it?
faqs.answer: It has an upper limit of 4,000 words, and it is supervised by a member of staff at your child's school who holds formal responsibility for the process, including the recorded reflective sessions. A tutor may critique the scope of a research question, question method, and give feedback against the published criteria on material the student has already written. A tutor may not supply content, restructure a draft or provide text, because everything submitted must be the student's own work. The highest-value hours are spent early, testing whether the question can actually be answered within the limit.

faqs.question: What does Theory of Knowledge require a Diploma student to produce?
faqs.answer: Two assessed pieces: an exhibition, in which the student links objects to a prompt and explains why each one answers it, and an essay written on a prescribed title with a published word limit. Both are judged against criteria on a best-fit basis, which means polish does not move a band but the named qualities in the descriptors do. The choice of prescribed title effectively sets the ceiling, and a weak choice cannot be recovered by later work. That makes title selection the cheapest high-value thing a tutor can help a student think through properly.

faqs.question: Does CAS affect my child's Diploma result?
faqs.answer: CAS is not graded, but it is a requirement for the award, and a student who has not completed it to the school's satisfaction has a problem no subject grade compensates for. It runs across both Diploma years as a programme of creativity, activity and service with its own reflective requirements, overseen by a coordinator at the school. It is also the element a tutor has no business touching: the experiences and the reflections belong to the student. Where CAS is behind, the conversation is with the coordinator, not with a tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Which schools in Dubai run the full IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Diploma provision sits in a minority of the emirate's private schools, which served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25 with UK curricula the largest share by enrolment. Established Diploma cohorts include schools in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City and Al Jaddaf, and the emirate is adding three new International Baccalaureate schools among seven new private schools for 2026-27, creating 16,846 new places overall. For an authoritative current list, check the regulator's own school listing rather than any tutoring directory.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Specific rather than general. Students arrive with strong content recall and weak extended-response structure, because IGCSE rewards accurate short answers while the Diploma rewards sustained argument with weighted evidence. They also arrive with nothing in their experience resembling a 4,000-word independent essay. In mathematics the jump is in abstraction and in communicating method; in the sciences it is in quantitative treatment and a single extended investigation; in English it is from comprehension to unseen analysis. Six to ten hours in DP1 term one on timed extended writing closes more of that gap than thirty hours of content coverage.

faqs.question: Will a UAE university accept an IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Universities set their own entry requirements and the Ministry of Education runs a separate equivalency process for school certificates, so there are two things to check rather than one. For the British track the published equivalency rules are specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the International Baccalaureate no points threshold appears in that source, so nobody should quote you one. Check moe.gov.ae, the emirate's attestation authority, or your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: Does my child need Maths Analysis or Maths Applications for engineering?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the route most often expected for mathematics-heavy degrees including engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses, while Applications and Interpretation suits data-oriented and social-science destinations. That is a general pattern rather than a rule, because requirements differ by university and by course, they change between admission cycles, and institutions in the UAE, the UK, North America and Europe do not state them identically. Read the stated requirements for the specific courses on the specific universities' own admissions pages, in the cycle your child will apply in.

faqs.question: Is taking two Higher Level sciences too much for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on written output rather than on intelligence. Two Higher Level sciences means two extended investigations plus two sets of long written assignments, and in most schools those land in overlapping weeks. A student who plans ahead and drafts early handles it; a student who works to deadlines does not, and no amount of subject tutoring fixes the scheduling. If the combination is genuinely wrong, only the school can change the timetable, and the window for doing that comfortably is DP1 term one. That is why we offer a programme planning session separately from subject hours.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student start the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do, and specifically before the long summer break between the two Diploma years. The pattern we see in Dubai is that progress stalls over that break while families travel and no deadline is in sight, and students return to the second year with no usable draft, then lose the weeks they needed for subject revision. The target worth setting is a scoped research question by the end of DP1 term two and a usable draft before the break ends. Scoping work takes only a few hours and is the cheapest high-value support in the whole programme.

faqs.question: Can my child change a Higher Level subject after starting the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it gets harder every week. The decision belongs to the school, which has to consider timetable capacity, how much of the course has been covered and whether the student can realistically catch up. In practice DP1 term one is when a change is straightforward, DP1 term two is when it becomes difficult, and after that it is usually not possible. If the evidence points at a wrong combination rather than a weak student, the right move is a conversation with the coordinator immediately, not a tutoring plan that manages the symptoms for eighteen months.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the Diploma?
faqs.answer: They are separate requirements rather than part of the Diploma's six subjects, unless your child takes Arabic as their group 2 language acquisition subject. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For equivalency purposes, Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five-subject GCSE or IGCSE count.

faqs.question: How does a Dubai school report translate into a Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Loosely, and with a lag that catches families out. School reports average work produced over months, and internal predictions are the school's own judgement rather than a result. Internal assessment marks shown on a report are also provisional, because the school's marking is moderated by the IB against its own standard and a whole cohort can be adjusted. Treat a report as a direction of travel and look instead at artefacts: a timed extended response in each subject, internal assessment drafts at a changeable stage, and a mapped list of where marks were lost in the most recent paper.

faqs.question: How early should we arrange a Diploma tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: DP1 is both cheaper and better supplied than DP2, so the practical answer is earlier than most families act. Specialist availability in Dubai tightens from January to April because every Diploma cohort in the emirate converges on the same weeks, and the tutor who was bookable in November may not be in March at any rate. If you are not sure support is needed, run a free diagnostic session rather than committing: it costs nothing, produces a written statement of what is actually at risk, and frequently results in fewer hours than a family expected to buy.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Arabic A at Diploma level: Literature and Language and Literature, SL and HL, including the school-supported self-taught route. Each one marks to the published criteria rather than to a personal standard, so a parent can see which criterion moved and which did not.

intro.heading: Start with the script, not the syllabus
paragraphs: An IB DP Arabic A home tutor in Dubai is almost never hired at the start of DP1. The call comes after a report, a mock, or a returned Paper 2 with a mark the family did not expect. By then the useful question is narrow: on this script, under which criterion did the marks go, and is that a reading problem, a structure problem or a language problem? Those three failures look identical on a report card and need completely different lessons. A tutor who opens with a tour of the course has already wasted the first hour.

So the first session is a diagnostic on paper your child has already written. We ask for the most recent marked Paper 1 or Paper 2, the learner portfolio if the school keeps one, and the draft of whatever is next due. The tutor re-marks the script against the criteria, writes down a mark for each one, and compares that with the school's mark. Where the two disagree, that gap is the lesson: it is usually the difference between what the student thought the question asked and what the criterion rewards.

Arabic A carries a complication no other Group 1 subject in Dubai has. Your child probably speaks a dialect at home, reads fusha in class, and is assessed entirely in fusha. A student can be fluent, confident, the one the family relies on for translation, and still lose marks under criterion D because the register slipped. Marking that as a language weakness is accurate and useless. Naming it as dialect interference in a specific sentence, on a specific line of their own last essay, is something a student can correct inside a fortnight and then check for themselves on everything they write afterwards.

The second complication is Dubai itself. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. That means a DP student taking Arabic A is also carrying the school's mandatory Arabic provision, and the two do not always align. Families arrive assuming one subject is being taught; often two are, with different expectations and different teachers.

What we do about all of this is unglamorous and visible. Each fortnight your child produces one piece of timed work. It is marked criterion by criterion, the marks are written into a running record, and the next session starts from the lowest one. A parent does not have to take anyone's word about progress. The record either shows criterion B moving from 3 to 5 across four attempts, or it shows it flat, in which case the plan was wrong and we change it.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic A sits inside a longer arc. A Dubai student usually meets fusha in PYP or a national-curriculum primary, formalises it through MYP Language and Literature, and then chooses between Arabic A and Arabic B at 16. The programme notes below describe what each stage leaves unfinished.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, and the core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Arabic A occupies the Group 1 slot as either Literature or Language and Literature, at SL or HL. Assessment is three external components plus an internally assessed oral, and at HL a written essay produced across several months.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are unusually mixed in Arabic background: Emirati nationals, Arab expatriates from a dozen dialect regions, and heritage speakers born here who read fusha slowly. One class can hold all three. A tutor working one-to-one can set the register and reading-speed targets a shared classroom cannot.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Arabic appears as Language and Literature for first-language students and Language Acquisition for others. MYP marking uses four criteria out of eight each, with grades on a 1-7 scale derived from criterion totals, which is why MYP 6 and DP 6 mean very different things in Arabic.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Arabic A step catches Dubai families out more than any other transition we see. MYP rewards personal response and creative text production; Arabic A Paper 1 rewards close reading of an unseen passage against a guiding question. A student can hold a steady MYP 6 and open DP1 with a Paper 1 mark in the low teens out of 20.

programmes.name: School-supported self-taught Arabic A
programmes.description: Where a school does not teach a student's first language, the IB allows Literature SL to be taken self-taught with school support. The student reads the nine works independently, the school supervises the Individual Oral, and the external papers are identical to the taught course. It is available at SL only, never HL.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this route is used less for Arabic than it should be. Several British-curriculum schools here run no Arabic A class at all, so an Arab first-language student is pushed into Arabic B and assessed on a course beneath their reading level. The self-taught Literature SL route keeps the Group 1 slot and the bilingual diploma in reach.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller UAE presence than the Diploma, pairing DP courses with a career-related study and a personal and professional skills course. Students take fewer DP subjects, so a language choice carries more weight in the overall profile.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai CP student takes Arabic A as one of their DP courses, the tutoring plan narrows to the components that actually count rather than the whole course. That usually means Paper 1 technique and the Individual Oral, because those are the two that can be rehearsed to a timetable.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic A is one subject with several faces, and a tutoring plan has to name which one. The entries below are the components and skill areas we actually teach against, with the mark allocation attached to each.

subjects.name: Paper 1 guided literary analysis
subjects.levels: SL 1 h 15 min - HL 2 h 15 min
subjects.description: An unseen passage with a guiding question, marked out of 20 on criteria A to D. SL sits one analysis, HL sits two. The skill is reading a passage cold and building an argument that answers the guiding question from the first paragraph, not the last.

subjects.name: Paper 2 comparative essay
subjects.description: One question answered through two studied works, marked out of 30. The marks live in the comparison itself. Candidates who write a strong paragraph on each work and then a linking sentence at the end score under criterion B however good the two halves are.

subjects.name: Arabic A HL essay
subjects.description: A formal essay on one work or body of work studied, worth 20% of the HL grade and marked out of 20. The usual failure is a question too large to sustain. Narrowing it from a theme to an argument is a single session that changes the whole mark.

subjects.name: Arabic A Individual Oral
subjects.description: Fifteen minutes, marked out of 40: a ten-minute statement on how a global issue is presented in two extracts, then five minutes of questions. Extract choice decides the mark before the student speaks, which is why we rehearse selection before delivery.

subjects.name: Fusha register and dialect interference
subjects.description: The commonest criterion D problem in Dubai. Colloquial verb forms, dialect vocabulary and spoken sentence rhythm reach the page unnoticed because they sound right. We work from the student's own marked scripts, listing their specific slips rather than teaching grammar in general.

subjects.name: Classical and modern Arabic literary text handling
subjects.description: Pre-modern poetry, the modern novel and contemporary drama need different reading strategies. A qasida and a Mahfouz chapter cannot be annotated the same way. Students who have one method apply it everywhere and lose criterion A marks on whichever text it does not fit.

subjects.name: Works in translation
subjects.description: Arabic A: Literature requires works read in translation alongside works originally in Arabic. Students often treat a translated novel as if style were authorial. Separating what can be argued about a translation from what cannot is a criterion B skill examiners reward.

subjects.name: Learner portfolio discipline
subjects.description: Not assessed directly, but the portfolio is where the evidence for the Individual Oral and the HL essay accumulates. A student with a thin portfolio in DP2 term one has no material to choose from and ends up writing on whichever work is freshest.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature non-literary bodies of work
subjects.description: The Language and Literature course sets literary works against non-literary material such as advertising, journalism and political speech. The analytical vocabulary differs from Literature, and students moving between schools mid-DP often arrive with the wrong one.

subjects.name: Timed writing under exam conditions
subjects.description: Arabic handwriting at speed degrades, and criterion D notices. A student who scores well on coursework and poorly in mocks usually has a stamina problem rather than a knowledge problem. The fix is timed practice at the real paper length, fortnightly.

sections.heading: What a search for an Arabic A home tutor in Dubai is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase people type is home tutor. The need underneath it is a specialist who can mark Arabic A to the published criteria and explain the result. Those are different things, and in Dubai they pull in opposite directions. The pool of tutors who will drive to your villa is limited to whoever lives within a reasonable radius. The pool who can take apart a Paper 2 comparative essay in fusha is small across the whole emirate, and the odds that the two sets overlap in your community are poor.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Arabic A tuition here is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature. It is the reason a family in Arabian Ranches can work with an Arabic A Literature specialist rather than with the nearest available Arabic teacher, and the reason a 19:30 session is possible at all on a weeknight.

There is a second, duller advantage. A screen-shared script can be annotated live and saved. A paper script annotated at your dining table leaves the house with the tutor. Over two years, the saved record of marked work is the single most useful artefact the tuition produces, because it is what tells you whether criterion B is moving. Parents who have had both arrangements tend to notice this before they notice anything else about the format.

sections.heading: Which Arabic A course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Three or four different courses answer to the name Arabic A, and families regularly do not know which one is on the timetable. Literature and Language and Literature share a paper structure and a criteria set but study different material. SL and HL differ in the number of works, the length of Paper 1 and the presence of the HL essay. The self-taught Literature SL route differs again in who supervises the oral. A tutoring plan built on the wrong one of these wastes a term.

The practical test is to look at what the student is reading and how many works there are. Nine works and no non-literary material means Literature SL. Thirteen works means Literature HL. Four literary works alongside advertising, journalism or speeches means Language and Literature SL. If nobody at home can answer the question, the school's subject report or the learner portfolio will, and it is worth five minutes to establish before booking anything.

The table below is the version we work from in a first session. The weightings matter more than they look: at HL, Paper 2 drops to 25% while the HL essay takes 20%, so a student who ignores the essay until DP2 term two has left a fifth of the grade until the busiest point of the two years. At SL there is no essay, and the Individual Oral carries 30% instead, which changes where the revision effort should go entirely.

sections.heading: Reading the criteria off a marked script
paragraphs: A grade tells a parent that something is wrong. A criterion breakdown tells them what. Every Arabic A component is marked on four criteria, and the pattern of which ones are low is diagnostic. Low A with healthy B means the student is analysing confidently but has misread the passage or the question. Low B with healthy A means they understood it and then only described what they saw. Low C is structure. Low D is language, and in Dubai low D is dialect interference more often than it is weak grammar.

This is why the first thing we ask for is paper rather than a conversation. A parent's account of the problem is honest and second-hand; the script is first-hand. The tutor marks it blind, records four numbers, and only then compares with the school's marks. Two independent markings of the same piece, with the gaps named, is more information than most students get in a term, and it costs one session.

The table sets out where the marks sit and what we see go wrong most often in Dubai cohorts specifically. None of these failures is exotic. All of them are visible on a script, and each has a different fix: a reading drill, a structural template practised and then discarded, a personal error list for register. What they do not have is a shared solution, which is why a general Arabic tutor and an Arabic A tutor produce different results on the same student.

sections.heading: Fusha, dialect and the thing no competitor page mentions
paragraphs: Arabic is the only Group 1 language in a Dubai DP cohort where the version spoken at home and the version assessed are reliably different. A student may speak Emirati, Levantine, Egyptian or Maghrebi Arabic at home, hear a mixture of all four in the corridor, and be examined entirely in Modern Standard Arabic. Fluency is not the issue. Register is. The student who sounds most confident in the room is often the one whose written criterion D marks are lowest, because confidence carries spoken habits onto the page.

The correction is specific rather than general. We do not teach Arabic grammar from the start to a fluent speaker; that is insulting and it does not work. We build an error list from the student's own marked scripts: their particular colloquial verb substitutions, their dialect vocabulary, the structures they reach for under time pressure. Twelve to twenty items, usually. The student checks their own work against their own list before submission, and the list shortens over a term. Criterion D marks follow it.

There is a Dubai layer on top. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires that Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies are taught in separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. A DP student taking Arabic A is therefore often carrying mandatory Arabic provision as well. Knowing which teacher is assessing what stops a family chasing the wrong report.

sections.heading: The HL essay: a draft history, not a rewrite
paragraphs: The Arabic A HL essay is 1,200 to 1,500 words, worth 20% of the HL grade, marked out of 20, and produced over months rather than in a hall. That makes it the component where outside help is most tempting and most dangerous. The IB treats work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on whoever helped. So the boundary has to be stated rather than implied, and it has to hold when a deadline is three days away.

A tutor working on an HL essay may do four things. Help narrow a theme into an arguable question. Discuss whether the chosen evidence supports the argument. Read a draft and respond to it against the criteria. Teach the conventions of academic writing in Arabic. A tutor may not supply content, write or rewrite passages, edit the prose to a finish, or decide the argument. IB Gram does not write, redraft or complete any assessed component, and a tutor who offers to is a risk to your child's diploma rather than a shortcut.

In practice the honest version is also the one that scores. Most weak HL essays fail under criterion A or C, and both failures are decided at the question stage, before any writing happens. A question such as how one novelist presents exile is a theme, not an argument; it invites summary, and summary caps criterion B. Reworking it into a claim that can be contested takes one session and lifts the ceiling of everything written afterwards. We keep every draft, dated, so the school can see a progression that belongs to the student.

sections.heading: What Arabic A tuition costs in Dubai, and what the rate hides
paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages we examined for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. So here are the Dubai market bands in the currency families actually pay in, with the source and date attached to each. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list: our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the figure we quote depends on level, component and session length rather than on a published tier.

The number that moves most is not the hourly rate but what the rate includes. An in-home visit prices travel inside the billed hour, and in Dubai that can be twenty minutes of a sixty-minute session in each direction on a weekday evening. A coursework supervision block is priced differently from weekly subject support almost everywhere, because it involves reading drafts between sessions. And a rate quoted for Arabic frequently assumes Arabic B; Arabic A Literature at HL is a different specialism and a thinner market.

Set against Dubai school fees, the arithmetic is less dramatic than it feels. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Against a fee bill that is already fixed, a weekly one-to-one session across the two DP years is a small marginal line, and families tend to decide it on whether the marks move rather than on the hourly figure.

sections.heading: Is your Arabic tutor permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a question Dubai families ask late and should ask first. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Eligibility is wider than most parents assume. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students may all apply. That breadth is why a verification question is worth asking: a tutor being eligible and a tutor holding the permit are not the same thing, and the only person who can show you the permit is the tutor.

One boundary matters in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing in Dubai too. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct along the same lines. So the arrangement some families ask for first - your child's own Arabic teacher, privately, for an hour on Saturday - is the one arrangement we will not broker. Verify any claim against MoHRE and the relevant authority directly; IB Gram holds no regulator licence and claims none.

sections.heading: Counting back from the May session
paragraphs: Arabic A is not a subject that can be rescued in six weeks, because two of its components close long before the written papers. The Individual Oral is recorded inside a school window in DP2, and the HL essay is submitted earlier still. By the time a family starts worrying about May, 40% of an HL grade and 30% of an SL grade may already be fixed. Working backwards from the session is therefore the only planning method that survives contact with a real DP timetable.

The deadlines that bind are mostly set by the school, not by the IB, and they differ between Dubai schools by several weeks. Ask the DP coordinator for the subject's internal deadline calendar in DP1, not DP2. Two local factors shift it further. Ramadan moves earlier each year and compresses the revision weeks before the session, with families often preferring post-Iftar session times. And the long summer between DP1 and DP2 is where portfolio work either consolidates or evaporates.

We publish no specific IB exam or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date we quoted would be second-hand, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date. Confirm every session, upload and results date with your child's DP coordinator or on ibo.org. What is safe to plan against is the shape below, which is the same in every Dubai school even when the calendar dates are not.

sections.heading: What the evidence looks like after eight weeks
paragraphs: A parent paying for weekly tuition is entitled to something better than an impression. So the record is deliberately boring. Every marked piece gets four numbers, one per criterion, dated, in a running table the family can see. After eight weeks there are four marked pieces and sixteen numbers, and the pattern in them is the answer to whether this is working. Criterion C climbing from 3 to 5 while A stays at 3 is a clear message: the structure teaching landed and the reading work has not started yet.

That record also changes the conversation with the school. A subject teacher with twenty-four students and a mandatory-subject timetable cannot produce a criterion history for each one. A parent who arrives at a consultation with four dated markings is asking a different question from a parent who arrives with a worry, and in our experience gets a more specific answer. The school remains the authority on the student's predicted grade; the record simply makes the discussion concrete.

Where the numbers do not move, we say so. Eight weeks of flat criterion B usually means one of three things: the diagnosis was wrong, the student is not writing between sessions, or the match is not right. All three are fixable and only the third requires changing tutor. What none of them justifies is another term of the same plan, which is what happens by default when nobody is counting the criterion marks from one piece to the next.
