sections.heading: What a session fixes, what it does not, and what it costs
paragraphs: Honesty about scope is more useful than enthusiasm. Six weeks of one-to-one Arabic B work will reliably fix text type conventions, Paper 1 structure, visual stimulus handling, reading question technique and a named list of recurring accuracy errors. Six weeks will not build broad vocabulary or fluent listening from a low base, because both are functions of hours of exposure that no tutor can compress. Families who know which of their problems is in which column make better decisions about how much tutoring to buy.

The Dubai market context is worth stating plainly because so few pages do. Published rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour in this city, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-500 with travel priced inside the hour. Those are market figures from October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. We start with a free trial lesson and quote against component and level.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Arabic B lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format is a mild advantage rather than a concession, because shared audio with precise replay is what listening practice needs and because the oral rehearsal recording is kept for the student to mark themselves.

process.title: Send a marked mock, not a description
process.description: The most recent Arabic B paper with marks on it, ideally with the criterion breakdown. If the school marked a full mock, that single document usually identifies which of the three components is producing the grade, which is the question the first session exists to answer.

process.title: Free trial spent diagnosing the component
process.description: The trial session re-marks the writing against language, message and conceptual understanding, runs five minutes of listening at exam speed, and asks the student to speak for two minutes on an unseen image. Three numbers out, and a priority order. No card is required for the trial.

process.title: Write down the component order
process.description: Paper 2 first if listening is the hole, text type first if criterion C is the hole, oral first if the school window is close. The order and the reason go in writing with dates, so at week eight it is possible to check whether the plan was right rather than argue about it.

process.title: Weekly session on a three-component rotation
process.description: Sessions run live online in Gulf Standard Time, generally after 18:00 on a Dubai weekday. The rotation keeps all three components live, with one marked written piece every fortnight and the student's error list updated from their own work each round.

whyPoints.title: The three components treated separately
whyPoints.description: Arabic B grades hide which component is failing. We diagnose writing, Paper 2 and the oral independently, and build the plan from whichever is lowest rather than from the course order. A student weak only in listening should not spend a term polishing essays.

whyPoints.title: Text type conventions taught as a finite list
whyPoints.description: Six conceptual understanding marks are available for about a fortnight of attention to how each text type opens, addresses its reader and signs off. It is the highest return per hour on the whole paper and it is the work most often skipped.

whyPoints.title: Listening drilled the way it actually improves
whyPoints.description: Short audio spans, transcription and replay rather than whole papers. Shared clean audio with precise replay control is one of the few concrete advantages of a live online lesson over a tutor sitting at the kitchen table with a phone.

whyPoints.title: Error lists built from the student's own scripts
whyPoints.description: A fluent heritage speaker does not need a grammar course; they need their twelve to twenty recurring substitutions written down and checked before submission. Items leave the list when they stop appearing, which makes progress countable.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer on Arabic B versus Arabic A
whyPoints.description: Where a reading diagnostic suggests your child is in the wrong course, we say so, even when the honest answer costs us the booking. The subject decision belongs to your child's DP coordinator; the diagnostic just makes it evidence-based.

whyPoints.title: Scope stated before you buy a term
whyPoints.description: Text type, structure and accuracy respond inside six weeks. Vocabulary breadth and fluent listening do not, because both need exposure hours. Saying which is which in advance is how a family decides how much tutoring is worth buying.

faqs.question: How much does an Arabic B tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table put qualified online subject tutors in Dubai at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450, budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-500 with travel sitting inside the billed hour. Those are market figures from October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. We begin with a free trial lesson and quote against level and component, because an oral intensive before a school recording window and a weekly Paper 2 rebuild are different pieces of work.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Arabic B SL and Arabic B HL?
faqs.answer: Higher Level studies two literary works and Standard Level studies none, which is the structural difference that matters most. HL also has a longer Paper 1, an hour and a half against an hour and a quarter, and a longer listening component, an hour against forty-five minutes. The weightings are the same at both levels: Paper 1 25%, Paper 2 50%, individual oral 25%. The oral itself differs, starting from a visual stimulus at SL and from a literary extract at HL, so HL preparation has to begin while the works are being taught.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well on Arabic B writing but badly overall?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 writing is only 25% of the grade and Paper 2 is 50%. Listening and reading together outweigh the component most students practise, and listening is the one almost nobody drills alone because doing so is unrewarding. A student with solid written Arabic and a weak Paper 2 will land a grade that looks inexplicable next to their classwork. The marked mock usually shows it immediately. The remedy is a listening and reading block worked by question type, not more essays, however much better essays feel to produce.

faqs.question: What are the five prescribed themes in Arabic B?
faqs.answer: Identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet. They are contexts rather than vocabulary lists, which is the misreading that costs marks. Paper 1 tasks are set within them and the individual oral moves through them, so useful preparation means arriving with two or three positions you could defend in each, not forty memorised nouns. Dubai students have an underused advantage here: every theme has a specific local example to hand, from residency and identity to desalination under sharing the planet, and specifics read as real content in the oral.

faqs.question: How is the Arabic B individual oral marked at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Out of 30, across language, message and interactive skills, over fifteen minutes with preparation time beforehand. The student presents a visual stimulus linked to one of the five themes, holds a conversation about it, then discusses at least one further theme. Marks are lost most often by describing the image rather than arguing from it, because a description leaves nothing for the message criterion and gives the conversation no foundation. Cold practice on unseen images, with the recording played back and self-marked, moves this faster than any amount of rereading theme notes.

faqs.question: My child is in Arabic B but speaks Arabic at home. Are they in the right course?
faqs.answer: Possibly not. Heritage speakers are routinely placed in Arabic B because their written Arabic looks weak, when the real limit is fusha reading speed rather than language ability. The test is whether they can read an unfamiliar Modern Standard Arabic page at reasonable pace and discuss it. If they can, Arabic A: Literature is within reach and dialect interference in their writing is correctable. If they decode slowly and lose the thread, Arabic B is genuinely the better fit. Raise it in DP1 with the DP coordinator, while the timetable can still change.

faqs.question: What text types can come up on Arabic B Paper 1?
faqs.answer: A blog post, a formal email or letter, an article, a speech, a report, a review, a diary entry, a set of instructions, a proposal or an interview, among others. The task names the type, and six of the thirty marks go to getting audience, purpose, context and register right for it. A strong essay written where a speech was requested keeps the language marks and forfeits those six entirely. Each type has a short list of conventions, which makes this a fortnight of learning rather than a term, and the highest return per hour on the paper.

faqs.question: How do we practise Arabic B listening when there is nothing to practise with?
faqs.answer: Use any clean Modern Standard Arabic audio and change the method rather than hunting for exam material. Take three to five minutes of recording. Play ten seconds, transcribe what was heard including the gaps, replay, fill in, replay once more, then read the transcript. The aim at this stage is not comprehension but training the ear to segment connected fusha speech, which is the actual bottleneck for students who hear dialect daily and fusha only in lessons. Twenty minutes three times a week outperforms one full paper at the weekend.

faqs.question: Do the two HL literary works appear on the Arabic B written papers?
faqs.answer: No. The two works studied at Higher Level exist mainly to supply the extract the HL individual oral starts from, and they are not examined on Paper 1 or Paper 2. That is precisely why students neglect them: they look optional relative to the written papers. A student who skimmed both arrives at the oral with no foothold when an extract is placed in front of them. Annotating both texts for themes, characters and a few quotable moments during DP1, then practising cold on extracts, is what makes the HL oral manageable.

faqs.question: Can an Arabic B tutor come to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Arabic B tuition for Dubai families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which usually means an evening slot on a weekday or a weekend morning. For this subject the online format is mildly better rather than worse: listening work needs clean shared audio with precise replay control, and oral rehearsals can be recorded for the student to mark themselves before the tutor comments.

faqs.question: Which grammar mistakes cost Arabic B candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: The same families recur on almost every script we see: hamza placement, feminine endings written as haa instead of taa marbuta, alif maqsura confusion, broken plurals avoided by using singulars, idafa constructions built in the wrong order, and the reverse agreement of numbers three to ten applied the ordinary way round. The language criterion is twelve of the thirty marks on Paper 1 and twelve on the oral, so these are expensive. The method that works is a numbered personal error list drawn from the student's own marked work, checked before every submission.

faqs.question: Is six weeks of Arabic B tutoring before the exams worth it?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which problem you have. Six weeks will reliably fix text type conventions, Paper 1 structure, reading question technique, visual stimulus handling and a named set of recurring accuracy errors. Six weeks will not build broad vocabulary or fluent listening from a low base, because both are functions of exposure hours that cannot be compressed. So the honest answer is yes if the marks are being lost on technique, and only partly if the gap is exposure. The trial session tells you which, before you commit to a block.

faqs.question: How does mandatory school Arabic relate to the Arabic B Diploma course?
faqs.answer: They are separate obligations. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA sets requirements for how they are taught, including separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. Arabic B is a Diploma Group 2 subject your child has chosen and is examined on by the IB. The mandatory provision is not satisfied or replaced by tutoring, and it is sometimes a different teacher with a different report, which is worth clarifying before chasing feedback.

faqs.question: Does a private Arabic tutor in the UAE need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Eligibility is broad, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Being eligible and holding the permit are different things, so ask the tutor directly. IB Gram holds no regulator licence and claims none.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see after two months of Arabic B sessions?
faqs.answer: Four marked written pieces with language, message and conceptual understanding scored separately, a listening record kept as marks per question type rather than as a total, and at least two recorded oral attempts the student has marked themselves. Criterion C should be the first thing to move, because text type conventions are learnable quickly. Language marks move more slowly and should show the error list shortening. If nothing has moved in eight weeks, the diagnosis was wrong, the student is not working between sessions, or the match is poor, and we will say which we think it is.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start by finding out which component is actually failing
dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-home-tutor.closingBody: An Arabic B grade tells you something is wrong. It does not tell you whether the problem is writing, listening, reading or the oral, and those four need different work. Send the most recent marked mock and the date of the school's oral window, and the free trial lesson produces three component scores and a priority order you keep whichever way you decide. Sessions run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time. If the diagnostic says your child belongs in Arabic A rather than Arabic B, we will tell you that too.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Arabic B at Standard and Higher Level. Each one works in Modern Standard Arabic as the language of instruction, uses the five prescribed themes as the planning spine, and marks written work against the published criteria before the lesson that discusses it.

intro.heading: Arabic B is a written-language subject wearing a spoken-language label
paragraphs: Most Dubai families who search for an IB DP Arabic B online tutor are not looking for conversation practice. They are looking for a fix to a specific and very common mismatch. The child speaks Arabic fluently at home, follows a family conversation without effort, and then sits a Diploma Paper 1 task and loses marks on orthography, agreement and register. Arabic B assesses Modern Standard Arabic in writing, under timed conditions, against three named criteria. Fluency at the dinner table does not transfer to that paper automatically, and nobody at school has the timetable space to say so.

The subject sits inside Group 2 of the Diploma, the language acquisition group, at Standard or Higher Level. Both levels share the same five prescribed themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet. Both are assessed through Paper 1, which is a single piece of writing worth a quarter of the grade; Paper 2, which is listening and reading and carries half; and the individual oral, which is internally assessed and carries the remaining quarter. Higher Level adds two literary works studied in Arabic, and the Higher Level oral is built on an extract from one of them rather than on a photograph.

That structure decides what a useful lesson looks like. A session that only talks has covered a quarter of the assessment. A session that only drills grammar has covered none of it directly, because no criterion awards marks for grammar in isolation: Criterion A rewards the range and accuracy of language in service of the task, Criterion B rewards the message against what the task asked for, and Criterion C rewards conceptual understanding, which in practice means text type, register and audience. Students who write well and score badly are almost always losing Criterion B and C marks on a task they answered beside rather than answered.

Dubai adds a second layer that no other market has. KHDA requires Arabic in every private school in the emirate regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so most Diploma students carrying Arabic B are also carrying a school Arabic requirement that is assessed differently, taught from Ministry-set content, and reported separately. Parents reasonably assume the two are the same subject. They are not, and tuition that treats them as one wastes half the hour.

What one-to-one online tuition changes here is the size of the pool. Diploma Arabic B is a narrow specialism: a tutor needs Modern Standard Arabic at academic register, familiarity with the current subject guide, and the patience to mark text types rather than correct sentences. Across a single Dubai community, the number of people who meet that description and are free at 5pm on a Tuesday is very small. Delivering the lesson over live video removes the twenty-minute radius from the decision, which is the whole reason this page exists.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic appears in all three IB programmes a Dubai school may be authorised for, and it behaves differently in each. The notes below describe how the subject is organised at each stage and what that means for a student heading towards Arabic B in the Diploma years.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic B sits in Group 2 as a language acquisition course at Standard or Higher Level. Assessment is Paper 1 writing at 25 per cent, Paper 2 listening and reading at 50 per cent, and the internally assessed individual oral at 25 per cent. Higher Level adds two literary works and bases the oral on an extract from one of them. The five prescribed themes frame every task, and conceptual understanding of text type is marked explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is the smaller of the two post-16 routes by enrolment, with International Baccalaureate schools accounting for 7 per cent of private-school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, on KHDA's 2024-25 figures. That makes Diploma Arabic B a small cohort inside a small cohort, and it is why a student is often the only person in their year group taking Arabic B at Higher Level.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Arabic is taught as language acquisition in phases rather than year groups, so two students in the same class may sit in different phases. Assessment uses four criteria covering comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating in response to text, and using language in spoken and written form. The phase a student finishes MYP in largely decides whether Arabic B at Higher Level is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's MYP cohort is unusual because a large share of students arrive mid-programme from another system, often with Arabic study that stopped and restarted. A student entering Year 10 from a British school in another emirate may have three years of mandatory Arabic and no phase record at all, and the school places them on evidence collected in the first fortnight.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Arabic appears as an additional language inside transdisciplinary units rather than as a discrete subject with papers. There is no external assessment, so the useful signal for parents is whether the child can decode unfamiliar words and write a connected sentence by the end of Year 6. Those two skills, not vocabulary breadth, are what decide how much ground has to be made up later.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA sets mandatory Arabic from the start of primary in Dubai private schools, and its guidance on instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson runs for at least 25 minutes. Schools may restructure the timetable provided weekly totals are met, which is why two Dubai schools can both comply and still deliver very different amounts of reading practice.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Diploma student rarely needs Arabic B alone. The list below covers the subjects Dubai families most often pair with it, with a note on what each one is actually assessed on, so a combined plan can be built around the heaviest deadline rather than the loudest complaint.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: The page's subject. Marks are lost on Criterion C more than anywhere else: a student writes a competent piece of prose where the task asked for a blog post, a formal letter or a set of instructions, and the text-type conventions were never taught as content.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 route for students who use Arabic as a school language. It assesses literary and non-literary analysis in Arabic, not language acquisition. Students sometimes sit in Arabic B when Arabic A would suit them better, and the misplacement shows up as boredom rather than as low marks.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Designed for genuine beginners and restricted to students with little or no previous exposure to the language. Its prescribed topics are narrower and its written tasks much shorter than Arabic B's. A student who has had years of school Arabic in Dubai is generally not eligible, however weak their marks look.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The commonest Group 1 pairing in Dubai. Paper 1 is unseen guided analysis, and students who find Arabic B's Criterion C hard usually find the same conceptual work hard here. Teaching text type once, across both subjects, is more efficient than teaching it twice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Sits at the opposite end of the week from a language subject and competes for the same revision hours. The practical reason it matters on this page is the internal assessment: the mathematics exploration deadline usually lands in the same term as the Arabic B oral.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Popular in Dubai and useful to Arabic B students because its command terms overlap. A student who can distinguish describe, explain and evaluate in Business can be shown the same distinction inside an Arabic B writing task without learning a new vocabulary of instruction.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Assessed heavily through extended writing and source work. For an Arabic B student the transferable skill is paragraph shape: a claim, support, and a link back to the question. The same structure earns Criterion B marks in Arabic, where students often supply content with no visible argument.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram-led and definition-heavy, with internal assessment commentaries drawn from news articles. The commentary habit of reading a text for its argument rather than its vocabulary is directly useful in the Arabic B reading paper, where questions reward inference over recognition.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay both ask students to handle abstraction in writing. Students who struggle to hold a position in English often cannot hold one in Arabic either, and the Arabic B conceptual criterion is where that weakness becomes a mark penalty.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Can be written in Arabic as a Group 2 essay, which is a serious undertaking and a genuine differentiator on a university application. A tutor's role here is teaching research method and giving feedback on the student's own drafts, never supplying text.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where Dubai's Arabic B students are, and what that does to a session time
dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Arabic B students are spread thinly across the emirate rather than concentrated in one or two communities, which is exactly why a local search returns so little. The notes below describe what each area does to the practical question of when a lesson can start.

regions.name: Jumeirah
regions.note: A dense cluster of IB and British schools within a short radius, so pick-up finishes early and a 4.30pm start is realistic. Many families here run two or three subject tutors in parallel, which makes a fixed weekly slot more valuable than a flexible one.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Several large IB and British schools sit close together, and Al Barsha households often include a child in MYP Arabic and a sibling in Diploma Arabic B. Sequential online slots on the same evening work well because no travel sits between them.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: A strongly Arabic-speaking community where students usually arrive with confident spoken Arabic and uneven writing. Lessons here spend more time on orthography, hamza placement and ta marbuta than on comprehension, which is the reverse of the usual pattern.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: School runs here involve genuine traffic on Damascus Street and Al Ittihad Road, and a 4pm in-home slot is often a 4.25pm start in practice. An online slot removes that loss, which over a two-year Diploma is a substantial number of hours.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools and a young cohort, so more MYP phase questions than Diploma ones. Families here often want a tutor who can keep a child on a path towards Arabic B Higher Level rather than fix an immediate mark.

sections.heading: What a search for an Arabic B tutor in Dubai is usually about
paragraphs: Three distinct problems bring Dubai parents to this search, and they need different lessons. The first is a fluent speaker scoring in the middle band: the child talks easily, understands everything, and writes Arabic that reads like transcribed speech. Marks are lost on register, on orthography and on text type. The second is a student placed in Arabic B who has had years of patchy school Arabic and cannot follow the Paper 2 audio at Diploma speed. The third is a Higher Level student who is comfortable in the language but has never read a literary work in Arabic and now has an oral built on an extract from one.

These three cases look identical on a report card, which usually shows a 4 or a 5 and a comment about effort. They are not identical. The fluent speaker needs editing discipline and text-type conventions and could gain a grade in a term. The patchy-exposure student needs listening volume and a vocabulary base, which takes longer and should start a year before the exam. The Higher Level literature case needs reading support on two specific texts, which no generic Arabic tutor can give without reading them first.

The diagnostic that separates them takes about twenty minutes and is the first thing a trial lesson should do. Give the student an unseen Paper 1 task, let them write under time, and read what comes back. Orthography errors with sound argument point one way. Correct spelling with no argument points another. An inability to start at all usually means the task's text type was never understood, which is a Criterion C problem masquerading as a confidence problem. Everything on the rest of this page assumes that diagnosis has happened first, because planning a two-year language subject on a report-card grade alone is guesswork.
bullets: Fluent speaker, mid-band marks: register, orthography and text type
Patchy school Arabic: listening volume and core vocabulary, started early
Higher Level literature gap: reading support on the school's two chosen works
A twenty-minute unseen writing task tells you which case you have

sections.heading: Arabic A, Arabic B or Arabic ab initio: how the route gets decided
paragraphs: Three Arabic routes run through the Diploma and students are routinely in the wrong one. The school makes the placement, usually in the spring of Year 11, on evidence from MYP phase records, an internal assessment, and what the parent says at home. Each of those three inputs is unreliable on its own. Phase records transfer badly between schools. Internal assessments are often short. And parents reasonably describe a child who chats with grandparents as fluent, when what the Diploma assesses is the formal written register that nobody chats in.

The most consequential error runs in one direction. A strong home speaker placed in Arabic B rather than Arabic A will typically coast to a 6 and resent the course, which costs them nothing in points but wastes two years of Group 2 study. The reverse error, a student with modest Arabic placed in Arabic A, is far more damaging and much harder to unwind after the first term. The third error is a Dubai speciality: a student with years of mandatory school Arabic asking to switch to ab initio because the marks are low. Ab initio is restricted to students with little or no prior exposure, and a Dubai school Arabic record generally rules it out.

The table below sets out what each route is designed for. Take it to the Diploma coordinator rather than to the Arabic department, because the decision is a timetable and eligibility decision as much as a language one. Ask specifically what evidence was used, whether the student's MYP phase was recorded at the previous school, and what the deadline for changing is. In most Dubai schools that deadline sits early in Year 12, and after it a change means dropping and restarting a two-year course.

sections.heading: How Arabic B is assessed, component by component
paragraphs: The assessment model is the same across Group 2 languages, so anything written here about Arabic B holds for French B or Spanish B too. Paper 1 is a single piece of writing produced from a choice of three tasks, each tied to one of the prescribed themes, and each specifying a text type. Standard Level candidates write 250 to 400 words; Higher Level candidates write 450 to 600. It carries a quarter of the final grade and it is marked on three criteria: Criterion A for language, Criterion B for message, and Criterion C for conceptual understanding, which is where text type, register and audience are judged.

Paper 2 carries half the grade and is sat as one paper in two halves. The listening section comes first and the reading section follows, with the Higher Level listening section running longer than the Standard Level one. Recordings are played twice and candidates cannot control them, which makes note-taking technique a scoring skill rather than a study habit. The reading section uses authentic texts at a range of registers and asks inference and reference questions that reward reading the whole text before answering.

The individual oral is internally assessed by the school and externally moderated, and it carries the last quarter. At Standard Level the student is given a visual stimulus linked to one of the themes, prepares under supervision, presents, and then answers follow-up questions before moving to a wider conversation on other themes. At Higher Level the stimulus is an extract from one of the two literary works studied on the course. Four criteria apply, covering language, the message in response to the stimulus, the message in conversation, and interactive skills. Language and interactive skills together carry twice the weight of the two message criteria, which is why a student who answers accurately but minimally scores lower than one who talks fluently with a few errors.

sections.heading: Where Arabic B marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Orthography does the most damage and gets the least teaching. Hamza placement, the difference between ta marbuta and a final ha, alif maqsura against a final ya, and the sun and moon letter rules in writing all produce errors that a fluent speaker never hears because speech does not distinguish them. Each one is a small Criterion A deduction, and across a 500-word Higher Level task they accumulate into a band. The fix is mechanical rather than conceptual: an error log kept across a term, with the same categories revisited until they stop appearing.

Register is the second loss, and it is a conceptual one. Modern Standard Arabic has a formal written range that dialect does not provide, and students substitute a colloquial construction that is perfectly intelligible and plainly wrong for the task. Verb-subject agreement in formal written Arabic, the use of the dual, and the broken plural patterns are the usual casualties. A student who reads Arabic news reporting for fifteen minutes a day for a term absorbs more of this than any amount of grammar instruction delivers, because register is learned by exposure and corrected by feedback.

The third loss is text type, and it is the one nobody is taught. A Paper 1 task naming a blog post expects a blog post: a title, a voice, an audience and the conventions that go with them. A task naming a set of guidelines expects imperative structures and no personal narrative. Students who write a good essay in response to every task cap themselves on Criterion C. Teaching the eight or nine text types that recur, with a model and a checklist for each, is a term's work and the single highest-return thing a tutor can do on this subject. The same is true of the oral: a candidate who answers in one sentence loses interactive marks that no vocabulary work can recover.
bullets: Hamza, ta marbuta and alif maqsura: inaudible in speech, visible on the page
Dialect constructions in a formal task: intelligible, and still marked down

sections.heading: Modern Standard Arabic against the Arabic spoken at home
paragraphs: Arabic is a diglossic language, which means a formal written variety and a set of spoken varieties coexist and do different jobs. Modern Standard Arabic is what newspapers, broadcast news, textbooks and the Diploma use. Emirati, Egyptian, Levantine and Maghrebi dialects are what families use. A child raised in Dubai may hear three or four dialects in a week and no Modern Standard Arabic outside a classroom. That is the structural reason a fluent speaker can struggle in Arabic B, and it is almost never explained to parents in those terms.

The practical consequences are specific. Negation differs between varieties, so a student writes a dialect negation in a formal task. Question formation differs. Future marking differs. Numbers behave differently, and the agreement rules for numbers in formal written Arabic catch out speakers who have never needed them. Vocabulary diverges most of all: everyday nouns that differ between dialect and the standard variety are exactly the words a student reaches for under exam pressure. None of this is a deficiency in the child's Arabic. It is a different variety doing a different job.

A session that takes diglossia seriously is a different session. It treats the student's dialect as an asset for the oral's interactive criterion, where confidence and flow are rewarded, while building the standard variety deliberately for the papers. It uses reading aloud of standard text to train the ear towards Paper 2 audio, which is delivered in Modern Standard Arabic and is the component home fluency helps least with. And it stops apologising for the mismatch, because a student who understands why they are losing marks stops concluding that they are bad at their own language.

sections.heading: KHDA's mandatory Arabic and how it sits beside Diploma Arabic B
paragraphs: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, with the requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and from April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The authority also requires schools to organise separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Language of instruction is specified rather than left open. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students receive Islamic Education and the moral, social and cultural strand in their school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and the guidance advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

One rule matters directly for tuition. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting a child's school Arabic therefore works on the skills the Ministry-set content demands rather than substituting a parallel syllabus, and a tutor supporting Diploma Arabic B works from the IB subject guide instead. Those are two jobs, two sets of criteria and often two different reports home. Families who understand the split stop asking why the school Arabic grade and the Diploma Arabic B grade move in opposite directions.

sections.heading: What Arabic tuition costs in Dubai, and what online changes
paragraphs: Dubai's tutoring market publishes very little in dirhams, which makes the figures below unusual rather than authoritative. They are market rates collected from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table, with each band attributed to whoever published it. They are not IB Gram's price list. What they do show clearly is that format, not subject, drives the number: the same tutor delivering the same hour costs materially more when a car is involved, because travel time is working time and somebody pays for it.

Arabic B sits at the specialist end of the market for a supply reason. The pool of tutors who can teach Modern Standard Arabic at academic register, know the current Diploma subject guide, and mark text types against the published criteria is small in absolute terms. Restrict that pool to people who will drive to one Dubai community at 5pm and it becomes very small indeed. Online delivery is what keeps the match possible at a sane rate, because it is drawn from a pool defined by subject rather than by postcode.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, which for a language subject is closer to parity than it is for a practical science. Writing is shared on screen and annotated live. Audio is played and replayed under exam conditions. Oral practice is recorded, played back and reviewed, which is harder to do well across a dining table. The one genuine loss is informal conversation before and after the hour, and a tutor who builds two minutes of it into the session recovers most of that.

sections.heading: The Diploma language year counted backwards
paragraphs: Language subjects fail quietly because nothing is due until suddenly everything is. The external papers sit at the end of Year 13 in the May session that UAE schools use, and the internal oral sits months earlier in a window the school chooses. Working backwards from those two fixed points, rather than forwards from September, produces a plan that survives the term when three internal assessments arrive together. Get the school's own dates from the Diploma coordinator in the first fortnight of Year 12 and treat them as the calendar, because they are the ones that bind.

In Year 12 the work is accumulation. Themes are covered in the school's order, writing is produced in volume at task length, and the error log is built. Higher Level students should have started both literary works by the end of the year, which is the single most commonly missed milestone on this course: the oral depends on them, and a work read in the final term is not a work the student can discuss. Listening is the other Year 12 priority, because it improves slowly and cannot be crammed.

Year 13 reverses the emphasis. The oral window dominates the first half, and the weeks before it are worth protecting from everything else. Once the recording is done, attention moves to Paper 2, which carries half the grade and is the component most students have practised least, and to Paper 1 under timed conditions across the full range of text types. Mock results arrive mid-year and are the last useful diagnostic. The exam-session dates themselves are set by the IB and published by the school, so confirm them with the coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taking any figure from a tutoring website, including this one.
bullets: Get the school's oral recording window in the first fortnight of Year 12
Both Higher Level literary works started before the end of Year 12
Listening practice weekly from the start, because it will not cram
Confirm every IB session date with the Diploma coordinator or ibo.org

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma work
paragraphs: IB academic honesty rules apply to every piece of assessed work a Diploma student submits, and the boundary matters most in the components a tutor is most likely to be asked to help with. The rule in practice is that the student's submitted work must be their own, and a tutor teaches, questions, models and gives feedback on what the student has produced. Feedback on a draft the student wrote is support. Supplying sentences that end up in the submission is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor.

For the individual oral this means practice stimuli, recorded rehearsals and feedback on fluency and structure are all legitimate, while a script to memorise is not, and would in any case score badly against the interactive criterion. For an Extended Essay written in Arabic, a tutor can teach research method, discuss sources, question an argument and comment on a draft the student has written. For Paper 1 practice there is no honesty question at all, because the work is not submitted, which is why timed practice tasks are the safest and most productive thing to set.

This boundary is worth stating plainly because this market does not always observe it. One provider found in the Dubai search results sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach that triggers IB malpractice procedures against the student who submits it. A tutor who declines to supply text is not being unhelpful; they are the only kind of tutor worth paying for on an assessed component. Ask any prospective tutor what they will do with a draft, and listen for whether the answer involves giving feedback or handing something over.

process.title: Tell us the level, the school and the next deadline
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, the Dubai school, and the date of the next thing that matters: an oral window, a mock, a school report. Those three facts decide which tutor fits and how a term is planned. If the level is still under discussion with the school, say so, because the placement conversation is a different and more urgent one.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial with an unseen writing task
process.description: The trial lesson is free, lasts 45 minutes, and takes no card details. Most of it is diagnostic: an unseen Paper 1 task written under time, read back with the student, and mapped onto Criteria A, B and C. You get a written summary of what the marks are actually being lost on, whether or not you continue.

process.title: A term plan built backwards from the school's dates
process.description: We ask for the school's oral recording window and internal deadlines, then plan the term from those backwards. For Higher Level students that includes when each literary work has to be finished. The plan names text types and themes rather than hours, so progress is visible against something other than attendance.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work returned first
process.description: Tasks are set between lessons and marked against the criteria before the session that discusses them, with the criterion named on every comment. The error log travels with the student across the course, so the same orthography mistake is not diagnosed fresh in March that was diagnosed in October.

process.title: Change the tutor if the fit is wrong
process.description: A language tutor who does not suit a student is worse than none, because the hour becomes something to survive. Say so early and we rematch without argument or a fee. If no Arabic B specialist is free at the time you need, we say that rather than offering a general Arabic tutor and hoping.

whyPoints.title: The tutor is chosen for the subject guide, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Diploma Arabic B is a narrow specialism, and the number of people in any one Dubai community who can mark a Higher Level task against Criterion C is small. Online delivery means the match is made on who knows the course, which for a subject this specific is the difference between a useful hour and a conversation class.

whyPoints.title: Written work is marked before it is discussed
whyPoints.description: A task read for the first time during the lesson wastes the hour. Work is set between sessions and marked against the published criteria first, so the lesson starts from a diagnosis. Each comment names the criterion it relates to, which teaches the student to read the mark scheme rather than the mark.

whyPoints.title: Dialect treated as an asset, not an error
whyPoints.description: A student who speaks Emirati or Levantine Arabic at home has something valuable for the oral's interactive criterion. The job is to build the standard variety alongside it for the papers, not to treat the home language as a mistake. Students who understand the diglossia stop concluding they are bad at Arabic.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the components fluency does not help
whyPoints.description: Home fluency helps least with Paper 2 listening in Modern Standard Arabic and with formal written register. Saying so early sets a realistic timeline: listening improves slowly and cannot be crammed, which is why it starts in Year 12 rather than in the spring of Year 13.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning, modelling and feedback on the student's own drafts, with no text supplied for submission. The rule protects the student, since IB malpractice procedures fall on them. It is also the clearest way to separate a tutor from the providers in this market selling finished coursework.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives a Dubai term
whyPoints.description: Sessions are timed to Gulf Standard Time around school finish times, co-curricular fixtures and Ramadan hours, and can shift to post-Iftar slots when the calendar requires it. No travel sits between a 4pm and a 5pm booking, so siblings in different year groups can be taught back to back.

faqs.question: My child speaks Arabic at home but scores a 4 in Arabic B. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Arabic is diglossic: the Arabic families speak is a dialect, and the Diploma assesses Modern Standard Arabic in formal writing. Fluency at home does not supply the written register, the orthography or the text-type conventions the papers reward. A student can understand everything in a Paper 2 recording and still lose Criterion A marks on hamza placement and dialect constructions in Paper 1. The gap is structural rather than a sign of weak Arabic, and it responds quickly to an error log plus explicit text-type teaching, because the underlying language is already there.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 1 ask an Arabic B student to produce?
faqs.answer: One piece of writing, chosen from three tasks that each tie to one of the five prescribed themes and each specify a text type. Standard Level candidates write 250 to 400 words and Higher Level candidates 450 to 600. It carries a quarter of the final grade and is marked on three criteria: Criterion A for language, Criterion B for message, and Criterion C for conceptual understanding. Criterion C is where most marks go missing, because students produce a competent essay when the task named a blog post, a formal letter or a set of guidelines.

faqs.question: How much of the Arabic B grade sits in the individual oral?
faqs.answer: A quarter. The oral is assessed internally by the school and externally moderated. At Standard Level it starts from a visual stimulus linked to one of the five themes; at Higher Level it starts from an extract from one of the two literary works studied on the course. Four criteria apply, covering language, the message in response to the stimulus, the message in the conversation, and interactive skills. Language and interactive skills together carry twice the weight of the two message criteria, so a candidate giving accurate one-sentence answers scores below one who talks fluently with some error.

faqs.question: Does my child really have to read two literary works for Arabic B Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, at Higher Level only. Two works are studied in Arabic across the course, and the Higher Level individual oral is built on an extract from one of them. Standard Level has no literature requirement, which is the most practical difference between the two levels. The common failure is leaving the reading until the final term: an extract from a work the student skimmed three weeks earlier produces a thin presentation and a thinner discussion. Both works should be finished before the end of Year 12 for a student sitting the oral in Year 13.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Paper 2 listening if the lessons are over video?
faqs.answer: Listening is one of the components online delivery suits best. Audio is shared directly rather than played across a room, so the sound quality is better than a classroom speaker, and the recording can be played twice as the paper requires and then replayed afterwards for analysis, which is the part that teaches. Note-taking technique is taught explicitly before the second hearing, and an error log by question type shows whether marks are being lost on detail, inference or speed. Weekly practice from early in Year 12 matters more than intensity later, because listening improves slowly.

faqs.question: Should a strong home speaker in Dubai be taking Arabic A instead of Arabic B?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is worth asking the Diploma coordinator rather than the Arabic department, because the decision involves eligibility and timetabling as well as language. Arabic A is a Group 1 language and literature course that assesses literary and non-literary analysis in Arabic at academic register. A confident conversational speaker who reads Arabic slowly can struggle badly in it. A student who reads Arabic comfortably and finds Arabic B unchallenging is usually in the wrong course. Most Dubai schools set a deadline early in Year 12, after which a change means restarting a two-year course.

faqs.question: Is my child eligible for Arabic ab initio if their Arabic B marks are low?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Ab initio is restricted to genuine beginners with little or no previous exposure to the language, and a student who has carried KHDA's mandatory school Arabic through a Dubai education generally does not meet that description, however disappointing their marks look. Schools apply the restriction because the course is designed for a different starting point and its tasks are much shorter. Low Arabic B marks are normally a register and text-type problem rather than a placement problem, and they respond to the diagnosis described on this page faster than a course change would.

faqs.question: How does Dubai's mandatory school Arabic differ from Diploma Arabic B?
faqs.answer: They are separate requirements with separate content and separate reporting. KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and the content is set by the Ministry of Education. Diploma Arabic B is an IB course assessed against the IB subject guide. A tutor supporting school Arabic works on the skills the Ministry-set content demands, since using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic B works from the IB guide. Confusing the two wastes half an hour every week.

faqs.question: What does Arabic B tutoring cost in Dubai at market rates?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with premium examiner-led providers publishing up to AED 650. Those figures come from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table, not from us. Format drives the number more than subject does, because travel time is working time somebody pays for.

faqs.question: Do you send an Arabic tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a language subject the trade is a favourable one: writing is annotated live on a shared screen, exam audio is played under proper conditions, and oral rehearsals are recorded and reviewed, which is difficult across a kitchen table. The real gain is the tutor pool, which is selected on knowledge of the subject guide rather than on driving distance.

faqs.question: How many Arabic B sessions a week does a Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week across Year 12 is the common pattern, rising to two in the term containing the individual oral and again in the weeks before the papers. More than two hours weekly rarely helps on a language subject, because the limiting factor is independent reading and listening volume rather than contact time. What changes outcomes is consistency: a task written and marked every fortnight for a year beats an intensive block in the spring, since orthography and register respond to repeated correction rather than to concentrated instruction.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do your Arabic B students come from?
faqs.answer: Mostly the emirate's IB Diploma schools, including Dubai International Academy at Emirates Hills and Al Barsha, GEMS World Academy Dubai, Dubai American Academy, Deira International School, Uptown International School, Raffles World Academy and Emirates International School Jumeirah. Students also come from British-curriculum schools that transfer into a Diploma school for Years 12 and 13. Schools are named as market context only, with no affiliation or endorsement implied. What a tutor needs from a school is its internal calendar: the oral recording window and the mock dates drive the whole plan.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on an Extended Essay written in Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundaries IB academic honesty sets. A tutor can teach research method, discuss sources, question an argument, explain what the assessment criteria reward, and give feedback on drafts the student has produced. What a tutor must not do is supply text that ends up in the submission, because malpractice procedures fall on the student. A Group 2 Extended Essay in Arabic is a demanding choice and a genuinely distinctive one on a university application, and it works best when the research question is narrowed early with help and written entirely by the student.

faqs.question: Can Arabic B sessions move during Ramadan or exam leave?
faqs.answer: Yes. Session times shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan when families prefer that, and reduced school hours during the month usually free earlier afternoon slots as well. Exam leave, study leave and school trips are planned around rather than paid for, and a term plan is agreed against the school's own calendar rather than a fixed weekly grid. The one period we ask families to protect is the fortnight before the school's internal oral recording window, because that is the component with a fixed date and the least room to recover.

faqs.question: What happens if no Arabic B specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than offering a general Arabic tutor and hoping it works out. Diploma Arabic B at Higher Level in particular is a narrow specialism, and the honest options are a different time slot, a short wait for a specialist to free up, or a fortnightly rhythm with written work marked between sessions. What we will not do is put a conversational Arabic tutor in front of a Higher Level student with a literary extract oral in six weeks, because that hour helps nobody and the family finds out too late.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a diagnosis, not a booking
dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-online-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step on Arabic B is not a schedule, it is finding out which of the three common problems you have. Send the level, the Dubai school and the date of the next thing that matters, and the free 45-minute trial will put an unseen Paper 1 task in front of your child, mark it against Criteria A, B and C, and tell you in writing what the marks are being lost on. No card details are taken for the trial. If the answer is that your child is in the wrong Arabic course, we will say that too, because it is more useful than a term of lessons.

intro.heading: The question Dubai parents actually ask first, answered in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars - a currency no UAE family transacts in. One of them asks the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. That is the state of the market, and it is why this page leads with numbers rather than with an argument about quality.

On published figures, Arabic B tuition in Dubai runs from about AED 45 an hour at the bottom of the online market to AED 650 at the examiner-tier top. The band that matters for a Diploma candidate is narrower: roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is published at AED 180 to AED 500, and the difference is travel, not teaching. Those are market rates gathered from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, not IB Gram's price list.

What a parent needs beyond the band is which variables move a quote, because that is where the money is actually decided. Level moves it: Arabic B HL carries two literary works that have to be prepared outside the session. Component moves it: individual oral rehearsal with playback takes more tutor time per hour of lesson than marking a written task. Lead time moves it most of all: the same eight sessions booked in September cost less per hour than booked in March, because in March the only available specialists are the ones already carrying a full Year 13 load.

There is a second reason cost sits at the front of an Arabic B page specifically. Arabic B is one of the cheapest Diploma subjects to fix, because the three things that usually hold a Dubai student back - dialect interference in written Modern Standard Arabic, untrained listening, and no practice with the prescribed text types - all respond to a small number of well-targeted sessions. Families routinely spend more than they need to, over a longer period, because nobody diagnosed which of the three was the problem before the invoicing started.

IB Gram delivers Arabic B as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school day. We do not offer home visits in the UAE - sending a tutor to an address is a service we run only in India - and that is also a pricing fact: you are not paying for a car crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:00 in either direction. Our own figure is quoted after the free trial lesson, when the level, the component and the session length are known, rather than advertised as a band that moves at checkout.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic B appears in more than one IB programme, and the cost of support differs sharply between them because the assessment load does. These are the programmes Dubai schools run and what each one typically costs a family in tutoring hours rather than in fees.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic B sits in Group 2 as a language-acquisition course, taken at SL or HL. Three assessed components: a written task, listening and reading comprehension, and an individual oral. HL adds two literary works in Arabic. For costing purposes the Diploma is the expensive end, because the components are externally assessed and the oral is moderated, so preparation is not optional.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma families typically buy Arabic B support in one of two shapes: a weekly session across Year 13, which at published specialist rates is a substantial two-term commitment, or a block of six to eight sessions aimed at one component. The second shape is cheaper and, where the problem has been diagnosed properly, often just as effective.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Arabic acquisition in the Middle Years Programme is assessed in phases against four criteria, internally, with no external paper. That changes the economics: there is no exam to prepare for, so support is about building the register and the reading habit that the Diploma will later assess. Rates for MYP work sit lower than Diploma rates across the market because the specialism required is narrower.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest Arabic B intervention available to a Dubai family is also the earliest one. An hour a week in Year 10, building Modern Standard Arabic reading and writing, costs less per hour than Year 13 crisis support and removes the need for most of it. Very few families buy it, because nothing has gone wrong yet.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where Arabic B is taken as one of the Diploma courses inside the Career-related Programme, the student sits the same components and is marked on the same scale, so the preparation cost is the same. The surrounding load differs, with a reflective project in place of some written coursework, which usually leaves more weekday time available for language work.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of Dubai schools are authorised to run the Career-related Programme, so a CP student is often the only one in their year taking Arabic B on that route. School revision groups are timetabled for the Diploma cohort, which pushes these students towards paid one-to-one support earlier than their classmates.

dubai/ib-dp-arabic-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic B is the course on this page, and families pricing it are usually pricing one or two other language courses at the same time. These are the Group 1 and Group 2 courses IB Gram covers, with the cost-relevant difference between them.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Acquisition Arabic for students with conversational or dialect Arabic and limited Modern Standard Arabic. Written task, listening and reading, and an individual oral. HL adds two literary works, which is the single biggest driver of the HL-over-SL price difference across this market.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: For genuine beginners with no prior Arabic study. Cheaper to support than Arabic B because the prescribed vocabulary and themes are narrower, but not available to students who have studied Arabic at school, which excludes most Dubai residents.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 route for first-language Arabic speakers. Sits at the top of the market's rate band because the pool of tutors who teach the HL essay and the moderated oral in Arabic is small. Relevant here mainly to families deciding between the A and B routes.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: The commonest Group 2 pairing for an Arabic A student, and sometimes taken by a student who also needs Arabic B support for school-level Arabic. Priced in the same band as Arabic B across this market, with far more tutors available.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: Priced slightly above Arabic B in Dubai because the supply of French B specialists working to Gulf Standard Time is thinner. Useful comparison when a family is choosing which Group 2 language to commit a child to in Year 11.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Chosen by Dubai students with no heritage connection to the language, which makes the HL literary works the costly part. Market rates match Arabic B; the difference is how many hours a student needs rather than the hourly figure.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word prescribed-title essay plus the exhibition. Usually bought as a short block of three or four sessions rather than a weekly commitment, which makes it one of the cheapest pieces of IB support a Dubai family will buy.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Arabic B
subjects.description: A 4,000-word essay in Arabic in one of three categories. Supervision is about scope and source quality and is typically priced as a small number of checkpoint sessions across a year, not as weekly support. The writing is always the student's own.

subjects.name: IGCSE Arabic as a Foreign Language
subjects.description: Held by many Dubai students on entry to Arabic B, and the qualification that sets their habits. Its reward structure for fixed formats is what Arabic B's conceptual-understanding criterion penalises, so the first sessions often cost money to undo earlier learning.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic language acquisition
subjects.description: Internally assessed, no external paper, and the cheapest point in a Dubai family's whole language-support timeline. Support bought here costs less per hour and reduces the hours needed in Year 13, which is the clearest value available in this subject.

sections.heading: What an IB DP Arabic B tutor costs in Dubai, in AED
paragraphs: The band is AED 45 to AED 650 an hour across the whole Dubai market, and quoting that range is almost useless, so here is the narrower version. A university-student tutor working online is published from AED 45 to AED 150. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to AED 300. An IB or IGCSE specialist is published at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A named or examiner-tier tutor reaches AED 500 to AED 650. An in-home one-to-one visit in Dubai runs AED 180 to AED 500, and that figure includes the travel you are funding in both directions.

For a Diploma Arabic B candidate the honest answer is that the two lower tiers are usually a false economy and the top tier is usually unnecessary. Conversational Arabic practice at AED 60 an hour does not move a grade that is being lost on the conceptual-understanding criterion, because the tutor has never read the criterion. Equally, a AED 650 examiner-tier hour buys nothing extra for a student whose problem is that they have never written a formal email in Modern Standard Arabic under timed conditions. The middle band is where the work gets done.

Monthly packages are also published in this market: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider or the rate table that published it. IB Gram quotes its own figure after the free trial lesson, once level, component and session length are known.

sections.heading: The six variables that move an Arabic B quote in Dubai
paragraphs: An hourly band is a starting point, not a quote. Six things decide where inside the band a particular family lands, and five of the six are under the family's control. Knowing which ones matter turns a negotiation about price into a conversation about scope, which is the only version of that conversation worth having.

Level is the first. Arabic B HL carries two literary works that the tutor must also have read and prepared, which is unpaid time that gets priced into the hourly rate. Component is the second: marking a written task takes a tutor twenty minutes outside the session, while oral rehearsal with playback and examiner-style questioning takes closer to an hour. Lead time is the third and the largest. The same block of eight sessions booked in September and booked in March are different products, because in March the available specialists are the ones with a full Year 13 timetable already.

The remaining three are session length, delivery format and frequency. Ninety-minute sessions usually carry a lower effective hourly rate than sixty-minute ones because the preparation overhead is spread further. Format decides whether travel is in the price at all. And frequency cuts both ways: weekly work gives the tutor continuity and justifies a tighter rate, while sporadic one-off sessions cost more per hour because each one needs re-diagnosing.

The variable nobody lists is who is doing the quoting. A marketplace adds a platform margin to the tutor's own figure, an agency adds account management, and a freelancer quotes net but may not hold the permit the law requires. The same teacher can appear at three different prices in the same week depending on which route you reach them through, and none of those three prices tells you anything about their Arabic B experience. Ask for the component history first and the number second. The table below sets out the direction and the rough size of each effect so a quote can be interrogated rather than accepted.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a tuition centre: the Dubai comparison
paragraphs: Parents searching for Arabic B help in Dubai are choosing between four delivery models, and the published price differences between them are mostly about logistics rather than teaching. An in-home visit prices two journeys. A tuition centre prices premises and prices a group. An independent freelancer prices whatever the local market will bear and may or may not hold the permit the law requires. Online one-to-one prices teaching time and preparation and nothing else.

The quality question runs on a separate axis from the price question, which is why a straight comparison of hourly figures misleads. A group class at AED 90 per student per hour is cheap and will not fix a conceptual-understanding problem, because the tutor cannot mark six students' written tasks against criteria inside one lesson. A premium in-home rate on Palm Jumeirah is not buying more expertise than the same tutor would bring to a video call; it is buying the drive. The useful comparison is cost per unit of marked, criterion-referenced work produced.

IB Gram offers one model: one-to-one lessons over live video. We make no home visits in the UAE and we hold no UAE premises, so the comparison below is between what the Dubai market charges for each model rather than between products we sell. Where a family genuinely needs a tutor physically present - a young child, a specific access need - an online platform is the wrong choice and we will say so rather than take the booking.

sections.heading: Why Arabic B is cheaper to fix than most Diploma subjects
paragraphs: Arabic B grades in Dubai are usually held down by three specific, diagnosable things, and all three respond to a small number of sessions. That is unusual. A Physics HL problem can be spread across eight topics and a year of missing foundations; an Arabic B problem is almost always one of three, which means the correct intervention is a block of six to eight sessions rather than a standing weekly commitment running to the end of Year 13.

The first is dialect interference in written Modern Standard Arabic. A Dubai student who speaks Gulf, Egyptian or Levantine dialect at home will carry dialect vocabulary and syntax into written responses under time pressure, and lose marks on the language criterion for things that are mechanical rather than conceptual. Timed writing, marked for register and returned with the pattern named, closes this in six to eight weeks. The second is listening. It is a trained skill, it is worth a substantial share of the grade, and almost no Dubai school timetables practice for it because there is no neat homework to set. Twice-weekly recorded practice over two months moves it.

The third is the prescribed text types. The written task names a text type - a blog, a formal letter, a speech, a set of guidelines - and its conventions carry marks under the conceptual-understanding criterion. Students who have never written a formal letter in Arabic lose those marks every time. This is the cheapest fix of the three: a session per text type, drilled in pairs on identical content, and the problem is gone. Families who buy a year of general Arabic conversation instead typically spend several times as much for less movement.

sections.heading: What the components cost in preparation hours
paragraphs: Arabic B has three assessed components: a written task from a choice of prompts, listening and reading comprehension, and an individual oral that is recorded and moderated. HL adds two literary works in Arabic which supply the material for the HL oral. Converting those components into hours is the piece of arithmetic no competitor page does, and it is the only way to turn an hourly rate into a budget.

The numbers below are typical preparation requirements for a Dubai student starting from a mid-band position, not a promise about any individual. A student further behind needs more; a student with a single narrow gap needs far less. What they show is the shape of the spend: the oral is the most expensive component per mark available, listening is the most expensive in elapsed weeks, and the written task is the cheapest to improve. A family with limited budget and a broad problem should spend it on text types and listening, in that order.

Confirm every weighting with your child's Diploma coordinator before planning around it, because the IB revises course structures on a cycle and schools set internal deadlines months ahead of external ones. The budgeting logic holds regardless: price the component, not the subject, and ask any tutor to tell you how many hours they think a component needs before you agree a rate.

One arithmetic point is worth doing out loud, because families rarely do it. Twelve hours of listening work at the mid band is a four-figure sum in AED, and it buys a component worth a substantial share of the final grade. Four hours of text-type drill at the same rate is a far smaller sum and often buys more movement, because the conceptual-understanding marks were being dropped wholesale rather than partially. Ordering the spend by marks-per-dirham rather than by what feels most urgent is the difference between a budget that works and one that runs out in April with the oral still unrehearsed.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: A tutoring invoice looks different next to a Dubai school fee bill. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat this year. Tutoring rates are not covered by that decision and have not behaved as though they were.

Scale matters too. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with IB programmes accounting for roughly a fourteenth of enrolment. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by six per cent. More IB places means more Arabic B candidates competing for the same small pool of specialists, which is a supply pressure on rates rather than a quality one.

The practical conclusion for a Dubai family is that tutoring is the variable line in an education budget and the school fee is the fixed one. A single weekly specialist hour across two Diploma terms is a meaningful sum. Six targeted sessions after a proper diagnosis is a fraction of it.

There is one more item families forget to budget for, and it is not tutoring. A student sitting any component as a private candidate, or re-sitting in a later session, pays entry fees to the school or centre administering the examination, and those are set by the centre rather than by the board. Ask your school's examinations officer for the figure early, because it lands in the same term as the heaviest tutoring months and it is the expense that most often arrives unannounced.
