sections.heading: When the slot you need is taken
paragraphs: Standard Level Biology is easier to staff than Higher Level Chemistry, but the Dubai evening is still the Dubai evening. Between four and eight on Gulf Standard Time, in the weeks after February mocks, the slots a working family can actually use are the ones everybody wants. Here is what happens rather than what is advertised.

If no Biology specialist is free in your preferred slot, you get the real options: a different time in the same week, a weekend morning, or a named date when a slot opens with nothing charged until it does. For an evidence-led arrangement the weekend morning is often the better choice anyway, because the timed papers that anchor the whole plan give a truer reading from a rested student than from one who has been at school since seven. If no specialist whose day overlaps Gulf Standard Time can cover the brief, we say so and state what is available, including any time difference, before you decide. No competitor page examined for this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

And if the evidence says you do not need us, that is also an answer. A student whose error log is dominated by command terms needs two or three sessions and then nothing. A student with no marked papers at all needs to attempt one before anybody is paid. A student who is not working between sessions is not short of teaching. We would rather write that in a verdict and lose the booking than keep an arrangement running that the marked work cannot justify.

process.title: Send the evidence you already have
process.description: The last two marked Biology papers with annotations, the most recent report, and if it exists the IGCSE component breakdown. Most Dubai families already hold more evidence than they realise and have never lined it up. Doing so before the first session usually identifies the dominant error category straight away.

process.title: Run the baseline paper in week one
process.description: A timed past paper under exam conditions, marked with annotation, producing the first error log. This is the measurement everything afterwards is compared against, which is why it happens before any teaching rather than after a few comfortable sessions have shifted expectations.

process.title: Teach only what the log identifies
process.description: Sessions aim at the dominant category and nothing else, with a note after each one naming the specific errors addressed. Declining to teach topics the marked work has not flagged is what makes a short arrangement productive instead of merely reassuring.

process.title: Re-test under the same conditions
process.description: A second timed paper at week five, same length, same conditions, marked the same way, so the two scripts are genuinely comparable. The point is not the mark but whether the dominant category in the error log has shrunk, which is the question the whole plan is built to answer.

process.title: Read the six-week verdict together
process.description: A written document setting both scripts side by side, stating what moved, what did not, and which of continue, change or stop the evidence supports. We commit to all three outcomes in advance, including the one that ends the arrangement and the invoice with it.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts, not reassurance
whyPoints.description: A session note after every lesson, an annotated script roughly every third, a running error log and dated draft feedback. All readable, all yours, all challengeable. The week-nine conversation in which nobody can say what has been achieved does not happen when documents exist.

whyPoints.title: Errors sorted, not counted
whyPoints.description: Marks lost are sorted into content, command term, misread question, time and processing. A script losing twelve marks entirely under command term needs two sessions; the same twelve marks spread across categories needs four small interventions. The sorting is what tells you which.

whyPoints.title: Comparable measurements
whyPoints.description: A timed paper under exam conditions at the start of a block and another at the end, marked identically. Two numbers that can honestly be compared beat six weeks of impressions, and they make a plateau visible early rather than in a February mock.

whyPoints.title: A verdict that can be negative
whyPoints.description: At six weeks a written verdict says continue, change or stop, and stop is a real option we commit to in advance. A provider who has never recommended that a family stop paying has not been measuring anything.

whyPoints.title: No invented statistics
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no average grade improvement, no success rate, no self-awarded star rating, no guaranteed outcome. We cannot publish the sample size, date range and method those would need, and a number without them is decoration rather than evidence.

whyPoints.title: A draft trail that protects the student
whyPoints.description: Dated written feedback on each investigation draft shows what was advised, when, and that the changes were the student's own work. We supply no text and no method. That record is the cleanest demonstration available that the honesty line was respected.

faqs.question: How will we know in writing whether the Biology sessions are working?
faqs.answer: By comparing two timed papers marked the same way, and by watching whether the dominant category in the error log shrinks. A paper under exam conditions in week one gives a baseline; another in week five gives a comparable measurement; the written verdict at week six sets them side by side and states what moved. Everything else, including how the sessions feel and what your child says about them, is weaker evidence. If no marked scripts exist after six weeks of weekly sessions, the question cannot be answered, and that absence is itself the finding.

faqs.question: What exactly do we receive after each session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was covered and, more usefully, what the student got wrong during the session. The second part is the one that matters, because a note saying only the topic is a receipt rather than information. Roughly every third session you also receive an annotated marked script with the mark reasoning visible, and the running error log is updated each time. During the investigation period, each draft comes back with dated written feedback. All of it is kept on file so a pattern across weeks is readable rather than remembered.

faqs.question: Can we see a marked paper with the reasoning rather than just a score?
faqs.answer: That is the only form of marking worth paying for. A score tells you where a student stands and nothing about why, which means it cannot generate a next step. An annotated script shows the exact point where a mark was lost, whether the biology was absent or the instruction was missed, and which questions were rushed. Ask any prospective provider to annotate one paper before you commit, and ask how quickly it comes back. A marked script returned three weeks later has stopped being evidence and become a souvenir.

faqs.question: Our daughter's grade has not moved in six weeks. Does that mean it is failing?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the error log settles it. Three innocent patterns exist: the score can fall while the work improves, because she has started attempting extended-response questions she previously skipped; it can sit flat and then jump, because command-term discipline is a habit that holds or does not; and it can rise on a kinder paper while the underlying category is unchanged. What is not innocent is the same category dominating the log after six weeks of work aimed at it. That means the approach is wrong rather than insufficient, and more of it will not help.

faqs.question: How many marked papers should a Standard Level Biology student have attempted before mocks?
faqs.answer: Enough that timed conditions are ordinary rather than an event, which in practice means several complete papers rather than one. The number matters less than the marking: three papers attempted and properly annotated are worth more than eight attempted and self-scored, because self-scoring cannot see a command-term failure, which is where most of the marks go. The other requirement is comparability. Papers attempted under different conditions, at different times of day, with different amounts of help, do not form a trend you can read.

faqs.question: What does an error log look like and who keeps it?
faqs.answer: One page, maintained by the tutor and shared with you, listing each mark lost from each marked script against five categories: content not known, command term not met, question misread, time ran out, and processing error. After three scripts the distribution is visible at a glance, and that distribution is the brief. Most Dubai parents seeing it for the first time are surprised how little of the loss is missing content. The student should also keep a copy, because reviewing their own pattern before a paper changes behaviour more reliably than being told about it does.

faqs.question: Do you publish a success rate or an average grade improvement?
faqs.answer: No, and we would be suspicious of anyone who does. A meaningful statistic needs a sample size, a date range and a stated method, and a figure lacking those three things carries no information whatever it looks like. Pages in this market display satisfaction percentages with none of them, and at least one carries a self-awarded star rating in its structured data that differs from the figure printed on the page. What we provide instead is evidence about your own child, which is the only sample relevant to your decision, including when it is unflattering.

faqs.question: How do we check the tutor actually read the investigation draft properly?
faqs.answer: Read the feedback. Genuine draft feedback is specific to that draft and that student: it names the research question's weakness, says whether the replication will support a mean with a defensible measure of spread, points at a particular paragraph where the evaluation is thin, and identifies a conclusion that has run past its data. Generic feedback that could be pasted onto any report is visible immediately. The feedback is dated and kept on file, so you can also see what changed between drafts, which tells you whether the comments were acted on.

faqs.question: Who keeps the record if we change tutors mid-term?
faqs.answer: You should, and that is an argument for insisting on documents from the start. If the session notes, the annotated scripts and the error log sit in your hands rather than in a departing tutor's head, a new tutor begins with the diagnosis already done and the first two sessions are not spent rediscovering it. This is the single most practical reason to require a written trail even when you are happy with the current arrangement. Tutors move, families relocate, and an undocumented six weeks has to be bought again.

faqs.question: Can the school see the session notes, and should they?
faqs.answer: They can if you share them, and often it helps. A subject teacher who knows that a student's lost marks are concentrated under explain questions can reinforce exactly that in class at no cost to you, and may well have noticed the same thing. What should not happen is anything resembling a negotiation about the internal mark on the scientific investigation; that mark is the school's and a paid tutor has no part in it. Share the diagnosis, not a request. Most Dubai teachers respond well to a parent arriving with specific evidence rather than a general worry.

faqs.question: What counts as evidence that the problem was never Biology?
faqs.answer: Three things show up clearly. If the error log is dominated by command term rather than content, the student knows the biology and is answering the wrong instruction, which is a writing problem. If the processing-error category dominates and the same student struggles with a bare algebraic rearrangement outside any biology context, the limitation is mathematical. And if performance is strong on untimed work and collapses under a clock, the issue is pacing and exam conditions. None of those three is solved by more biology teaching, and all are visible within two marked scripts.

faqs.question: Is a monthly progress report enough, or do we need notes every week?
faqs.answer: A monthly report is a summary of something, and if nothing was recorded weekly it is a summary of memory. Weekly notes cost the tutor a few minutes and give you the raw material: what was covered, what the student got wrong, what they should do before next time. The monthly or half-term document then has something to summarise and a verdict can rest on it. The practical test is whether a report names specific errors from specific sessions. If it describes effort and attitude in general terms, nothing was recorded along the way.

faqs.question: What does the evidence look like when we should stop paying?
faqs.answer: Three signatures. The named target has been hit and the marked scripts show it, in which case stopping is success rather than abandonment. The same error category dominates the log after six weeks of work aimed squarely at it, which means the approach is wrong and buying more is the costliest possible response. Or the student has begun doing the work independently and the marked papers hold up without sessions, which was the goal. The fourth case is an absence: no marked scripts after six weeks means there is nothing to justify the next invoice.

faqs.question: Is the evidence trail different for Standard Level Biology than for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Same artefacts, different pacing. Standard Level is 150 taught hours against 240, so a smaller body of content has to be covered and a plateau becomes interpretable sooner: six weeks of marked work genuinely tells you something. At Higher Level there is more material in play, so a flat sequence of scripts can reflect breadth not yet covered rather than a technique problem. One Standard Level specific point matters: ignore any question drawn from Higher Level-only material, because a Standard Level student failing it has produced no information about their own course.

faqs.question: Our son says the sessions are going well but the marks say otherwise. Which do we trust?
faqs.answer: The marks, but read them before concluding anything. Sessions can genuinely go well while marks stay flat, because understanding in the presence of a tutor is not the same as retrieving under a clock, and that gap is the commonest finding in the whole of paid tutoring. The error log tells you which it is. If the log shows content being secured and time running out, the sessions are working and the pacing is not. If the log shows the same content gaps recurring, the sessions feel productive and are not landing, and the approach needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: Does a recorded session count as evidence of what was taught?
faqs.answer: Of what was taught, yes; of what was learned, no, and the distinction decides how useful it is. A recording is genuinely valuable to the student, who can revisit an explanation of membrane transport in February having met it in October. As evidence for a parent it is weak, because nobody will watch an hour of it and watching would not reveal whether anything stuck. The written note, the annotated script and the error log are compact and diagnostic. Keep recordings for the student's revision and judge the arrangement on the documents.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the documents before you agree the first session
dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-home-tutor.closingBody: The difference between a Standard Level Biology arrangement that works and one that merely continues is usually not the tutor. intro.heading: Why a student who knows the biology still scores a 4
paragraphs: The most frequent description Dubai parents give of a Standard Level Biology problem is that their child knows the material. Quite often they are right. The student can define osmosis, name the stages of mitosis, and explain what an enzyme does. Then the paper arrives, and the questions are about an unfamiliar organism, a graph nobody has seen, and a method the student has to criticise. Knowledge is necessary and it is not sufficient, and a page that pretends otherwise is not going to help.

Diploma science papers are written against assessment objectives that go well beyond recall: knowing things, applying them to new situations, analysing and evaluating evidence, and demonstrating the skills of investigation. Paper 1 at Standard Level is ninety minutes and 36% of the grade, with a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is also ninety minutes and 44%, built from short answers and extended responses. The investigation is 20% and is marked out of 24. Across all of it, the proportion of marks available for simply stating something is much smaller than students assume.

This is why defining everything correctly produces a 4. The definition marks are banked, the application marks are partly earned, and the analysis and evaluation marks are largely missed, because nobody has ever shown the student what an answer to one of those questions looks like. The content is not where the hours should go. The question types are.

There is a second, cheaper problem sitting alongside it, and Biology is unusual in having it: drawing marks. Labelled diagrams, annotated drawings, magnification and scale calculations, interpreting a micrograph. These are marks awarded for a technique nobody practises, routinely lost for things as small as drawing with a sketchy double line or writing a label where an annotation was required. Fixing that is one session, and it shows up on the next assessment.

Everything here runs online, one student at a time, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time slots arranged around your child's school week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we provide only in India. A shared screen is the right surface for marking a drawing and for working a data question with the figure in front of both people, which is the bulk of what these sessions do.

The page also sets out the DP2 calendar by who controls each deadline, because most of the dates that govern a Dubai Biology student's year are set by their own school rather than by the IB. The first lesson is free, lasts 45 minutes, covers one subject and asks for no card details. Every AED figure quoted below is a market rate with its source and the month it was read.

programmes.countryNote: Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate candidates at 7% of enrolment, and seven more schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake. Standard Level Biology sets in these schools are often the largest science groups on the timetable, which is the practical reason an individual student's drawing technique has never been corrected.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-19 · Career pathway with DP courses
programmes.description: Career-related Programme students take at least two Diploma Programme courses alongside their career-related study, the reflective project and the personal and professional skills course. Standard Level Biology is a common choice for health and sports pathways. The examination is identical to the one a full Diploma candidate sits, including the investigation and its four criteria, which is not always obvious from the way the pathway is described.
programmes.countryNote: The number of Dubai schools running the Career-related Programme is small but increasing. Its students are the easiest in any school to under-serve, because revision sessions, mock timetables and study groups are built for the full Diploma cohort. A Career-related Biology candidate is frequently the only student in their band sitting that paper.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years Sciences is integrated and criterion-assessed, and its investigations reward process. A student arriving in Standard Level Biology has usually had more practice designing an experiment than answering a question about somebody else's. The two things to build before DP1 begins are reading a question for what it asks rather than what it is about, and producing precise definitions from memory rather than in context.
programmes.countryNote: Because Middle Years criterion grades look reassuring, Dubai families rarely test either skill before the Diploma starts. A short block in the final Middle Years term aimed at question analysis is more useful than content preview, and it costs less than the remediation it prevents in the first term of DP1.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Standard Level Biology rarely arrives alone in a request. The grid below shows the subjects Dubai families most commonly ask about alongside it, and what the real request usually turns out to be once the first session has happened.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Themes A to D at common-core depth: unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Sessions concentrate on application and analysis questions, on drawing and annotation marks, and on the data-based section of Paper 1 where Standard Level candidates lose most.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken alongside Biology by students keeping a health pathway open. The usual request is quantitative rather than conceptual, since the moles and concentration arithmetic is what blocks progress, and a session shaped like maths often helps the chemistry grade more than one shaped like chemistry.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Overlaps heavily with Biology physiology and uses the same assessment model, including the identical investigation criteria. Dubai students often take both, and anything learned about annotated diagrams or evaluating a method counts in both subjects without extra work.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A frequent third Standard Level. Shares the skill of evaluating a study rather than reciting it, and the research-methods content supports the investigation's data analysis criterion. Students who find evaluation hard in one subject almost always find it hard in both.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Pairs well with Biology because both reward reading a figure and writing an evaluated conclusion from it. Where a Biology data question is failing, a Geography resource-interpretation question usually is too, and one block of sessions can address both.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Common in Dubai timetables as a Standard Level alongside Biology. Its internal assessment matures in the same DP2 window as the Biology investigation, so families ask for both coursework calendars side by side before allocating any hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The usual maths route for a Standard Level Biology student. Its statistics and graph work map directly onto Paper 1B, which is the section most Biology students lose marks in, so the two subjects are better planned together than separately.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Shares ecology content and the diversity index with Biology theme C, and counts in Group 3 or Group 4. Students taking both need help distinguishing the two subjects' command terms, since the systems paper rewards weighing competing perspectives.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Requested by Diploma students whose week already contains the mandatory UAE subjects. Where Arabic and Biology are both being supported, the scheduling question comes first, because the fixed mandatory lessons determine which evenings are genuinely free.

sections.heading: What a Standard Level Biology paper is actually testing
paragraphs: The Diploma science guides set out assessment objectives that cover more than knowledge: demonstrating what you know, understanding and applying it in new situations, analysing and evaluating evidence, and demonstrating the skills needed to carry out an investigation. A student who treats the course as a body of facts to be memorised is preparing for one of those four and hoping the others look after themselves.

In practice the examination is built the other way round. A multiple-choice item usually requires a fact to be applied rather than merely recalled. A data-based question gives an unfamiliar figure and asks what it supports. A Paper 2 extended response asks for a mechanism in sequence, or for a comparison, or for a judgement on whether the evidence is good enough. Very few marks are available for the definition alone.

This is the single most useful thing a parent can understand before buying tutoring hours, because it determines what the hours should contain. If your child's school report says their knowledge is sound but their examination performance is weak, the answer is not revision in the usual sense. It is practice at the three objectives nobody has drilled: application, analysis, evaluation.

The table maps each objective to where it dominates and how it is practised, because the practice method differs for each. Application needs unfamiliar contexts. Analysis needs figures the student has not seen. Evaluation needs somebody else's flawed method to criticise. None of those can be generated by rereading a textbook, which is why the subject resists the revision style that works for a vocabulary list.

sections.heading: The question types in a Standard Level Biology paper, one by one
paragraphs: Students revise content and sit question types, and the mismatch is where a term of effort disappears. There are not many types. Once a student can name the type in front of them and say what form the answer takes, their mark rises without any new biology being learned. That is an uncomfortable fact for anyone selling content teaching, and it is consistently what marked Dubai scripts show.

The hardest type for Standard Level candidates is the comparison. Asked to distinguish between two structures or processes, students write a paragraph about the first and a paragraph about the second. Mark schemes award for linked differences, stated on the same axis: this one does X whereas that one does Y. The same content, reorganised, scores twice as much, and the reorganisation takes one session to teach.

The second hardest is evaluation. Asked whether a method supports a conclusion, students either accept it or list every limitation they can think of. Neither scores well. The mark scheme wants the limitations that actually matter for the conclusion drawn, ranked, with a statement about what could still be claimed. Students find this easier once they see that it is a judgement rather than a list, and it is the skill that most reliably separates a 5 from a 6.

The table below sets out the types, what each one needs, and the error that recurs. It is worth keeping beside a past paper: the student names the type before writing anything, which slows the first thirty seconds of each answer and saves several marks across the paper.

A list of true statements with no causal link

Two separate descriptions, one per structure

sections.heading: Drawings, labels and scale: the marks Standard Level candidates hand back
paragraphs: Biology is the only Group 4 subject where drawing technique carries marks in its own right, and it is the cheapest set of marks on the whole course to recover. Examiners expect clean single lines rather than sketchy double ones, proportions that match what was observed, and no shading. Students who have never been told this draw the way they draw in a notebook and lose marks for presentation alone, with the biology entirely correct.

The label and annotation distinction is worth more. A label names a structure. An annotation says something about it: a function, a property, a relationship to another structure. Mark schemes ask for one or the other, and a student who writes labels where annotations were required has answered a different question. Annotations are sentences, and teaching a student to write them as sentences takes about twenty minutes.

Magnification and scale are the third piece. Calculating magnification from a scale bar, or working an actual size from a stated magnification, appears regularly and is lost to unit confusion more than to method. Micrometres and millimetres, converted in the middle of a calculation, with the answer left without a unit. It is a procedure, and like all procedures it holds once practised four or five times.

This whole area is two or three sessions. Drawings are photographed and marked on screen, which works better than marking them in a classroom because the image can be enlarged and annotated live. Of everything on this page it has the shortest gap between the session and the visible result, which is why families with an assessment three weeks away are often pointed here first.

sections.heading: Biology as the sixth subject: what good enough looks like
paragraphs: A large share of Standard Level Biology students in Dubai are not going anywhere near biology after the Diploma. They took it to satisfy Group 4, or because it was the least unappealing science, and their Higher Levels are the subjects their university offer depends on. For these students the right question is not how to maximise the Biology grade. It is how few hours it takes to stop Biology costing them points they need elsewhere.

That is a legitimate question and it deserves a straight answer rather than an upsell. The Diploma total is built from six subject grades plus points from the core, with a published minimum and conditions attached, so a Standard Level subject contributes to the total without being the number a university reads closely. A student two marks short in Biology and five marks short in a Higher Level that matters should not be spending equal hours on each.

For that student the highest-yield work is almost entirely technique: the question types table above, the drawing marks, and enough data-question practice to stop losing Paper 1B. That is a block of six to eight sessions, not a term, and it can be done in DP1 and left alone. Content gaps in secure areas can be ignored deliberately. Saying so costs us hours and it is the honest advice.

The students who do need more are the ones whose degree target includes Biology, who are weighing a move up to Higher Level, or who have a genuine content deficit from a mid-cycle school change. Those three cases are visible in the first session, and they get a different recommendation. The first conversation should establish which of the four situations your child is in, because they do not share a plan.
bullets: Establish first whether Biology is a points subject or a target subject

sections.heading: The Standard Level investigation inside forty practical hours
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20% of the Standard Level grade, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. The criteria are identical to Higher Level, which routinely surprises families. What is different is the practical budget: 40 hours across the whole Standard Level course rather than 60, and a school laboratory shared with every other set in the year.

The result is a predictable failure. A student designs a method that needs five concentrations, five replicates and three weeks of growth, gets two sessions of laboratory time, and ends up writing a conclusion from a data set that cannot support one. Research design and data analysis both suffer, and since each criterion is a quarter of the marks, one planning error can cost eight of the twenty-four.

The single most valuable session in this component happens before any data is collected, and it is mostly arithmetic rather than biology: how many laboratory periods are actually available, how many measurements fit in one, what range of the independent variable that permits, and whether a secondary-data or database investigation would produce better evidence than a thin wet-lab one. Database investigations are legitimate and well suited to a tight practical budget, provided the data source is properly identified and the processing is the student's own.

On support boundaries: a tutor teaches and gives feedback. Worked examples of error handling, an explanation of what an evaluation has to weigh rather than list, criterion-by-criterion comments so the student can see which marks are unearned. No sentence of the report comes from anyone but the student, and every checkpoint leaves a written record the school may inspect. Anyone selling a finished investigation is selling a risk that lands on the candidate's Diploma, not on theirs.
bullets: Four criteria, six marks each, identical at Standard and Higher Level
40 practical hours across the course, shared laboratory access
Count the available laboratory periods before fixing the method
Database and secondary-data investigations suit a tight practical budget

sections.heading: The DP2 year counted backwards, and who sets each deadline
paragraphs: Almost every date that governs a Dubai Diploma student's second year is set by their own school rather than by the IB, and families consistently discover this too late. The school sets the investigation draft deadline, the final internal submission date, the mock examination window, and the point at which predicted grades are issued. Those four dates shape the autumn entirely, and they can be obtained in writing from the Diploma coordinator in September.

The IB sets the examination session and the release of results. This page does not publish those dates. Automated access to the IB's own pages is blocked, which means no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and publishing an unverified examination date on a tutoring page would be worse than publishing none. Your school's coordinator has the confirmed calendar, and it should be read from there.

What a family can do with the school-set dates is work backwards. If the investigation draft is due in the second week of November, data collection has to finish in October, which means the method has to be fixed in late September, which means the research question needs to be settled before the autumn half term. Written out like that, the autumn is tight but manageable. Discovered in November, it is neither.

The table lists the milestones with who controls each one and what should be finished by then. It is deliberately silent on specific dates, because the whole point is that your school's version is the one that matters and a generic calendar would mislead. Filling in the middle column from the coordinator's reply takes ten minutes and is the most useful planning any Diploma parent does.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and KHDA's requirements for these subjects applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Diploma student this is not a footnote. It is several fixed periods a week that sit outside the six Diploma subjects and outside the core, and it is the first thing that determines which evenings are actually free.

KHDA also sets how these classes are organised. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students are taught in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is why a tutor supporting Arabic works within the school's own material rather than bringing a parallel syllabus.

The practical consequence for Biology is scheduling, and the table makes it concrete. Map the fixed mandatory periods first, then place the Biology slot. Families who do this in September keep the same slot all year; families who do not find themselves renegotiating in October when the timetable settles. No competitor page reviewed in this market mentions these subjects at all, which is strange given how much of a Dubai student's week they occupy.

sections.heading: What Standard Level Biology support costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an IB or A Level specialist at roughly AED 200-450 and above, from agency rate pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table as read in October 2026. Platform rates for university-student tutors advertise from around AED 33-150. In-home visiting rates including travel are quoted at AED 180-500, and a premium named tutor is advertised at up to AED 650 an hour.

Standard Level usually sits in the lower half of the specialist band, because the pool of tutors who can teach it well is larger than the Higher Level pool. Several providers quote one International Baccalaureate rate regardless of level, so it is worth asking directly. Monthly packages visible in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

The more important question for a Group 4 student is total hours rather than hourly rate. A technique block of six to eight sessions at a mid-band rate costs less than a term of weekly content teaching and will usually move the grade further. A provider who recommends a term before seeing any of your child's work is recommending a revenue plan. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page; the first lesson is free and the rate is agreed in writing before the second.

For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring in this market run from AED 240-600 at the budget end to AED 600-1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year.

sections.heading: Scheduling, coverage and the permit a paid tutor needs
paragraphs: Sessions are booked in Gulf Standard Time against the school's own week, with the mandatory UAE subject periods mapped first. For a Standard Level technique block, weekly works better than fortnightly, because each session builds on a specific drill rather than testing retention. Once the block is finished most families stop, which is the intended outcome rather than a lost customer.

Ramadan shortens the school day and moves the evening. Post-Iftar sessions are available and they work, particularly for drawing and data practice which does not require long sustained concentration. Agreeing the change before Ramadan starts is what makes it work rather than deciding in the first week. Eid is normally a clean pause, and a six-session block simply runs over eight weeks instead of six.

Coverage is disclosed before you book. A Standard Level Biology specialist in a narrow early-evening window is a more specific request than it sounds, and some weeks it cannot be met. The alternatives are a different time with the right specialist, a dated waiting period, or a tutor whose Standard Level experience is adjacent rather than exact, stated plainly so you can judge it yourself. No page reviewed in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

On the legal position: individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so none is quoted here. MoHRE's own service page is the official route to apply.

process.title: Describe what goes wrong in one sentence
process.description: Not the grade, the symptom. Knows the definitions and loses marks on long questions. Blank on data figures. Drawings always marked down. That sentence places your child in a row of the question-types table, and the first session is built from it rather than from a syllabus overview.

process.title: Say what Biology is for
process.description: A Group 4 requirement and a points subject needs a different plan from a subject a university offer depends on. We ask this in the first message because the honest recommendation for the first case is often a short block, and that answer is easier to give before anything is booked.

process.title: Free 45-minute first lesson
process.description: One subject, 45 minutes, no card details taken. The student works one data question, one explain question and one drawing, which between them identify the problem. You receive a written note naming the question types to drill and an estimated number of sessions.

process.title: Run the block, then stop
process.description: Technique blocks are finite. Six to eight sessions for the assessment objectives, two or three for drawing and data, and the block closes when the drill holds. Continuing afterwards is a decision to make on new evidence, not a default.

process.title: Test it cold on an unseen paper
process.description: At the end of a block the student sits unseen questions of the same types with no warning and no revision. The mark on those is the evidence. It is more informative than asking whether the student feels more confident, which almost everyone says yes to.

whyPoints.title: Built on question types, not a content tour
whyPoints.description: Most Standard Level Biology marks are lost in application, analysis and evaluation rather than recall. Sessions drill those directly with unfamiliar contexts and unseen figures, which is the work that cannot be done by rereading a textbook at home.

whyPoints.title: Drawing marks treated as marks
whyPoints.description: Biology awards marks for clean lines, correct proportion and annotations written as sentences, and almost nobody teaches it. Two or three sessions covers the whole area, and it is the fastest visible improvement available on the course.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks when short blocks are right
whyPoints.description: A Group 4 points subject rarely needs a term. If six sessions is the honest answer, that is what gets recommended, and the block ends when the drill holds rather than when a subscription runs out.

whyPoints.title: Your school's calendar, not a generic one
whyPoints.description: The deadlines that govern a DP2 Biology student are set by their own school. This page names who controls each one and where to get it, and publishes no unverified IB examination date, because none in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory UAE subjects accounted for
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies occupy fixed periods in every Dubai private school week. Those are mapped before a Biology slot is chosen, which is why these bookings survive the October timetable settling.

whyPoints.title: Online, with the reason stated once
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we provide only in India. A shared screen is the better surface for marking a drawing or working a figure, and it puts a Standard Level specialist within reach of every community in the emirate.

faqs.question: How much of Standard Level Biology is memorising and how much is applying?
faqs.answer: Far less memorising than students assume. The Diploma science guides set objectives covering knowledge, understanding and application, analysis and evaluation, and investigation skills, and only the first is satisfied by learning definitions. Multiple-choice items usually require a fact applied to a new case. Data questions give unfamiliar figures. Paper 2 extended responses want a mechanism in sequence, a linked comparison or a judgement. A student who can define everything and scores a 4 has banked the recall marks and missed most of the rest, which is a technique problem rather than a knowledge one.

faqs.question: Are marks really awarded for biological drawings, and how are they lost?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are lost mostly to presentation rather than biology. Examiners expect clean single lines rather than sketchy double ones, proportions that match what was observed, and no shading. Students who have never been told this draw as they would in a notebook and lose marks with the biology entirely correct. Add the magnification and scale calculations, which go wrong on unit conversion between micrometres and millimetres more often than on method. Two or three sessions covers the whole area and it shows up on the next assessment.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a label and an annotation in a Biology drawing?
faqs.answer: A label names a structure. An annotation says something about it: what it does, a property it has, how it relates to another structure. Mark schemes specify which is wanted, and a student writing labels where annotations were required has answered a different question and scores accordingly. The practical fix is to teach annotations as sentences rather than as words, which takes about twenty minutes and then needs practising on four or five different drawings before it becomes the default.

faqs.question: My son can define everything and still scores a 4. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: He is almost certainly answering the topic rather than the question. The commonest pattern in marked Standard Level scripts is a comparison question answered as two separate descriptions, and an evaluation question answered either by accepting the method or by listing every limitation that comes to mind. Mark schemes award for linked differences on the same axis, and for the limitations that matter to the conclusion, ranked. The content he has is sufficient; the organisation of the answer is what is costing the marks, and it is a few sessions of drilling rather than a term.

faqs.question: How much less content does Standard Level Biology cover than Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Ninety taught hours less, 150 against 240, and twenty fewer practical hours. Standard Level covers the common core of themes A to D and omits the Higher Level extensions, which cluster in cell respiration and photosynthesis in detail, neural signalling, gene expression and inheritance with linkage. Standard Level papers also run ninety minutes each rather than two hours and two and a half. The investigation is identical: same four criteria, same twenty-four marks, same share of the grade, which regularly catches families expecting something lighter.

faqs.question: What does a Standard Level Biology tutor charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with International Baccalaureate and A Level specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above, from published agency rate pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table as read in October 2026. Platform rates for university-student tutors start near AED 33-150. Standard Level usually sits in the lower half of the specialist band because the tutor pool is larger, and several providers quote one rate for both levels, so it is worth asking directly before accepting a figure.

faqs.question: There are three weeks until a school assessment. What is still worth doing?
faqs.answer: Triage, not coverage. Three weeks is enough to drill two or three question types and to fix drawing technique, and not enough to repair a term of content. The useful sequence is: get the assessment's stated content, identify which question types carry the most marks in it, practise those with unseen material, and explicitly abandon the rest. Writing down what you are not going to revise is the part students resist and the part that makes the plan work. One timed section should be sat before the day so pacing is known.

faqs.question: Can the Standard Level investigation use data from a database instead of a laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, and inside a 40-hour practical budget with shared laboratory access it is often the better choice. A database or secondary-data investigation can produce far stronger evidence than a thin wet-lab data set collected across two rushed periods, provided the data source is properly identified and all the processing and reasoning are the student's own. The criteria do not favour one approach over the other; they reward a design that can actually answer the question. This is worth deciding before the research question is finalised, not afterwards.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect a Diploma student's week in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They occupy fixed periods that sit outside the six Diploma subjects. Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The practical effect is that those periods determine which evenings are genuinely free, so they should be mapped before a tutoring slot is chosen.

faqs.question: Which deadlines does a DP2 Biology student actually have to meet?
faqs.answer: Mostly ones the school sets: research question approval, data collection, the investigation draft, the final internal submission, the mock examination window and the issuing of predicted grades. The IB sets the examination session and the release of results. This page publishes no IB date, because automated access to the IB's own pages is blocked and no session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Ask your Diploma coordinator in September for the school's calendar in writing, then work the autumn backwards from the draft deadline.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level Biology accepted for nursing or other health degrees?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, but it depends entirely on the programme and the country. Nursing, nutrition, physiotherapy, public health and several biomedical routes list Biology at Standard Level as acceptable, sometimes with Chemistry alongside it. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary science generally require Higher Level sciences. Requirements vary between institutions and are revised between cycles, so the only reliable source is each university's current admissions page. Tutoring does not change a published prerequisite, and it is not required for any application.

faqs.question: Does a Standard Level student need to learn the statistics as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, though a smaller set than at Higher Level. Standard deviation for spread, standard error and error bars for confidence in a mean, correlation for the strength of a relationship, and the reciprocal diversity index in ecology. These appear in the data-based section of Paper 1 and in the investigation's data analysis criterion. Most marks are lost not in the calculation but in the sentence afterwards, where a student claims more than the statistic permits. One or two sessions covers what a Standard Level candidate needs.

faqs.question: Our school marks harshly. Should we worry about the predicted grade?
faqs.answer: It is worth understanding rather than worrying about. Predicted grades come from internal assessment data, and schools differ in how severely they set internal papers and how they weight components. The practical move is to ask which past papers the internal examinations were built from and how Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks were combined in the reported grade. With that known, the tutoring hours can be put where the weighting is heaviest. No tutor can promise a grade change, and a provider who offers one on a timetable is describing something they cannot control.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Standard Level Biology and Geography?
faqs.answer: Often, and the pairing is more sensible than it looks. Both subjects reward reading a figure, quoting a value or trend from it, and writing a conclusion that is evaluated rather than asserted. A student losing marks on Biology data questions is usually losing them on Geography resource questions for the same reason, and one block of work addresses both. Where it does not work is when one subject needs content teaching and the other needs technique, since those are different specialisms. Describe the symptom in each and the matching follows.

faqs.question: What if we need to stop after two sessions?
faqs.answer: Then you stop. Sessions here are booked as blocks or as individual hours rather than as a subscription, and nothing continues automatically. If the first two sessions show that the problem is smaller than expected, or that the fit is wrong, saying so is a reasonable outcome and the written note after each session is designed to make that judgement possible early. The free first lesson exists for the same reason: a diagnosis before a commitment, with no card details collected at that stage.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education require anything particular from a Biology grade?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and it is not something a tutoring provider performs, influences or guarantees. For the British curriculum route the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No verified International Baccalaureate points threshold has been read on the ministry's own pages, so none is published here. Confirm current requirements with the ministry directly.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-online-tutor.closingHeading: Tell us the symptom, not the grade
dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-online-tutor.closingBody: Standard Level Biology problems are usually narrower and cheaper to fix than the grade suggests. Send one sentence describing what actually goes wrong, say whether Biology is a points subject or a target subject, and take the free 45-minute first lesson. Your child works one data question, one explain question and one drawing, which is enough to name the question types to drill and the number of sessions it should take. If that number is six, you will be told six, and the block will end when the drill holds.

intro.heading: What a Biology SL tutor in Dubai costs, and what the money actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the number, because every parent in Dubai starts with the number and most tutoring sites refuse to print one. Rates read from live UAE tutoring pages in October 2026 put budget online help at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, a qualified subject teacher at AED 150 to AED 300, an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to AED 450, an in-home visit at AED 180 to AED 500 with the drive inside the fee, and named or examiner-tier tutors above AED 500. Those are market rates from other providers, with the band and the source named, not an IB Gram price list. What IB Gram does is match a Biology SL specialist to your child and let a trial lesson settle whether the teaching is worth a block.

The spread between AED 150 and AED 450 for the same hour is not a mystery and it is not mostly brand. It is five or six concrete variables, and a Dubai family can move four of them deliberately. Session length changes the per-hour figure. The distance between your community and the tutor changes it, because an in-home hour in Arabian Ranches carries a drive from Al Barsha or Business Bay that somebody pays for. Proximity to the May session changes it, since specialist diaries in this city fill from January and a late booking buys whatever is left at the top of the band. Whether your child needs syllabus teaching or criterion-level work on the scientific investigation changes it most of all, because those are different skills and a generalist cannot fake the second one.

Dubai is also the place where this calculation matters most, because the private-school market here is the densest in the country. KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, oversees the quality of private education in the emirate, and in 2024-25 the sector ran 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula. The Diploma Programme accounts for about 7 per cent of that enrolment, with UK-curriculum schools at 37 per cent, Indian at 26 per cent and American at 14 per cent. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, three of them International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. So the pool of Biology SL students is growing faster than the pool of teachers who have actually examined the course.

One more piece of local context belongs in a cost conversation. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the Dubai Media Office valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That freeze is the only fixed line in a Dubai education budget this year, which is why families are reading tutoring quotes more carefully than they did in 2024. A page that answers the cost question honestly, with the band, the source and the date, is more useful than one that asks you to request a callback to find out.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes feed a Biology SL result in Dubai: the Diploma Programme itself, the Middle Years Programme that is supposed to prepare students for it, and the IGCSE year that many Dubai students arrive from instead. The gap between what each one trains and what Biology SL rewards is where most of the lost marks live.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology at standard level runs across the two Diploma years and is assessed by two written papers and one scientific investigation. Paper 1 pairs multiple-choice questions with a data-based section and carries 36% of the grade. Paper 2 is short-answer and extended-response work at 44%. The investigation is the remaining 20%, marked out of 24 against four criteria. Standard level is not a lighter version of the same exam: it is a shorter syllabus assessed with the same command terms and the same marking severity.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Biology SL is usually chosen by students whose university target is not medicine, which means the subject is competing for revision time against a higher-level science and a higher-level maths. That is the pattern a tutor has to plan around here. Sessions that try to re-teach the whole syllabus waste a Dubai student's scarcest resource. The useful plan picks the two or three topics that carry the most Paper 2 marks for that student, and treats the investigation as a separate project with its own timeline.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students arrive in DP1 fluent in inquiry language and often weak on recall under time pressure, because the MYP rarely asks for twenty marks of precise biological detail in forty minutes. The transition subject is not content, it is examination discipline.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs a large number of full IB continuum schools, so a significant share of Biology SL students here have never sat a terminal written paper before DP1 mocks. Families in Mirdif and Al Barsha whose children came up through an MYP school see the same symptom: strong investigation design, thin Paper 1 recall. A tutor working with that profile should spend early sessions on timed recall and command-term precision, and leave inquiry skills alone, because those are already the student's strength.

programmes.name: IGCSE and British Year 11
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum students in Dubai reach the Diploma from Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 or a Pearson International GCSE equivalent. Those courses reward accurate recall of defined content and a tight practical-skills set. Biology SL then asks for the same recall plus explanation across topics, plus an independent investigation designed from nothing. Students who scored a 9 or an A* at IGCSE are frequently the ones most surprised by their first DP1 Paper 2 mark.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools hold the largest share of Dubai's private-school enrolment, which makes the IGCSE-to-SL step the single most common tutoring brief in this city. The gap to close is specific: naming a variable versus justifying its range, describing a trend versus explaining a mechanism, and writing to a command term instead of writing everything known. Six to eight focused sessions in DP1 usually close more of that gap than a year of weekly homework supervision.

dubai/ib-dp-biology-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Biology SL is rarely tutored alone in Dubai. The subjects below are the ones that sit next to it on a Diploma timetable here, and each carries its own failure pattern. A tutor who knows which of these is actually dragging the points total is worth more than one who simply teaches the subject you asked about.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Two written papers and one scientific investigation at both levels. Standard level drops the higher-level extension content but keeps the command terms and the 24-mark investigation. Marks are lost on explanation questions where students describe a trend rather than give a mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the investigation structure with Biology and the same four criteria, so a student taking both can be coached once on investigation design and twice on content. Dubai students most often lose marks on energetics and equilibrium reasoning rather than on calculation.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary, available as either a science or an individuals-and-societies choice. Students who found Biology SL content heavy sometimes move here in DP1. The assessment rewards systems reasoning and named case studies, which is a different writing discipline from Biology Paper 2.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Overlaps Biology on physiology, energy systems and data handling. A student taking both can reuse one set of statistics skills across two investigations. Marks go missing where answers stay descriptive instead of linking structure to measured performance.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Shares the biological approach to behaviour with Biology SL, including hormones, neurotransmitters and genetics. The examination style is different: command terms demand studies, dates and evaluation rather than labelled mechanisms, and that switch catches science-strong students.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content here is what a Biology investigation actually needs: correlation, standard deviation, error bars and significance testing. Students taking Biology SL alongside Analysis and Approaches often have the weaker statistical toolkit for their own data analysis criterion.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Timetabled against Biology in most Dubai IB schools. Shares graph-skills and uncertainty treatment, which transfer directly into the Biology data-based section of Paper 1. Students lose marks there on uncertainty and significant figures, not on biology.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay sit on the same DP calendar as the Biology investigation, usually in the same term. Families who plan tutoring around one deadline and ignore the other end up paying for emergency sessions in both subjects in the same fortnight.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A Biology extended essay is a separate 4,000-word project with its own supervision rules and its own research question standard. Support here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never drafting or completion of the work itself.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. It takes real timetable space in DP1, which is why a Biology plan built for a Dubai student has fewer free evenings than one built for a student abroad.

sections.heading: Biology SL assessment: two papers, one investigation, and where the marks go
paragraphs: Biology at standard level is assessed by Paper 1, Paper 2 and one scientific investigation. Paper 1 runs for an hour and a half and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, together worth 36% of the grade. Paper 2 also runs an hour and a half, mixes short-answer with extended-response questions, and carries 44%. The investigation is worth the remaining 20% and is marked out of 24. The course structure follows the Biology guide with first assessment in 2025, and a family should confirm the exact component timings for their child's cohort with the school's Diploma coordinator, because schools sit different sessions.

The distribution tells a tutor where to work. Paper 2 is the largest single block of marks and the one most responsive to teaching, because it rewards a writing discipline rather than raw recall. The command term sets the task: state wants a fact, outline wants a brief account, explain wants a mechanism with a cause, distinguish wants a pairwise contrast, and evaluate wants a judgement supported both ways. Students who write everything they know about a topic and hope the marks are in there somewhere are the single most common profile we see in Dubai, and it is a fixable one.

The data-based section of Paper 1 is the quiet mark thief. It asks students to read an unfamiliar graph or table from real research and reason from it, which is a skill the MYP trains well and IGCSE trains narrowly. Students who came through Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 are often fluent on content and shaky on uncertainty, error bars and significance. Those are maths habits rather than biology knowledge, which is why a student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Biology SL frequently outperforms a stronger biologist on this section.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the Biology SL grade is one piece of work the student designs, runs and writes alone, marked out of 24 against four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Nobody in the competitor set names a single criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are where the marks are and they are published. A parent who knows that conclusion and evaluation are twelve of the twenty-four marks will never again accept a draft that stops at a graph.

Research design is lost early and lost quietly. A research question that cannot be answered within the available time, equipment and word count is a six-mark problem disguised as enthusiasm. Dubai students with access to a well-equipped school laboratory often over-reach here, while students planning a database or secondary-data investigation under-specify their variables. The fix is a single session, before any data is collected, spent narrowing the question and writing the variables down with units and ranges.

Data analysis and evaluation are where tutoring earns its fee. Analysis wants processed data, appropriate statistics, uncertainty treated honestly and graphs that answer the question. Evaluation wants the student to name the specific weaknesses of their own method and propose realistic improvements, not generic ones about human error. Conclusion wants an answer to the original question, with reference to the data and to the accepted biology. A tutor can question, challenge and point at the criterion; the student writes every word. That boundary is the difference between legitimate support and an academic-honesty breach.

The principle that catches families out is that entry deadlines sit months before the examinations, set by the board and administered by the school registrar rather than by the student. Working backwards also fixes the tutoring budget question from the previous section. sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a Biology tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers IB malpractice procedures, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. A Dubai family paying for Biology SL support deserves the boundary written down, because it is the question most parents are too polite to ask directly and the one that decides whether the money spent protects the Diploma or threatens it.

Here is the line. A tutor may teach the biology, explain what a criterion rewards, ask why a variable was chosen, point out that an evaluation is generic, show how uncertainty is normally treated, read a draft the student wrote and return written feedback on it, and teach the student how to act on their teacher's comments. A tutor may not write the research question, write or rewrite any part of the investigation, supply data, produce graphs for the student to paste in, edit the text to a finished state, or draft any part of an extended essay or TOK essay. Support is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own work.

That boundary is also a practical test of a tutor you are considering. Ask what happens if your child sends a draft two days before the school deadline. A legitimate answer describes feedback against the criteria and the student doing the next version. An answer that promises to fix it, polish it or take care of it is describing something the IB treats as malpractice. Keep every draft and every feedback note, because a documented trail of the student's own progression is the best protection available if a question is ever raised.

The one fixed point this year is the fee freeze: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees in the emirate will not increase for 2026-27, under an incentives package the Dubai Media Office valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Against a flat school fee, tutoring is the variable line, and the arithmetic below shows what each pattern of support actually adds per month at the mid-band rate.

Two further lines belong in the budget and are usually forgotten. The first is examination entry, which for a school candidate is administered through the school and appears on a school invoice rather than a tutoring one. The second is the cost of a late decision: specialist availability in Dubai tightens from January for a May session, so a family that waits pays the upper end of the band for the hours that remain. sections.heading: Permits, verification and what a Dubai parent can actually check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is worth knowing before any money changes hands. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone providing private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you as fact.

The application route is public: MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is used through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. A parent can ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold the permit. A legitimate tutor will answer plainly. A provider who cannot explain the permit, or who implies tutoring is unregulated, has told you something useful about how they operate.

Two further checks are worth making. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school; treat that as press-reported and verify it against current policy. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence issued to institutions with a physical centre. IB Gram does not hold a regulator licence of that kind, does not operate a UAE centre, and makes no claim of approval or endorsement by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.
