sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for private tutoring in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit regime, and the cost question and the legality question are connected: a provider quoting an unusually low cash rate is sometimes a provider operating outside it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. There is no fee for the tutor to pass on, so no rate should be justified by the cost of the permit.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so no amount appears here.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. That requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the UAE, and nothing on this page should be read as a claim to any regulator's approval or endorsement. Delivery here is live video, one to one, from tutors working remotely.

There is one more boundary worth knowing before you pay anyone. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than taken from the current policy text, so verify it with ADEK if it bears on a decision. The underlying principle holds across the UAE: paying the person who marks your child's internal work is a conflict of interest, whatever the rate.

sections.heading: Scheduling a Business Management session into a Dubai week
paragraphs: The free hours in a Dubai Diploma student's week are fewer than the subject list implies, and a session booked into a slot that does not really exist is money spent on cancellations. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 where the school year begins in April. Instructional time for them is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit.

KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. More discrete timetable blocks means less timetable slack, and a family that picks one fixed weekly slot and protects it loses fewer paid sessions than a family that arranges each week by message. For the mandatory subjects, additional or different content without prior Ministry permission is not permitted, which is a genuine constraint on how any Arabic or Islamic Education support can be described.

Ramadan moves the whole pattern later, and a post-Iftar slot is a normal arrangement that costs nothing extra over video. Internal deadlines cluster in DP2, so a student taking Business Management alongside a science and a language will meet several internal submissions inside a few weeks. Mapping those at the start of DP1 is unglamorous and it prevents the emergency bookings that cost the most per hour.

On examination timing, this page publishes no IB dates. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no session or results date here is confirmed from the IB directly; UAE schools sit the May session and some candidates sit November, and the exact windows belong to the school's Diploma coordinator or ibo.org. For families also sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers, the published pattern is instructive: Cambridge's March 2027 series has final entries due 27 November 2026 against an exam period starting 3 February 2027, and forecast grades due 27 February 2027. Entry administration months ahead of the paper is normal, and leaving it to the student is how an entry gets missed.

process.title: Say which component and which unit
process.description: Business Management, finance and accounts, unseen paper, nine weeks to go is a brief that can be priced. Needs help with business is not. Naming the component and the unit determines which specialist fits and how many hours the work genuinely requires, which is what makes a quote honest.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a written output
process.description: The first session costs nothing and produces something: a short timed question attempted live, marked, and returned with the specific habits it exposed written down. That document is what you judge the match on, before any money moves. A trial that produces only a conversation has told you nothing.

process.title: Get the plan and the price in writing together
process.description: Before a block starts, you should have the session count, the frequency, the units to be covered, how many marked scripts you will receive, the per-session price, and the cancellation terms. Every item on that list is a cost driver, and anything absent from it tends to be absent in practice too.

process.title: Weekly or fortnightly sessions with work returned marked
process.description: Sessions run over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. Set work comes back annotated against the published criteria before the next session, so each paid hour starts from a named weakness rather than a general review. Fortnightly is the cheaper shape and often the right one in DP1.

process.title: Review at six weeks against what you received
process.description: Count the marked scripts, read the feedback, and decide: continue, change frequency, change tutor or stop. If no Business Management specialist is free in your window, you are told at the enquiry rather than matched with a general business graduate and charged specialist rates for it.

whyPoints.title: Published rates, attributed, in AED
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page names the provider or survey that published it. That is uncommon in this market: three of the six pages ranking for these searches quote no price, and the two that do quote in dollars. You can hold any Dubai provider to the bands in the table above, including this one.

whyPoints.title: No travel cost in either direction
whyPoints.description: Delivery to UAE families is live video, so there is no travel time inside the rate and no commute at the student's end. In-home quotes in Dubai sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour partly because somebody is driving. Removing that cost is a real saving, not a marketing line.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts as the deliverable
whyPoints.description: The unit worth comparing is cost per annotated script, not cost per hour of talking. Timed work marked against published criteria and returned before the next session is what changes a Business Management answer, and it is what the quoted plan commits to in writing.

whyPoints.title: The cheap hours bought early
whyPoints.description: The pre-released case study can be prepared at low intensity across months, which makes fortnightly DP1 sessions the best value in this subject. A plan that front-loads cheap preparation and reserves intensive work for the unseen paper costs less across two years than crisis booking does in one term.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on what can be promised
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantee, no fabricated statistics, no claim of KHDA, MoHRE or IB approval, which this platform does not hold. No offer to produce assessed work at any price. Where availability for a component is thin, that is said at the enquiry rather than discovered in week three.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen on subject, not drive time
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over video across the UAE, the match is made on depth in Diploma Business Management rather than on who lives near your community. A family in Dubai Investments Park gets the same pool as a family in Al Barsha, which is not true of any in-home arrangement.

faqs.question: What should an IB DP Business Management online tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: On published Dubai figures as of October 2026, a qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a Diploma subject specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB rates from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey puts specialist exam-year work in the AED 200 to 450 and above band. Those are market rates from the sources named, not a price list for this platform. The more useful question is what the hour contains, because a rate that excludes marking is a different product at the same headline number.

faqs.question: For Business Management, does a monthly package beat an hourly booking in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the condition attached is what decides it. Packages seen on the Dubai market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The effective hourly rate inside a package is usually below the equivalent single-session rate, which is the point of it. What to check is what happens to unused sessions, whether a cancelled session rolls forward, and whether the package includes marking of timed work. A cheaper rate that quietly forfeits two sessions a month is not cheaper.

faqs.question: Which Business Management unit takes the most tutoring hours to repair?
faqs.answer: Finance and accounts, in almost every cohort. Its content is sequential, so a student who never secured contribution per unit will mis-handle break-even, cash flow forecasting, ratio interpretation and investment appraisal downstream, and those cannot be fixed in parallel. Repair therefore takes teaching time rather than practice time, which is slower and more expensive. Human resource management and the introductory unit are usually the cheapest to improve, because the content is intuitive and the lost marks come from answer structure, which responds quickly to marked timed practice. Diagnose before buying hours, and buy the expensive repair early.

faqs.question: How far in advance does the Business Management case study reach schools?
faqs.answer: The case study used for one of the two written papers is released to schools ahead of the examination series, well before the paper itself. Confirm the exact release and the version your child's school holds with the Diploma coordinator, since this page publishes no IB dates: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing here is confirmed from the IB directly. What matters commercially is the implication. Months of low-intensity preparation on the organisation costs a fraction of compressed work in the final term, which makes early fortnightly sessions the best-value shape available in this subject.

faqs.question: How long is the business research project allowed to be?
faqs.answer: The project is capped at 1,800 words in the current guide, and the ceiling should shape the question rather than the editing. A narrow question with identifiable evidence fits inside the limit with room left for analysis and a justified recommendation. A broad question about a large organisation's whole strategy does not, and cutting an over-length draft back is the most wasteful work in the subject. The practical sequence is to test the question for answerability first, agree where the evidence comes from, then outline to the word budget. Confirm the current limit with the school's coordinator before drafting begins.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level sit a longer case study paper than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Higher Level version of the case study paper runs longer and typically carries additional unseen stimulus material alongside the familiar organisation, which is why deep familiarity with the case pays back more at Higher Level than at Standard Level. The written paper spanning all five units and the research project are common to both levels. For a family budgeting, the implication is that Higher Level students get more value from early low-intensity case study preparation, and that the extra paper length is a reason to practise under full timing rather than on single questions.

faqs.question: Is a group revision class a cheaper way to prepare for the written papers?
faqs.answer: Per student per hour, yes, and for the right student it is genuinely good value. Group provision works when a student is broadly secure and needs pace, structure and the discipline of a timetable. It does not work when the problem is a specific diagnosable weakness, because group formats almost never include individual script marking, and individual marking is the mechanism that moves an applied-analysis mark. Paying less for a format that cannot deliver the mechanism is not a saving. Diagnose first, then choose the format that matches the diagnosis rather than the budget.

faqs.question: What does the management toolkit actually add to an answer?
faqs.answer: A tool earns marks when it changes the conclusion and loses marks when it decorates the answer. A student who draws a framework, labels it correctly and then recommends what they would have recommended anyway has spent writing time for nothing. A student who uses the same framework to show which option survives scrutiny has used it analytically. The toolkit splits into situational and decision-making frameworks, with several reserved for Higher Level. Teaching each tool to the point where it alters a recommendation takes about one session per tool and pays back across both written papers.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise as the examination series approaches?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens and rates firm up rather than soften, which is a reason to plan early rather than a reason to panic. Specialist Diploma tutors fill their best slots first, so the family booking in February for an April start is choosing from a thinner pool at the top of the published bands. The counter-move is the cheap-hours strategy: fortnightly sessions through DP1 on case study preparation and foundational units, then a short intensive block for timed papers. That shape costs less across two years than any single term of emergency booking does.

faqs.question: Does the quoted hourly rate include marking a timed paper?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the answer varies and it is the largest hidden variable in Dubai tutoring pricing. Marking a Business Management response properly takes a specialist a meaningful share of a lesson's length, since applied analysis cannot be checked against an answer key. Some providers include it, some bill it separately, and some simply do not do it. A rate card gives no clue either way. Get the answer in writing alongside the session count, the units to be covered and the cancellation terms, and compare providers on cost per marked script rather than on the headline hourly figure.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Business Management and Economics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. The two subjects reward different answers: Economics wants diagram accuracy and theoretical chains of reasoning, Business Management wants application to a specific organisation using named tools. A tutor strong in one and merely competent in the other will improve one grade and leave the other alone. Where a genuine specialist in both is available, a single tutor reduces cost and keeps the two evaluation styles deliberately separate, which students taking both subjects frequently confuse. Where they are not, two specialists beat one generalist at the same combined price.

faqs.question: Is Business Management a weaker Diploma choice than Economics for a business degree?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements rarely turn on which group three subject was taken, and more often on the mathematics route and the overall points. Some courses name Higher Level Mathematics or a specific mathematics option; few name Business Management or Economics specifically. The reliable method is to read the admissions pages of three or four target universities before subject choices close at the end of DP1, and to note whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is specified. No tutoring page, this one included, is a source for an admissions requirement.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai family budget for two years of Business Management support?
faqs.answer: Work from a shape rather than a single number. A fortnightly session across DP1 at the mid band, a short research project supervision block, and a weekly timed-paper block in the final term is the pattern most families settle into. Using Bestimate's published monthly bands, mid-market weekly sessions run roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month and specialist exam-year work roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Fortnightly roughly halves the monthly figure. Build the estimate from the frequency you actually need in each term, then hold the provider to the marked-script count.

faqs.question: Who in the UAE is allowed to charge for private tutoring?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring is permit-regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here. A business with premises needs a KHDA training-institute permit instead.

faqs.question: Are there cheaper options than one-to-one for a student only slightly behind?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are worth trying first. A student who understands the content and loses marks to structure can often be fixed by past papers marked by their own teacher, a study group working through the case study together, and the published assessment criteria used as a self-check list. That costs nothing. One-to-one earns its rate when the weakness is specific, when individual marking is the missing mechanism, or when nobody at the school has capacity to read the student's own work closely. Spending money before exhausting the free options is the commonest avoidable cost in this market.

intro.heading: Buy a plan with a number on it, not an hour with a rate on it
paragraphs: Ask what a Business Management tutor costs in Dubai and the answers you get are all technically true and none of them useful. Rates published in this emirate run from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya's budget end and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik's, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, to the AED 200 to 450 specialist band on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with BartyED quoting AED 650 for premium named tutoring. Every one of those numbers is the market. None of them tells you what your child's situation will actually cost, because the hourly rate is the smallest variable in the calculation.

The variable that matters is how many hours the plan needs, and that depends on three things a rate card cannot see: when you start, which components are weak, and whether the research project has been begun. A DP1 student who needs one unit closed and a project question approved is buying twelve to eighteen hours across two years. A DP2 student six weeks from the papers with no project draft and a 4 in the mocks is buying twenty-five hours in a fortnight, at a higher rate, for a smaller movement. Same subject, same emirate, same tutor quality, four times the invoice.

Business Management also prices differently from a science or a mathematics course because of where its marks sit. A substantial share of the grade comes from a written response to a case study the school receives in advance, and another large share from a research project the student designs around a real organisation. Neither is content you can cram. Both reward work done early, which is why in this subject specifically the cheapest tutoring is bought in the first year and the most expensive tutoring is bought in the last term.

One more thing to settle before any money changes hands: what the tutor will not do. The research project has to be the student's own work, built on data the student gathered or sourced. A provider who offers to hand over a finished project is selling an academic-honesty finding that attaches to your child's Diploma, not to their invoice. Legitimate support is slower and duller, and it is the only kind worth paying for. The boundary belongs in writing before the first session, not in a conversation after a problem.

So read this page in that order. The first section prices three plans a Dubai family might realistically buy, with the hours and the totals stated at the published market bands. The sections after it explain what those hours are spent on: the command-term ladder that mid-band scripts keep failing to climb, the organisation choice that decides whether the research project works, and the difference the Higher Level extension makes to both. Then the practical layer: permits, VAT, trial conditions, and how many evenings a Dubai Year 12 week actually leaves free.

dubai/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.programmesIntro: Business Management is a final-two-year subject, but the skills it is marked on are built across the whole IB continuum: reading a stakeholder's position, using a tool rather than naming it, and handling evidence without exaggerating it. Here is what each IB programme a Dubai school runs contributes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no MYP business course. The groundwork arrives through Individuals and Societies and through the MYP personal project, which is the first time most students scope a piece of independent work, keep a process journal and meet a word limit. That is closer to the Diploma research project than anything else in the continuum, and students who took it seriously arrive able to plan a timeline.
programmes.countryNote: Many Dubai Diploma candidates come from an MYP cohort on the same campus, and departments here report the same inheritance each year: students who can discuss a company's decisions fluently but cannot apply a named management tool to a specific problem. The repair is technical rather than conceptual and takes two or three sessions per tool.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Business Management sits in Group 3 and runs across both years at Standard or Higher Level. Candidates sit a written paper based on a case study released to schools in advance, a second written paper built on unseen data, and submit a business research project built around a real organisation within a stated word limit. Confirm the current component weightings and limits in the IB subject guide at ibo.org.
programmes.countryNote: Business Management is one of the most frequently chosen Group 3 subjects in Dubai Diploma schools, often running alongside Economics in the same block so students pick one. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale and its published reports name subject-level strengths, which is worth reading before deciding whether a mid-term grade reflects teaching or workload.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Business Management is a common pairing because the career-related study often sits in the same field. A CP student sits the same Business Management papers and submits the same project, so the subject support required is identical to a Diploma student's.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme, which means a CP student taking Business Management is frequently the only one in the building on that route. The practical consequence is scheduling: the reflective project and the career-related study compete for the same evenings as the business research project, usually in the first term of the second year.

dubai/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.subjectsIntro: Business Management is five units plus a set of analytical tools, assessed through two written papers and one research project. Below is what a tutor works through with a Dubai candidate, and where the marks most often go missing in each part.

subjects.name: Unit 1: Introduction to business management
subjects.description: Business types, sectors, objectives, stakeholders, growth and the external environment. It reads as background and carries real marks, because almost every extended answer in the subject requires a stakeholder position and most candidates assert one instead of justifying it from the case material.

subjects.name: Unit 2: Human resource management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, leadership, motivation theory, industrial relations and change management. The commonest deduction is theory recited rather than applied: a candidate who explains a motivation theory in general terms without connecting it to the named employees in the case loses the application marks entirely.

subjects.name: Unit 3: Finance and accounts
subjects.description: Sources of finance, costs and revenues, break-even, final accounts, ratio analysis and cash-flow forecasting. This is where Dubai candidates most often need teaching rather than technique, and where a calculation shown without a unit or a conclusion scores the method mark and loses the rest.

subjects.name: Unit 4: Marketing
subjects.description: Market research, segmentation, the marketing mix, branding and international marketing. Students enjoy this unit and over-write it. The marks go to answers that choose between options and justify the choice with case evidence rather than listing every element of a mix the examiner already knows.

subjects.name: Unit 5: Operations management
subjects.description: Production methods, quality management, location, supply chain, research and development and crisis management. It is the unit most often rushed at the end of DP2 and the one that appears most reliably in unseen data questions, which makes it the highest-risk gap to leave open.

subjects.name: The pre-released case study
subjects.description: A case study reaches schools well before the examination, and preparation for it can begin the moment it arrives. Candidates who treat it as reading material rather than as a research task arrive knowing the story and not the numbers, the stakeholders or the tools the case invites.

subjects.name: The unseen data paper
subjects.description: Short and extended responses built on stimulus material and quantitative extracts never seen before. The skill is reading quickly, extracting the right figure, and spending the writing time on the evaluative part rather than on describing the business in the opening paragraph.

subjects.name: The business research project
subjects.levels: Internal assessment, Standard and Higher Level
subjects.description: An independent investigation into a real organisation and a real issue, within a stated word limit and marked against published criteria. Most lost marks come from a question that cannot be answered with the data available, which is a problem created in week one and discovered in month four.

subjects.name: The management toolkit
subjects.levels: Both papers, with Higher Level additions
subjects.description: SWOT, Ansoff, BCG, decision trees, force-field analysis, the business plan and more, with some tools reserved for Higher Level in the current guide. Examiners reward a tool used to reach a judgement, not a tool drawn and left unexplained beside the answer.

subjects.name: Command terms and the mark ladder
subjects.description: Define, describe, apply, analyse, discuss and evaluate carry different expectations and different mark allocations. Practising the same stem under two different command terms in one session is the fastest way to show a student why their long answers are scoring in the middle.

dubai/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.regionsIntro: For a Business Management student, the practical effect of where you live in Dubai is two-fold: when a weekday session can start, and which organisations are close enough to approach for primary research. Below are the communities the enquiries come from, with both in mind.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living with short school runs and an unusual advantage for this subject: a dense concentration of small businesses, head offices and service firms within walking distance, which makes a primary-research interview genuinely arrangeable rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Barsha Heights and Emirates Hills
regions.note: The deepest band of Diploma provision in the emirate, where Business Management usually runs as a full class at both levels. Requests here are weighted towards the pre-released case study and towards marking, because the five units are generally covered on schedule.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Two schools inside the district and several more one interchange away, so a 4.30pm start works most days. The retail and food-service businesses at ground level in both towers clusters are the commonest subjects of research projects from this area.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Bigger households and later bus arrivals push a realistic session start towards half past six. Smaller Diploma cohorts here sometimes mean Business Management is taught alongside another Group 3 subject by the same teacher, which shows up as thin coverage of finance and accounts.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Al Quoz
regions.note: Short runs to several Diploma schools, and families who tend to buy ninety-minute sessions because a timed paper and its read-back will not fit into sixty minutes. The Al Quoz industrial and creative district next door is useful for an operations-focused project.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and Motor City
regions.note: Inland communities where the school run can take forty minutes each way at the wrong hour, which is why online tuition was normal here before it was normal elsewhere. Weekend morning sessions are more popular in this band than anywhere else in Dubai.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha and Emirates Hills Diploma band
schoolClusters.note: Where Business Management is most reliably offered at both levels with a dedicated teacher. Families in this band usually want case-study preparation and marked papers rather than content teaching, and they tend to start asking in the first term of DP2 once the case study has arrived.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Mirdif and the Festival City corridor
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts, where Business Management is sometimes taught by a teacher covering two Group 3 subjects. The common request from this corridor is finance and accounts taught properly from the start, plus supervision of a research project that has not yet found a usable question.

Teaching finance and accounts from scratch, preparing a pre-released case study, and supervising a research project need different session lengths, different cadences and different levels of specialism.

modes.description: Sixty minutes every second week, running slightly behind the school's scheme of work, so units close as they are taught rather than accumulating. This is the lowest total cost across two years and the plan fewest Dubai families choose, because in DP1 the grade still looks recoverable without help. Finance and accounts is the unit this shape protects best.

sections.heading: Three realistic plans, priced against what the Dubai market publishes
paragraphs: A plan is the only unit of purchase that can actually be compared between providers, so here are three, costed at the published bands rather than at any price of ours. The first starts in DP1 and keeps the subject from going wrong. The second starts after the DP2 mock examinations and repairs specific components. The third starts in the final six weeks and does what can still be done. The hourly rate is similar in all three. The totals are not remotely similar.

Notice what the table shows about timing. The DP1 plan uses more calendar and fewer hours, because a unit closed in the week it is taught takes two hours and the same unit rebuilt in April takes five, alongside five other subjects competing for the same evenings. The final-term plan is not bad value per hour; it is expensive because it is buying technique under a clock, usually at two sessions a week, and because by then the research project is either finished or a crisis.

Use these as a template for interrogating any quote you receive. Ask the provider to state the number of sessions, the length of each in minutes, whether marking between sessions is included, and what the total comes to. If they cannot or will not put a total next to a plan, you are not being sold a plan. You are being sold an open-ended hourly arrangement with your family's exam calendar as the only thing limiting it.

sections.heading: Why the hourly rate is the least informative number in the decision
paragraphs: A Dubai parent comparing AED 220 against AED 380 an hour is comparing the wrong two things. The cheaper option may need three sessions to teach break-even analysis properly and may not mark a timed paper at all; the dearer one may do it in a single session and return a marked script with band descriptors attached. On a per-mark basis the dearer tutor can be the cheaper purchase, and on a different task the opposite is true. The rate tells you almost nothing without the task attached to it.

Three things sit inside a rate and are rarely itemised. Marking: reading a Business Management data-response paper properly takes a tutor twenty-five to forty minutes, and whether that happens between sessions or not at all is the largest hidden variable in a Dubai invoice. Session length: 45, 60, 90 and 120-minute sessions are all quoted as a session fee here, so convert everything to a per-sixty-minute figure before you compare. Written feedback to the parent: some include it monthly, some never produce anything in writing.

There is a fourth, specific to this subject. Ask whether research project supervision is billed at the same rate as teaching. Some providers charge a premium for it, some refuse it, and some quietly offer the thing they should not offer. Settle it in the first conversation. A plan that covers the two written papers and leaves the project unsupervised has left a substantial share of the grade outside the arrangement you just paid for.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the ladder your child's long answers are failing to climb
paragraphs: The most frequent complaint from Dubai parents in this subject is that their child writes at length, clearly knows the material, and scores in the middle. The cause is almost always the command term. Business Management mark schemes attach different expectations to define, describe, apply, analyse, discuss and evaluate, and the mark allocation follows the term rather than the topic. A candidate who answers an evaluate question with a well-organised description has written a good answer to a question that was not asked.

The ladder is learnable in a handful of sessions because it is structural rather than conceptual. An apply question wants the theory tied to the named business in the stimulus. An analyse question wants a chain of consequence with a because in it. A discuss question wants both sides. An evaluate question wants both sides plus a judgement that follows from the weight of the argument and refers to the organisation's own objectives and context. Most mid-band scripts stop one rung short, consistently, in every question.

The drill that moves it fastest is unglamorous. Take one stem and answer it twice in one session under two different command terms, then compare the two answers against the descriptors side by side. Students see the difference immediately in a way no explanation achieves. Three or four sessions of that, plus a marked paper between each, is typically what separates a candidate writing competent middle-band prose from one writing shorter answers that score higher.

sections.heading: Choosing a Dubai organisation the research project can actually use
paragraphs: The research project goes wrong in week one, not in month four. A student picks a business they find interesting, writes a question they cannot answer with any data they will be able to obtain, and discovers the problem after the school's first draft deadline. Rescuing that costs more tutoring hours than the entire rest of the subject, which makes the first two hours of project supervision the highest-value money in this plan. The test is simple and can be applied before anything is written: name the data, name the source, name the date you will have it.

Dubai gives students more options than most cities, and some of them are better than others. A family-owned business with a cooperative owner yields primary interview data and genuine internal detail. A listed company on the Dubai Financial Market yields published accounts that support ratio analysis without needing anyone's permission. A large multinational's regional office is interesting and usually impenetrable, because nobody at that level answers a student email. A free-zone startup is accessible and often has no accounts worth analysing yet.

There is a practical and ethical layer too. Anything a business shares in confidence has to be handled as the owner permits, anonymised if asked, and never published in a way that identifies individuals without consent. Teach that early: it is both good research practice and the way the project criteria expect the student to behave. A tutor's job here is to make the student sceptical about their own question before the school's deadline makes the point for them.

sections.heading: Standard against Higher Level, and what the difference costs in hours
paragraphs: Higher Level Business Management adds content within the units, additional tools, and a longer and more demanding written response to the pre-released case study. Confirm the current structure and weightings in the IB subject guide at ibo.org rather than taking them from any tutoring page, including this one, because guides are revised and tutoring websites are not. What does not change is the practical consequence: Higher Level needs more hours for the same grade, and it needs them in different places.

The honest comparison matters at two moments. The first is the level decision at the start of DP1, where the deciding factor is usually the rest of the timetable rather than the subject itself. The second is a level change partway through, which Dubai schools will sometimes permit in the first year and almost never in the second. A family considering the move should price the catch-up before the conversation with the coordinator, because the extra content is real and arrives all at once.

For hiring, the difference is specific rather than general. Ask a prospective tutor which Higher Level tools they teach and how they prepare the longer case-study response, and ask how many Higher Level candidates they have taken through to a May session. A tutor who teaches both levels well can answer in two sentences. A tutor who mostly teaches Standard Level will answer in generalities, and your child will find the gap in the first week of the final term.

sections.heading: Business Management or Economics: picking the Group 3 subject that fits the degree
paragraphs: Many Dubai schools block Business Management and Economics against each other, so the choice is real and is usually made with poor information. The short version: Economics is more analytical and more diagrammatic, with a stronger mathematical flavour and an assessment built on timed written argument. Business Management is more applied, more case-based, and carries a research project built on a real organisation. Neither is harder in the abstract. They are difficult in different ways and they suit different students.

For university routes, the pattern matters more than the prestige. Quantitative economics degrees typically specify a mathematics course rather than Economics itself, most commonly Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and some will accept Applications and Interpretation. Business, management and marketing degrees generally accept either Group 3 subject and care more about the overall points total. Finance programmes vary enough that the only reliable method is reading the published entry requirements for the specific courses on your child's list.

For students who already know they want to run or join a business, the research project is a genuine argument for Business Management: it is the only part of the Diploma where a student negotiates access to a real organisation, gathers data from it and reaches a judgement a stakeholder could act on. For students who enjoy abstract reasoning and diagrams, Economics tends to feel better and to score better. A diagnostic hour in each, with a marked piece of work from both, settles the question faster than any advice.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, secondary data and the project boundary
paragraphs: The research project must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach method, explain what each criterion rewards, ask whether the data gathered can support the conclusion being reached, and point out that a section does not answer its own research question. A tutor may not supply the text, select the organisation, construct the analysis or rework a draft to completion. That line is not a stylistic preference, and the consequence of crossing it attaches to the candidate's Diploma rather than to the tutor's invoice.

Secondary data brings its own rules. Published accounts, market reports and news coverage can be used, and they must be cited where they came from, with the date. Reproducing an IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus document, a mark scheme or a grade-boundary table is not permitted and no tutor should be circulating them; the correct move is to reference the official page and link to it. If a student uses a generative AI tool for anything, from summarising an article to tidying a sentence, the school's own policy governs it and the honest route is to declare it.

There is a cheap test any Dubai parent can run without reading the project. Ask your child to explain, without notes, why they chose that organisation, what data they have, and what the data does not let them say. A student who did the work answers in under a minute, including the limitations. A student who did not will describe the company instead. Any tutor charging a specialist rate will have run that test already and should be willing to tell you what the answer was.

sections.heading: Permits, VAT, trial conditions and the Dubai week
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated, and the detail is worth knowing because it gives you a question that separates a professional from an opportunist. Individuals offering private lessons need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure you see quoted.

Ask about approval claims as carefully as about price. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and no platform should describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson unless it holds the specific permit and can produce the number. IB Gram holds none of them and does not occupy premises in the UAE. On money, ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT and ask what the condition on any free trial is, since a trial with an undisclosed condition is not free.

Then do the timetable arithmetic, because it decides whether a plan survives contact with reality. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies alongside its licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring these arrangements from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and calculating the time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Add six Diploma subjects, the core, travel and any after-school commitment, and most Year 12 weeks have one usable weekday evening plus part of a weekend. During Ramadan, sessions commonly move later; schedule that in advance rather than renegotiating weekly.

sections.heading: Availability, fallback and the honest version of getting started
paragraphs: Business Management is widely taught in Dubai Diploma schools, so specialist coverage at Standard Level is usually good and a match is normally made within a few days. Higher Level case-study work in the fortnight before a mock series is the pinch point, and project supervision in the weeks around a school draft deadline is the second. We would rather tell you the slot is full than fill it with whoever happens to be free, which is the commonest quiet failure in this market and one no competing page in this search discloses.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with sessions recorded so revision does not depend on notes taken live, a shared whiteboard for break-even charts and ratio work, and screen sharing for case-study appendices. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. In-home tuition is a real product here, published at AED 180 to 350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 table with some home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and the premium buys presence while narrowing the pool of specialists to those willing to drive to your community at your hour.

The honest version of getting started is short. Tell us the level, the next school deadline, and whether the research project has a question yet. Take the free first lesson, which is one per student with no card details taken, and use it as a diagnostic that produces a marked script. Read the plan and the total. Start, change tutor, or stop. If the marks are flat after six weeks of consistent attendance, the diagnosis was wrong, and the plan should change or end rather than renew.

Three of the six pages competing for this search publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which makes any comparison impossible before you commit.

whyPoints.description: A substantial share of this grade sits in one independent investigation, and plans that quietly cover only the written papers leave it outside the arrangement you paid for. Project supervision is priced as milestones because projects move in bursts, and a weekly slot bills you for the quiet weeks in between.

whyPoints.description: Reading a Business Management data-response script properly takes a tutor twenty-five to forty minutes. Whether that happens between sessions, during them, or not at all is the largest hidden variable in a Dubai tutoring invoice, so we settle it in writing in the first conversation rather than in month two.

whyPoints.description: There are no home visits in the UAE. whyPoints.description: The research project is the student's own work. We teach method, read drafts against the criteria and ask the questions a moderator would ask. We do not supply text, select the organisation or rework a draft to completion, and we put that in writing, because the providers selling the alternative are selling your child a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy Business Management support in DP1 or wait for the DP2 mock results?
faqs.answer: DP1, by a wide margin, and the saving is in hours rather than in the hourly rate. A DP1 maintenance plan is typically twelve to eighteen hours across two years, because a unit closed in the week it is taught takes about two hours. The same unit rebuilt after the mocks takes four or five, alongside five other subjects competing for the same evenings, and usually at two sessions a week. At the AED 200 to 450 specialist band published for Dubai, that is the difference between roughly AED 2,400 to 8,100 and AED 4,000 to 12,600 for a smaller movement.

faqs.question: How many hours does supervising a business research project usually take?
faqs.answer: Three to five sessions, if they are spent in the right places. The first and most valuable tests whether the research question can be answered with data the student can actually obtain, which is where most projects fail. The second covers method and the organisation's cooperation. The third reads a draft against each criterion with the descriptor open. A fourth and fifth tighten structure and the judgement. Booked as milestones rather than as a weekly slot, because projects move in bursts around school deadlines and a standing weekly session pays for the quiet weeks in between.

faqs.question: Which command terms carry the most marks in a Business Management paper?
faqs.answer: The evaluative ones, and they are where mid-band scripts stop a rung short. Define and describe questions are small and should be answered briefly. Apply questions require the theory tied explicitly to the named organisation in the stimulus. Analyse questions need a chain of consequence with a because in it. Discuss needs both sides. Evaluate needs both sides plus a judgement that follows from the weight of argument and refers to the organisation's own objectives. A student who writes well but never climbs the last rung will score consistently in the middle across every long question on the paper.

faqs.question: Can my child use a Dubai company for the research project?
faqs.answer: Yes, and local access is one of the real advantages of studying here. The deciding factor is data rather than interest. A family-owned business with a cooperative contact gives primary interview material and internal detail. A company listed on a UAE exchange gives published accounts that support ratio analysis without needing anyone's permission. A regional office of a multinational is usually impenetrable to a student email. Settle what may be published and what must be anonymised in writing before any interview takes place, because a project built on data the owner later withdraws cannot be rescued near a deadline.

faqs.question: Does a free-zone startup work as the subject of a research project?
faqs.answer: Access is often excellent and financial history is often the problem. Founders in free zones tend to answer emails, explain decisions candidly and give a student more detail than a large company ever would, which makes the method section strong. What they frequently cannot provide is two or three years of comparable figures, so any question requiring trend or ratio analysis collapses. Test that before committing: ask what financial information exists, for how many years, and in what form. If the answer is one incomplete year, keep the organisation and change the question to something qualitative that the available evidence can support.

faqs.question: What primary data can a Dubai student realistically collect from a business?
faqs.answer: Interviews with one or two decision-makers, a short structured questionnaire to staff or customers where the organisation permits it, observation of a process, and internal documents the owner agrees to share. What students usually cannot get is anything commercially sensitive, anything about identifiable individuals without consent, or anything from a company whose regional office never replies. Plan for a response rate far below what the student expects and build the question around the data they will definitely have rather than the data they hope for. Consent, anonymisation and the date of collection all belong in the method section.

faqs.question: Business Management or Economics for a student heading to a business degree?
faqs.answer: Most business, management and marketing degrees accept either and care more about the overall points total, so choose on fit rather than on prestige. Economics is more analytical and diagrammatic with a stronger mathematical flavour; Business Management is more applied, case-based and carries an independent research project. Quantitative economics degrees usually specify a mathematics course rather than the Group 3 subject, commonly Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Read the published entry requirements for the specific universities on your child's list, then use a diagnostic hour in each subject to settle the preference with marked work rather than opinion.

faqs.question: What extra content does Higher Level Business Management add?
faqs.answer: Additional content inside several of the five units, further tools in the management toolkit that Standard Level candidates do not meet, and a longer, more demanding written response to the pre-released case study. Confirm the current structure and weightings in the IB subject guide at ibo.org rather than relying on any tutoring page. In tutoring terms, Higher Level typically needs two to four extra hours per unit where the extension content is examined, and the case-study block grows from about four sessions to six and needs to start earlier. The research project component is the same, with a higher expectation of depth in the judgement.

faqs.question: Do we pay more for a tutor who has marked Business Management papers?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth it for one job rather than all of them. Someone fluent in the band descriptors is valuable when the problem is technique: a marked script that names the rung the answer stopped at is worth several sessions of general teaching. For closing a gap in finance and accounts, that premium buys nothing extra. Note also the caution on examiner claims: nobody should describe a tutor as a current IB examiner without evidence, and examiner status must never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content. Ask what they have marked and when.

faqs.question: How do we compare a per-session fee with a monthly block in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Convert both to a cost per sixty minutes of teaching, then add what is missing. Monthly online blocks advertised in the emirate sit around AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home blocks at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Neither usually states whether marking between sessions is included, whether unused sessions roll over, or what notice cancellation needs. Ask those three questions in writing. A block is good value for continuous DP1 consolidation and poor value for project supervision, because project work clusters around deadlines and a monthly block bills you for the gaps.

faqs.question: Why does my child write long answers in Business Management and still score 4?
faqs.answer: Almost always the command term rather than the content. Long answers that describe when the question said evaluate, or that explain a theory correctly without connecting it to the named organisation, sit in the middle band however fluent they are. The diagnosis takes one marked script: if the content is accurate and the structure is orderly, the problem is the rung the answer stopped at. The fix is three or four sessions of the same stem answered under two different command terms and compared against the descriptors, plus a marked timed paper between each session to check the habit is transferring.

faqs.question: What should a Business Management diagnostic lesson actually produce?
faqs.answer: A marked piece of work you can read, not a conversation about your child's potential. Ask for one timed extended response, sat before the session and marked before it starts, returned with the command term identified, the band stated, the rung the answer stopped at named, and three specific corrections. A specialist produces that in the free first lesson. A generalist offers encouraging comments and a package. The marked script also tells you which of the three purchases you are actually making, which is the only way to judge whether a quoted total is reasonable.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to have worked with the pre-released case study before?
faqs.answer: Not that specific case, which is new each time, but they should have prepared candidates for one. The skill is a process: building a stakeholder map, pulling the numbers out of the appendices, deciding which tools the case genuinely invites rather than listing all of them, and rehearsing the extended response with the case open under timed conditions. Ask how they would spend the first two sessions after the case reaches the school. Someone who has done it answers concretely and immediately. Someone who has not will talk about reading it carefully, which is not a method.

faqs.question: Which evenings are actually free in a Dubai Year 12 week?
faqs.answer: Fewer than parents assume, and the arithmetic is worth doing before buying a weekly slot. Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies alongside its licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring these arrangements from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and calculating the time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Add six Diploma subjects, the core, travel, and any sport or service commitment. Most households end up with one usable weekday evening and part of a weekend. Plans built on two weekday sessions in such a week are abandoned within a month, and the missed sessions are money gone.

faqs.question: What should we ask about a tutor's permit before paying?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. A legitimate tutor knows what it is, knows it costs nothing, and answers plainly. Anyone who says tutoring is not really regulated here, or quotes a permit fee, has told you how they treat other rules. Also check approval claims: no provider should describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson without holding the specific permit and being able to show the number.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Business Management and an Extended Essay written in it?
faqs.answer: Often, and it can be efficient, but check the fit rather than assuming it. An Extended Essay in business and management is a research task with its own criteria, word limit and supervisor at the school, and the school's supervisor remains the person responsible for the process. A tutor who teaches the subject well can help a student sharpen a research question, understand what the criteria reward and read a draft critically. They must not write any part of it or construct the argument. Confirm the current requirements with the school's coordinator, and keep the supervisor informed about any outside support.

dubai/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.closingHeading: Price the plan, then decide whether to buy it
dubai/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits Business Management at a Dubai school, ask for a plan with a total on it rather than an hourly rate. Tell us the level, the next internal deadline, whether the pre-released case study has arrived and whether the research project has a question yet. The free first lesson produces a marked extended response with the band and the missing rung named, which is what tells you whether you are buying content, technique or structure. One free lesson per student, no card details taken. Lessons run live and one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits in the UAE, and that service runs only in India.

dubai/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The mentors listed below have run CAS programmes and read CAS portfolios, which is a different skill from teaching a subject. Their job is to ask the questions a coordinator will ask, early enough that the answers can still change. Book the free trial and bring the portfolio as it stands.

intro.heading: Nobody marks CAS, and that is exactly why it causes trouble
paragraphs: Creativity, Activity, Service is the one part of the DP core that carries no marks at all. There is no grade, no criterion, no band, nothing that feeds the 45 points. A student can produce the finest CAS portfolio in the emirate and gain not one point for it. That fact is widely known in Dubai staffrooms and almost unknown in Dubai living rooms, and the gap between the two is where most of the panic in this search comes from.

The second fact is the one that matters. Completing CAS is a requirement for the award of the diploma. A candidate who has not completed it does not receive the diploma, regardless of how many points their subjects produced. So the component with no marks has the harshest consequence in the entire programme, and the only two states it has are complete and not complete. There is no partial credit and no recovery through good performance elsewhere.

Put those together and the honest brief for an IB DP CAS home tutor in Dubai becomes narrow and useful. Nobody can improve a CAS mark, because there is no mark. What a mentor can do is make sure the student has evidenced all seven learning outcomes, has a project that meets the duration and collaboration requirements, has a portfolio that a coordinator can sign off, and has the three documented interviews behind them rather than ahead of them. That is a completion problem, not a performance problem, and it is almost entirely about sequencing and reflection.

It is also a component where we turn work down. A DP1 student with a sport, an instrument, a service commitment and a habit of writing a few honest lines after each experience needs no help with CAS and should not be paying for any. We say so in the trial session and are happy to. The families who genuinely need mentoring are a smaller group: students fifteen months in with an empty portfolio, students whose project never met the one-month requirement, students whose coordinator has flagged a missing learning outcome with one term remaining, and students who have arrived in Dubai mid-DP from a school that recorded CAS differently.

This page therefore spends its space on what completion requires. The seven learning outcomes with what evidences each one. The CAS project and the two requirements it most often fails. The portfolio and what the three interviews are actually for. The hours question, which is the single most common piece of outdated advice circulating in Dubai parent groups. Where CAS goes wrong in this city in particular, which has a lot to do with the long summer absence and the way service opportunities work here. And the honesty boundary, which in CAS means a portfolio written by the student rather than tidied by anyone else.

A plain word on delivery. Home tutoring is the phrase parents search, and the in-home market in this emirate is set out further down with its real costs. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai students are mentored one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. CAS mentoring in particular suits that format, because the useful session is twenty minutes with the portfolio open on a shared screen and a coordinator's checklist beside it - not an hour of someone sitting in the room while a student types.

dubai/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Experiential learning runs through the whole IB continuum, and each programme hands the student a different piece of what CAS later asks for. Here is what arrives with them and what does not.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: CAS runs alongside the six subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and is expected to span at least eighteen months with a reasonable balance across creativity, activity and service. It includes one collaborative project of at least a month. It is monitored through a portfolio and three documented interviews with a CAS coordinator or adviser, and it is a completion requirement rather than a graded component.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical pressure on CAS is the calendar rather than the content. School years here are punctuated by a long summer when a large share of families are out of the country, and the DP2 autumn is dense with internal assessment deadlines. Students who treat CAS as something to catch up on in DP2 find the eighteen-month span has quietly closed behind them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP carries service as action throughout and culminates in the personal project, which requires a process journal and a defence of choices. Students who kept that journal honestly already have the habit CAS depends on. The gap MYP leaves is scale: service as action tends to be arranged by the school, while CAS expects the student to initiate and plan.
programmes.countryNote: A number of Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 before DP1, and their students generally arrive with reflection habits intact. Students coming from an IGCSE Year 11 often arrive having done plenty of genuine volunteering with no record of any of it, which is a documentation problem rather than an experience problem.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP core includes service learning as one of its components rather than CAS, with its own structure and expectations. The distinction matters for families comparing routes, because service learning and CAS are not interchangeable in a diploma application and the evidence one produces will not simply transfer into the other.
programmes.countryNote: Only a few Dubai schools offer CP. Any move between programmes is governed by registration deadlines your DP coordinator holds, and the sensible role for a mentor in that conversation is to describe each component's requirements accurately and send the decision back to the school.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP builds action into the learner profile from the start, and the Year 6 exhibition typically includes a service element the children choose themselves. It is where IB students first experience the loop CAS formalises: notice something, decide to act, do it, then say what changed in you.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's PYP intake is large and movement between schools at Year 7 is common, so plenty of DP students here learned to reflect at a school nobody in their current staffroom knows. The habit survives the move; the records rarely do.

dubai/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: CAS has no subjects. What it has is strands and experience types, and choosing badly across them is the usual reason a portfolio ends up missing a learning outcome. Below is the map Dubai students actually work within.

subjects.name: Creativity through the arts
subjects.description: Music tuition, theatre, dance, visual art, film. The most commonly logged CAS activity in Dubai and the one most often under-evidenced, because a student who has played piano for eight years struggles to show a new skill or a challenge undertaken. The fix is a new piece, a new ensemble or a performance commitment, not more of the same.

subjects.name: Creativity outside the arts
subjects.description: Designing something, coding a tool for a real user, writing and editing a publication, building a prototype. Often stronger evidence than arts activity because the output is visibly new and the planning is visible. Works well where a student can show the version that failed first.

subjects.name: Activity through team sport
subjects.description: School teams and club sport, which Dubai supplies in quantity. Easy to log and easy to under-reflect: attendance records are not evidence of growth. Collaboration and perseverance outcomes are genuinely available here if the student writes about a season rather than a fixture.

subjects.name: Activity through individual training
subjects.description: Running, swimming, climbing, martial arts, structured gym programmes. Suits students whose timetable cannot hold a team commitment. The strongest portfolios here show a progression plan with a target and an honest account of what happened when it slipped.

subjects.name: Direct service
subjects.description: Face-to-face work with people or an environment, which carries the clearest evidence of engagement and ethics. In the UAE it needs permissions and a host organisation willing to take a sixteen-year-old, so it has to be arranged earlier than students expect.

subjects.name: Indirect service
subjects.description: Work that benefits a community the student is not physically with: producing materials, translating resources, building something a charity will use. Frequently the most practical route for a Dubai student with a long school day, and perfectly legitimate when the beneficiary is real and identified.

subjects.name: Advocacy
subjects.description: Campaigning on an issue for a public audience, which maps directly onto the global significance outcome. The common failure is an awareness campaign with no audience and no measurable reach; the fix is naming who was reached and what they did differently.

subjects.name: Research-based service
subjects.description: Gathering or analysing information a community organisation actually needs. Under-used by Dubai students and well suited to those already comfortable with data from their subject work, provided the organisation has asked for it rather than being told it exists.

subjects.name: The CAS project
subjects.description: A collaborative undertaking of at least one month, planned and initiated by students. The two requirements that fail most often are duration and genuine collaboration: a one-day fundraising event and a project where one student did everything both miss the point of the component.

subjects.name: Combined experiences
subjects.description: Coaching a junior team covers activity and service; designing materials for a charity covers creativity and service. Efficient for a crowded timetable and legitimate, but each strand still needs separate reflection rather than one entry claiming both.

subjects.name: Ongoing commitments
subjects.description: A weekly commitment sustained across terms is the clearest possible evidence for perseverance and for the eighteen-month span. One long commitment plus two or three shorter experiences is a stronger portfolio shape than a dozen fragments.

subjects.name: School-arranged experiences
subjects.description: Trips, service weeks and house activities organised by the school. These count, and they are useful, but a portfolio built entirely from them cannot evidence the outcome about initiating and planning, which requires the student to have started something.

dubai/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the CAS problem each one brings
dubai/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.regionsIntro: CAS enquiries from across Dubai divide along practical lines: how far a student travels to a service placement, how much of the summer the family spends abroad, and how structured their school's CAS programme is. Here is the pattern.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: Apartment living with high family turnover and students often arriving mid-DP from schools that logged CAS differently. The first conversation is usually reconstructing what already counts from a previous school's records.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Settled families with long-standing sport and music commitments, so creativity and activity are rarely the problem. Service is, and specifically the initiating outcome, because so much here is arranged by clubs and schools.

regions.name: Tilal Al Ghaf and Dubai Land Residence Complex
regions.note: Newer communities a long way from most service organisations, where travel time is the binding constraint on direct service. Indirect and research-based service are usually the realistic routes, and that choice is best made early.

regions.name: Mudon and Serena
regions.note: Younger DP cohorts and a strong preference for weekend activity. Projects here often start as community initiatives within the compound, which satisfies collaboration well provided the duration requirement is planned for.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Dubai Design District
regions.note: Proximity to studios, galleries and workshops makes genuinely new creativity experiences easy to arrange. The recurring problem is documentation: a student with real studio hours and no portfolio entries for any of them.

regions.name: Deira and Bur Dubai
regions.note: Established communities with dense local organisations and the shortest journeys to direct service placements in the city. Permissions remain the gate, and students here benefit most from starting those conversations in DP1.

regions.name: Dubai Healthcare City and Oud Metha
regions.note: Students interested in medicine cluster here and all want the same kind of placement, which makes availability tight and advance planning essential. Observation that is not service needs reframing before it goes in a portfolio.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City and Motor City
regions.note: Sports infrastructure on the doorstep, so activity is well covered and often over-logged. Coaching younger players is the usual bridge into service, and it evidences collaboration more convincingly than playing does.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools running tightly structured CAS programmes
schoolClusters.note: Where a school schedules CAS lessons, sets portfolio checkpoints and chases missing entries, families rarely need outside help at all. Students we support attend schools in this group, and the honest answer in most of those conversations is that the school already has it covered.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where CAS is largely student-led
schoolClusters.note: Some programmes trust students to drive their own CAS with light-touch adviser contact. Highly capable students thrive; students who defer things do not. Students we support attend schools in this group, and the common request is an external deadline to work to.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools with large DP cohorts and one CAS coordinator
schoolClusters.note: A single coordinator holding a large cohort can only interview and chase so much, so gaps surface late. Students we support attend schools in this group, and most of our genuine CAS work comes from here, in DP2, with a learning outcome already flagged as missing.

modes.title: Portfolio audit, single session
modes.description: One session with the portfolio open on a shared screen. We go through the seven learning outcomes and mark each one as evidenced, partly evidenced or missing, then check whether the project meets the duration and collaboration requirements and whether the interviews have happened. The output is a one-page gap list the student takes to their coordinator. For most Dubai families this is the only CAS session they need.

modes.title: Planning session in DP1
modes.description: A single session near the start of the programme, which is the cheapest moment to intervene. We map the student's existing commitments onto the strands, identify which outcomes nothing currently evidences, and plan a project with a realistic month-long shape. Service permissions and host organisations are discussed here because in the UAE they take weeks rather than days to arrange.

modes.title: Reflection coaching, two or three sessions

Reflection is a skill and it is teachable in a couple of sessions: what the outcome actually asks, what counts as evidence of a challenge rather than of attendance, and how to write four honest sentences instead of a paragraph of description. The student writes every entry themselves; we ask the questions.

Which outcomes can still be evidenced from experiences already completed, which need something new, what can realistically run inside the time available, and what has to be escalated to the school immediately rather than solved privately. Honest, unpleasant, occasionally the difference between a diploma and no diploma.

sections.heading: Unmarked, mandatory, binary: how CAS differs from the rest of the core
paragraphs: The DP core has three parts and they behave completely differently. Theory of Knowledge is graded A to E and feeds the points matrix. The Extended Essay is graded A to E and feeds the same matrix. CAS is not graded at all and feeds nothing. What CAS does instead is gate the diploma: without completion there is no award, whatever the subject points say.

That structure explains why CAS advice in Dubai parent groups is so unreliable. Families reason by analogy with graded components, so they ask how to do CAS well, how to make it impressive, whether a particular activity will look better. Those questions have no mechanism behind them. There is no scale on which one portfolio outranks another, and a coordinator's sign-off is not a quality judgement; it is a confirmation that the requirements are met.

Where CAS does carry weight is outside the IB. University applications, scholarship interviews and conversations with admissions readers all draw on what a student actually did, and a student with a sustained commitment and a real project has something to say. That is a genuine benefit and worth pursuing for its own sake. It is simply not what the IB is measuring, and conflating the two leads families to spend money optimising a component that cannot be optimised.

The binary nature of the requirement changes the risk calculation too. A student weak in a graded subject loses points proportionally; a student who has not completed CAS loses everything. That asymmetry is why the practical advice on this page is boring: start early, keep a record as you go, get the three interviews done on time, and make sure the project genuinely runs a month. None of that is difficult. It is simply easy to postpone, and the postponement has no warning signal attached because there is no mark to slip.
The table below sets the three core components side by side, because seeing them together is usually the moment a parent understands why this page recommends fewer sessions rather than more.
