dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-online-tuto.programmesIntro: Computer Science arrives in the Diploma by three different routes in Dubai, and the route decides what the first block of tuition should repair. A student from IGCSE Computer Science has notation habits; a student from MYP Design has project habits; a student from neither has both to build.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Design assesses inquiry and analysis, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating, which maps unusually well onto the Diploma's developed solution. Students from this route tend to document instinctively and to under-estimate the algorithmic content of the written papers. Their first gap is almost always pseudocode notation and trace discipline rather than project management.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's continuum schools feed MYP Design students into Diploma Computer Science, and in several of them the MYP Design teacher is also the Diploma Computer Science teacher. That continuity is an advantage in the solution and a blind spot in the written papers, which is where outside marking tends to be most useful.

programmes.name: IGCSE Computer Science as the pre-Diploma route
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 covers data representation, networks, hardware, software, security, databases, algorithm design and programming. Students arriving from it have real notation fluency and a habit of short, closed questions. The Diploma asks for extended reasoning about system design and for a sustained independent project, which is a different discipline entirely.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools hold the largest share of Dubai's private enrolment, so 0478 is the commonest feeder into Diploma Computer Science in the emirate. The reliable early intervention for this group is extended-response practice, because the IGCSE habit of answering in three lines caps marks on Diploma questions worth considerably more.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Computer Science
programmes.description: Written papers covering system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, computational thinking and abstract data structures, plus an internally assessed developed solution built for a real client with documented planning, design, development and evaluation. Higher Level extends the content and adds a paper based on a pre-released case study. The course was revised recently, so check which guide the cohort follows.
programmes.countryNote: Computer Science is offered by a minority of Dubai's IB Diploma schools, and cohorts are frequently small. That produces two effects a family should expect: fewer classmates to debug alongside, and a teacher splitting limited code-review time across students whose solutions share no common architecture.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. Computer Science appears inside technology-oriented CP pathways, and the assessment demand for that single Diploma course is identical to the full Diploma version, developed solution included.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools run CP with Computer Science inside it, so a student on that route may have no cohort at all for the subject. One-to-one over video is less a preference than a practical necessity there, and the solution supervision is the part that most needs an external second reader.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-online-tuto.subjectsIntro: Computer Science students in Dubai usually carry a mathematics commitment and often a science. The notes below say what each neighbouring subject assesses, because that determines whether one tutor can reasonably hold two of them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Written papers on system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, computational thinking and abstract data structures, plus a developed solution for a real client. Higher Level adds a case-study paper. Marks are lost in documentation and in pseudocode notation far more often than in programming ability.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most computer science degrees expect. Algebraic manipulation, sequences, calculus and proof. Higher Level Paper 3 rewards extended problem solving, which is the closest thing in the Diploma to the reasoning an abstract data structures question demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and matrices, with graph theory at Higher Level. Useful alongside Computer Science for data-oriented solutions, but worth checking against target university entry requirements, which frequently specify Analysis and Approaches for computing degrees.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity and fields, with an experimental internal assessment. Shares with Computer Science the discipline of quantitative reasoning under timed conditions, and competes with it directly for internal-deadline time in DP2.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Assessed partly through a design project with staged documentation, which is procedurally similar to the Computer Science solution. Students taking both meet two large documented projects in the same academic year, and the scheduling collision is predictable enough to plan around.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Replaces the older information technology course, covering data, computing, networks and the social impact of technology through written papers and an inquiry project. Less programming, more argument. Some students switch into it from Computer Science in DP1, which is a decision worth taking early rather than late.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Written papers plus a scientific investigation. Appears alongside Computer Science in medicine-adjacent and engineering-adjacent subject combinations, and brings its own internal deadline into the same DP2 term.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Extended response and data response papers plus a portfolio of short commentaries. A common fourth subject for Computer Science students in Dubai; the transferable habit is quantitative reading of supplied data rather than answering from memory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, comparative essay and oral components. The relevant transfer for Computer Science is extended written structure, which is exactly what the longer written-paper questions reward and what IGCSE-trained students most often lack.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-online-tuto.regionsIntro: Computer Science is thinly distributed across Dubai's IB schools, so this list is about which communities have a Diploma Computer Science cohort nearby and what that does to a student's access to code review.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The emirate's main Diploma corridor and the likeliest place to find a Computer Science cohort of reasonable size. Even here, HL groups are often under ten, so individual code review is scarce rather than absent.

regions.name: Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Continuum schools whose Computer Science intake comes largely from MYP Design. Strong on documentation instinct, weaker on pseudocode notation, which is a predictable and quickly fixable starting diagnosis.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Technology-oriented households and proximity to higher-education campuses. Students here often arrive with real programming experience from outside school, which helps the solution and does nothing for the written papers.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Apartment living, so a shared desk and a headset is the realistic setup. A 60-minute session with the student's editor on screen works better here than a long block in a busy room.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Long school runs in both directions. Families in these communities often place the Computer Science session on a weekend morning, when debugging a solution for ninety minutes is actually feasible.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Mixed British and IB households, which means some students arrive from IGCSE 0478 and some from MYP Design. The opening session establishes which, because the teaching order differs sharply.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland, Meydan and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Newer and established international provision respectively. Students in both clusters frequently take Computer Science alongside Design Technology, which produces two documented projects in one DP2 term.

schoolClusters.note: Where Diploma Computer Science provision in Dubai is most concentrated, which in practice still means small groups. A student with an unusual architecture in their developed solution is frequently the only one in the cohort facing that problem. Students we support attend schools in this area; no relationship with any of them is implied.

sections.heading: The four artefacts a Dubai parent can inspect without reading a line of code
paragraphs: Begin with the direct answer. A Diploma Computer Science student in Dubai should be accumulating four kinds of evidence, and a parent can interrogate all four without any technical knowledge: the dated documentation for the developed solution, the version history of the code, the recording that demonstrates functionality against agreed criteria, and a file of marked written-paper scripts. Each one answers a different question about whether the work is real and whether it is improving.

The documentation is the easiest to check and the most predictive. The developed solution is assessed across staged components, and a student who has a client, a written set of success criteria, a design record and a development log is on track procedurally even if the code is unfinished. A student with four hundred lines of code and no documentation is in trouble, because the marks are allocated to the documented process at least as much as to the artefact. Ask to see the documents, note the dates on them, and ask what changed between versions.

Version history carries information that nothing else does. A solution that grows across dozens of small commits over several months reflects sustained independent work. One that appears in two large commits in the final fortnight invites a question, and it is better for a family to ask that question in February than for a school to ask it at submission. This is not about suspicion of the student; it is about the fact that incremental development is also better practice and produces a better solution.

The functionality recording and the marked scripts complete the picture. The recording should show the solution doing the things the success criteria said it would do, in order, which is a test a parent can apply directly. The marked scripts show whether pseudocode notation and trace discipline are improving, and because those are mechanically right or wrong, a parent reading annotated marking can see movement without understanding the content. Delivery of all this work for UAE families is live video, one student at a time; nothing on this page involves a tutor travelling to an address in Dubai.

sections.heading: The written papers: pseudocode, traces, and the questions that are not about programming
paragraphs: A persistent misconception sinks capable Dubai students every year: that the written papers test programming. They do not test programming in any named language. They test computational thinking expressed in the examination's own pseudocode notation, alongside substantial content on system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and abstract data structures that involves no code at all. A student who has written games in Python since Year 8 can still sit in the middle bands on these papers, and usually knows it before anyone tells them.

Notation is the first mechanical loss. The examination uses a defined pseudocode with its own conventions for loops, conditionals, input, output and collection access. A student who answers in Java syntax, or in Python's indentation-based style, is relying on an examiner's goodwill rather than on the mark scheme. This is trivially fixable in two or three sessions and it is almost never fixed by a student working alone, because nothing in the self-taught programming world rewards learning a notation nobody runs.

Trace questions are the second. A trace table asks for the state of every relevant variable at every iteration, written out. Strong programmers hate them, because they can see the answer and resent showing the steps, and so they write the final value and lose most of the marks. The marks are in the intermediate rows. Practising traces by hand, slowly, with the tutor watching the student write each row, breaks that habit faster than any amount of explanation.

The third loss is structural. Extended-response questions on networks, system design or data structures reward organised argument: the concept named, the mechanism explained, the trade-off identified, the context applied. A student trained on IGCSE short-answer questions writes three sentences and stops. Marked practice with the mark allocation written beside each paragraph makes the shortfall visible, which is the point of returning annotated scripts rather than a score.

sections.heading: The developed solution: the documentation is the grade, not the program
paragraphs: This is the single most expensive misunderstanding in Diploma Computer Science. Students believe the internally assessed component is a programming task and that the documentation is paperwork wrapped around it. The assessment criteria say the opposite: marks are distributed across planning, design, the record of development, the demonstration of functionality and the evaluation. A technically impressive program with thin documentation scores poorly. A modest program with rigorous documentation scores well. Every experienced Computer Science teacher knows this and many students refuse to believe it until they see a marked example.

The planning stage requires a real client with a real problem, and success criteria agreed with that client in writing. Dubai students often choose a parent's business, a school club or a community organisation, which is a sound instinct provided the client interaction genuinely happens and is recorded. A fictional client is detectable and undermines the whole submission, because every later criterion refers back to the agreed criteria. Getting this stage right in the first fortnight prevents most of the problems that surface in the final month.

The design and development stages require evidence that decisions were made and recorded: structure diagrams, data flow, algorithm design, and a dated record of the tasks undertaken with the techniques used. The common failure is retrospective documentation, written in one sitting after the code is finished, which reads as retrospective and tends to be internally inconsistent. Building documents alongside the work is both easier and better rewarded, and it is the main thing a supervision session should enforce.

The evaluation stage requires honest assessment against the original success criteria, including the ones not met, plus recommendations for extension. Students systematically over-claim here, declaring every criterion satisfied. A criterion honestly reported as partially met with an explanation scores better than a criterion dishonestly reported as met and visibly not working in the functionality recording. The recording and the evaluation are read together, so inconsistency between them is the easiest deduction an examiner ever makes.

sections.heading: Why the strongest coder in the class is often not the highest scorer
paragraphs: This pattern repeats across Dubai cohorts with enough regularity to be worth naming directly. A student who codes confidently outside school arrives with real ability and three habits that cost marks. They skip notation, because nobody they have ever coded with uses examination pseudocode. They skip documentation, because in self-taught programming the working artefact is the whole point. And they skip the non-programming content, because system fundamentals and network theory feel like reading rather than doing.

None of those habits reflects weakness, which is why telling the student to work harder achieves nothing. The intervention is targeted: three sessions on notation with marked scripts, a documentation routine enforced weekly so it becomes part of development rather than an afterthought, and timed written practice on the theory content where the student can see the marks going missing. Capable students respond fast to this because the gap is procedural, and the evidence file makes the improvement visible within a half-term.

The mirror-image student also exists and needs the opposite plan. A careful, organised student with limited programming confidence usually documents beautifully and then under-builds, submitting a solution too simple to access the upper bands on the development criteria. For that student the paid time goes on technical ambition, scaffolded carefully: choosing a problem that genuinely requires a non-trivial technique, then building it in increments small enough not to stall. Those two students need completely different six weeks, which is why a diagnostic first session matters more here than in most subjects.

A third pattern, less discussed, is the student whose solution is architecturally wrong in a way that will cap their mark regardless of effort. Discovered in November of DP2 this is a serious problem; discovered in March of DP1 it is a conversation. An external reader looking at the plan early is cheap insurance, and it is a genuinely useful thing to buy from a specialist who has supervised a number of these projects and recognises an unrecoverable design when they see one.
bullets: Notation: answer written papers in the examination's pseudocode, not in a real language
Traces: write every intermediate state, even when the answer is obvious
Documentation: build it alongside the code, with dates that reflect reality
Theory: timed practice on networks and system fundamentals, which feel like reading and mark like doing
Ambition: the solution must be complex enough to reach the upper development bands

sections.heading: Reading the Higher Level case study properly
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit an additional paper built on a case study released ahead of the examination session. It is a specific technology domain, described in a document that schools receive in advance, and it is examined with extended questions that assume genuine understanding rather than recall of a summary. This is the component with no textbook chapter, no past-paper bank that transfers from previous years, and consequently the one most often left until the last month.

The work that scores has three layers. The first is terminology: the case study introduces specialist vocabulary which must be understood rather than listed, because questions use the terms rather than defining them. The second is underlying technology: students who read beyond the document, from primary sources, can explain mechanisms rather than naming them. The third is applied reasoning about the specific domain, including trade-offs, limitations and the ethical and social dimensions that the case usually invites.

This is the ideal component for low-intensity online supervision spread across months. Thirty to forty minutes a fortnight with reading set between sessions, the document annotated collaboratively on a shared screen, and written summaries reviewed, accumulates into the depth the paper rewards. Compressed into three weeks it becomes vocabulary memorisation, which is exactly what the extended questions are designed to defeat.

One honest caution. No tutor can predict the questions, and anyone implying that they can should be treated with real scepticism. The value of the preparation is that comprehension time in the examination room drops to near zero, leaving the whole of the writing time for reasoning. On timing more generally, this page publishes no IB dates: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing here is confirmed from the IB directly. Confirm the case study release and the session windows with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the work is code, and when code generation tools exist
paragraphs: Computer Science has always had an attribution question that essay subjects do not: code is routinely assembled from libraries, snippets and documented patterns, and some of that is legitimate professional practice. The Diploma position is that assessed work must be the student's own, and that any external source used must be acknowledged. A library used and cited is fine. A tutorial's architecture reproduced wholesale and presented as original design is not. The practical rule is that the student must be able to explain every line and must have recorded where anything external came from.

Generative code tools make this sharper rather than different. A student who asks a model to produce a working function, pastes it in, and cannot explain it has not demonstrated the skill the criteria assess, and has an attribution problem on top. Schools set their own policies on these tools and they differ, so the first thing to establish is what the student's own school and the current IB guidance permit. Where use is permitted at all, it must be acknowledged, and the student must still be able to justify the design decisions as their own.

The tutor's boundary is the same as in every other subject and worth stating plainly, because this is the subject where blurring it is easiest. A tutor may teach a technique, explain why an approach will not scale, point to the part of a design that will cap the mark, ask what a function is supposed to do, and review a draft document. A tutor may not supply working code for submission, author any part of the documentation, or fix a program while the student watches. Debugging alongside a student who holds the keyboard is teaching; taking the keyboard is substitution.

The incremental version history discussed earlier is a defence as well as evidence. A student who can show that their solution grew in small steps across months, with a development log recorded at the time, has an answer to any question about authorship. One who cannot has only their word, and in a subject where authorship is genuinely hard to verify, that is a weaker position than it should be. Any provider offering to supply a finished solution should be refused outright; the consequence of malpractice falls on the student, not on the seller.
bullets: Every external library, snippet or pattern used must be acknowledged in the documentation
The student must be able to explain every line they submit, in their own words
Establish the school's and the IB's current position on code generation tools before using one
A tutor teaches, questions and reviews; the student holds the keyboard throughout

sections.heading: What Computer Science tuition costs in Dubai, and why this subject sits high in the band
paragraphs: The published market bands for Dubai apply to Computer Science as they do to any Diploma subject, but availability pushes this one towards the upper end. A qualified online subject tutor is published at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB or IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, as of October 2026. For Diploma Computer Science specifically, the pool of people who can both teach the written-paper content and supervise a developed solution is small, and scarcity shows up in the rate rather than in the availability calendar.

There is a second reason this subject costs more per hour than it looks like it should: the unbilled work. Reviewing a student's repository and documentation properly takes time outside the session, and marking a pseudocode script by hand takes longer than marking a multiple-choice set. A provider quoting at the bottom of the band is usually quoting for contact time only. The question to put to any provider is whether code and document review between sessions is inside the rate, because the answer changes the real cost materially.

The table below is organised by the kind of work bought rather than by brand, with the publisher of each AED figure named. Every figure is a market rate from the source stated, not a price list for this platform. Monthly package pricing circulating on the Dubai market includes around AED 799 for eight online sessions at the budget end. Rates firm up rather than soften as the examination series approaches, and specialist slots for a thin subject fill earliest, so a family waiting until February is choosing from the top of the band.

One piece of local context makes the decision easier to frame. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A family planning two years of Diploma support is budgeting against a flat school fee, which is unusual and worth factoring into a decision about whether to buy the cheap early hours that this subject rewards.

sections.heading: Small cohorts, thin provision, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: Computer Science is offered by a minority of Dubai's IB Diploma schools, and this has consequences a family should understand before they start searching. Within a school, a small cohort means limited individual code review and no peer group facing the same architectural problem. Outside school, the pool of genuine Diploma Computer Science specialists in any single emirate is thin, which is precisely the condition under which a location-bound search produces either nobody or whoever is nearest.

That is the substantive argument for live-video delivery here, and it is stronger in this subject than in most. A family in Dubai Investments Park or Mirdif looking for someone who has supervised developed solutions and marks pseudocode by hand is choosing from a national pool rather than a drive-time radius. The subject is also unusually well suited to the format: the student's editor, repository and documentation all live on a screen already, and screen sharing with the student driving the keyboard is closer to professional practice than sitting side by side at a desk.

Honesty about limits belongs here too, because no competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all. The pool for Diploma Computer Science is wider than a Dubai-only search suggests and it is not unlimited. A narrow weekly window, Higher Level, and a case-study block in the same request can genuinely mean no match this week. When that happens the answer should be the nearest available slot or a short wait, stated at the enquiry. What should never happen is a general programming tutor being presented as a Diploma specialist, which wastes a term and is the commonest failure mode in a scarce subject.

Scheduling has one Dubai-specific constraint worth planning around. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in the Arabic first-language, Islamic Education and Social Studies strands. More timetable blocks means less slack, so a fixed protected weekly slot outperforms a flexible arrangement. Ramadan shifts sessions later, and a post-Iftar slot is a normal request that costs nothing extra over video.

process.title: Name the component and the guide version
process.description: Diploma Computer Science HL, developed solution at design stage, plus trace questions on the written paper is a brief that can be matched precisely. Confirming which version of the guide the cohort follows matters here more than in most subjects, because a recent revision means some older resources no longer apply.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a diagnostic
process.description: The first session costs nothing and produces evidence: one pseudocode question and one trace table attempted live, plus a look at the current state of the solution documentation. You receive the marked script and a written note of the specific habits to target. That is what you judge the match on.

process.title: Agree the artefact plan
process.description: Before a block starts, the plan should state which syllabus content will be covered, how many marked scripts you will receive, and which solution documents will exist by when. In this subject the dated documents are the grade, so putting them on a calendar is the single most useful planning act available.

process.title: Sessions with the student at the keyboard
process.description: Sessions run over live video in Gulf Standard Time with the student's editor and repository shared. The student types; the tutor teaches, questions and reviews. Work set between sessions comes back marked, and repository and documentation review happens outside the session where that is included in the arrangement.

process.title: Six-week review against the four artefacts
process.description: Count the documents, look at the version history, watch the functionality recording if there is one, and read the marked scripts. Then continue, change frequency, change tutor or stop. If no Diploma Computer Science specialist is free in your window, you are told at the enquiry rather than matched with a general programming tutor.

whyPoints.title: Inspectable work, not progress reports
whyPoints.description: Four artefacts accumulate: dated solution documents, an honest version history, a functionality recording and marked written-paper scripts. A parent who writes no code can interrogate all four. A verbal assurance that the student is doing well is not evidence and should not be accepted as one.

whyPoints.title: Pseudocode marked by hand
whyPoints.description: Written-paper answers are marked in the examination's own notation rather than in whichever language the student prefers. That is the cheapest substantial improvement available in this subject and it is almost never made by a student working alone, because nothing outside the examination rewards that notation.

whyPoints.title: Documentation enforced alongside development
whyPoints.description: The solution's marks sit in the documented process. Supervision sessions produce a dated document or a working increment each time, so the record of tasks is built in real time. Retrospective documentation written in one sitting reads as retrospective and marks accordingly.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen from a national pool
whyPoints.description: Diploma Computer Science provision is thin across Dubai's IB schools and specialist tutors are scarce. Live-video delivery means the match is made on depth in this specific subject rather than on who lives nearby, which matters more here than in a subject every school offers.

whyPoints.title: Clear authorship boundaries
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and reviews; the student holds the keyboard and submits only their own work, with every external library or pattern acknowledged. No finished code, no written documentation, no keyboard takeovers. The incremental version history protects the student as well as evidencing the work.

whyPoints.title: Figures and rules with their sources

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Computer Science online tutor in Dubai charge an hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures as of October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and a Diploma or IGCSE specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB rates from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate survey covers the specialist band. Those are market figures from the sources named, not a price list for this platform. Computer Science tends to sit high inside those bands, because the pool of people who can both mark pseudocode and supervise a developed solution is small.

faqs.question: Is the developed solution marked on the code or on the documentation?
faqs.answer: On both, with more of the marks attached to the documented process than most students expect. The criteria distribute marks across planning with a real client and agreed success criteria, design with diagrams and justified techniques, a dated record of development, a recording demonstrating functionality, and an honest evaluation against the original criteria. A technically strong program with thin documentation scores poorly; a modest program with rigorous documentation scores well. The practical consequence is that supervision should produce a dated document every session rather than only working code.

faqs.question: Which programming language do the written papers examine?
faqs.answer: None. The written papers use a defined pseudocode with its own conventions for loops, conditionals, input, output and collection access, and answers are marked against that notation. A student who writes Java or Python syntax is depending on examiner goodwill rather than the mark scheme. This is one of the cheapest fixes in the subject, usually two or three sessions of marked practice, and it is almost never fixed by self-study because nothing outside the examination room uses that notation. Schools commonly teach development in a real language, which is appropriate for the solution and irrelevant to the papers.

faqs.question: Can a tutor debug my daughter's program for her?
faqs.answer: A tutor can work through a problem alongside her while she holds the keyboard, which is teaching, and that is both permitted and the most useful thing a session can do. A tutor taking the keyboard and fixing the program is substitution, and the submitted work would no longer be entirely hers. The useful form is questioning: what is this function supposed to return, what does the output actually show, where would you put a print statement to find out. Students who learn that sequence can debug the next problem alone, which is the whole point.

faqs.question: What goes into the functionality recording and how long should it be?
faqs.answer: It should demonstrate the solution doing the things the agreed success criteria said it would do, in an order a viewer can follow, within the length the current guide specifies. Confirm that length with the school's coordinator, since this page publishes no figure it has not verified. The substantive point is consistency: the recording and the evaluation are read together, so a criterion declared met in the evaluation and visibly not working in the recording is the easiest deduction an examiner makes. Record it after development is substantially complete, and check it against the original criteria document line by line.

faqs.question: My son has no client for his solution. What should he do?
faqs.answer: Find a real one, early, because every later criterion refers back to the criteria agreed with that client. Dubai students commonly use a parent's business, a school club, a sports team, a community group or a family member with a genuine administrative problem. What matters is that the interaction actually happens and is recorded: a conversation, a stated problem, and measurable success criteria written down. A fictional client is detectable and weakens the whole submission, because the planning document stops being evidence of anything. One session spent on this in the first fortnight prevents most late-stage problems.

faqs.question: Does the Higher Level case study need separate tuition?
faqs.answer: It needs separate time, which is not quite the same thing. The case study is a specific technology domain with its own terminology, examined through extended questions that assume real understanding rather than a memorised glossary. There is no textbook chapter and no transferable past-paper bank. The work that scores is terminology understood, underlying technology read from primary sources, and applied reasoning about trade-offs and limitations. Low-intensity fortnightly sessions across months suit it well. Compressed into three weeks it becomes vocabulary memorisation, which the extended questions are designed to catch.

faqs.question: Why do students lose marks on trace tables when they know the answer?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are in the intermediate rows, not the final value. A trace question asks for the state of every relevant variable at every iteration, written out. Confident programmers see the result, write it, and lose most of the available marks for work they could do in their heads. The fix is mechanical and slightly tedious: traces worked by hand, slowly, with the tutor watching each row being written, until showing the state is automatic. Two or three sessions usually breaks the habit, and the gain is immediate because trace questions appear reliably.

faqs.question: Can my child use an AI coding assistant on the developed solution?
faqs.answer: Establish what the school's own policy and the current IB guidance permit before anything else, because policies differ and they change. Where any use is permitted, two rules hold regardless. It must be acknowledged, like any external source. And the student must be able to explain and justify every line they submit as their own design decision, because that is the skill the criteria assess. Code pasted in and not understood fails the criteria and creates an attribution problem at the same time. A dated incremental version history is the student's best protection on both counts.

faqs.question: Few Dubai schools offer Computer Science. Does that make a tutor harder to find?
faqs.answer: It does, and nobody in this market usually says so. Diploma Computer Science runs in a minority of Dubai's IB schools, cohorts are often under a dozen, and the pool of tutors who can both mark pseudocode and supervise a developed solution is correspondingly thin. A search bounded by drive time will return either nobody or whoever is nearest. Live-video delivery widens the pool to a national one, which is the real argument for the format in this subject. It is still not unlimited: a narrow window plus Higher Level plus case-study work can mean a short wait.

faqs.question: What progress can I see if I do not read code myself?
faqs.answer: More than in most subjects. Look at the dates on the solution documents and ask what changed between versions. Count the separate working sessions in the version history and ask whether the increments are small and regular. Watch the functionality recording against the written success criteria and check each one yourself. Read the marked written-paper scripts and ask whether the same notation error is still appearing six weeks on. None of that requires technical knowledge, and together it is a far better account of progress than any score a provider generates about itself.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level Computer Science enough for a computing degree?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the course and the country, and the mathematics route is usually the bigger factor. Many computing degrees specify mathematics at Higher Level, often Analysis and Approaches, and say nothing about Computer Science at all; some name Computer Science or Physics as an alternative. The reliable method is to read the entry requirements on the admissions pages of three or four target universities before subject choices close at the end of DP1. No tutoring page, this one included, should be relied on for an admissions requirement.

faqs.question: How does a programming lesson actually work over live video?
faqs.answer: Better than it works at a shared desk, for this subject specifically. The student's editor, terminal and repository are on screen already, so screen sharing puts the tutor inside the real working environment rather than looking over a shoulder. The student types throughout; the tutor watches the sequence of decisions, which is where the teachable material is, and intervenes with questions rather than corrections. Documents can be annotated collaboratively in the same session. Between sessions, repository and documentation review happens offline and comes back written, where that is part of the arrangement.

faqs.question: Does my child need a development environment ready before the first session?
faqs.answer: For the trial session, no. The diagnostic uses one pseudocode question and one trace table on paper or on a shared document, plus a look at whatever solution documentation exists, and none of that needs a working toolchain. For ongoing solution supervision, yes: the student should be working in whatever environment their school uses, with version control in place if the school permits it, because the version history is both good practice and the best evidence of independent work. Setting that up is one short session if it has not happened yet.

faqs.question: What happens if the student wants to change solution topic in DP2?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's Diploma coordinator first, because internal deadlines govern what is still possible. Where a change is feasible, treat it as a planning problem rather than a coding one: a new client, newly agreed success criteria, a fresh design record, and a realistic assessment of whether the remaining time supports a solution complex enough for the upper development bands. Where it is not feasible, the better route is usually to narrow the existing project to something deliverable and document the narrowing honestly in the evaluation. Either way, the decision belongs with the coordinator, not with a tutor.

intro.heading: A thin market prices differently, and that is the whole story here
paragraphs: Computer Science is the Diploma subject where Dubai families most often find that the cheap option does not exist. For Economics or Biology a parent can choose between a university student at AED 45 to 65 an hour, a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300, and a Diploma specialist in the AED 200 to 450 band published on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table. For Computer Science the bottom of that ladder is largely occupied by people who can program but have never read the subject guide, and hiring them costs a term before the mismatch becomes obvious.

The reason is arithmetic. Dubai has 227 private schools and seventeen curricula, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for roughly 7% of private enrolment in 2024-25. Computer Science is an optional Group 4 choice within that minority, so a given Diploma school may run it with eight candidates across two years, or not at all. The teaching population follows the cohort size. That is why a specialist in this subject commands a rate closer to the top of the band, and why the honest advice to a Dubai family is to pay for fewer hours of the right person rather than more hours of the wrong one.

Knowing that changes how you buy. In a thin market the expensive mistakes are made on diagnosis, not on price. A student who is actually losing marks on pseudocode and trace questions does not need another term of project help, and a student whose documentation is weak does not need more programming practice. One marked paper and one look at the solution documentation tells you which problem you have, and in this subject the two problems have almost nothing in common beyond the word computing.

There is also a verification layer worth settling early. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, issued free of charge for two years, and nobody should be describing themselves as approved by the IB, KHDA or anyone else. In a market where a strong developer can plausibly present themselves as a Diploma tutor, the two questions that separate the professionals are what they have taught and what they will not do with a student's own code.

So this page is organised around that market rather than around the syllabus. It starts with why the rate card looks the way it does in Dubai, then shows how to tell Computer Science apart from Digital Society before you pay anybody, then maps the components so the first twenty hours go in the right order. After that come the parts of the course that are not programming, how a solution review works over video, the six screening questions worth asking, the calendar counted backwards, what we do when nobody suitable is free, and the mathematics and equivalency layer behind a computing application.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.programmesIntro: Computer Science belongs to the final two years, but the thinking it assesses starts much earlier in the IB continuum, in design cycles and systematic investigation rather than in syntax. Here is what each programme a Dubai school runs contributes to a Diploma Computer Science grade.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Design is the relevant ancestor, not a coding club. Its cycle of inquiring, developing ideas, creating a solution and evaluating against self-authored criteria is almost exactly the shape of the Diploma developed solution. Students who worked that cycle honestly arrive able to write success criteria and test against them, which is the single most transferable habit in the subject.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts vary widely in how much programming they meet, from a full text-based language to block-based work only. Departments here report the same DP1 split every year: students who can build something but cannot document why they built it that way, and students who can write about design but have never debugged anything of their own.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Computer Science sits in Group 4 and runs across both Diploma years at Standard or Higher Level. Candidates sit written papers covering the core, an option topic chosen by the school, and submit an independently developed computational solution with substantial documentation. Higher Level adds further content and a case study published ahead of the examination. Confirm the current structure and weightings in the IB subject guide at ibo.org.
programmes.countryNote: Provision in Dubai is patchy by design rather than by neglect: a school with a small Group 4 cohort will often offer Physics and Biology and leave Computer Science to a handful of candidates or to Digital Society. That is why a Dubai parent should establish which subject is actually on the timetable before hiring anybody, because the two courses need different tutors.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Computer Science is a natural pairing with a technology-focused career study, and a CP candidate sits the same written papers and submits the same developed solution, so the subject support needed does not differ.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme, so a CP candidate taking Computer Science is often alone on that route in the building. The practical impact is scheduling rather than content: the career-related study and the reflective project land in the same months as the developed solution, and something has to give unless the calendar is planned in DP1.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.subjectsIntro: Computer Science is a core syllabus, a school-chosen option topic, and one substantial piece of independent work. Below is what a tutor covers with a Dubai candidate, and where the marks go missing in each part.

subjects.name: System fundamentals and planning
subjects.description: Planning a computerised system, change management, compatibility, usability, and the roles of stakeholders. It is the least technical part of the course and often the worst answered, because candidates who enjoy programming skim it and then meet it as a long-answer question worth real marks.

subjects.name: Computer organisation
subjects.description: The architecture layer: the processor, primary memory, the machine instruction cycle, binary representation and logic gates. Marks are lost on precision rather than understanding, especially on describing the fetch-decode-execute sequence in the order the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Networks
subjects.description: Network types, standards, the layered model, data packets, transmission media, compression and wireless security. Dubai candidates often answer these questions from general technology knowledge rather than from the syllabus vocabulary, which caps the mark even when the explanation is broadly right.

subjects.name: Computational thinking and problem-solving
subjects.description: Abstraction, decomposition, algorithm design, flow charts, pseudocode, trace tables and standard algorithms on arrays and collections. This is where the gap between a capable programmer and a high-scoring candidate is widest, and where most of a Standard Level repair plan goes.

subjects.name: Abstract data structures
subjects.description: Linked lists, stacks, queues, binary trees, recursion and the reasoning about efficiency that goes with them. Recursion in particular rewards hand-traced practice over code-first experimentation, and students who learned to program by building apps often find this the hardest content in the course.

subjects.name: The option topic
subjects.description: The school selects one option from the available list, and the choice changes revision entirely. Establish which one your child's department teaches before hiring, because an excellent tutor for one option can be learning the material alongside your child in another.

subjects.name: The developed computational solution
subjects.description: An independently built product with a real client or stated need, plus documentation covering planning, design, development, a demonstration of functionality and evaluation. The documentation carries the marks that students assume the code carries, which is the commonest misunderstanding in the whole subject.

subjects.name: The Higher Level case study
subjects.description: A scenario published ahead of the examination, requiring independent research into a technical field and the vocabulary that goes with it. It is the one component that can be prepared almost a year in advance and the one most often left until the final weeks.

subjects.name: Pseudocode and trace tables
subjects.description: The examination uses its own pseudocode conventions rather than any production language, and traces must be completed by hand in a specified format. Strong programmers lose marks here routinely, because fluency in Python is not fluency in the examination's notation.

subjects.name: Academic honesty with code
subjects.description: Library use must be acknowledged, borrowed code must be attributed, and the student's own contribution must be identifiable. The arrival of code-generating tools has made this both easier to breach and easier to detect, and the school's own policy is the binding document.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.regionsIntro: Location changes two things for a Computer Science family in Dubai: which schools near you actually offer the subject, and what time a session can start once the school run is finished. Here are the areas the enquiries come from.

regions.name: Dubai Internet City, Barsha Heights and Al Barsha
regions.note: The part of the emirate where a student is most likely to have a parent working in software and least likely to need motivating. The requests from this band are usually about the written papers rather than the solution, because the coding is already fluent and the pseudocode notation is not.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Close to several universities and technology employers, which makes finding a client for the developed solution unusually straightforward. Sessions here often start at five, and the common ask is documentation discipline rather than programming help.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Deep Diploma provision within a short drive, and the band where Higher Level Computer Science is most likely to be offered at all. Ninety-minute sessions are the norm, because a timed paper and its read-back does not fit into sixty minutes.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown Dubai and DIFC
regions.note: Apartment living, short school runs and plenty of small firms within reach for a solution client. Candidates from this band are often the only Higher Level Computer Science student in their year, which makes an outside specialist the only discussion partner they have.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
regions.note: Later bus arrivals push a realistic start past half past six, and the Diploma cohorts here are smaller. This is the band where Computer Science is most often taught by a teacher whose main subject is something else, which shows up in the option topic first.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, The Springs and Motor City
regions.note: Forty-minute school runs at the wrong hour and almost no local specialist supply for this subject. Families here were buying online tuition for Computer Science long before it became ordinary elsewhere, usually in a weekend morning slot.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills band
schoolClusters.note: Where Diploma Computer Science is most reliably offered, sometimes at both levels. Families in this band tend to ask for written-paper technique and Higher Level case-study preparation, because the department usually has a dedicated teacher and the core is covered on schedule.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Mirdif, Al Jaddaf and the Festival City corridor
schoolClusters.note: Smaller Group 4 cohorts, where Computer Science may run with a handful of candidates or be replaced by Digital Society. The requests from this corridor are weighted towards teaching the option topic and towards supervision of a solution that has no client yet.

dubai/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.modesIntro: Computer Science support splits into three jobs with different price behaviour: written-paper technique, solution supervision, and the Higher Level case study. Buying them as one undifferentiated weekly hour is why some Dubai families finish a year of tuition with the same mark they started with.

modes.description: Sixty to ninety minutes a week spent on the parts of the course that are examined on paper: pseudocode in the examination's own notation, hand-traced algorithms, architecture, networks and the long-answer questions on system planning. Sat-then-marked rather than taught-then-set, so the hour goes on correction rather than on writing.

Starting this early is the cheapest decision available in Higher Level Computer Science, and almost nobody makes it.

sections.heading: Why Computer Science sits at the top of the Dubai rate card
paragraphs: The price of tutoring tracks the depth of the local supply, and in Dubai the supply for Diploma Computer Science is thin. Dubai's private sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes taking roughly 7% of enrolment. Computer Science is an optional Group 4 choice inside that share, so the pool of people who have actually taught the course here is a fraction of the pool who have taught Diploma Biology or Mathematics. Rates reflect that, and they should.

What makes this subject distinctive is that the apparent supply is much larger than the real supply. Dubai has a substantial technology workforce, and a competent software engineer can reasonably describe themselves as able to help with school computing. Many can. What most cannot do is mark a long-answer question on system planning against the band descriptors, teach the examination's pseudocode conventions rather than a production language, or tell a student which parts of their documentation will not earn credit. That is the gap families discover in month two.

The practical consequence is counter-intuitive. In a thin market, buying fewer hours from the right person is cheaper than buying more hours from the wrong one, because the wrong purchase leaves the actual problem untouched while the calendar runs down. A parent who spends AED 400 an hour for six well-diagnosed hours usually spends less and gains more than one who spends AED 150 an hour for thirty hours of general programming help, and the second family arrives at the mock examinations with the same marks and no time.

sections.heading: Computer Science or Digital Society: establish which one before hiring
paragraphs: A surprising number of Dubai enquiries for a Computer Science tutor turn out to concern a different subject. Several schools in the emirate offer Digital Society rather than Computer Science, or offer both and let the Group 4 or Group 3 block decide. The two courses share vocabulary and share nothing else: one is a technical course with programming, algorithms and an independently built product; the other examines the social and ethical dimensions of digital systems through inquiry and evidence. A tutor for one is not a tutor for the other.

The check takes a minute and saves a term. Look at the subject name on the school report, not at what the student calls the lesson. Ask whether there is a programming language in use and which one. Ask whether the internally assessed work is a built product with documentation or a research inquiry. Ask whether the department chose an option topic. Those four answers identify the course unambiguously, and they are worth confirming with the Diploma coordinator in writing if there is any doubt.

It matters financially as well as pedagogically. Digital Society sits closer to the AED 150 to 300 qualified-subject-tutor band in Dubai because the supply of capable humanities and inquiry teachers is deeper. Computer Science sits in the specialist band for the reasons set out above. A family quoted a specialist rate for a Digital Society candidate is overpaying, and a family who hires a Digital Society tutor for a Computer Science candidate has bought something that cannot teach abstract data structures or review a developed solution.

sections.heading: A cost map of the components, so you can buy in the right order
paragraphs: Diagnosis decides the budget in this subject more than anywhere else, because the components fail independently. A student can write excellent code and score poorly on paper. A student can ace the architecture questions and submit documentation that earns half the marks available. The two problems need different tutors on different schedules, and a provider who does not ask which one you have will sell you the one they prefer teaching.

Buy in the order that respects the calendar. The Higher Level case study comes first in time, because it is published well ahead of the examination and preparing it early costs three to five hours while preparing it late costs twice that and competes with everything else. Solution milestones come next, pinned to the school's draft deadlines. Written-paper technique is continuous and the easiest thing to add or stop. Core content gaps should be closed in the term they appear, which is a two-to-four hour purchase per topic.

One further caution on the solution. The marks that students assume sit in the code mostly sit in the documentation: planning, design decisions, testing, the recorded demonstration of functionality and the evaluation against criteria the student set. A tutor who spends every session improving the program and none on the documentation is improving the part that is not being assessed directly. Ask explicitly how many of the planned sessions will be spent reading documentation rather than reading code, and ask for that answer as a number rather than as a reassurance.

sections.heading: The parts of the course that are not programming at all
paragraphs: Parents hire a Computer Science tutor imagining code, and a large share of the written examination is not about code. System fundamentals asks about planning a computerised system, stakeholder roles, compatibility issues and change management, in long-answer form. Computer organisation asks for the machine instruction cycle and binary representation in the order the mark scheme expects. Networks asks for syllabus vocabulary rather than a general grasp of how Wi-Fi works. None of this is taught by building projects, and all of it is examined.

This is where the strongest programmers in a Dubai cohort quietly lose their grade. A student who has shipped a working app can explain what a server does in practical terms and still fail to use the layered-model language the question requires. A student who writes elegant Python can get a trace table wrong because the examination's notation differs from the language they think in, or because they ran the algorithm mentally rather than filling in every column at every step as the format demands.

The repair is specific and quick, which is the good news in an expensive subject. Hand-traced practice in the required format, long-answer questions marked against the descriptors, and a vocabulary discipline that insists on syllabus terms rather than industry shorthand. Six to ten hours spread across a term usually moves this part of the paper substantially, and it is the work least likely to happen if you hire for programming help, because a working engineer will naturally gravitate to the code and away from the parts of the paper they find trivial.

sections.heading: Reviewing a developed solution over video without touching the student's work
paragraphs: The question Dubai parents ask most about online delivery in this subject is whether a tutor can really help with a build they cannot sit beside. The answer is that screen sharing is better for this than sitting beside it, for one reason: the student stays on the keyboard. When a tutor is physically next to a struggling student, the path of least resistance is for the tutor to take over and fix it. Over video the student types, the tutor watches and asks, and the student is the one who makes the change.

A good review session has a shape. The student shares the editor and runs the program while describing what they expect to happen. The tutor asks what the success criterion for this feature was, in the student's own words, and whether the test the student just ran actually proves it. Where it fails, the tutor asks what the student would check first, and then narrows the search by questioning rather than by reading the code aloud. The student records the outcome in their own documentation during the session.

This is also where the academic-honesty line is kept visibly. A tutor does not edit the student's files, does not supply blocks of code, and does not take the keyboard. Library use and anything borrowed must be acknowledged in the student's own documentation, and if a code-generating tool has been used anywhere the school's policy governs it and declaring it is the only safe route. A session recording helps everybody here: it shows exactly who did what, which is a reassurance for the student as much as for the parent.

sections.heading: Six checks on a Computer Science tutor that cost nothing
paragraphs: In a market where the apparent supply exceeds the real supply, screening matters more than negotiating. The six questions below take ten minutes, cost nothing, and are better than any amount of reading reviews. They are built around what this subject specifically requires: the examination's own conventions, the option topic, the documentation that carries the internal marks, and the honesty boundary around a student's own code.

Pay particular attention to the option topic question. Because the school chooses the option, a tutor can be genuinely excellent and still be learning your child's option material a week ahead of them. That can be acceptable if it is disclosed and priced honestly, and it is a problem if it is concealed. The same applies to level: Higher Level abstract data structures and recursion are the content a generalist most often cannot teach, and the case study needs someone who has prepared candidates for one before.

Treat examiner claims with care. No tutor should be presented as a current IB examiner without evidence, and examiner status must never be implied to give access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. Nor should any provider describe itself as approved, accredited or licensed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education; IB Gram holds none of those and says so. What a tutor can legitimately offer is experience, a method, and a marked script you can read, which is a stronger basis for a decision than any badge on a website.

sections.heading: The Computer Science year counted backwards
paragraphs: No competitor page in this search publishes a calendar, which is odd, because in this subject the calendar is the budget. The developed solution and the Higher Level case study are both time-bound tasks whose cost rises steeply the later they start, and both are governed by school deadlines rather than by the examination session. Get those dates from the coordinator in DP1 and the plan more or less writes itself.

Work from the end backwards rather than from today forwards. The written papers are the last thing that happens. Before them come the mocks, which are the best diagnostic any family gets for free. Before those comes the school's internal submission window for the solution, which in Dubai schools is usually weeks ahead of the IB's own deadline. Before that come the solution milestones, and before everything comes the case study for Higher Level candidates, which is published far enough in advance to be prepared calmly.

On IB dates specifically, be sceptical of any tutoring site that prints them, including this one. UAE schools sit the May session and results reach candidates during the summer that follows, but windows change year to year and the IB is the publisher. Confirm every date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For a sibling sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications in the same house, note that Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and that using the wrong zone timetable is the family's risk, not the board's.

sections.heading: Coverage, fallback and how the lessons actually run
paragraphs: Specialist coverage in this subject is the thinnest of any Group 4 course, so we would rather be explicit about it than quietly allocate whoever is free. A Standard Level request on a weekday evening is normally matched within a few days. A Higher Level request that also needs a specific option topic, in the fortnight before a mock series, is the hardest booking in the Dubai calendar and sometimes cannot be filled at the hour requested. No competing page in this search discloses a coverage limit at all, which does not mean they never reach one.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Sessions are recorded, so a student can rewatch a trace or a design discussion rather than relying on notes taken while thinking. Screen sharing runs in both directions for code and for documentation, and a shared whiteboard handles logic gates, trees and traces. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and this page says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.

In-home tuition does exist in this market, published at AED 180 to 350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table with some home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, and for most subjects the premium buys presence. For this one it also narrows the field severely: a family in Arabian Ranches hiring locally is choosing among Diploma Computer Science specialists willing to drive inland for a 6.30pm start, which in a subject this thinly staffed may be a list of nobody. Online, the same family is choosing among everyone who teaches the course at that hour.
