sections.heading: Where Dubai Design Technology candidates lose marks
paragraphs: The first pattern is the untestable specification, and it accounts for more lost marks in this subject than any content gap. It is also the easiest to fix, which is why it belongs in the first session rather than the tenth. A student who has written 'the product must be durable' has written something that cannot be marked; a student who has written a drop height, a number of cycles and a pass threshold has written something that generates testing pages on its own.

The second is confusion between kinds of modelling. The core topic distinguishes between graphical, physical and computer-based modelling, and each has its own purpose and limitations. Students answer modelling questions by describing whichever kind they personally used, rather than selecting the appropriate kind for the stated scenario and justifying it. The same confusion damages the folder, where a CAD render is offered as evidence of testing a physical property.

The third is sustainability answered as a list. Resource management and sustainable production is a core topic with real analytical content: life-cycle thinking, material selection trade-offs, end-of-life routes. Students write a list of environmentally friendly gestures. The fourth is classic design, where answers are offered as opinion when the topic has named criteria for what makes a design classic, and examiners mark against those. The fifth, specific to Higher Level, is treating the four extension topics as general knowledge rather than as examinable content with its own vocabulary.

sections.heading: How an online session reviews a CAD model and a folder
paragraphs: The mechanics matter in this subject more than in most, so they are worth describing plainly. The student shares their screen with the model open, whether that is Fusion, Onshape, SolidWorks or Inventor, and the tutor talks through the feature tree and the design intent while both are looking at the same geometry. A student who cannot explain why a feature exists usually cannot defend the decision in the folder either, and that conversation is faster on a shared screen than over a photographed drawing.

Folder pages are reviewed as exported files rather than as a live document, so comments attach to a fixed version. That gives the version history that makes progress visible later. Physical prototypes are photographed against a scale and discussed, which is a real limitation of online delivery and worth stating: a tutor cannot feel a joint or test a finish. What a tutor can do is judge whether the testing evidence the student recorded is adequate, which is what the criterion actually rewards.

For papers, the student works on a shared document and keeps the annotated file. Timed questions are done at home under real conditions and marked before the session, so the session is spent on diagnosis rather than on invigilation. All of this runs in Gulf Standard Time, and written notes mean a student who misses a session for a fixture or a school trip does not lose the content. The files accumulate into something genuinely useful by February: a dated sequence of folder versions and marked scripts that shows what the term actually did.

sections.heading: Workshop access, Dubai school provision, and designing within real limits
paragraphs: Design Technology provision in Dubai varies more than any other Group 4 subject, because it depends on physical facilities. Two KHDA-inspected schools a few kilometres apart can hold completely different design suites: one with a laser cutter, a three-dimensional printer and a small machine shop, another with hand tools and a computer room. A project designed without knowing which of those the student has access to is a project that stalls at development, and that is the commonest structural failure in Dubai DT folders.

So the first review question is logistical rather than creative: which processes can you actually reach, with what lead time, and who supervises them. Where school facilities are limited, Dubai does offer alternatives that students use legitimately: commercial printing and prototyping services, maker spaces, and the manufacturing neighbours around areas such as Dubai Investments Park and Al Quoz. All of that is permissible as long as the student's own decisions and documentation remain their own work.

The emirate's design economy also helps with the parts of the project that are hardest to fake. Primary research needs real users, and a student in Dubai Design District or near the industrial districts can arrange an interview or an observation that a student working from a textbook cannot. If the school does not run Design Technology at all, the honest position is that an online tutor cannot substitute for the course: the subject must be taken at the school. What a tutor can do is support a design-based Extended Essay or an alternative Group 4 choice instead.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a project with a client, a workshop and a CAD library
paragraphs: Design Technology creates more honesty questions than most Diploma subjects, because real projects involve other people. A technician operates the laser cutter. A parent who happens to be an engineer has opinions. A client gives feedback. None of that is prohibited, and all of it has to be documented for what it is. The rule is authorship of decisions: the student decides, the student records why, and any assistance received is acknowledged in the folder.

A tutor's boundary is narrower still. A tutor teaches the content, marks against published criteria, questions a decision and explains why a page does not score. A tutor does not generate concepts, produce CAD geometry, or put sentences into a student's folder. Every page of an internal assessment must be the student's own work. Any provider offering a finished design project is offering an academic-honesty breach, and the consequences of that land on the student, not on the seller.

Two newer issues deserve naming. Downloaded CAD components and texture or model libraries are widely used in industry and must be credited where they appear in a student's model; passing a downloaded assembly off as modelled work is misconduct of exactly the kind examiners are alert to. And generative tools can produce concept imagery in seconds, which is precisely why the development criterion rewards documented decisions rather than pictures. If a student cannot explain how a concept came about, the folder cannot evidence development, whatever the renders look like.

sections.heading: Grade movement, honest limits, and how delivery works
paragraphs: What can be said about movement is narrow and true: criterion-level feedback acted on across a term produces folder pages that score against more criteria than they did before, and marked scripts with a shrinking error log produce better paper performance. What cannot be said is where the final grade lands. Boundaries move between sessions, moderation adjusts internal marks, and the student sits the papers alone. Any tutor offering a guarantee in this subject is making a claim about marketing rather than about teaching.

Published market bands give the cost context. Collected in October 2026, other Dubai providers advertise AED per hour figures from roughly AED 45 to 65 for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, with one provider quoting AED 650 at examiner level. In-home visiting in Dubai is published at AED 180 to 500, with travel priced into the hour. IB Gram publishes no rate card here; the trial lesson is free with no card required, and a quote follows the component and the hours.

Delivery itself is settled. Lessons are online, one to one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run in-person lessons in Dubai, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Anyone providing private tuition inside the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own e-services; the official service is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. And where no Design Technology specialist is free in the window you need, we say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

process.title: Send the folder and the last marked script
process.description: Two files tell us more than a phone call: the current state of the design project folder and the most recent marked paper. From those we can usually name the weakest criterion and the dominant written error before the first session, which is what makes the trial lesson useful rather than introductory.

process.title: We match on evidence of having marked design projects
process.description: The filter is narrow and specific: experience teaching the six core topics, experience with the four extension topics for Higher Level students, and experience marking design-project work against the published criteria. If nobody who meets that is available in your window, you are told rather than quietly matched to someone broader.

process.title: A free trial lesson on your own pages
process.description: The trial runs on the student's real folder or script, with no card required to book it. It ends with a named criterion, one rewritten specification point or one reworked question, and an estimate of how many hours the fix needs. If the honest estimate is small, that is the estimate you get.

process.title: A review cycle with written actions
process.description: Fortnightly folder reviews, weekly marked papers, or a mix, with pages submitted in advance so the review is prepared. Every session ends with a written note naming what was addressed and one action before the next session, dated. That note is the record a parent reads.

process.title: A criterion audit before the internal deadline
process.description: Two weeks or more before the school's own submission date, the whole folder is read end to end in the order an examiner would read it, with a list of absences, assertions and limit breaches. The student has time to act on the list, which is the only sequence in which an audit is worth anything.

process.title: The block ends at submission or at the papers
process.description: A folder block ends when the project goes in; a paper block ends at the May session. There is no rolling commitment and no minimum term. Families who want to stop after one lesson stop after one lesson, and most come back for the next component rather than staying on a monthly plan.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can hold, not progress you are told about
whyPoints.description: A marked script with the mark-scheme logic shown, folder pages annotated against named criteria, a dated action list after every session. In a subject where 40% of the grade is a document that accumulates slowly, that record is the difference between teaching and company.

whyPoints.title: Specification work first, because everything refers back to it
whyPoints.description: Untestable specification points are the largest single source of lost marks in Design Technology, and they damage development, testing and evaluation at once. Rewriting them properly in the first sessions is unglamorous and changes more of the folder than any later intervention can.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level extension topics treated as examinable
whyPoints.description: User-centred design, sustainability, innovation and markets, and commercial production are taught late in most Dubai schools and revised last, which is why Paper 3 underperforms. A dedicated block on those four topics is often the highest-yield purchase a Higher Level family makes.

whyPoints.title: Designing within the facilities the student can actually reach
whyPoints.description: Dubai school design suites differ enormously, and a project that depends on an unavailable process stalls at development. The first review question is which processes are genuinely reachable, with what lead time and whose supervision, because that answer reshapes the project.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor marks, questions and explains. Concepts, CAD geometry and written pages stay the student's own, third-party assistance is acknowledged in the folder, and downloaded libraries are credited. The boundary is published because the risk of crossing it falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: No promises about the grade
whyPoints.description: Boundaries move, internal marks are moderated, and the student sits the papers alone. What is promised here is criterion-level feedback, marked work returned, and an honest statement when a specialist is not available. Anything beyond that would be a claim nobody can keep.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Design Technology tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures from other Dubai providers, collected in October 2026, run from about AED 45 to 65 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, with one provider advertising AED 650 for examiner-level review. In-home visiting is published at AED 180 to 500 with travel included in the hour. Design Technology sits at the specialist end because folder marking experience is uncommon. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page; the trial lesson is free with no card required and the quote follows the component and the hours.

faqs.question: What should a Design Technology tutor actually send us after each session?
faqs.answer: A note naming the criterion or the question part addressed, what changed, and one dated action for the student before the next session. For a folder review that means annotated pages; for a paper session it means a marked script with the mark-scheme logic made explicit. If what arrives is a sentence about how the lesson went well, you have no evidence of anything. In a subject where 40% of the grade accumulates in a document over months, that written trail is also the only way to see direction before results day.

faqs.question: Why does the design project carry so much weight in Design Technology?
faqs.answer: Because the subject assesses designing, and designing cannot be examined in two hours with a pen. The commonly published structure puts the project at 40% at both Standard and Higher Level, with the remainder split across two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher Level. Practically, this is good news for a family: the largest component is visible, reviewable and improvable months before the exams, unlike a paper performance nobody sees until August. Confirm the current weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning a revision timetable around them.

faqs.question: What is wrong with my child's design specification?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly that the points state intentions rather than measurements. 'Must be durable', 'should appeal to teenagers' and 'must be sustainable' cannot be tested, so they generate no testing pages and no evaluation. A testable point names a quantity, a method and a threshold: a drop height, a number of cycles, a mass limit, a measured task time. Rewriting six specification points properly is usually the single highest-value hour in the whole project, because development, testing and evaluation all refer back to them.

faqs.question: My child's folder is full of beautiful renders. Why is the mark low?
faqs.answer: Because renders are presentation and the criterion rewards development. Examiners look for a decision being made: two or more genuinely different options, a stated reason for choosing one, a rejected route and an explanation of why it was rejected. A sequence of increasingly polished images of the same idea reads as a project with no development, however good the drawing is. The fix is documentation rather than more drawing, and it is usually recoverable if there is still time to record the reasoning behind choices already made.

faqs.question: How is Paper 3 different from the other Design Technology papers?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat by Higher Level students only and examines the four extension topics: user-centred design, sustainability, innovation and markets, and commercial production. Each has its own vocabulary and methodology, which students cannot bluff from general knowledge. The structural problem in Dubai schools is timing: these topics are usually taught late in DP2 while the design project is consuming every spare hour, so they get revised last. A short dedicated block on the four topics is often the highest-yield purchase a Higher Level family makes.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really review a CAD model properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in some ways better than in a room. The student shares their screen with the model open in Fusion, Onshape, SolidWorks or Inventor, and both parties look at the same feature tree while the student explains why each feature exists. A student who cannot justify a feature usually cannot defend the decision in the folder either, and that is the conversation that moves marks. The honest limitation is physical: a tutor cannot feel a joint or a finish, so prototypes are photographed against a scale and judged on the testing evidence recorded.

faqs.question: Our school's design suite is very basic. Does that limit the grade?
faqs.answer: It limits the project, which is different. Dubai school facilities vary enormously, and the structural failure we see most often is a project designed around a process the student cannot reach, which then stalls at development. The right sequence is to establish which processes are genuinely available, with what lead time and whose supervision, and design within that. Commercial prototyping services and maker spaces are legitimate routes provided the decisions and documentation remain the student's own. Examiners mark the designing, not the sophistication of the workshop.

faqs.question: Does my child need Physics alongside Design Technology for engineering?
faqs.answer: For most engineering destinations, assume Physics and a demanding maths route are the requirements and Design Technology is the supporting subject rather than the qualifying one. Entry requirements are published per course, per university, per year of entry, and they differ more than families expect, so read the specific course page before DP1 subject selection rather than in DP2 when the timetable has closed. Design Technology does strengthen an application to architecture, product design and industrial design programmes, where a portfolio often matters as much as the subject list.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if our school does not offer Design Technology at all?
faqs.answer: Not as a substitute for the course. The design project is internally assessed and moderated through the school, so a student cannot take Design Technology privately while enrolled elsewhere in the Diploma. The honest options are a different Group 4 subject, or a design-based Extended Essay supervised by the school, which a tutor can give feedback on. Several Dubai IB World Schools do offer the subject; if it matters enough to change schools, ask each one which design processes their suite actually supports before committing.

faqs.question: How many hours does a design-project folder review block usually take?
faqs.answer: A full cycle across an autumn term is typically ten fortnightly or weekly sessions, front-loaded onto analysis and specification because everything later refers back to them. A shorter intervention on a folder already in trouble runs four to six hours: one pass to diagnose, two or three to rebuild the specification and development pages, one to plan testing. A pre-submission criterion audit is a single long session plus a written list, scheduled at least a fortnight before the school's internal deadline so the student has time to act on it.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with a design project, and what not?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the content, marks pages against the published criteria, questions a decision and explains why something does not score. A tutor does not generate concepts, produce CAD geometry or put sentences into the folder. Every page must be the student's own work. Third-party help that genuinely occurred, from a technician operating a machine to a client giving feedback, is acknowledged in the folder, and downloaded CAD components are credited where they appear. Any provider offering a completed design project is offering a breach that the student carries, not the seller.

faqs.question: Does my child need to acknowledge downloaded CAD parts and AI-generated images?
faqs.answer: Yes, where they appear in submitted work. Downloaded components, assemblies and material libraries are normal in industry and must be credited rather than presented as modelled work. Generative image tools raise the same issue in sharper form, which is exactly why the development criterion rewards documented decisions rather than pictures: a student who cannot explain how a concept arose cannot evidence development whatever the render looks like. If in doubt, declare it and describe the role it played; undeclared use is the problem, not use.

faqs.question: Will tutoring raise my child's Design Technology grade?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise that, and a tutor who does is telling you about their marketing. Grade boundaries move between sessions, internally assessed marks are moderated, and the student sits the papers alone. What can be shown is narrower and real: folder pages that score against more criteria than they did a month ago, a marked-script error log that shrinks, specification points that generate testing rather than blocking it. Those are the measurable things, and they are what the session notes on this service are built to record.

faqs.question: How do sessions fit around a Dubai school week and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: A fixed weekday slot in Gulf Standard Time holds far better than a flexible arrangement, and families who agree to find a time each week lose a significant share of sessions. Design Technology has a specific complication: workshop access is timetabled, so making happens at school on days the student cannot be in a session. Reviews are therefore scheduled the day after a workshop slot wherever possible. During Ramadan school days compress and the usable evening window narrows, so the shift to later timing is agreed before the month begins rather than renegotiated weekly.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-online-tut.closingBody: The quickest way to find out whether this is worth your money is to let someone read what your child has actually produced. Send the current design project folder and the most recent marked script. We will check who is genuinely available with design-project marking experience, run a free trial lesson on those pages with no card required, and tell you which criterion is weakest and roughly how many hours the fix needs. Lessons run online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time, and every session ends with a named criterion and one dated action.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Diploma Design Technology for Dubai students at both levels: the written papers, the core and extension content, the graphical and modelling skills, and the design project folder that carries the internal marks from first user research to final evaluation.

intro.heading: The making budget is the part of Design Technology nobody quotes for
paragraphs: Design Technology is the Diploma subject where a family can price the tutoring accurately and still be caught out. Teaching cost behaves like any other subject: an hourly rate inside the published Dubai bands multiplied by the weeks you commit to. What sits alongside it is a making cost that arrives in irregular lumps and belongs to nobody in particular. Materials for a prototype that gets rebuilt three times. Printing and plotting for a folder. Access to a machine the school does not own. A component ordered twice because the first dimension was wrong. None of that appears on a tutoring quote, and all of it lands on the same household.

The hourly figures in this market are public and spread extremely wide. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level support at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Each of those is the provider's own published figure, read in October 2026, and they appear here as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list.

Design Technology quotes tend to sit at the specialist end of that spread for a checkable reason. The subject needs a tutor who can read a technical drawing, judge a CAD model, mark a written paper, and supervise a folder against criteria that reward process rather than product. That combination is rarer than a physicist or a mathematician, so the price reflects supply. Content difficulty is not the mechanism, and a provider who explains the premium that way has probably not taught the subject.

Where families genuinely lose money is sequencing. A design project that is reviewed for the first time after the prototype exists cannot be redirected without either discarding work or submitting a folder whose early stages do not justify the thing that got built. The second outcome is common and it caps the mark. Reviewing a specification and a set of early ideas costs two or three hours; rescuing a folder built on a thin specification costs ten or more and still reads as a repair. Buying help earliest in this subject is the cheapest version of buying it at all.

Delivery is online. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which for a subject assessed through a documented folder is a better fit than it sounds: the student's own CAD model, drawings and folder pages are on screen for both parties, annotated, and saved. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. The making happens where the student makes things, which is their school workshop, their home or a facility they have arranged, and a tutor is not present for it in any delivery model.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.programmesIntro: The habits Design Technology assesses are started earlier and finished in the Diploma core. These are the three levels a Dubai family is normally dealing with when they contact us about this subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Design
programmes.description: Middle Years Design is where the design cycle is learned or faked. Its criteria reward inquiry and analysis, the development of ideas, the creation of a solution and honest evaluation, in that order. Students who have been rewarded for producing an attractive final object without documenting the reasoning behind it arrive in the Diploma with a habit that is actively penalised, because the Diploma folder marks the process and treats the artefact as evidence of it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai runs both routes into the Diploma: Middle Years Design to Year 11 in IB schools, and IGCSE Design and Technology in the British-curriculum sector. IGCSE students usually arrive with better making skills and less practice at documenting iteration, because their coursework rewarded the outcome more directly. We check which habit a student brings before planning any hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Design Technology
programmes.description: Design Technology is a Group 4 subject assessed through written papers and a design project documented as a folder with page or screen limits. The written papers test core design content plus extension material at the higher level, and the folder is marked on criteria covering analysis, development, modelling, testing and evaluation. Confirm the current component structure, criteria letters, mark allocations and page limits with your school's IB coordinator before planning against them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai provision varies enormously. Some schools have a well-equipped design suite with laser cutting, 3D printing and a technician. Others run the subject with a computer room and goodwill. Which of those your child is in determines what tutoring has to supply and what the making budget looks like, and it is worth asking the head of design directly rather than relying on a prospectus photograph.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and the Group 4 project
programmes.description: An Extended Essay in Design Technology is a research essay rather than a making project, and that catches students out: it needs a researchable question with evidence, not a prototype. The Group 4 project is collaborative and assessed on participation, and design students often contribute the modelling and prototyping skill the group lacks, which is useful experience and carries no marks for the artefact itself.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai offers genuinely strong Extended Essay material in this subject: cooling and shading in high ambient temperatures, materials behaviour in sustained heat, water use in buildings, and product adaptation for a market with a very wide range of household budgets. The constraint is finding evidence rather than finding a topic, and the first supervision session is spent on whether sources exist.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Design Technology students in Dubai usually need one or two neighbours covered as well. These are the related Diploma courses our tutors take for the same families, with the demand each one makes.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Assessed through written papers and a documented design project. Marks turn on the quality of the process evidence: a specification that is testable, development that shows real iteration, modelling that informs decisions, and evaluation against the original criteria. The commonest loss is a strong artefact with a folder that does not justify it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Where structural, mechanical and electrical decisions in a design project stop being guesses. Students taking both write stronger justifications on loading, materials and energy, and are far less likely to specify a mechanism that cannot work. The most useful pairing in this subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Relevant to any project with embedded control, sensing or an interface. The programming discipline also helps with documentation habits, since both subjects reward a record of what was tried and why rather than a presentation of the finished state.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Supplies the geometry, trigonometry and modelling a technical drawing and a dimensioned CAD model assume. Students weak here produce drawings that look right and do not resolve, and the error usually surfaces only when something is cut.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The better route for design students who need data handling more than pure technique: user research results, testing data and statistical treatment of trials. Directly useful in the testing and evaluation stages of the folder.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Underpins the materials content, including polymers, composites, corrosion and degradation. A design student with Chemistry writes material selection justifications that explain behaviour rather than restating a property table, which is where the better marks sit.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside Design Technology by Dubai students heading toward architecture or product design. The two reward different things: Visual Arts marks intention and critical framing, Design Technology marks the resolution of a specified problem. Keeping that distinction clear improves both folders.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Useful for the commercial side of the design content: markets, costing, production scale and product lifecycles. Students taking both are better at the commercial production sections of the papers, which other candidates tend to answer in generalities.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.levels: Both levels, confirm with your school
subjects.description: Overlaps on sustainability, life-cycle analysis and resource use. Helpful for a design student whose project claims an environmental benefit, because it supplies the vocabulary and the evidence standard to support that claim rather than asserting it.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research, and in this subject a research essay rather than a project. Supervision is questioning and written feedback on the student's own drafts; the school's registered supervisor signs the work off.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.regionsIntro: Lessons are online, so an address does not change who can teach. It does change the school's design provision, how far a student is from anywhere that can make a part, and when a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Khail Gate
regions.note: The emirate's workshop and fabrication district, and the most useful area in Dubai for a design student who needs something cut, printed or welded. Access is through a parent arranging a commercial job rather than through a student turning up, and minimum order quantities are the usual obstacle.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University campuses and technology-park facilities nearby, which occasionally open fabrication access through a school partnership. Worth asking the head of design whether such an arrangement exists, because where it does it removes most of the making budget.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Dubai Hills
regions.note: A dense cluster of IB and British schools, several with genuinely equipped design suites including laser cutting and 3D printing with a technician on site. Students here more often need folder discipline than fabrication access, which is a cheaper problem to solve.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Lake Towers
regions.note: Apartment living with no space, no ventilation and no tolerance for dust, so prototyping has to be modelled, printed or made at school. Projects designed around assembly of bought components rather than fabrication of new ones work far better for students here.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Villa households with garage or outdoor space, which makes hand-built prototyping feasible in the cooler months. Afternoon traffic on the beach-road corridor pushes session times past 17:00 for most families in this stretch.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Space to build and a long drive to anywhere that sells materials, so projects here benefit from consolidating purchases into one trip rather than iterating with repeat visits. Weekend morning sessions dominate because weekday evenings are taken by co-curriculars.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Wide catchment across several curricula, with retail and trade suppliers reasonably close. Design Technology candidates here are often the only ones in their year, which means the folder gets little peer comparison and benefits more than usual from outside review.

regions.name: Downtown, Business Bay and Jumeirah Village
regions.note: Mixed residential and commercial, with studio and maker-type facilities within reach. Shorter school runs make these among the most flexible areas in the emirate for scheduling, including the mid-afternoon slots most families cannot use.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools with established design provision
schoolClusters.note: Design Technology needs equipment, a technician and timetabled workshop access, so it appears in Dubai where a school has invested in all three. KHDA inspects these schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Ask the head of design what machines are available to a Diploma student unsupervised, and what the school pays for.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools where design students work with limited workshop access
schoolClusters.note: Plenty of Dubai schools run the subject with a computer room, a 3D printer and a willing teacher. That is a workable setting and it changes the project strategy: designs resolve around modelling, assembly of bought components and documented testing rather than around fabrication from raw material.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.modesIntro: Design Technology support works best bought against a stage of the project, because each stage has an obvious deliverable and a point past which help is worth much less. These are the four blocks Dubai families book.

modes.title: Specification and early-ideas review
modes.description: Two to four sessions, booked before anything is built, and the highest-value block in the subject by a wide margin. The work is interrogation: is the design problem defined from real user research, is every specification point testable, do the early ideas address the brief or restate it. A specification that cannot be tested produces a folder whose later stages have nothing to measure against, and that is a cap on the mark rather than a detail.
bullets: User research reviewed for evidence rather than assumption
Every specification point tested for whether it can be measured
Early ideas checked for genuine divergence rather than cosmetic variants
A testing plan sketched now, so the later stages have criteria to meet

modes.title: Folder review cycle
modes.description: Recurring sessions across the development and modelling stages, where the student brings the pages they have produced and gets them read against the criteria. The tutor annotates on screen, the student makes the changes, and the next session starts from the revised version. This is the block that prevents a folder drifting into a photograph album of a finished object with no visible reasoning.
bullets: Pages read against criteria rather than against taste
Annotation on a shared screen, with the student keeping file control
Iteration evidenced as decisions taken, not as images collected
Page and screen limits respected from the start rather than cut later

modes.title: Written papers block
modes.description: Weekly or fortnightly sessions on the examined content, which students treat as secondary to the project and should not. One timed question set per session, marked and returned, with teaching driven by the script. The extension material at higher level is scheduled as its own run of sessions because it is taught last and practised least, exactly like an option paper in other sciences.
bullets: One timed question set written and marked each session
Materials, production and commercial content taught with real examples
Higher level extension scheduled as a named block, not absorbed
A running list of the student's recurring errors

modes.title: Late-stage triage
modes.description: Booked when a project has stalled or a folder is thin weeks before an internal deadline. Sessions are honest about what can still change: usually the testing, the evaluation and the documentation of decisions already taken, rarely the specification or the direction. We say at the consultation which of those your child is in, because selling a rebuild that cannot happen is the easiest money in this market and the least useful.
bullets: A written statement of what can and cannot still be changed
Testing and evaluation prioritised, since those marks stay reachable
Existing decisions documented retrospectively but honestly
No pretence that a late folder review is the same as an early one

sections.heading: The making budget, and who actually pays for it
paragraphs: Ask the head of design two questions at the start of DP1: what does the school supply, and what does a family supply. The answers vary widely between Dubai schools and they determine a cost no tutoring quote will ever mention. Some schools provide sheet material, filament, consumables and technician time as part of the course. Some provide the machines and expect families to bring material. Some provide neither and the subject is run around what a student can source themselves.

The spend itself is not usually dramatic in a single line. It becomes significant through iteration, which is exactly what the criteria reward. A project that documents three physical iterations has bought material three times. A student who prints a part, finds the tolerance wrong and prints again has paid twice for one component. A folder printed and bound for submission costs more than families expect in a city where plotting and large-format printing are priced commercially. None of this is a reason to avoid the subject; it is a reason to plan it.

The practical lever is project strategy rather than frugality. A design resolved around the assembly of bought components, with modelling and simulation doing the iteration work, costs a fraction of one resolved around fabricating new parts, and it can score identically because the criteria reward documented reasoning rather than expenditure. Students in Marina apartments arrive at this strategy by necessity and often produce cleaner folders than students with a garage.

The table lists the spend lines, says who normally carries each in a Dubai school, and names the way to reduce it that does not cost marks. Confirm your own school's position before assuming any row applies, because provision in this emirate is genuinely inconsistent.

sections.heading: Where a Dubai student can actually get something made
paragraphs: This is the question that separates a workable design project from an ambitious one, and it has a Dubai-specific answer. The city has a large and accessible fabrication economy, concentrated in Al Quoz and the industrial areas, that will make almost anything. What it is not set up for is a school student arriving with one part and a drawing. Commercial workshops price for commercial jobs, with minimum charges and lead times, and they expect a drawing they can work from rather than a sketch.

The order of preference for a Diploma student is therefore reasonably clear. The school workshop first, because it is free, supervised and designed for this. Additive printing second, at school or on a domestic machine, because it absorbs iteration cheaply. Assembly of bought components third, which removes fabrication from the critical path entirely. A commercial job last, consolidated into a single order, with a dimensioned drawing prepared properly and a parent making the arrangement.

One route worth asking about specifically is institutional access. Several Dubai universities and technology parks run facilities that occasionally open to schools through a formal arrangement, and where your child's school has one, it changes the project's horizon. The head of design will know whether such an arrangement exists; a student emailing a university directly generally will not get far.

The table lists the routes with what each can realistically produce, how access works, and what to confirm before a project design depends on it. Confirm every access position yourself before committing a project to it: facilities, policies and supervision requirements change, and a design that depends on a machine the student turns out not to be allowed to use is a design that has to be rethought in the worst week of the year.

sections.heading: Costing support by project stage rather than by the hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate is a poor planning tool in this subject because the stages need wildly different amounts of help. The specification stage needs very few hours and they are the most valuable hours in the project. The development stage needs recurring short reviews. The testing and evaluation stages need a burst. The written papers need steady low-level work across two years. Quoting all of that as one monthly figure hides the shape of it and encourages a family to buy a uniform retainer, which is usually more expensive and less effective.

The breakdown below is what we see for a reasonably diligent Dubai student whose school teaches the subject competently. Where a school runs Design Technology without a specialist, the papers line roughly doubles and the folder line grows, because the tutor is teaching rather than supplementing. Where a school has a strong design department, families often buy only the specification review and the testing burst, and that is a perfectly sensible purchase.

The AED column applies other providers' published market bands rather than an IB Gram rate, and the hours are planning estimates for a committed student rather than promises. There is deliberately no total, because the stages are a menu. The single most common mistake we see is a family buying twelve months of weekly sessions when four well-placed blocks would have cost less and produced a better folder.

Read the first row against the second. Specification work costs the fewest hours of anything on the list and determines whether the rest of the project has anything to measure itself against. Development review costs the most hours and can only improve what the specification allowed. A family with a fixed amount to spend should buy the top of the table before the middle of it, which is the opposite of the order in which the market tends to be sold to them, because the early block is the one that looks unnecessary at the moment it is worth the most.

sections.heading: Software, file formats and the licences nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Design Technology families occasionally arrive having been told they need to buy professional modelling software, and they almost never do. Schools licence what they teach, and the sensible default is to work in whatever the school uses so that files move between home, school and the tutor without conversion. Where a student needs something at home, the major modelling packages run free or low-cost educational licences for individuals in full-time education, and the school's design department will know which applies.

The real costs here are smaller and less obvious. Cloud storage large enough for a two-year folder with full-resolution photographs. A drawing tablet, where a student does their ideation digitally and is fighting a trackpad. Printing, if the school submits physical folders. And the time cost of file conversion, which is not money but is the thing that goes wrong on the last weekend before an internal deadline when a model opens in the wrong units or a drawing loses its dimensions.

There is a discipline point attached. Students who work in one package, keep a sensible folder structure, and name files by version and date lose nothing on the last weekend. Students who have the same project spread across three applications and a phone camera roll spend the final days reconstructing rather than finishing, and the folder shows it. Imposing that structure takes one session and it is one of the quietly valuable things an outside reviewer does, because a teacher with a full class rarely has time to audit a student's file management.

Where generated or downloaded content enters the workflow, declare it. A downloaded CAD component, a texture, a reference image or anything produced by a generative tool has to be acknowledged in line with the school's own policy, and the coordinator is the person to ask what that policy requires. The folder is an argument about the student's own decisions, and unacknowledged material undermines the only thing it is marked on.
bullets: Work in the package the school licences, not a package you buy
Educational licences exist for the main modelling tools: ask the design department

sections.heading: The restart: the most expensive thing in a design project
paragraphs: A design project rarely fails because a student cannot make something. It fails because the direction was set on a specification that could not be tested, and that only becomes visible when the testing stage arrives and there is nothing to test against. At that point a student has two options and both cost. They can restart, which discards months of documented work in the term where there is least time. Or they can submit a folder whose later stages do not connect to its earlier ones, which reads exactly as it is.

This is why we price the specification review as the first block and the smallest. Two to four hours spent making every specification point measurable, and checking that the user research is evidence rather than assumption, routinely prevents the whole sequence. It is a hard thing to sell, because at that stage nothing appears to be wrong and the student is enthusiastic. It is also the only point at which the expensive failure is cheap to avoid.

If you are already past it, the honest answer is triage rather than rebuild, and we will say so at the consultation. Late in a project the reachable marks are in testing, evaluation and the documentation of decisions already made. The specification and the direction are usually fixed. A provider who offers to rebuild a folder in six weeks is selling something that does not exist, and a family who has been told the project can be transformed late should treat that claim with real scepticism.

There is a version of this that is worth paying for late, though. Where a student has done good work and documented it badly, the content exists and the folder can be reorganised to show it. That is a genuine recovery and it is different from a rebuild. Telling the two apart is what the first session is for, and it takes an hour rather than a term.

sections.heading: What the school already provides, and what you would be paying for twice
paragraphs: Before buying anything, map what the school already does. In a well-resourced Dubai design department, a Diploma student gets timetabled workshop access, a technician who can help with a machine, a teacher who reads folder drafts, deadlines enforced internally, and the examined content taught properly. A family buying weekly tutoring on top of that is paying twice for most of it, and the useful purchases narrow to a handful of things the school structurally cannot provide.

What a school cannot easily provide is unlimited draft reading, because a teacher with a full timetable cannot read a folder every fortnight for every student. It cannot provide an outside view, which matters because a teacher who has watched a project develop is the least able person to notice that its specification never made sense. And it cannot provide the file-management and documentation audit described earlier, which is boring, valuable and unglamorous.

Where a school does not have a specialist, the picture inverts and nearly everything is worth buying: the content, the folder supervision, the drawing standards and the project strategy. That is a different and larger purchase, and it should be priced as teaching rather than as supplementing. Families in this position are the ones who most need an honest conversation about hours before they commit.

The table sets the two settings side by side. Use it to decide what to ask for rather than what to buy: the fastest way to waste money in this subject is to buy a generic weekly slot when what was needed was three specific interventions.

sections.heading: Three questions that make two Design Technology quotes comparable
paragraphs: Quotes in this market are not comparable as given, because providers include different work at similar prices. Three questions resolve most of it, and all three can be asked in a first phone call before anything is paid.

The first is whether folder reading between sessions is inside the hourly rate or billed separately. In a subject assessed through a documented folder this is the main unit of work, and a tutor who reads eight pages properly has spent most of an hour doing it. A rate that covers contact time only is cheaper and leaves the central task undone. The second is what the tutor will refuse to do with a student's files, and the answer should be specific: no editing of the student's CAD model, no producing of drawings, no writing of folder text. A provider who cannot name a refusal is a provider with no line.

The third is about the examined papers, and it catches people out. Ask how the written content will be covered and when, because a tutor who is strong on projects and vague on the papers is half a Design Technology tutor. The folder carries internal marks and the papers carry the rest, and a student with a strong folder and unpractised papers lands in the middle regardless.

A fourth question is worth asking if the subject matters a great deal to your family: how many Diploma design projects has this person supervised to completion, and can they describe one that went wrong and why. The answer to the second half is the informative one. Everybody has a success story; the people who have genuinely done this have a specification failure they still think about.
bullets: Is folder reading between sessions inside the quoted rate?
What exactly will you refuse to do with my child's files?
How and when will the written papers be covered?
Describe a design project you supervised that went wrong, and why

sections.heading: Honesty when money can buy making
paragraphs: Design Technology has an integrity problem the other sciences do not, because part of the assessed work is a physical object and physical objects can be bought. A family in Dubai can commission a workshop to build something to a drawing, and the result will be better finished than anything a sixteen-year-old makes in a school workshop. If the folder then presents that object as the student's own making, the submission misrepresents what happened.

The workable distinction is between a process a student directed and a process a student outsourced. Commissioning a specific operation that the school cannot perform, documenting that it was commissioned, stating the drawing supplied and the instructions given, is legitimate engineering practice and can be written up honestly. Handing over a brief and receiving a finished product is not, and the folder cannot be made to say otherwise. Where there is any doubt, the coordinator decides, not the tutor and not the family.

Generated content raises the same question in a different register. A rendered image produced by a generative tool, a specification drafted by one, or an evaluation paragraph lightly edited from one is not the student's work. In this subject such text has a recognisable profile: fluent, plausible and untethered from the actual project, with an evaluation that would fit any product. The school's acknowledgement policy governs what must be declared, and the coordinator is the person to ask.

Our own line is narrow and we state it before anyone pays. A tutor may ask any question about the project and may not supply any sentence, any drawing or any model. The tutor can say that a specification point cannot be measured, that a tolerance will not work, that a folder page shows a result without the decision behind it, or that an evaluation is generic. The tutor does not propose the design, does not edit the student's files, and does not produce content that appears in the submission. We also do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those belong to the board and are the school's to distribute.

sections.heading: What a parent is entitled to ask, check and have deleted
paragraphs: Three things are worth knowing before engaging anyone for a UAE student, and they are rarely set out. The first is the permit position. Private tutoring here is lawful and regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, no figure is quoted here. A UAE-resident tutor can be asked to show their permit, and a reasonable one will.

The second is what nobody can claim. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, occupies no premises in the UAE, and claims no approval, accreditation, licensing or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. Any provider advertising regulator-approved tutors is making a claim worth asking them to evidence. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way, so a family should not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by their own class teacher.

The third is data, and it matters more in this subject than in most. A design project generates photographs of a student's work, sometimes of the student making it, drawings, models and written drafts. Under the UAE's personal data protection law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, a family is entitled to know what is collected about a child, why, how long it is kept and how to have it removed. Ask any provider those four questions. Ours is that session materials and shared files belong to the student, are used only to teach them, and are deleted on request; nothing of a child's work is published or used as marketing without written permission from a parent.

Delivery is online: one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and moved post-Iftar in Ramadan. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India. The making happens wherever the student makes things and no tutor is present for it in any model. If no Design Technology specialist is free in your slot we say so and estimate when one will be, rather than assigning a physicist quietly. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card required to book it.

process.title: Send the specification and two folder pages
process.description: The most informative first documents are the current specification and any two pages of the folder, plus the school's internal deadline. A specialist can tell from the specification alone whether the project is heading somewhere testable, which is the information a Dubai family most needs before spending anything.

process.title: We say which stage you are in, honestly
process.description: Early in a project, the useful block is specification review. Late, it is triage on testing, evaluation and documentation. These are different purchases at different prices and we name which one applies rather than offering a generic weekly slot that suits neither.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a real page
process.description: The trial is a working session, usually spent reading one folder page or one specification against the criteria and showing what a reviewer sees. No card is required and nothing is charged if you stop there. Families often take that single piece of feedback and act on it alone, which is a fine outcome.

process.title: A written plan by stage with deliverables
process.description: After the trial you receive a short plan naming the stages, the hours each needs, what exists at the end of each one, and what the student has to produce between sessions. The AED context on this page is other providers' market data; your own quote comes from the consultation.

process.title: Annotated pages stay with the student
process.description: Every review returns the student's own pages with annotation, and the files stay under the student's control throughout. Reading three consecutive reviews shows a parent whether the same weakness keeps recurring, which is how we decide a block is finished rather than letting it roll on.

whyPoints.title: The making budget is on the page
whyPoints.description: Every provider quotes the teaching and none of them mentions material, printing, components, iterations and external fabrication. We set those out with who normally pays each in a Dubai school, so a family can see the real cost of this subject before committing.

whyPoints.title: Costed by stage, not sold as a retainer
whyPoints.description: The specification stage needs two to four hours and is worth the most. Development needs recurring short reviews. Testing needs a burst. Pricing all of it as one monthly figure hides that shape, and families who buy the menu rather than the package usually spend less.

whyPoints.title: Fabrication routes that exist in this city
whyPoints.description: Al Quoz will make anything for a commercial job with a dimensioned drawing and a minimum charge, and that is a parent arrangement rather than a student errand. We plan projects around what a Dubai student can actually access, including when the answer is to design around assembly.

whyPoints.title: Files stay the student's
whyPoints.description: A tutor may ask any question about the project and may not supply any sentence, drawing or model. We do not edit a student's CAD files or write folder text, and we say that before any payment, which is a shorter list of refusals than most providers are willing to give.

whyPoints.title: A stated position on data about your child
whyPoints.description: Design projects generate photographs, drawings and drafts. Under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 you are entitled to know what is held, why and for how long. Ours is used only to teach your child, deleted on request, and never published without written parental permission.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry or examination-board approval and claims none. Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it and dated October 2026, and unverifiable figures, including IB session dates, are left out.

faqs.question: What does a Design Technology project actually cost to build in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Less than families fear if the project is designed well, and considerably more if it is designed around fabricating new parts. The lines are material and stock, additive printing consumables, bought components, repeat iterations when a dimension is wrong, folder output if submission is physical, and external fabrication with its minimum charge. Iteration is what grows the total, and iteration is also what the criteria reward, so the lever is strategy rather than frugality. A project resolved around assembly of bought components with modelling doing the iteration work can score identically for a fraction of the spend.

faqs.question: Does our school pay for prototype materials?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school and you should ask the head of design directly at the start of DP1. Dubai provision is genuinely inconsistent: some departments supply sheet material, filament, consumables and technician time as part of the course; some supply the machines and expect families to bring material; a few supply neither, and the subject runs on what students source themselves. The answer changes both your budget and the sensible project strategy, so it is worth having in writing. Ask at the same time which machines a Diploma student is permitted to use unsupervised.

faqs.question: Where can my child get a part printed or machined in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School first, because it is free and supervised. A domestic or school 3D printer second, since additive printing absorbs iteration cheaply. For anything the school cannot make, the commercial workshops in Al Quoz and the industrial areas will machine, weld or cut almost anything, but they price for commercial jobs with a minimum charge and a lead time, and they expect a dimensioned drawing rather than a sketch. That is a parent commissioning a job, not a student turning up. Consolidate every external part into one order, and confirm the drawing standard the workshop needs before relying on a date.

faqs.question: Which CAD software do we need to buy?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly none. Work in whatever package the school licences and teaches, so files move between home, school and any reviewer without conversion losing dimensions or units. Where a student needs access at home, the major modelling packages run free or low-cost educational licences for individuals in full-time education, and the design department will know which applies to your school. The costs that are real here are smaller: enough cloud storage for a two-year folder at full photographic resolution, and a drawing tablet if the student ideates digitally and is fighting a trackpad.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to restart a design project?
faqs.answer: More than anything else in the subject, which is why the specification review is the block we sell first. A restart discards months of documented work in the term where time is shortest, and the usual alternative, submitting a folder whose later stages do not connect to its earlier ones, caps the mark. Two to four hours making every specification point measurable, early, routinely prevents the whole sequence. If you are already past that point, ask for triage on testing, evaluation and documentation rather than a rebuild, and treat any offer to transform a folder in six weeks with real scepticism.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy support by stage or by the month?
faqs.answer: By stage, in most cases, and by a meaningful margin. The stages need very different amounts of help: specification needs two to four hours and is the most valuable, development needs recurring short reviews across two terms, testing and evaluation need bursts, and the written papers need steady low-level work. A uniform monthly retainer charges the same for all of that and encourages buying hours in the weeks where they add least. Families who treat the stages as a menu typically spend less and submit better folders, which is not what a retainer model is designed to encourage.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay for a folder review in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai bands put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialist IB support at AED 200 to 450 and above, with Design Technology sitting in the specialist band because the tutor needs to read drawings, judge a CAD model and mark papers. Those are other providers' own figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. The question that actually changes the value is whether reading the pages between sessions is inside the rate, because in a folder-assessed subject that reading is the main unit of work.

faqs.question: Does the higher level of Design Technology cost more to support?
faqs.answer: Usually in hours rather than in rate. Any extension material is taught last, revised least and practised almost never, which makes it behave like an option paper in the other sciences: it needs its own named block of question practice rather than absorption into weekly lessons. Schedule it in the term before mocks, when the time exists, rather than alongside the folder write-up when it does not. Confirm the current structure and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning hours against them, because cohorts in Dubai are working from different guide versions.

faqs.question: Can my child commission a workshop to build the prototype?
faqs.answer: A specific operation the school cannot perform can be commissioned and written up honestly, provided the folder states that it was commissioned, what drawing was supplied and what instructions were given. That is ordinary engineering practice. Handing over a brief and receiving a finished product is different, and a folder cannot be made to describe it as the student's making. The distinction is between a process the student directed and one they outsourced. Where there is any doubt, the IB coordinator decides what is acceptable for your child's cohort, not the tutor and not the workshop.

faqs.question: Who owns the photographs of my child's prototype?
faqs.answer: Your child does, and you are entitled to say what happens to them. A design project generates photographs of work and sometimes of the student making it, plus drawings, models and drafts. Under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection, a family can ask any provider what is collected, why, how long it is kept and how to have it removed. Our position is that session materials and shared files belong to the student, are used only to teach them, are deleted on request, and are never published or used as marketing without written parental permission. Ask every provider the same four questions.

faqs.question: What questions make two Design Technology quotes comparable?
faqs.answer: Three, and all of them can be asked before paying. Is folder reading between sessions inside the hourly rate, or billed separately? What exactly will you refuse to do with my child's files? How and when will the examined papers be covered? A fourth is worth asking if the subject matters: how many Diploma design projects have you supervised to completion, and describe one that went wrong and why. The second half of that answer is the informative part, because everyone has a success story and only people who have really done this have a specification failure they still think about.

faqs.question: What if our school has no workshop at all?
faqs.answer: Then the project strategy changes and the grade ceiling does not have to. The criteria reward documented reasoning, iteration and testing rather than fabrication expenditure, so a design resolved around the assembly of bought components, with modelling and simulation carrying the iteration evidence, can score as well as one built from raw stock. Additive printing covers most form and fit testing cheaply. Confirm with the teacher whether your cohort's criteria accept digital-only testing for any stage. Students in Dubai apartments reach this strategy by necessity and frequently submit cleaner folders than students with a garage.

faqs.question: Is a Design Technology tutor more expensive than a Physics tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is supply rather than difficulty. A Design Technology tutor has to read a technical drawing, judge a CAD model, mark a written paper and supervise a folder against process criteria. That combination is rarer than a physicist or a mathematician in this market, so quotes sit in the published AED 200 to 450 specialist band rather than the AED 150 to 300 qualified-tutor band. If a provider explains the premium by saying the subject is harder, ask instead how many design projects they have supervised, because that is the competence being priced.

faqs.question: How many hours does a two-year design project need?
faqs.answer: For a student in a well-resourced Dubai design department, around fifteen to twenty-five hours of outside review across the whole project: two to four on the specification, six to ten of recurring folder reviews, two to four on drawing and CAD critique, and bursts of two to three each on testing and evaluation. Where the school runs the subject without a specialist, expect that to roughly double because the tutor is teaching rather than supplementing. Those are planning estimates for a committed student, not promises, and the written papers are a separate line on top.

faqs.question: Can we pay for only the written papers and skip project support?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some students it is the right purchase. If the school has a strong design department reading folder drafts and the weakness is examination technique, buying only the papers block is sensible and cheaper. The reverse also happens: a student whose papers are fine and whose folder is drifting should buy reviews rather than lessons. We would rather say which of those applies at the consultation than sell both. What does not work is buying neither and hoping, since the folder and the papers each carry a substantial share of the grade.

faqs.question: What should the first Design Technology session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Reading real work, not touring the syllabus. A useful first hour takes the current specification and two folder pages and reads them against the criteria, which tells a family immediately whether the project is heading somewhere testable and whether the folder is showing decisions or just progress. It should also establish what the school supplies, which machines the student may use, and which guide version the cohort follows. A first session spent explaining what Design Technology is has answered a question nobody asked and cost a family an hour of diagnosis.

dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.closingHeading: Send the specification before you send anything else
dubai/ib-dp-design-technology-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB DP Design Technology tutor in Dubai, send the current specification, two pages of the folder and the school's internal deadline. A specialist will tell you whether the project is heading somewhere testable, which stage block is worth buying, and what the making budget is likely to look like given your school's provision. The AED figures on this page are other providers' published market bands from October 2026, given so you can place a quote before taking a call. The first lesson is free, no card is needed, and lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.
